# Commit hooks exec a hard-coded per-user path → `git worktree add` and `wl sync` fail

## Problem statement

The committed hooks `.githooks/post-checkout`, `.githooks/post-merge` and
`.githooks/post-rewrite` unconditionally `exec` the absolute path
`/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`. That path is
per-user and machine-specific, so on any host where it is absent (a different
username, a clean machine, CI) every checkout, merge and `git worktree add` in
this repository exits 127 — which in turn breaks `wl sync` (its
temporary-worktree merge) and `implement.py start`/`finish` worktree creation.
The repository already commits the real script as `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`,
but no wrapper references it.

## Impact

Agents and developers on any machine — not just this one — can now create worktrees, check out, merge and run `wl sync` without the committed git hooks failing on a hard-coded per-user path.

## Reproduction

```sh
cd /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents
# The wrapper hard-codes an absolute path, so the failure is independent of
# $HOME. Simulate a host where that path does not exist by moving the central
# symlink aside for one command (restore it afterwards):
LINK=$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull
mv "$LINK" "$LINK.bak"
git worktree add --detach /tmp/sa-wt-repro HEAD
mv "$LINK.bak" "$LINK"
# → .githooks/post-checkout: 4: exec: /home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull: not found
# → rc=127 (verified during intake)
```

On the current agent host the immediate trigger is masked because
`/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` exists as a symlink to
this repo's committed script (installed by `scripts/install_pi.sh`), so normal
runs here exit 0 ("worklog: sync failed or not initialized; continuing"). The
defect is therefore latent on this host and reproduces on every host or clean
clone where that absolute path is absent.

## Users

- **AI agent driving `/skill:implement`** — needs `implement.py start`/`finish`
  to create worktrees without a hook failure aborting the run.
  Story: *As an implementing agent, when I start work on an item, the worktree
  is created successfully even though the machine has no central hook install.*
- **Agent or developer running `wl sync`** — needs the sync push to complete.
  Story: *As an agent publishing Worklog data, `wl sync` completes its push
  step on a clean clone without setting `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` or
  `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`.*
- **Developer on a second machine / CI checkout** — needs the committed hooks
  to be portable.
  Story: *As a developer whose username is not `rgardler`, cloning and
  checking out this repository does not emit `exec: ... not found`.*
- **Framework maintainer** — needs the behaviour pinned by a regression test.
  Story: *As a maintainer of the agent framework, I need a test that fails if a
  committed hook regains a hard-coded per-user path.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **No hard-coded per-user path.** The three wrappers
      (`.githooks/post-checkout`, `post-merge`, `post-rewrite`) resolve the
      post-pull script without any absolute `/home/<user>` path: they first try
      the repository-relative `<toplevel>/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, then
      `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, and when neither exists
      they print one clear line to stderr and exit 0 (never 127, never a silent
      failure).
- [ ] **Regression test proving `git worktree add` succeeds.** A hermetic test
      asserts (a) the committed wrappers contain no absolute `/home/<user>` or
      other machine-specific path; (b) in a temp repository built from the
      committed `.githooks/` with `core.hooksPath=.githooks`, a sandboxed
      `$HOME` that has no `.config/pi`, and a stubbed `wl` on `PATH`,
      `git worktree add --detach <tmp> HEAD` exits 0, emits no
      `exec: ... not found`, and reaches the repo-relative
      `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`; and (c) the same setup with
      `worklog-post-pull` absent takes the graceful no-op path (one stderr
      notice naming the attempted locations, `rc=0`, no sync attempted).
- [ ] **`wl sync` completes its push step** in this repository on a host
      without the central hook install (sandboxed `$HOME`), without the
      `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` / `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` workaround.
- [ ] **Hooks cannot recurse.** A hook-triggered sync from `wl`'s own
      `.worklog/tmp-worktree-*` (and from a linked worktree) exits before
      calling `wl sync`, matching the guards already present in the sibling
      ContextHub/AI_Hell hooks.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries —
      specifically replacing the portability caveat in `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md`
      and updating the `install_pi.sh` fail-open warning to match the new hook
      behaviour.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Hooks are POSIX `sh` executed by git; they must stay dependency-free (no
  python, no network) and fast, because they run on every checkout/merge.
- `$HOME` and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` must both be treated as
  best-effort: hook execution inherits git's environment, and earlier incidents
  (SA-0MV0G9BF7008S01K, SA-0MUIZSXEY008NGR8) showed `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_*` pollution
  in spawned sessions. Every resolution step fails open.
- Keep the shared-script model (one implementation in
  `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`) rather than inlining a copy into each wrapper;
  the sibling repositories' self-contained hooks are precedent for the guards,
  not for duplicating sync logic.
- Do not touch the `pre-push` hook behaviour (`worklog:pre-push-hook:v3`) or the
  full-suite gate; this item changes only the post-pull chain.
- Sibling project checkouts (`ContentCreator`, `ContextHub`, `AI_Hell`) are out
  of scope; the ContextHub/AI_Hell copies are reference implementations only,
  and any divergence found there becomes a linked follow-up item.
- Build → test → commit order; no ad-hoc `pytest` — use the test skill /
  `run_tests.py`.
- Preserve the existing bypass variables (`WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1`,
  `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1`) and their documented semantics.

## Existing state (verified during intake)

- The three wrappers are 184-byte files with header
  `worklog:post-pull-hook:v1` and a single
  `exec "/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull" "$@"` line
  (`.githooks/post-checkout`, `post-merge`, `post-rewrite`).
- `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` **is committed** (514 bytes; runs `wl sync`,
  honours `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1`, fail-open when `wl` is absent). Nothing
  in the repository invokes it: `rg worklog-post-pull` finds only the wrappers'
  hard-coded path, `scripts/install_pi.sh` (central install), one test file and
  the docs.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` installs the central script as an executable symlink
  to the repo copy (`create_symlink`, idempotent, `PI_SKIP_HOOK_INSTALL=1`
  gated) and then emits a **warning only** when a project's committed wrapper
  does not reference that central path. The warning does not fix the wrapper.
- `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` (~lines 100–120) documents the delegation and
  carries a "Portability caveat (SA-0MVK1Q30O0067NXX)" paragraph describing
  exactly this defect as unresolved.
- Sibling repositories (`ContextHub`, `AI_Hell`) ship
  self-contained `post-checkout`/`worklog-post-pull` hooks that (a) skip
  `*tmp-worktree-*` paths and (b) skip linked worktrees
  (`git rev-parse --git-dir` vs `--git-common-dir`). The SorraAgents copy of
  `worklog-post-pull` lacks both guards. (`ContentCreator` is reported in the
  consolidated duplicate item to have the same self-contained pattern, but that
  checkout is not present on this host, so it was not verified directly.)
- Verified on this host: `git worktree add --detach /tmp/sa-wt-intake-check HEAD`
  now exits 0 ("worklog: sync failed or not initialized; continuing") because
  the central symlink exists — the hard-coded path is what breaks elsewhere.
- `tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` covers the *installer* and writes
  its own synthetic hooks; no test asserts the content or behaviour of this
  repository's committed wrappers.
- `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` and `tests/test_pre_push_hook_fallback.py`
  cover the pre-push wiring only.

## Desired change

1. Rewrite the three wrappers to resolve the post-pull script in this order:
   repository-relative (via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, falling back to
   `dirname "$0"`), then `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, then a
   single-line stderr notice + `exit 0`. No literal `/home/<user>` anywhere.
2. Add the `*tmp-worktree-*` and linked-worktree guards to
   `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` so a hook-triggered sync cannot nest inside
   `wl sync`'s own temporary worktree, mirroring the sibling implementations.
3. Update the `install_pi.sh` portability warning to reflect the fixed
   behaviour (warning remains a guard for *forked/older* wrappers only).
4. Replace the docs caveat with the actual resolution order and the no-op
   behaviour; document the bypass variables.
5. Add the hermetic regression test described in the ACs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.githooks/post-checkout`, `.githooks/post-merge`, `.githooks/post-rewrite` — replace the hard-coded `exec` with portable resolution + graceful no-op.
- `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` — add tmp-worktree and linked-worktree guards; keep `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL` bypass.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — adjust the fail-open portability warning/message to the new contract.
- `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` — replace the portability caveat with the resolution order and no-op semantics.
- `tests/test_githooks_portability.py` — new hermetic regression tests (worktree add succeeds under a sandboxed `$HOME`; no-op path; bypass; no hard-coded `/home/<user>` in committed hooks).
- `tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` — extend only if the installer warning contract changes.

## Related work

- `SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP` — *Chore: install central wl post-pull hook
  (~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull) missing* (completed): installed the
  central symlink and the wrapper-to-central delegation this item now makes
  portable.
- `SA-0MVK2PK7F002LET6` — *SorraAgents committed git hooks exec a missing
  central script* (closed as duplicate of this item; its reproduction
  transcript, sibling self-contained-hook precedent and `WORKLOG_SKIP_*`
  behaviour are folded in above).
- `SA-0MV8M4OVX000QHSM` — *install_pi.sh propagates the SorraAgents-only test
  gate to non-SorraAgents projects* (completed): precedent for project-vs-framework
  hook variants in the same installer block.
- `SA-0MV0G9BF7008S01K`, `SA-0MUIZSXEY008NGR8` — hook/GIT environment
  investigations that motivate fail-open resolution.
- `SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX` — pre-push git-identity guard (same hook family; do not
  regress it).
- Related docs: `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md`, `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`.
- Related files: `.githooks/pre-push` (v3 pattern for `git rev-parse`-based
  resolution), sibling `.githooks/{post-checkout,worklog-post-pull}` in
  `ContextHub`/`AI_Hell`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** repo-relative resolution is the intended shape (the ACs allow
  either repo-relative delegation or inline logic; the repository already
  commits `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, so reusing it is the minimal change).
- **Assumption:** keeping `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` as a
  second candidate preserves compatibility with framework projects whose
  wrappers are installed by `install_pi.sh`.
- **Risk:** `git rev-parse` inside a hook can be misled by `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_*`
  pollution. Mitigation: `2>/dev/null`, fall back to `dirname "$0"`, then
  `$HOME`, then no-op.
- **Risk:** a no-op can hide a broken install. Mitigation: the stderr line names
  both attempted paths and points at `scripts/install_pi.sh`.
- **Risk:** the new test could invoke real `wl` (network/sync side effects).
  Mitigation: sandboxed `$HOME`, stub `wl` on `PATH`, or assert the no-op path
  only; never perform a real sync in the test.
- **Scope-creep risk:** rewriting hooks in sibling repositories, redesigning
  `wl sync`, or changing the pre-push gate are out of scope; record as linked
  follow-up items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were asked in this intake: the seed brief, the
reproduction transcript from the consolidated duplicate, and repository
inspection supplied enough detail to draft an unambiguous brief.

Research performed (evidence links):

- Q (self-resolved): "Does the repository already contain the post-pull
  script?" — Answer: **yes**, `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` is committed
  (514 bytes) but unreferenced by the wrappers. Evidence: `rg worklog-post-pull`;
  file contents.
- Q (self-resolved): "Why does the failure not appear on this host?" — Answer:
  the wrappers hard-code `/home/rgardler`, and on this host the
  `scripts/install_pi.sh` install (`SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP`) provides that exact
  path as a symlink to the repo script, so checkout succeeds and the defect is
  latent. Removing the symlink for one command reproduces `rc=127`; changing
  `$HOME` alone does not, because the path is absolute. Evidence:
  `mv …/worklog-post-pull …; git worktree add …; mv back` (verified during
  intake), `ls -la ~/.config/pi/.githooks`.
- Q (self-resolved): "Is there a precedent implementation?" — Answer: **yes**,
  `ContextHub` and `AI_Hell` ship self-contained post-checkout hooks with
  `*tmp-worktree-*` and linked-worktree guards. Evidence: sibling `.githooks/`
  contents (`ContentCreator` not present on this host).
- Q (self-resolved): "Is the defect already tested?" — Answer: **no**.
  `tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` tests the installer with synthetic
  hooks; nothing asserts the committed wrappers. Evidence: `rg` over `tests/`.
- Duplicate check performed: `wl search "post-pull hook"` / `"worklog hook"`
  found `SA-0MVK2PK7F002LET6` (same defect), closed as a duplicate of this item;
  no other overlapping open or completed item found.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVK2PK7F002LET6** – SorraAgents committed git hooks exec a missing central script (~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull) (completed)
- **SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP** – Chore: install central wl post-pull hook (~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull) missing (completed)
- **SA-0MV0G9BF7008S01K** – GIT_DIR evidence: trace non-destructive env propagation path (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: aborting, absent, absolute, acceptance, acs (+344 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: absent, absolute, acceptance, acs, actual (+314 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: aborting, absent, absolute, actual, add (+294 more)
## Plan (2026-10-27)

**Decision: single leaf item — no child decomposition.** The change is one
atomic fix to a small, tightly-coupled hook contract (three wrappers + the
script they exec + installer wiring + docs) estimated **Small / Medium**
(5.42h expected). Splitting it into child items would leave intermediate
commits with a half-portable hook chain and a red suite — the committed suite
must be green at every commit — so the work is implemented as one vertical
slice that cuts through hooks, installer, tests and docs.

Rationale recorded per the plan skill's step 5 (phasing not required for an
item of this size; documented rather than silently skipped).

**Duplicate check:** `wl search "post-pull hook" | "worklog hook" |
"githooks portability" | "worktree add 127"` found no open item covering these
ACs. `SA-0MVK2PK7F002LET6` is the already-closed duplicate of this item;
`SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP` (completed) installed the central symlink;
`SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1` (open) is precedent for the *local-then-global
resolution* pattern in the pre-push hook and stays a separate item.

### Implementation order (test-first; suite green at each commit)

1. **Tests first** — add `tests/test_githooks_portability.py`, hermetic and
   offline, covering:
   - (a) static: no committed wrapper contains `/home/<user>` or another
     machine-specific absolute path (guards AC1);
   - (b) temp repository built from the committed `.githooks/` with
     `core.hooksPath=.githooks`, a sandboxed `$HOME` with no `.config/pi`, and
     a stub `wl` on `PATH` → `git worktree add --detach` exits 0, prints no
     `exec: ... not found`, and the repo-relative
     `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` is the script that ran (marker file);
   - (c) same setup with `worklog-post-pull` removed → `rc=0`, exactly one
     stderr notice naming both attempted locations, stub `wl` never invoked;
   - (d) `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` bypasses the sync;
   - (e) recursion guards: `PWD` containing `tmp-worktree-`, and a linked
     worktree (`--git-dir` ≠ `--git-common-dir`), both exit before `wl sync`.
2. **Rewrite the three wrappers** (`.githooks/post-checkout`, `post-merge`,
   `post-rewrite`) to resolve `worklog-post-pull` as: repo-relative
   (`<toplevel>/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, falling back to
   `dirname "$0"/worklog-post-pull`) → `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/...` →
   one-line stderr notice + `exit 0`. Test for existence/executability before
   `exec` so a missing script can never produce 127. Keep the
   `worklog:post-pull-hook:v1` marker (no version bump: `install_pi.sh`
   detects wiring by content, and the sibling projects use v1 markers).
   *Commit A: tests + wrappers.*
3. **Add recursion guards** to `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`: skip
   `*tmp-worktree-*` paths and linked worktrees before the `wl sync` call,
   mirroring the ContextHub/AI_Hell copies; keep the
   `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` bypass first.
4. **Update `scripts/install_pi.sh`**: the fail-open portability warning must
   now fire only for *legacy/foreign* wrappers (no repo-relative resolution and
   no reference to `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`), and must no
   longer warn about this repository's fixed wrappers; refresh the explanatory
   comment block. *Commit B: guards + installer.*
5. **Docs**: replace the "Portability caveat (SA-0MVK1Q30O0067NXX)" paragraph
   in `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` with the resolution order, the no-op
   behaviour and the bypass variables. Touch
   `tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` only if the installer warning
   contract changed. *Commit C: docs.*
6. **Verify**: changed-scope tests, then the full suite via `/skill:test`
   (AC6); capture AC3 evidence (see below). *Commit D only if fix-ups are
   needed.*

### AC → verification map

| AC | Proven by |
|----|-----------|
| No hard-coded per-user path | static scan (test 1a) + resolution/`exit 0` behaviour in tests 1b/1c |
| Regression test proves `git worktree add` succeeds | tests 1a, 1b, 1c |
| `wl sync` completes its push step without the central install | see *AC3 evidence* note |
| Hooks cannot recurse | test 1e |
| Docs updated | review diff of `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md`, comment blocks and `install_pi.sh` |
| Full suite passes | `/skill:test` full scope before the dev push |

**AC3 evidence note.** No automated test may perform a real sync (risk noted
below). Preferred proof: a hermetic temp clone with a **local bare remote** and
a sandboxed `$HOME`, running `wl sync` so its push step completes with no
network access and no `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` / `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`
workaround. If `wl` cannot push to a local remote in that sandbox, record the
manual transcript (commands + exit codes) as a comment on this item instead —
the AC is satisfied by evidence, not necessarily by a test.

### Implementation notes

- Keep the shared-script model: the wrappers delegate; only
  `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` contains sync logic (no inlined copies).
- Survive `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_*` pollution (`SA-0MV0G9BF7008S01K`,
  `SA-0MUIZSXEY008NGR8`): every `git rev-parse` is `2>/dev/null`-guarded and
  falls through to `$HOME`, then the no-op.
- Do not touch `.githooks/pre-push` / `pre-push.v2`, the full-suite gate or the
  `worklog:pre-push-hook:v3` marker.
- Sibling checkouts (`ContextHub`, `AI_Hell`) are reference only; any
  divergence found there becomes a linked follow-up item, not an edit here.

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-27** — Plan applied: single-leaf decision recorded, test-first
  implementation order, AC→verification map and AC3 evidence note added;
  duplicate check performed (no overlapping open item); effort/risk reused from
  the 2026-10-23 estimate (Small / Medium, 5.42h expected); stage advanced to
  `plan_complete`.

## Appendix: Plan session (2026-10-27)

No clarifying questions were put to the producer: the intake brief plus the
files verified during this session supplied the plan inputs. Self-resolved
items (each with evidence):

- Q: "Does the repository's committed wrapper content still match the intake
  description?" — **Yes.** Each of `.githooks/post-checkout`, `post-merge` and
  `post-rewrite` is the 3-comment-line wrapper ending in
  `exec "/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull" "$@"`; the
  committed `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` is the shared script and lacks the
  `*tmp-worktree-*` and linked-worktree guards. Evidence: file contents read
  this session.
- Q: "What exactly do the sibling guards look like, for reuse?" — **Answered**
  by `ContextHub/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` and `AI_Hell/.githooks/
  worklog-post-pull`: `case "$PWD" in *tmp-worktree-*) exit 0 ;; esac` then
  `[ "$(git rev-parse --git-dir 2>/dev/null)" != "$(git rev-parse
  --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)" ] && exit 0`, both before the `wl sync` call.
  Precedent for the *resolution* shape comes from
  `SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1` (local-then-global runner lookup in the v3 pre-push
  hook).
- Q: "How does `install_pi.sh` currently decide to warn?" — **It greps the
  project's `.githooks/post-checkout` for the central path it just installed**
  (`scripts/install_pi.sh`, "Fail-open portability check" block). After this
  change the wrappers no longer name that absolute path first, so the check
  must be rewritten to detect *legacy* wrappers (no repo-relative resolution
  and no `$HOME` candidate) rather than deleted — recorded as step 4.
- Q: "Can the hermetic test really avoid a real sync?" — **Yes, for ACs 2, 4
  and 5**: a stub `wl` on `PATH` records invocation, so no sync runs. AC3
  needs the sync's push step, so the cost/shape is recorded as the *AC3
  evidence* note (local bare remote preferred; transcript otherwise).

OPEN QUESTION (directed to the implementer, not blocking): whether a `wl sync`
push to a **local bare remote** works inside a sandboxed `$HOME` without
credentials. If it does not, the AC3 transcript route applies — no change to
the AC text is needed and the plan is unaffected.

# implement.py finish reports status changes that the main worklog store does not show

> **Provenance:** transferred from `OSL-0MVFHAT31007ZILJ` (ContentCreator) per operator decision — this SA item carries the full brief; the OSL item is closed as transferred. The fix belongs here because the defect is in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` and shared `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`, which live in this repo.

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` prints and logs a `completed`/`in_review` transition, but
the work item in the main checkout's worklog store can still read `open` /
`intake_complete` afterwards, so a successful finish can leave an item orphaned
in the queue while the tool claims it is `in_review`.

## Users

- **AI agent driving `/skill:implement`** — needs the post-`finish` state to be
  trustworthy so the next `wl next` does not re-pick a finished item.
  Story: *As an implementing agent, when finish reports `in_review`, a
  subsequent `wl show` from the main checkout must report
  `status=completed, stage=in_review`, so I do not rework a finished item.*
- **Producer/operator auditing the queue** — needs the store to reflect reality.
  Story: *As the producer, I need the queue to show finished items as
  `in_review` without manual repair, so audit does not report phantom open
  work.*
- **Maintainer of the implement skill** — needs the write path to be provable.
  Story: *As a skill maintainer, I need a regression test that pins which store
  finish writes to, so future worklog-resolution changes cannot silently
  regress it.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Reproduce deterministically.** On a scratch work item, run the finish
      sequence (claim → commit → push stub → status transition) from a
      worktree, then read the item from the main checkout; capture, per `wl`
      call, the store (`--worklog-dir`) it targeted. Reproduction is recorded
      in the SA item as a comment with the command transcript.
- [ ] **Prove and fix the target store.** Establish which store each status
      write in `finish` targets (the `StatusLifecycle.__exit__`
      `completed`/`in_review` write in particular) and make the transition
      deterministically target the **main checkout** store — resolved from the
      repo root (`state.repo_root`), not from cwd — for the whole finish run.
- [ ] **Unit regression test.** Test that worklog resolution returns the main
      checkout's `.worklog` when cwd is `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/<wt>`
      (uninitialised worktree store) and that `finish` passes that explicit
      path to every `wl` status/comment call it makes (injected fake runner,
      no real git).
- [ ] **Integration regression test.** A hermetic test that creates a temp git
      repo plus worklog store, runs the finish status transition from a
      worktree, and asserts the **main store** reads `completed`/`in_review`
      afterwards (no network, stubbed push).
- [ ] **Document the finding** — write ordering (the status transition happens
      at `StatusLifecycle.__exit__`, *after* push and worktree removal) and the
      confirmed root cause — in the implement skill reference
      (`skill/implement/SKILL.md`) and, if the resolution rule changes,
      `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`.
- [ ] **File the linked pre-push sync gap** as a separate `discovered-from`
      item: a push from a worktree cwd makes the pre-push hook's
      `wl sync --git-branch refs/worklog/data` fail (`wl` reports
      "not initialized"), so a worktree push never publishes worklog data.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Fix lands in **SorraAgents** (`skill/` is agent infrastructure); do not edit
  the ContentCreator project-local `.pi/` or any vendored copy. The OSL item is
  tracking only and closes as transferred.
- `StatusLifecycle` and `resolve_worklog_flags` are shared by every skill —
  keep the resolution change narrow; existing tests in
  `skill/shared/tests/test_status_lifecycle.py` and `skill/implement/tests/`
  must keep passing without weakening.
- The integration test must be hermetic: temp dirs, a local bare remote or a
  stubbed `git_push_to_dev`, no network, no real `wl sync`.
- Build → test → commit order; no direct `pytest` invocations (use the test
  skill / `run_tests.py`).
- Do not increase the status blast radius: `open` must never be re-applied to
  an item that already reached `completed`/`in_review`.

## Existing state (verified during intake)

- `finish` wraps commit → push → worktree removal → parent-branch sync inside
  `with StatusLifecycle(work_item_id, target_stage="in_review"):`
  (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, ~line 4460); the
  `completed`/`in_review` write therefore happens at `__exit__` (~line 4614),
  after the push.
- `git_push_to_dev(cwd=worktree_path, ...)` pushes **from the worktree**, so
  the pre-push hook runs with cwd = worktree.
- A worktree's `.worklog/` holds `config.yaml`, `config.defaults.yaml`,
  `cache/`, `plugins/` only — no DB, no `initialized` marker. Verified:
  `wl show <id> --json` from `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/<wt>`
  returns `{"success": false, "initialized": false, "error": "Worklog system is
  not initialized…"}`.
- `.githooks/pre-push` runs `wl sync --git-branch refs/worklog/data`; from a
  worktree that command has no item id, so no `--worklog-dir` is injected and
  it fails — the hook prints `WARN: worklog sync failed — pushing anyway`.
  `refs/worklog/data` does not exist in ContentCreator.
- `resolve_worklog_flags` / `worklog_dir_flag` (`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`)
  do resolve the main checkout store from a worktree (prefix-to-sibling scan
  first, then the nearest *initialized* ancestor), and `wl_show` /
  `wl_add_comment` inject those flags — so "the `__exit__` write went to a
  worktree-local store" is **not yet proven**; the observation
  `Captured original status …: open` (the claim was lost before `finish`)
  points at a separate revert path (stale `wl sync` import, or a late
  in-progress reset).
- The store is SQLite (`.worklog/worklog.db`), so "which store did this write
  to" is directly observable by file path and row state.

## Desired change

1. Finish resolves the main checkout store **once** from `state.repo_root` and
   passes it explicitly to every `wl` call it makes, including the
   `StatusLifecycle` transition and the completion comment — no reliance on
   cwd-derived resolution anywhere in the finish path.
2. Verbose/debug logging records, per `wl` mutation, the resolved
   `--worklog-dir`, so a future regression is diagnosable from the log alone.
3. Tests as described in the ACs pin both the resolution rule and the
   observable end state.
4. A short "status write ordering" note in the implement skill reference: the
   transition is written at `__exit__` after push; worktree pushes cannot sync
   worklog data because the worktree store is uninitialised.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — resolve `--worklog-dir` from `repo_root` for the finish path; log the target store per mutation; pass it through `StatusLifecycle`.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — only if the resolution rule needs tightening (e.g. explicit `worklog_dir` support on the context manager); otherwise unchanged.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_status_store.py` — new unit + integration regression tests.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_status_lifecycle.py` — extend resolution assertions for the worktree cwd case.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — document the finding and the write ordering in the reference section.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — cross-reference the worktree-store behaviour if the rule is documented there.

## Related work

- `OSL-0MVFHAT31007ZILJ` — source item, transferred to this item (observed during `OSL-0MVE0A51L0072XSJ`).
- `OSL-0MUI78ROQ005B37N` — *Fix cross-repo worklog resolution in implement.py wl_* helpers (OSL items unfetchable from SorraAgents)* (completed) — precedent: the `resolve_worklog_flags` injection this item builds on.
- `OSL-0MUFG3PJA00379CT` — *implement.py: symlink nested package node_modules into worktrees* (completed) — worktree environment setup.
- Related docs: `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`, `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` (SorraAgents), `skill/implement/SKILL.md`.

**Automated related-work check** (find-related run on the source OSL item):
relevant hit `OSL-0MUI78ROQ005B37N`; the other two hits were generic refactoring items and the repo-file matches were keyword noise (`.llm-wiki` source extracts, unrelated READMEs). Full report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-OSL-0MVFHAT31007ZILJ.md` (ContentCreator).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Root cause unproven.** The write path may already be correct and the revert
  may come from a stale `wl sync` import. Mitigation: AC1 (instrument and
  reproduce) precedes AC2 (fix); the brief does not pre-commit to a cause.
- **Shared helper blast radius.** Changing `resolve_worklog_flags` affects all
  skills. Mitigation: prefer an explicit-path change in `implement.py` over
  changing shared resolution semantics.
- **Integration test cost/flakiness.** Mitigation: hermetic temp repo, stubbed
  push, no network; keep the suite fast.
- **Scope creep.** The pre-push `wl sync` gap and any worklog-sync redesign are
  out of scope — the gap is filed as a linked item (AC6), nothing more.
- **Assumption:** the main checkout's store is the single source of truth for
  an item during implementation (documented in `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`);
  if a project opts into a per-worktree store, the fix must not break it.
- **Assumption:** priority stays `low` (matches the source OSL item); the
  observable impact is queue noise plus manual repair, not data loss.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which repo should carry the fix, tests, and docs — (a) SorraAgents, (b) ContentCreator, or (c) split?" — Answer (operator, interactive reply): **(a) SorraAgents**, plus "close this item when the SorraAgents item is created and synced". Source: interactive reply, this session. Evidence: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` and `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` both live in SorraAgents, symlinked at `~/.pi/agent/skills`.
- Q: "How much of the observed chain is in scope — (a) status visibility only, (b) status visibility plus the pre-push worklog-sync gap, or (c) status visibility now with the sync gap filed as a `discovered-from` follow-up?" — Answer (operator): **(c)**. Source: interactive reply. Evidence: pre-push gap confirmed by probing `wl show` from a worktree (`initialized: false`).
- Q: "Regression test level — (a) unit only, (b) integration only, or (c) both?" — Answer (operator): **(c) both**. Source: interactive reply.
- Prior answers if changed: none.

# Intake Brief — wl sync: guard the push side against sentinel worklog identities (SA-0MVKMVIAK005981E)

> Discovered-from: SA-0MVK4F993008D9S2 (during the SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS epic).

## Problem statement

`wl sync` quarantines *inbound* worklog commits authored by an incident-era sentinel identity (`t@t.com` et al.) — the author-identity gate — but nothing stops a checkout that still carries a sentinel `user.email` from *publishing* worklog commits under that identity in the first place. That is the 2026-10-22 incident (host `RossGameDev` pushed `T <t@t.com>`; every other clone refused to sync until the refs were re-authored by hand) and it recurred with two further inbound `t@t.com` commits on 2026-10-23 (`dec50d4d6`, `893203e8d`). `scripts/check_git_identity.py` detects the state but is advisory and fail-open (pre-push hook only) — a direct `wl sync` (as agent sessions run) has no guard, so the push side remains the durable gap.

## Users

- **Operators** syncing worklog data from any machine/checkout — a checkout with a stale sentinel identity (e.g. `RossGameDev`) must be stopped *before* it publishes.
  - *As an operator, I want `wl sync` to refuse to push when my checkout's identity is a sentinel, so I never strand worklog data for every other clone again.*
- **Agents** invoking `wl sync` directly in sessions — they skip the pre-push hook and currently have no protection.
  - *As an agent, I want the refusal to name the identity and the remedy, so I can fix `git config user.email` instead of shipping a poisoned ref.*
- **Every other clone/consumer** of `refs/worklog/data` — the pull-side gate keeps working, but prevention at the source means no more blocked syncs.
  - *As a syncing clone, I want sentinel-authored commits to never reach the remote ref, so my `wl sync` never refuses on inbound history again.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — A `wl sync` that would push worklog data while the effective `user.email` is empty or an exact incident-era sentinel refuses *before* pushing, naming the identity and the remedy (`git config user.email …`); the refusal applies when push would run (not with `--no-push` and not on the zero-change fast path).
- AC2 — The refusal never applies to the project's configured identity or to `syncAllowedAuthors` entries; the sentinel comparison is exact-email only (lowercased/trimmed match against the `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS` set: `t@t.com`, `t@t`, `test@test.com`, `test@test`, `cache test@test.com`), never a wildcard/substring match.
- AC3 — An explicit escape hatch (`--allow-sentinel-author`) permits a deliberate one-off push, mirroring `--allow-foreign-author`: it never bypasses the empty-email refusal and it is audit-logged in the sync output/log when used.
- AC4 — Regression tests cover the sentinel/empty/config-identity decision as a pure function (Cartesian over effective/configured email × allow-list) plus one CLI-level refusal test; no network.
- AC5 — Documentation: worklog sync docs describe the pull-side gate and the new push-side guard together (remedy, escape hatch, and why sentinels can never be allow-listed).
- AC6 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (ContextHub CLI suite for the new guard; SorraAgents suite remains green).

## Impact

Operators can no longer accidentally publish worklog commits under an incident-era sentinel identity, so every clone's `wl sync` stays mergeable and the manual re-authoring drill (2026-09-26, 2026-10-22, 2026-10-23) becomes unnecessary.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo delivery:** the fix belongs in the **ContextHub worklog CLI** (TypeScript: `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/src/...`, released as the `worklog` npm package), while this item is tracked in the **SorraAgents** worklog because the incident surfaced here. The implement workflow's worktree isolation is repo-scoped — the delivery mechanism (linked ContextHub/WL child item vs. cross-repo delivery directly from this item, cf. SA-0MVZEO59E004BCI8) must be settled at plan time, *before* `implement.py start` (precedent: WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K kept this exact question open until planning).
- **Sentinel set parity:** reuse the `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS` rule from `scripts/check_git_identity.py` verbatim (duplicated in TypeScript — no cross-language import); keep both sets in sync via cross-referencing comments.
- **Escape-hatch symmetry:** `--allow-sentinel-author` mirrors `--allow-foreign-author` — never bypasses the empty-email gate, overrides config for that run only, does not modify `syncAllowedAuthors`.
- **No new dependencies; bounded, non-interactive; no network in tests.**

## Existing state

- **Pull side (guarded):** `ContextHub/src/sync/author-identity.ts` — `checkAuthorIdentity`/`enforceAuthorIdentityGate` refuse inbound commits whose author email is empty or foreign (allow-list `syncAllowedAuthors`, exact-email). Wired into `performSync` (`src/commands/sync.ts`) after the fetch, before any merge.
- **Push side (unguarded):** `ContextHub/src/sync/push.ts` — `gitPushDataFileToBranch` commits the JSONL export with the ambient git identity and pushes to `refs/worklog/data`. `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` (the `wl doctor foreign-items --apply --push` force-rewrite path) commits and force-pushes the same way. Neither checks the authoring identity.
- **Advisory guard only:** SorraAgents `scripts/check_git_identity.py` (owner SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX) detects sentinel/empty/mismatched identities, fail-open in `.githooks/pre-push` — a direct `wl sync` (the agent-session path) bypasses it.
- **Policy:** incident sentinels may never enter `syncAllowedAuthors` — pinned by `tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py` (`test_incident_sentinel_emails_are_absent_from_the_project_allowlist`). Project allow-list: `250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com`, `pi@local`, `sorra@thewizardscode.com` (`.worklog/config.yaml`).

## Desired change

1. In the worklog CLI, before the push step of `wl sync`, read the effective `user.email` (same identity git will commit with in the temp worktree) and refuse — with the identity named and the `git config user.email …` remedy — when it is empty or an exact sentinel match. Applies only when a push would actually run.
2. Pure, deterministic decision function mirroring `checkAuthorIdentity` (same input → same result for dry-run and normal modes): inputs = effective email, configured/expected email, `syncAllowedAuthors`, sentinel set; outputs = allow / refuse + reason. Guard order: empty → refuse unconditionally; exact sentinel → refuse unless `--allow-sentinel-author`; otherwise pass (non-sentinel configured/allow-listed identities are never refused — exact-email rule, no wildcards).
3. New `--allow-sentinel-author` flag wired through `SyncOptions` → `performSync`; when used, the sync output and sync log record the bypass (audit trail).
4. Same guard applied to the shared commit path used by `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` (force-rewrite path) so a sentinel identity can never author any worklog-data commit.
5. Regression tests: pure-function coverage of the sentinel/empty/config-identity matrix (unit, no network) plus one CLI-level refusal test (`wl sync` with a sentinel `user.email` refuses before pushing).
6. Documentation: `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` updated to describe pull gate + push guard together; code comments cross-reference `scripts/check_git_identity.py` as the sentinel-set source of truth.

## Key Files:

- `ContextHub/src/sync/push.ts` — add the pre-push identity guard to `gitPushDataFileToBranch` (and the shared commit path used by `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`).
- `ContextHub/src/sync/author-identity.ts` — add the sentinel set (`INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS`) + the pure push-side decision function next to the existing pull-side gate (or a new `src/sync/push-authority.ts`).
- `ContextHub/src/commands/sync.ts` — wire `--allow-sentinel-author` (option, `performSync` options, audit log output).
- `ContextHub/src/cli-types.ts` — `SyncOptions` typing for the new flag.
- `ContextHub/tests/sync-author-gate.test.ts` and `ContextHub/tests/cli/sync-author-gate.test.ts` — pure-function matrix + CLI-level refusal (no network).
- `SorraAgents/docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` — document the push-side guard alongside the existing author-identity gate (AC5).
- `SorraAgents/scripts/check_git_identity.py` — canonical `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS`; cross-reference (source of truth for the TS set).

## Related work

- **SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX** (completed, high) — *Restore wl sync: main-checkout git identity was left as incident-era 'T <t@t.com>'* — owns `scripts/check_git_identity.py`, the advisory guard this item makes redundant-at-source.
- **SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC** (completed, high) — *Repair wl sync: allow operator GitHub identity, purge incident-era t@t.com commits* — established the pull-side allow-list/exact-email semantics this push guard mirrors.
- **SA-0MVK4F993008D9S2** (completed, high) — *wl sync blocked again: inbound t@t.com-authored worklog commits on refs/worklog/data* — discovery parent; the 2026-10-23 recurrence.
- **SA-0MVLJDS04002KI1W** (completed, high) — *wl sync blocked again: inbound t@t.com-authored worklog commits fail the author-identity gate* — 2026-10-23 second recurrence.
- **SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS** (completed, high) — *wl sync blocked: pi@local* — the epic this item was discovered during; `pi@local` allow-listing context.
- **SA-0MVVX9PAT009Q45H** (open, high) — *wl sync blocked: sorra@thewizardscode.com* — pull-side allow-list edge (deliberately allow-listed real identity — the carve-out pattern AC2 protects).
- **WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K** (completed, ContextHub store) — *wl sync to be run before refactor and standup skills* — precedent for cross-repo items and for recording delivery-location as an explicit question before implement.
- **SA-0MVZEO59E004BCI8** (completed) — *implement.py drive: refusal-aware finish recovery (cross-repo delivery record)* — precedent for delivering cross-repo work from a tracking item.

## Risks & assumptions

- **AC2 interpretation (recommended, pending producer confirmation):** the sentinel/empty refusal is **absolute** — it fires even when the sentinel email also equals the configured identity or an allow-list entry. AC2's "never applies to the configured identity / allow-list" carve-out protects *non-sentinel* identities only (exact-match rule); project policy already forbids allowing sentinels (pinned by `tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py`), so the two clauses do not overlap in any policy-compliant state. Guard order enforces this: empty → refuse; exact sentinel → refuse unless `--allow-sentinel-author`; else pass.
- **Cross-repo delivery risk:** `implement.py` refuse changes outside the item's worktree; the fix must be delivered to the ContextHub repo through a linked item or cross-repo delivery. **Mitigation:** flag at plan time before `start`; record delivery mechanism as a decision in the work item.
- **Sentinel-set drift risk:** the TS set must stay byte-identical to `check_git_identity.py::INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS`; no shared import exists across languages. **Mitigation:** cross-referencing comments + a unit test pinning the exact set (as `test_author_gate_allowlist.py` does on the SorraAgents side).
- **Escape-hatch abuse risk:** `--allow-sentinel-author` could be used routinely instead of fixing identity. **Mitigation:** audit-log the bypass in sync output/log (AC3) + docs frame it as incident-only, mirroring `--allow-foreign-author`.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "guard every git write in wl" is a tempting generalisation. **Mitigation:** scope strictly to the two worklog-data push paths (`wl sync` push + doctor force-rewrite); track anything broader as a separate item.
- **Assumption:** the effective `user.email` read at guard time is the identity git commits with — the temp push worktree shares the repo's config (including local overrides), so reading `git config user.email` from the repo root is sufficient. If a future git version allows per-environment author identity (env vars/`-c` overrides), the guard may need to consider `GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL`/`GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL`; out of scope today.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (AC2 scope — recommended interpretation, pending confirmation): "AC2 says the refusal never applies to the project's configured identity or `syncAllowedAuthors` entries. If a checkout's effective `user.email` IS an incident sentinel (e.g. the 2026-09-26 leaked-config state), must `wl sync` refuse anyway?" — **Recommended:** yes, refuse — the sentinel/empty gate is absolute and the configured-identity/allow-list carve-out protects only non-sentinel identities (guard order: empty → sentinel → pass). Rationale: sentinels are policy-forbidden from the allow-list (`tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py`), so the clauses never overlap in a compliant project; a literal carve-out would re-create the incident. Source: AC1 text (`user.email` set to a sentinel → refuse), `.worklog/config.yaml` policy comments, `check_git_identity.py` remedy text ("incident sentinels such as t@t.com never"). Pending producer confirmation at review.
- Q2 (push-path scope — recommended, pending confirmation): "Should the guard also cover `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` (the `wl doctor foreign-items --apply --push` force-rewrite) or only the `wl sync` push step?" — **Recommended:** both — either path publishes worklog-data commits under the ambient identity and a sentinel-authored force-rewrite poisons the remote ref identically. Source: `src/sync/push.ts` structure (shared commit path). Pending producer confirmation at review.
- Q3 (cross-repo delivery — flagged for plan time): "This SA item is the requirement/incident record, but the change lands in the ContextHub worklog CLI. Delivery mechanism?" — **Recommended:** implement via a linked ContextHub (WL) child item, or cross-repo delivery from this item per SA-0MVZEO59E004BCI8; settle before `implement.py start` (worktree isolation is repo-scoped). Precedent: WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K. Producer decision.
- Q4 (empty-email bypass — derived, no confirmation needed): "Does `--allow-sentinel-author` bypass the empty-email refusal?" — No: it mirrors `--allow-foreign-author`, which *never* bypasses the empty-email gate (documented in `src/commands/sync.ts` flag help and `src/sync/author-identity.ts`). Source: existing code, `--allow-foreign-author` semantics.

## Problem

The audit merge gate (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` → `_resolve_item_integration_evidence`) mines every hex token from the work item's description and comments and keeps those that resolve to **any** git object in the owning repo (`_commit_object_exists`). It does not filter by which ref the commit is reachable from.

When an item's text cites commits that exist only on `refs/worklog/data`, its backup refs, or other non-`dev` refs (e.g. a worklog history-rewrite item quoting incident-era SHAs), `_verify_merged_in_dev` finds no ancestor of `origin/dev` among the candidates and the gate proceeds to `_integrate_into_dev`, which cherry-picks those commits onto a worktree at `origin/dev` — conflicting and failing the audit closed with a spurious `Ready to close: No` merge-gate blocker.

## Observed (2026-10-23, SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC)

- Audit run 1: `git cherry-pick 345ea154a -> rc=1` conflict; verdict `Ready to close: No` (merge-gate blocker). `345ea154a` is a `refs/worklog/data` commit, never a `dev` commit.
- Workaround applied: the item description now records a real `dev` commit (`92fee5c30`, an ancestor of `origin/dev`), so the ancestor scan short-circuits to merged before any cherry-pick. Fragile — it depends on authors remembering to cite a `dev` commit and on the scan order.
- Related (already completed): SA-0MTQAF62U0085BEV (foreign hex that is not an object at all) and SA-0MTECRNGR000VKLV (decimal literals mined as SHAs). This is a third variant: the token **is** a commit object, but not on the delivery ref.

## Desired behaviour

- Restrict integration-evidence candidates to commits reachable from the item's delivery surface (branches matching `wl-<id>-*`, and any commit that is an ancestor of `origin/dev` or of a referenced feature branch) — or, at minimum, skip candidates not reachable from any `refs/heads/*` / `origin/*` ref of the owning repo, recording the skip as evidence.
- Commits reachable only from `refs/worklog/*`, `refs/backup/*` or unreachable objects must never be cherry-picked onto `dev`.
- Keep fail-open behaviour for evidence-less items and fail-closed behaviour for genuinely unmerged feature work.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1:** A work item whose description cites commits reachable only from `refs/worklog/data` (or a backup ref) does NOT trigger `_integrate_into_dev`; the gate records a skip note naming each excluded candidate and its non-delivery ref.
2. **AC2:** Regression test (in `skill/audit/tests/`) builds a fixture repo with a `dev` branch, a `refs/worklog/data` commit and a description citing that commit, and asserts `_phase_merge_gate` passes without invoking cherry-pick (no stray worktree, no blocker).
3. **AC3:** Existing behaviour is unchanged for: the real delivered commit (ancestor of `origin/dev` → merged), genuinely unmerged feature-branch work (still integrates), and evidence-less items (fail-open).

### Related work items

- **SA-0MW3H07A8004Q54C** – finish: retry the local-dev fast-forward after the recovery rebase and report a pushed-commit-guard refusal distinctly (completed)

# Intake Brief — `wl sync`: file-lock age-expiry steals a live holder's lock (residual lost-update hazard)

## Problem statement

`acquireFileLock()` (`~/projects/ContextHub/src/file-lock.ts`) unlinks a lock whose `acquiredAt` is older than `DEFAULT_MAX_LOCK_AGE_MS` (5 min) **even when the holder PID is alive on the same host**. `wl sync` holds this lock for its whole fetch → merge → write → push operation, so a slow sync (>5 min: slow network, large store) has its lock stolen mid-operation; two writers then proceed concurrently and the sync writes back its pre-operation snapshot over whatever the stealer committed — the general lost-update class that WL-0MUV2U9QF002S9J1 closed for short operations. The claim-hold guard (SA-0MVE34D9B005TUYJ) prevents the user-visible reverted-claim symptom, but non-claim field writes are still exposed in that window.

## Users

- **Agents running long `wl sync` operations** (fetch/merge/push over a slow network or a large store). *User story:* "As a sync running longer than five minutes, I want my lock to stay mine for the whole fetch → merge → write → push, so a second writer can never run concurrently and clobber my write-back."
- **Auto-sync spawners and `wl sync --if-idle` callers** (herdr scheduling, worklist auto-sync). *User story:* "As an idle-gated sync, I want to skip (not steal) when a live sync holds the lock, so I never become the second concurrent writer."
- **Producers/operators and downstream gates** that trust the worklog store. *User story:* "As a producer, I want a long sync to never lose concurrent field updates, so `wl show` and the gate decisions stay trustworthy."

## Acceptance Criteria

- The same-host live holder is authoritative: `acquireFileLock()` must **not** remove a lock whose holder PID is alive on the same host, regardless of `acquiredAt` age exceeding `maxLockAge`. The two existing unit tests that encode the current steal-the-live-lock behaviour (`tests/file-lock.test.ts`: "should remove a lock older than maxLockAge even if PID is alive"; "should still remove an age-expired lock when skipIfLocked is set") are inverted to assert the lock is kept, and a new unit case asserts a same-host live PID with an age-expired lock stays in place.
- Stale-lock semantics are retained where PID liveness cannot be trusted: same-host dead-PID locks, foreign-host locks, corrupted/unparseable locks, and parsed-but-missing-field locks are still cleaned up exactly as today (existing `tests/file-lock.test.ts` cases keep passing unchanged).
- Deterministic regression proof that a sync's lock is never stolen mid-operation: a test in `tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts` (git-shim fetch-parking technique plus a back-dated lock file — no sleep-based timing) holds a live sync with an age-expired lock and proves a second `wl sync`/mutation either waits on the lock or, with `--if-idle`, skips (`LockBusyError`); the parked sync's write-back is then the only write and no concurrent update is clobbered.
- The existing lost-update/claim-revert suites stay green: `tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts` and `tests/cli/sync-claim-revert.test.ts` still pass; comments in `sync-claim-revert.test.ts` describing mechanism (a) ("the claim therefore acquired it") are updated where they describe the now-eliminated lock-steal path, without changing the suite's assertions.
- All relevant documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries; the full ContextHub test suite must pass with the new changes (excluding CI/CD pipeline tests; CHANGELOG.md is managed by the release pipeline).

## Impact

A slow `wl sync` can no longer lose its lock to a competing writer, so concurrent field updates survive long syncs and the worklog store is never silently clobbered.

## Constraints

- **Change site is the ContextHub repo** (`~/projects/ContextHub`, prefix `WL`) — the same cross-repo pattern as the sibling claim-hold children (e.g. SA-0MVKWV2V2006JC8E landed in ContextHub, commit `4eb0cc6b`). This item is tracked in the SA store; implementation and tests live in ContextHub.
- Surgical change to `src/file-lock.ts`; no change to the `DEFAULT_MAX_LOCK_AGE_MS` default (producer-confirmed scope A). Under the fix it governs only dead-PID/foreign-host/unparseable locks.
- `skipIfLocked` semantics preserved: a same-host live holder (any age) must yield `LockBusyError` → `wl sync --if-idle` skips, it never steals.
- Deterministic tests only — the git-shim parking + back-dating techniques, no sleep-based timing races.
- All lock consumers (`wl sync`, mutating commands, `wl unlock`, `withFileLock`) must keep the same mutual-exclusion guarantees.

## Existing state

- `src/file-lock.ts` `acquireFileLock()` (≈line 330): after the dead-PID check, an unconditional age-expiry branch removes any lock older than `maxLockAge` — "treat it as stale regardless of PID status" — even when the holder is alive on the same host.
- Two unit tests assert that behaviour: `tests/file-lock.test.ts:459` ("even if PID is alive") and `tests/file-lock.test.ts:311` (same, under `skipIfLocked`). They must be inverted by the fix.
- `tests/cli/sync-claim-revert.test.ts` mechanism (a) documents the residual hazard precisely ("withFileLock() treats any lock older than maxLockAge ... as stale even when the holder is alive and unlinks it"); the claim-hold guard masks the damage for claims, which is why this item is a *residual* hazard.
- `tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts` already has the parking harness (git shim inside `git fetch`, release-file gate) that the new regression test reuses.

## Desired change

Make the same-host live holder authoritative (producer-confirmed scope A): when the lock's PID is alive on the local host, never age-expire it. Keep age-expiry for same-host dead PIDs, foreign-host locks, and unparseable/corrupt locks. The heartbeat refresh (scope B/C) is explicitly out of scope (see Appendix Q1).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Hung-holder lockout (same-host).** Removing age-expiry for a same-host live PID means a genuinely stuck (non-crashing) sync holds the lock indefinitely; nothing auto-recovers it. Mitigation: the manual `wl unlock`/`releaseFileLock` escape remains; the heartbeat option (scope B) was considered and deliberately **declined** by the producer (Q1 → A) — a heartbeat is a possible follow-up item, not added scope. Dead-process locks (the common crash case) are still reclaimed by the PID check.
- **PID recycling without a heartbeat.** A crashed holder whose PID is later reused could in theory look permanently live. Recorded as an accepted, practically-negligible risk (Linux PID reuse takes far longer than the window between syncs); producer confirmed scope A, so the heartbeat (which would eliminate it entirely) is out of scope and could be a follow-up.
- **Cross-host long syncs stay stealable** (age-expiry retained for foreign-host locks per the suggested direction) — acceptable in this single-host environment; noted in the appendix so it is a conscious choice.
- **Test inverts may look like regressions.** The two unit tests that flip expectation are the *correct* outcome of the fix; the brief pins their new expectation explicitly so review does not re-revert them.
- **Scope-creep guard:** heartbeat refresh (scope B/C), cross-host live-authority, and `maxLockAge` default changes were offered as Q1 options; the producer chose **A (minimal)** — none of the alternatives become scope. Heartbeat remains a candidate follow-up item if the hung-holder/PID-recycling concerns ever bite.
- **Assumption:** change site is ContextHub with SA-store tracking, mirroring the claim-hold sibling pattern (SA-0MVKWV2V2006JC8E).

## Key Files

- `~/projects/ContextHub/src/file-lock.ts` — `acquireFileLock()` stale-check branch: same-host-liveness authority before age-expiry.
- `~/projects/ContextHub/src/commands/sync.ts` — sync's `withFileLock` acquisition (≈line 800); no change expected for scope A, verify only.
- `~/projects/ContextHub/tests/file-lock.test.ts` — invert the two live-PID age-expiry tests (lines ≈311, ≈459); add same-host-live-authoritative cases (alive+old kept; dead+old still removed; foreign-host old still removed per direction).
- `~/projects/ContextHub/tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts` — new deterministic regression test (parked sync + back-dated lock + second writer waits/skips).
- `~/projects/ContextHub/tests/cli/sync-claim-revert.test.ts` — must stay green; mechanism comments updated if they describe the eliminated steal path.

## Related work

**Potentially related work items** (via `wl search "file lock"` / `"lost-update"` in the SA store, and WL store lookups):

- **SA-0MVE34D9B005TUYJ** — `wl sync --if-idle` reverts actively-worked items (completed): the claim-hold fix this item is discovered-from; its guard masks (but does not eliminate) this hazard.
- **SA-0MVKWV26Y000G3B9** — Reproduction: sync reverts a held in_progress claim (completed): proved mechanism (a), the same lock-steal this item eliminates at the source.
- **SA-0MVKWV2V2006JC8E** — TTL-bounded monotonic claim-hold guard (completed, ContextHub `src/claim-hold.ts`, commit `4eb0cc6b`): defence-in-depth that stays after this fix.
- **WL-0MUV2U9QF002S9J1** — Fix lost-update race: wl sync clobbers concurrent mutating commands (completed, ContextHub, commit `ed0acc60`): closed the short-operation lost-update class; this item closes the long-operation residual.
- **SA-0MW7Z77KI005MK0B** — Audit runner leaves items open after a failing audit when a concurrent wl sync races its restore (lost update) (open): downstream consumer of the same hazard class.
- **SA-0MWFMUYHJ004Z18S** — Race-clobber restore regression tests (open): test-first sibling covering the audit-restore slice.
- **SA-0MVCF5RKF0099K4R** — Worklog: stale-lock detection and bounded backoff for wl mutations (open): complementary stale-lock work in the same file.
- **SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5** — Ship release must verify in-scope work items are actually closed (completed): records a real lost close from this race.

**Potentially related docs:**

- `~/projects/ContextHub/src/file-lock.ts` (header comment documents the stale-lock rationale).
- `~/projects/ContextHub/tests/cli/sync-claim-revert.test.ts` (header documents mechanism (a) — the residual hazard).
- `~/projects/ContextHub/docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` (audit-restore lost-update context) — verify only, no doc change expected outside ContextHub docs.

*Duplicate check performed: no overlapping completed item found — related items are complementary (fix predecessor, reproduction, and downstream consumers), not duplicates.*

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Fix scope. `src/file-lock.ts` currently age-expires any lock older than 5 min regardless of PID liveness. Which scope should this item implement? **A) Minimal (recommended):** same-host live PID is authoritative — never age-expire it; keep age-expiry for same-host dead PIDs, foreign-host locks, and unparseable/corrupt locks. **B) Minimal + heartbeat:** also refresh `acquiredAt` during long syncs (protects foreign-host readers; removes the PID-recycling corner). **C) Heartbeat only:** keep age-expiry but make the live holder refresh the lock." — Answer (producer/operator): **"1. A" — minimal fix; same-host live PID is authoritative; heartbeat is out of scope.** Source: interactive reply to the intake handoff (question comment SA-C0MWGANT20005TAAQ, answered 2026-11-14).

- Research summary: inspected `src/file-lock.ts` (`acquireFileLock()` stale-check, ≈lines 320–350), `src/commands/sync.ts` (`withFileLock`, ≈line 800, `skipIfLocked` path), `tests/file-lock.test.ts` (two tests at ≈lines 311/459 encode the steal-live-lock behaviour; surrounding dead-PID/foreign-host/corrupt cases must be preserved), `tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts` (git-shim parking harness reusable for the regression test), and `tests/cli/sync-claim-revert.test.ts` (header documents mechanism (a) — the exact residual hazard; its assertions stay green but mechanism comments may need updating). No heartbeat mechanism exists anywhere in the codebase today; the PID-recycling concern that motivated age-expiry is documented in the `acquireFileLock()` comment ("handles PID recycling and environments where PID checks are unreliable").

### Related work items

- **SA-0MVKWV46J007EM51** – Claim-hold regression suite and full-suite gate (completed)

## Goal

As an operator running `/skill:machine-hygiene`, I want the CPU and I/O stall-pressure thresholds to reflect real PSI stall data now that `/proc/pressure` parsing works, so the pressure diagnosis fires on genuine contention instead of staying green until the host is near-dead.

## Problem statement

`cpu_pressure` (warning 70 / critical 85, `some` avg10) and `io_pressure` (warning 50 / critical 80, `full` avg10) were inherited from the pre-parser-fix configuration and have never been validated against real stall data. The IO threshold is worse than unvalidated: a 50 % `full`-line stall is effectively never reached, so `io_pressure` stays permanently green even under genuine I/O starvation — the exact signal the PSI work (SA-0MVLJ8VD60091JLW) was meant to surface.

## Users

- **Operator running `/skill:machine-hygiene`** — "As an operator, I want the before-table pressure rows to flag real CPU contention and I/O starvation at levels my multi-agent host actually reaches, so I am told about a problem while it is still actionable."
- **Agent triaging a slow host** — "As an agent, I want `analyze_pressures()` to surface an actionable pressure with contributors when the host is genuinely starved, instead of skipping a permanently-green `io_pressure` row."
- **Skill maintainer** — "As a maintainer, I want the calibrated values consistent across `config.yaml`, `config.py::_DEFAULTS` and `SKILL.md`, with boundary tests, so a future parser change cannot silently re-introduce the silence."

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — `cpu_pressure` is calibrated to **warning 30 / critical 60** (`some` avg10) and `io_pressure` to **warning 5 / critical 20** (`full` avg10) in `config.yaml` and `config.py::_DEFAULTS`, mirroring the `memory_pressure` full-line calibration for IO.
- **AC2** — Calibration is validated against real stall data: the archived busy-host observations (CPU `some` avg10 = 11.58 at load 11.92 on 16 cores → `low`; CPU `some` avg10 = 88.78 at load ~44 → `critical`) classify as expected, and **at least one bounded controlled I/O-stall sample** is captured (e.g. a short `dd`/write burst) showing a numeric IO `full` value that currently stays green under 50/80, with the sample and classification recorded in a comment on this item.
- **AC3** — Unit tests cover the new classification boundaries for both metrics: cpu `some` 29.9 → `low`, 30.0 → `warning`, 60.0 → `critical`; io `full` 4.9 → `low`, 5.0 → `warning`, 20.0 → `critical` — replacing the old 70/85 and 50/80 boundary assertions.
- **AC4** — `config.yaml` comments and `SKILL.md` document the new values, their `some`/`full` line basis, the observed-data provenance (including the induced IO sample), and why the IO warning never fired under 50/80. `SKILL.md`'s "Threshold provenance" paragraph is updated to state the validated values rather than "not yet validated".
- **AC5** — All related documentation in this repository is updated: `config.yaml` comments, `config.py` docstrings/comments, `SKILL.md` metric table and provenance section, plus any code comments in `metrics.py` that reference the thresholds. This skill has no README or docs-site entry, so no other documentation surface needs an update.
- **AC6** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — calibration basis:** the archived samples (11.58 busy / 88.78 extreme) plus one induced IO sample bracket realistic stall ranges on this 16-core multi-agent host; other hosts (fewer/more cores, different workloads) can still override per-host values in `config.yaml`.
- **Risk — false amber at 30 % CPU `some`-stall:** a heavily loaded-but-healthy multi-agent host can briefly cross 30 % `some` (at least one task stalled) during test-suite bursts; acceptable — it is the honest stall signal, and `some` semantics are designed to fire early.
- **Risk — induced IO sample disturbs the live host:** the bounded burst must be short and small (e.g. a few hundred MB write/read) so it does not itself cause a false-positive pressure reading on a busy host; time it outside the brief write window.
- **Risk — doc drift:** three surfaces (`config.yaml`, `config.py::_DEFAULTS`, `SKILL.md`) must stay in lock-step; AC4/AC5 and the existing `test_shipped_config_matches_defaults` guard this.
- **Scope-creep risk:** adjacent recalibration ideas (e.g. load-average multipliers vs. PSI, per-host dynamic thresholds) are recorded as linked work items, not folded into this item.

## Impact

Operators now get honest CPU and I/O stall alarms at levels a real multi-agent host reaches — CPU contention flagged at 30 % `some`-stall and genuine I/O starvation at 5 % `full`-stall — instead of a metric that stays green until the box is thrashing.

## Constraints

- **Scope:** threshold values + consistent config/docs/tests + one bounded controlled I/O-stall sample for validation. No parser, line-selection, metric-key, or action behaviour changes.
- **Stable metric keys:** `cpu_pressure` / `io_pressure` must not change (consumed by `pressure_analysis._PRESSURE_METRICS` and the before/after table).
- **Classification semantics:** `classify_metric` is inclusive at the warning/critical lower bounds (`value >= critical` → critical, `value >= warning` → warning); boundary tests assert exactly those edges.
- **Line bases unchanged:** cpu → `some`, io → `full` (decided in SA-0MVLJ8VD60091JLW); no fallback on missing lines.
- **No new dependencies**; stdlib/unittest only.
- **Repo boundary:** changes land in `skill/machine-hygiene` in this repo (worktree), never the installed global copy by hand.

## Existing state

- `skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/config.py::_DEFAULTS` — `cpu_pressure: warning 70 / critical 85`; `io_pressure: warning 50 / critical 80`.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/config.yaml` — same values, with comments claiming ">70 % indicates moderate CPU contention" (70 % `some`-stall is far past moderate) and ">50 % I/O stalled — noticeable slowdown" (never reached on `full`).
- `skill/machine-hygiene/SKILL.md` — "Threshold provenance" says cpu/io thresholds "have not yet been validated against real stall data".
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_config.py` — asserts the 70/85 and 50/80 defaults and file-override behaviour.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_metrics.py` — `test_cpu_pressure_boundaries` (69.9/70/85) and `test_io_pressure_boundaries` (49.9/50/80) lock in the old values.
- Real observed data: CPU `some` avg10 = 88.78 (2026-09-27, load ~44/16 cores) and 11.58 (2026-10-21 discovery, load 11.92); IO `full` avg10 = 0.00–0.05 (idle observations only — no busy IO sample yet).

## Desired change

1. `_DEFAULTS` and `config.yaml`: `cpu_pressure` → 30/60 (`some` avg10); `io_pressure` → 5/20 (`full` avg10, mirroring `memory_pressure`).
2. Update comments: cpu description corrected to "(moderate CPU contention)" at 30 %; io description explains `full`-line stall % semantics and that 50/80 never fired.
3. Update `SKILL.md` provenance paragraph with the calibrated values, the archived and induced sample evidence, and the rationale.
4. Update boundary tests in `test_metrics.py` and default tests in `test_config.py` to the new values.
5. Validation run: capture a bounded controlled I/O-stall sample (write/read burst, a few seconds), render the `io_pressure` classification under the new thresholds, and paste the sample + classification into a comment on this item.

## Key Files

- `skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/config.py` — `_DEFAULTS` cpu_pressure/io_pressure values (and any threshold-referencing comments).
- `skill/machine-hygiene/config.yaml` — cpu_pressure/io_pressure blocks, warning/critical values and explaining comments.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/SKILL.md` — "Threshold provenance" paragraph and any metric-table threshold notes.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_config.py` — default-value and file-override assertions for cpu/io pressure.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_metrics.py` — `test_cpu_pressure_boundaries`, `test_io_pressure_boundaries` and the `collect_metrics` pressure assertions.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVLJ8VD60091JLW** (completed) — PSI parser fix; this item's `discovered-from` source; established `some`/`full` line selection and the `memory_pressure` 5/20 calibration precedent.
- **WL-0MVI8YM07002Z9VY** (ContextHub, completed) — threshold miscalibration for multi-agent hosts (process/thread/swap); adjacent calibration work, shipped.
- **WL-0MVI8YJ1H007HUEZ** (ContextHub, open) — duplicate proposed-actions table/actions; same discovery session, independent defect.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: `cpu_pressure` calibration target (`some` avg10)?**
  - Options: (A) keep 70/85, validate + document; (B) lower to warn 30 / crit 60 to catch contention earlier; (C) middle ground (warn 50 / crit 75).
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **B**. **Recommended:** B — 70 % `some`-stall means the host is already severely degraded; an amber band from ~30 % lets the skill propose renice/kill remediation while the host is still responsive.
  - Evidence: real CPU `some` avg10 samples of 11.58 (busy, load 11.92) and 88.78 (extreme, load ~44) on 16-core hosts; current 70/85 classifies the former `low` and the latter `critical`.
- **Q2: `io_pressure` calibration target (`full` avg10)?**
  - Options: (A) mirror memory_pressure warn 5 / crit 20 (same full-line semantics); (B) slightly higher (10/30); (C) keep 50/80 but document.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **A**. **Recommended:** A — identical `full`-line semantics and an established 5/20 precedent; keeps the genuine I/O-starvation signal without false alarms at idle.
  - Evidence: observed IO `full` avg10 values are 0.00–0.05; 50/80 was never reachable so the metric stayed green under genuine I/O starvation.
- **Q3: validation data sufficiency (AC1)?**
  - Options: (A) archive observations + live `/proc/pressure` only; (B) also induce a bounded controlled I/O-stall sample.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **B**. **Recommended:** B — AC1 explicitly demands validation against observed busy-host stall percentages, and IO currently has zero busy samples; one bounded induced sample makes calibration evidence-based rather than assumed.
  - Evidence: no archived IO `full` sample exceeds 0.05; a short `dd`/write burst provides the missing busy data point.

No open questions remain.
