# `implement.py parent`/`drive` start children whose status is `blocked` — re-validate the block before starting or skipping

Discovered-from: **MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6** (tce-main-street) — producer decision Q3 (2026-10-29): *"yes, though it should first check that the block is still valid"*.

## Goal

As an implement agent running an epic, I need `implement.py parent`/`drive` to never start a child that is deliberately `blocked` unless the block no longer holds, so a verification child is not implemented against a prerequisite that has not landed and I am not asked to fabricate its evidence.

## Problem statement

`phase_parent()` classifies children with `_classify_child()` (`implement/scripts/implement.py:874`): terminal → `skip-terminal`, `in-progress` → `skip-in-progress`, **everything else → `implement`**. Status `blocked` therefore falls through to `implement`.

Blocker awareness exists but does not gate the start:

- `_in_chain_blockers()` only considers blockers that are **themselves children of the same parent** (`implement.py:5920-5975`), so a child blocked on anything outside the parent's children set is startable.
- `external_blockers` is populated from outbound `wl dep` edges only (`implement.py:5771-5790`) and is reported as a "coordination note". It is `[]` when the block is recorded in prose instead of as a dependency edge — which is how cross-project blocks are written (`**Blocked by (SorraAgents):** SA-…` in the child description).

**Live evidence (this item's origin):** on 2026-10-29 `implement.py parent MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` started child `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4` — status `blocked`, unblock condition "`SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2` is in `dev`/`in_review`", which was still `open`/`intake_complete` — created a worktree and reported `external_blockers: []`. The child had to be aborted (`implement.py abort`, worktree removed) to avoid producing unverifiable AC evidence.

The inverse failure matters too: a **stale** block must not strand a child forever. Once the blocker lands, the child must become startable again (or its status refreshed) rather than being skipped silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A child whose `status` is `blocked` is never started while its block still holds: `_classify_child()` (or the caller) yields a distinct `skip-blocked` outcome, and the child is reported in `children_processed` with its blocking ids — not started, not `skipped-in-progress`.
- [ ] **Re-validation of dependency-edge blocks:** for a `blocked` child the outbound `wl dep list` edges are resolved; the block is **stale** iff every blocker is terminal (`completed`/`done`/`in_review`) or soft-deleted, in which case the child is startable again (and the stale block is named in the report/log). Any non-terminal blocker holds the block.
- [ ] **Re-validation of cross-project and prose blocks:** blocker IDs declared in the child description's `Blocked by …` line (and/or a machine-readable `externalBlockers` field, whichever is implemented) are collected and surfaced in `external_blockers`; an unresolvable cross-project id holds the block and is reported with an actionable message (id + where to check it), never silently ignored and never silently startable.
- [ ] A block that cannot be validated (no dep edges, no parseable blocker line, unknown status) is treated as **holding** and reported as unvalidated — it must not default to startable.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: (a) `blocked` + open external blocker → not started, reported with ids; (b) `blocked` + blocker now terminal → stale block detected and child started; (c) `blocked` + no resolvable blocker → not started, message names the unresolved id; (d) `drive` propagates the same classification/report fields; (e) existing in-chain sibling ordering, cycles and terminal/in-progress behaviour unchanged (regression cases).
- [ ] Live evidence recorded on this item: re-running `implement.py parent MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` (three `blocked` verification children) starts nothing and reports all three with their `SA-…` blockers.
- [ ] `implement/SKILL.md` "Guards" list gains the blocked-child re-validation rule (stale blocks are re-evaluated, not honoured forever), and the parent-recursion section documents the new report vocabulary.
- [ ] Node and pytest suites green for the changed framework code (run through the test skill / finish gate, never an ad-hoc runner).

## Constraints

- Do not weaken the existing guards: dependency order, cycle fail-fast, "never re-implement terminal children", "never clobber another agent's `in_progress` claim", and `--finalise-stranded` semantics stay as they are.
- No change to `implement.py start`/`finish` single-item behaviour; this is the parent/`drive` fan-out classification only.
- Cross-project resolution must stay fail-open in the sense that an unresolvable id reports clearly and does not crash the phase — it just holds the block.
- Prose parsing must not become the only mechanism: prefer declared dependency edges, and keep the prose path narrowly scoped to an explicit `Blocked by` line.

## Key Files

- `implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_classify_child()`, `phase_parent()` (child classification, `_in_chain_blockers`), `phase_drive()` (report propagation), `wl_dep_blockers()`.
- `implement/scripts/tests/` (or the repo's existing implement test location) — new unit tests for the classification matrix.
- `implement/SKILL.md` — Guards + parent recursion report vocabulary.
- Reference cases: `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` children `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4`, `MS-0MVTEVKOD002OKSO`, `MS-0MVTEVL4Z009LUUR`, `MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1` (all `blocked`, blockers in prose).

## Related work

- `SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2`, `SA-0MVL7YOMJ006UMDO`, `SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z` — the three blockers of the origin item's verification children.
- `SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T` — introduced `external_blockers` as coordination notes; this item makes them gate the start.

---

## Plan (plan skill, 2026-10-30)

**Headline:** Split the fix into a test-first contract item, three vertical
behaviour slices (classification → prose/cross-project blockers → drive
reporting), a docs item and a live-evidence item, all under this parent, with
every parent AC mapped to a child.

### Child work items (test-first, dependency order)

| # | Id | Title | Type | Effort/Risk |
|---|----|-------|------|-------------|
| C1 | `SA-0MVUTD3IX004E03C` | Tests: blocked-child classification matrix for parent/drive | task | M / Medium |
| C2 | `SA-0MVUTD408005OFNW` | phase_parent: classify a still-blocked child as `skip-blocked` (dep-edge re-validation) | feature | M / Medium |
| C3 | `SA-0MVUTD4HS000O6AB` | Prose `Blocked by` and cross-project blockers hold a blocked child | feature | M / Medium |
| C4 | `SA-0MVUTD4ZD006O4N5` | phase_drive: propagate `skip-blocked` classification and blocker ids | feature | S / Low |
| C5 | `SA-0MVUTD5GQ004V6UO` | Docs: `implement/SKILL.md` guards + parent-recursion report vocabulary | docs | XS / Low |
| C6 | `SA-0MVUTD5YF001PLOF` | Live evidence: `parent MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` starts no blocked child | task | S / Medium |

Dependency edges (all wired with `wl dep add`):

```
C1 (tests, no blockers)
 └─ C2 ─┬─ C3 ─┬─ C4 ─┬─ C5 (docs)
        │      │      └─ C6 (live evidence)
        └──────┴────────┘
```

Ordering rationale: C1 writes the red contract first (parent AC 5); C2 lands
the dep-edge verdict (AC 1, 2, 4-dep-path); C3 adds the prose/cross-project
path (AC 3, 4-prose-path) and makes the fail-closed default actionable; C4
propagates the verdict through `drive` (AC 1 "reported in `children_processed`"
on the drive path); C5 documents the shipped vocabulary (AC 7); C6 produces the
live evidence (AC 6). Each slice is end-to-end: code + tests + the finish gate.

### Parent AC → child coverage

| Parent AC | Covered by |
|---|---|
| AC1 `skip-blocked` distinct outcome, reported in `children_processed` with blocking ids | C2 (classification + report), C4 (drive propagation), C1(a) |
| AC2 dep-edge re-validation, stale iff every blocker terminal/soft-deleted | C2, C1(b) |
| AC3 prose `Blocked by` / cross-project ids surfaced in `external_blockers`; unresolvable holds with an actionable message | C3, C1(c) |
| AC4 unvalidatable block holds and is reported unvalidated | C2 (no dep edges), C3 (no parseable line) |
| AC5 unit tests (a)–(e) | C1 |
| AC6 live evidence on `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` | C6 |
| AC7 `implement/SKILL.md` Guards + report vocabulary | C5 |
| AC8 node + pytest suites green through the test skill / finish gate | every child's finish gate; stated explicitly in C1 and C2 |

### Assumptions (recorded, not invented requirements)

- **A1 — test location.** The Key Files section above predicted
  `implement/scripts/tests/`; the repo's existing implement tests live in
  `tests/test_implement_*.py` at the repo root, so C1 creates
  `tests/test_implement_parent_blocked_child.py` there.
- **A2 — prose only, no schema change.** AC3's "and/or a machine-readable
  `externalBlockers` field, whichever is implemented" is satisfied by parsing
  the explicit `Blocked by …` line plus declared dependency edges; no `wl`
  schema change (wl is a separate ContextHub-owned CLI).
- **A3 — cross-project ids are resolvable in principle.** `implement.py`
  already routes `wl` calls through
  `shared/status_lifecycle.resolve_worklog_flags`, whose prefix-to-sibling scan
  maps an id prefix to its owning project's worklog. Verified on 2026-10-30:
  from `/home/rgardler/projects/tce-main-street`, prefix `SA` resolves to
  `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.worklog` and `MS` to the tce worklog.
  Whether C3 *uses* that to detect a landed cross-project blocker is Q3 below.
- **A4 — one existing test encodes the superseded contract.**
  `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py::TestParentDependencyOrder::test_external_blocker_reported_not_started_early`
  asserts that a `blocked` child with an out-of-chain blocker **is started**
  ("coordination notes" per `SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T`). This item deliberately
  supersedes that behaviour; C1 updates and renames the test rather than
  leaving two contradictory contracts.
- **A5 — legacy helper kept.** `_next_child_to_implement()` has no production
  call site (only `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py`); C2 keeps it
  consistent with the new rule instead of deleting it (dead code is reported,
  not removed, in a bug-fix slice).
- **A6 — the live-evidence run can start something.** The origin epic's AC1
  child `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4` is `open` (not `blocked`) with
  `assignee: Map` + tag `do-not-delegate`; `phase_parent` honours neither
  (that is `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876`, itself `blocked`). See Q1.
- **A7 — `blocked` status writes are unreliable.** `WL-0MVTUKSJZ003WK82`
  (ContextHub) records `wl update --status blocked` reporting success while the
  stored status reverted to `open`; the classification must therefore never
  depend on the framework being able to *write* `blocked`.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-30 — initial plan: 6 children created (`SA-0MVUTD3IX004E03C`,
  `SA-0MVUTD408005OFNW`, `SA-0MVUTD4HS000O6AB`, `SA-0MVUTD4ZD006O4N5`,
  `SA-0MVUTD5GQ004V6UO`, `SA-0MVUTD5YF001PLOF`), 11 dependency edges wired,
  six automated review stages run, AC coverage verified at 100 %.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Round 1 (2026-10-30, plan skill, downtime dispatch — **no interactive
producer available**; questions recorded here and flagged for producer review).

- **Q1 — What is the scope of the live-evidence AC (AC6)?**
  The origin epic `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` now has **three** `blocked` children
  (`MS-0MVTEVKOD002OKSO`, `MS-0MVTEVL4Z009LUUR`, `MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1`) and one
  **`open`** child (`MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4`) held only by `assignee: Map` + the
  `do-not-delegate` tag. `phase_parent` honours neither assignee holds nor
  `do-not-delegate` (that is `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876`, itself `blocked`), so the
  post-fix run will still start that open child — while AC6 as written says the
  run "starts nothing".
  Options: **(A)** scope AC6 to "none of the three `blocked` children is
  started, all three reported `skip-blocked` with their `SA-…` ids", and report
  the open held child truthfully with a cross-reference to
  `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876`; **(B)** widen this item to also gate on
  `do-not-delegate`/assignee holds (overlaps `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876`, which is
  already planned and blocked); **(C)** prove the behaviour on a synthetic
  fixture epic in this repo and record the MS run as pending until
  `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876` lands.
  **Recommended:** A — it proves exactly the bug this item owns (a `blocked`
  child is never started) without duplicating the do-not-delegate item, and
  keeps the live evidence honest about what the run did.
  **Answer:** **OPEN QUESTION** — directed to the producer. Why it matters: it
  decides whether C6 (`SA-0MVUTD5YF001PLOF`) can be executed at all, and
  whether the MS epic stays held after this fix lands.

- **Q2 — When a block is found stale, should the child's lifecycle status be
  refreshed, or only the start allowed?**
  AC2 says the child "is startable again (and the stale block is named in the
  report/log)"; the Goal paragraph adds "(or its status refreshed)".
  Options: **(A)** start the child and report/log the stale block, leaving the
  `blocked` status to the lifecycle owner (a comment on the child records the
  stale finding); **(B)** also flip the child to `open` via `StatusLifecycle`
  with an audit comment before starting; **(C)** flip to `open` and clear the
  prose `Blocked by` line.
  **Recommended:** A — it never silently erases a producer-set hold, it keeps
  `phase_parent` a reader of lifecycle state rather than a writer of it, and
  `WL-0MVTUKSJZ003WK82` shows blocked-status writes are unreliable in `wl`.
  **Answer:** **OPEN QUESTION** — directed to the producer. Why it matters: it
  determines whether C2 mutates child status (and therefore whether it needs
  the `StatusLifecycle` audit-comment path).

- **Q3 — Should a cross-project prose blocker be resolved through the sibling
  worklog scan (so a landed external blocker makes the block stale)?**
  `resolve_worklog_flags` already maps an id prefix to its owning project's
  worklog (verified for `SA` → SorraAgents and `MS` → tce-main-street), so
  resolution is technically available without any network call.
  Options: **(A)** resolve cross-project ids through that scan: terminal →
  stale (child startable), non-terminal → holds, and only a genuinely
  unresolvable id holds as unvalidated; **(B)** do not resolve cross-repo —
  every cross-project id holds, and the child's owner must refresh the child
  when the external item lands; **(C)** resolve opportunistically (try the
  scan, fall back to holds) but never cache the result.
  **Recommended:** A — it is what makes the origin epic self-unblocking when
  the three `SA-…` items land, which is the inverse failure the Goal names
  ("a stale block must not strand a child forever"); B leaves three MS
  children stranded forever and contradicts that Goal.
  **Answer:** **OPEN QUESTION** — directed to the producer. Why it matters: it
  changes C3's acceptance criteria (and its tests) materially.

All three questions are recorded on this item as a comment and the item is
flagged `needsProducerReview`. Planning itself is complete and independent of
the answers; only C6 (Q1), the status-refresh behaviour in C2 (Q2) and the
cross-project resolution in C3 (Q3) depend on them.

## Goal

As an agent running the changed-scope test gate, I want a changed `tests/unit/test-*.mjs` file to select the node suite for that directory, so a JS/TS test edit is actually executed before commit instead of only at the push-time full suite.

## Problem

`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::_is_test_file()` recognises `test_*.py`, `*_test.py`, `*.test.mjs` and `*_test.mjs` but **not** the repo's dominant node convention `test-*.mjs`. Consequences:

1. A changed `tests/unit/test-*.mjs` file is not classified as a test file, so `map_changed_to_tests()` tries the convention mapping instead (`test_<stem>.py` etc.) and selects nothing.
2. The same filter builds the `all_tests` pool used by import-graph expansion, so `test-*.mjs` files can never be selected there either.
3. Emission of a node command requires a selected `.mjs` path, so no `node --test` command is produced at all.

Verified while delivering SA-0MVTU1WHS002HN1C: editing three test files (`skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py`, `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs`, `tests/unit/test-check-final-validation.mjs`) produced a changed-scope command containing only `pytest ...` — no `node --test`. 46 of the 47 `tests/unit/*.mjs` files use the `test-` prefix, so the gap covers almost the whole node unit suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `_is_test_file()` recognises `test-*.mjs` (and the equivalent `test-*.js`/`test-*.ts` naming) as test files.
- A unit test asserts that changing a `tests/unit/test-foo.mjs` file selects `tests/unit/test-foo.mjs` and causes a `node --test` command to be emitted by the changed-scope command builder (no pytest-only command).
- The selection never invents a path that does not exist (the existing LP-0MTZYRTNF0092JKW existence filter still applies).
- Existing changed-scope selection tests stay green; the full suite stays green.

## Constraints

- Do not widen selection to arbitrary `.mjs` helper files (e.g. `cli-helpers.mjs`); only the test-file naming conventions.
- Keep the single-source-of-truth rule: one filter function, no duplicated naming logic.

**Key Files:**

# Tests: blocked-child classification matrix for `implement.py parent`/`drive`

Parent: **SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2** (*implement.py parent/drive start children whose status is blocked — re-validate the block before starting or skipping*).

**Test-first contract item.** Write these tests **before** the implementation
items C2 (`skip-blocked` via dep-edge re-validation), C3 (prose/cross-project
blockers) and C4 (`drive` propagation). They are expected to be **red** until
those land — they are the executable form of the parent's ACs 1–5.

## Goal

As an implement agent, I need an executable contract for how a child whose
`status` is `blocked` is classified, reported and (not) started, so that the
fix cannot silently regress and a stale block can never strand a child forever.

## Context (read before writing tests)

- `_classify_child()` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, ~line 1127)
  currently returns `skip-terminal` / `skipped-held` / `skip-in-progress` /
  `implement`. **`blocked` falls through to `implement`** — the defect.
- `phase_parent()` (~line 6609) populates `external_blockers` from outbound
  `wl dep` edges only and reports it as a coordination note; it never gates
  the start. `phase_drive()` (~line 7934) already re-propagates
  `blocked_children` from the parent report.
- The live failure: on 2026-10-29 `implement.py parent MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6`
  started child `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4` (status `blocked`, blocker in prose) and
  created a worktree; the child had to be aborted.
- Harness patterns to reuse: `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py`
  (`ParentHarness`, mocked `wl_show` / `wl_show_children` / `wl_dep_blockers` /
  `phase_start` / `_invoke_implement` / `_discover_worktree` /
  `StatusLifecycle.update_status` / `wl_add_comment` /
  `is_code_freeze_active`) and `tests/test_implement_drive.py`
  (`ScriptedParent` + `RecordingSpawner`).
- `wl show --children --json` already returns each child's `description` and
  `tags`, so prose blockers need no extra fetch; `wl dep list <id> --json`
  returns `outbound` entries carrying `id` and `status`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unit tests cover: (a) `blocked` + open external blocker → not started, reported with ids; (b) `blocked` + blocker now terminal → stale block detected and child started; (c) `blocked` + no resolvable blocker → not started, message names the unresolved id; (d) `drive` propagates the same classification/report fields; (e) existing in-chain sibling ordering, cycles and terminal/in-progress behaviour unchanged (regression cases).
- [ ] New module `tests/test_implement_parent_blocked_child.py` (pytest, module-scoped `implement_mod` fixture loading `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`; harness reused from `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py`, not re-implemented).
- [ ] **(a)** `blocked` child + **non-terminal** dep-edge blocker → child **not** started; its `children_processed` entry carries `action: "skip-blocked"` with `blocking_ids` naming the blocker, and is neither `skip-in-progress` nor `skipped-terminal`.
- [ ] **(b)** `blocked` child whose **every** dep-edge blocker is terminal (`completed` / `done` / `in_review`) or soft-deleted → **stale block** detected, child started, and the stale block is named in the report (e.g. `stale_blocks` / a message naming the blocker).
- [ ] **(c)** `blocked` child whose blocker is declared only in prose (a `**Blocked by (SorraAgents):** SA-…` line) with no dep edge and an id that cannot be resolved in this worklog → **not** started, and the report/message names that id together with where to check it (actionable, not silently ignored, not silently startable).
- [ ] **(d)** `phase_drive` propagates the same classification and blocker fields: no session is spawned for a `skip-blocked` child, and the drive report carries the child id plus its blocking ids (in `blocked_children` and/or the per-child entry).
- [ ] **(e)** Regression cases unchanged: in-chain sibling ordering (blocker implemented first), dependency cycle fail-fast (no child started, no status transition), terminal children never re-implemented, an `in_progress` child elsewhere is skipped and never clobbered, a soft-deleted sibling counts as terminal for in-chain gating.
- [ ] **Fail-closed case:** `blocked` child with **no** dep edges and **no** parseable `Blocked by` line → not started and reported as unvalidated (never defaults to startable).
- [ ] Update the superseded expectation in `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py::TestParentDependencyOrder::test_external_blocker_reported_not_started_early`: an out-of-chain blocker with no resolvable status must now **hold** the block (child reported `skip-blocked`, the startable sibling started) instead of the old "coordination note only, child started" behaviour. Rename the test so the new contract is obvious.
- [ ] Every test asserts a behaviour that production code (not a re-implementation) provides — no self-referential simulations (see `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`).
- [ ] Tests run through the test skill / finish gate (`/skill:test`), green together with the existing implement suites; never an ad-hoc runner. The full pytest + node suite is green at the dev-push gate (parent AC 8).

## Constraints

- Tests only — no production code in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` from this item.
- UK English throughout.
- Do not weaken or delete existing guards; the only expectation that changes is the superseded "external blocker is a coordination note only" case above.

**Key Files:**
- `tests/test_implement_parent_blocked_child.py` — new test module (the matrix).
- `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py` — harness pattern to reuse.
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` — scripted-parent/recording-spawner harness for case (d).
- `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py` — superseded external-blocker expectation to update.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — module under test (`_classify_child`, `phase_parent`, `phase_drive`).

## Related work

- `SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2` — parent (blocked-child re-validation).
- `SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T` — introduced `external_blockers` as coordination notes; superseded by this work.
- `SA-0MVS1QS9J009DGPT` — the *parent's own* outbound edges / `blocked` status (adjacent, distinct code path; do not fold into this item).
- `SA-0MVO6UL70000HT0J` — terminal blockers still gate topological ordering (adjacent, distinct).

## Impact

An epic no longer starts a child that is deliberately blocked against a prerequisite that has not landed — the block is re-validated first, so agents are never asked to fabricate evidence against missing work and a stale block can no longer strand a child forever.

# `phase_parent`: classify a still-blocked child as `skip-blocked` (dep-edge re-validation)

Parent: **SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2**. Test-first sibling: **C1** (blocked-child classification matrix).

## Goal

As an implement agent running an epic, I need `implement.py parent` to never
start a child whose `status` is `blocked` while its block still holds, and to
re-evaluate (not honour forever) a **stale** block, so a verification child is
never implemented against a prerequisite that has not landed and a landed
prerequisite never strands its dependent.

## Context

- `_classify_child()` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, ~line 1127)
  returns `implement` for `status: blocked`. Precedence today:
  terminal → `skipped-held` → `skip-in-progress` → `implement`.
- `phase_parent()` (~line 6609) builds `classifications` with
  `action`/`external_blockers` and gates the start only on **in-chain**
  blockers (`_in_chain_blockers`, blockers that are themselves children of the
  same parent, ~line 6787). `_next_child_to_implement()` (~line 1227) is a
  second, legacy classification path kept consistent by tests.
- `wl dep list <id> --json` → `outbound` entries with `id` and `status`
  (`wl_dep_blockers`, ~line 565).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `blocked` child whose block still holds yields a **distinct** classification (`skip-blocked`, i.e. `ACTION_SKIP_BLOCKED`) from `_classify_child()` (or its caller); it is never `implement`, `skip-in-progress` or `skipped-terminal`. Precedence is explicit and documented: `skip-terminal` → `skipped-held` → `skip-in-progress` → `skip-blocked` → `implement`.
- [ ] **Dep-edge re-validation:** for a `blocked` child the outbound `wl dep list` edges are resolved; the block is **stale** iff every blocker is terminal (`completed`/`done`/`in_review`, reusing `_is_terminal_status` / soft-delete semantics) — in which case the child is startable again and the stale block is named in the report (a `stale_blocks` entry, and a log/comment line naming the blocker ids). Any **non-terminal** blocker holds the block.
- [ ] `children_processed` entries for a held child carry `action: "skip-blocked"`, the child id, its status and `blocking_ids` (the ids that hold it); the report also lists them in `blocked_children` so `phase_drive`'s existing propagation keeps working.
- [ ] A block that cannot be validated (no dep edges, no parseable blocker line, unknown status) is treated as **holding** and reported as unvalidated (`unvalidated_blocks`) — it must not default to startable. (The prose/cross-project resolution that makes such a child actionable lands in C3; until then the fail-closed behaviour is the correct default.)
- [ ] A `blocked` child with at least one terminal blocker **and** one non-terminal blocker still holds (the non-terminal one wins); a `blocked` child whose blockers are all soft-deleted is stale/startable.
- [ ] `_next_child_to_implement()` (legacy helper, still covered by `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py`) applies the same rule so the two classification paths cannot diverge; it is kept, not deleted.
- [ ] Unchanged: dependency order, cycle fail-fast, terminal children never re-implemented, `skipped-held` precedence, `skip-in-progress` never clobbering another agent's claim, `--finalise-stranded` semantics, and single-item `start`/`finish` behaviour.
- [ ] The C1 tests for cases (a), (b) and (e) are green; the changed-scope suite is green through the finish gate (`/skill:test`) and the full pytest + node suite is green at the dev-push gate (parent AC 8).

## Minimal implementation sketch

- Add `ACTION_SKIP_BLOCKED = "skip-blocked"` beside `ACTION_SKIPPED_HELD` (~line 213).
- New helper, e.g. `_blocked_child_state(child, blockers) -> {"action", "blocking_ids", "stale_ids", "unvalidated"}`, called from `_classify_child`'s callers (`phase_parent`, `_next_child_to_implement`) with the child's outbound edges — `_classify_child` itself has no edge data, so either widen its signature with an optional `blockers` argument (defaulting to `None` → unvalidated/fail-closed) or keep the status test in `_classify_child` and resolve the blocked verdict in the callers. Prefer the smallest change that keeps both call sites consistent.
- Extend the `classifications`/`child_results` entries and the "no startable child" message to name the blockers.


## Impact

Running an epic no longer starts a child whose block still holds, and a block whose prerequisites have landed starts on the next run instead of stranding the child.

## Implementation notes (2026-11-09)

- `ACTION_SKIP_BLOCKED = "skip-blocked"` added beside `ACTION_SKIPPED_HELD`;
  precedence documented once in `_classify_child`: `skip-terminal` →
  `skipped-held` → `skip-in-progress` → `skip-blocked` → `implement`.
- New `_blocked_child_state(child, blockers, children)` re-validates a block
  against the outbound dependency edges. In-chain edges are resolved through
  the live child list when the edge payload omits `status`, so a sibling's real
  status wins; no edges ⇒ `unvalidated` ⇒ holds (fail closed).
- `phase_parent` records `blocking_ids` / `unvalidated` on the classification
  and the `children_processed` entry, adds report-level `stale_blocks` and
  `unvalidated_blocks`, names the blocking ids in the "no startable child"
  message, logs every stale finding and comments it on the child
  (Q2 = A: the lifecycle status is never rewritten here).
- `_next_child_to_implement` passes the same edge data, so the legacy path
  cannot diverge.
- Tests: C1's cases (a), (b), (e) and the fail-closed case are green (their
  `xfail` markers removed, as is the superseded-contract marker in
  `test_implement_parent_dependency.py`); new unit tests cover the helper,
  the classification precedence and the stale/held/unvalidated reporting.

## Constraints

- Do not weaken existing guards; do not change `start`/`finish` single-item behaviour.
- Prefer declared dependency edges over prose; no `wl` schema change, no `gh`/network calls.
- UK English throughout.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_classify_child` (~1127), `_next_child_to_implement` (~1227), `phase_parent` (~6609, incl. `_in_chain_blockers` ~6787), `wl_dep_blockers` (~565), `TERMINAL_STATUSES`/`_is_terminal_status` (~1082).
- `tests/test_implement_parent_blocked_child.py` — C1's matrix (red to green).
- `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py` — existing parent suite that must stay green.
- `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py` — existing dependency-order suite that must stay green.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2` — parent.
- `SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T` — introduced `external_blockers` as coordination notes (superseded here).
- `SA-0MVS1QS9J009DGPT` — the *parent's own* outbound edges / `blocked` status; distinct, do not implement here.
- `SA-0MVO6UL70000HT0J` — terminal blockers still gate topological ordering; distinct.

# Prose `Blocked by` and cross-project blockers hold a `blocked` child

Parent: **SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2**. Depends on **C2** (`skip-blocked` classification); test-first contract in **C1** (case (c)).

## Goal

As an implement agent, I need a blocker that is declared in the child's
description (the cross-project convention) to gate the start exactly like a
dependency edge, so a verification child is never started against an
unlanded prerequisite in another repository and the report tells me which id
to check and where.

## Context

- Cross-project blocks are written in prose, e.g. on
  `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4`:
  `**Blocked by (SorraAgents):** \`SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2\` — *Finish gate: …* (in progress; …)`
  followed by an `**Unblock condition:**` line. `wl dep list` on that child
  returns `outbound: []`, so today the phase reports `external_blockers: []`
  and starts it.
- `wl show --children --json` already returns each child's `description`, so
  no extra fetch is needed to parse it.
- Ids in this worklog look like `SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2` / `MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1`;
  ids belonging to another repository's worklog are **not** resolvable from
  this one (`wl show` fails).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A narrowly scoped parser extracts blocker ids from an **explicit** `Blocked by …` line only (case-insensitive, tolerating the bold/labelled form `**Blocked by (SorraAgents):**` and a plain `Blocked by:`); it must not treat arbitrary prose, `Unblock condition:` text or `Related work` ids as blockers.
- [ ] **Re-validation of cross-project and prose blocks:** blocker IDs declared in the child description's `Blocked by …` line are collected and surfaced in `external_blockers` (id + resolvable status, or `unresolved`); an unresolvable cross-project id holds the block and is reported with an actionable message (id + where to check it), never silently ignored and never silently startable. The merged set gates the start via C2's `skip-blocked` verdict.
- [ ] **Resolvable** prose blocker (present in this worklog): terminal → stale (child startable, blocker named); non-terminal → holds, reported with its status.
- [ ] **Unresolvable** (cross-project / unknown) prose blocker → **holds**, and the report/message names the id plus where to check it (e.g. "check the owning project's worklog", with the id's prefix as the hint). Never silently ignored, never silently startable.
- [ ] A `blocked` child with **no** dep edges and **no** parseable `Blocked by` line is reported as **unvalidated** and holds (fail-closed) — never defaults to startable.
- [ ] Parsing never crashes the phase (fail-open on the parser, fail-closed on the verdict): a malformed line yields "unvalidated" rather than an exception.
- [ ] No `wl` schema change and no new machine-readable field: prose + declared dep edges only (the parent AC's "and/or a machine-readable `externalBlockers` field, whichever is implemented" is satisfied by this choice). Cross-project ids are not resolved over the network.
- [ ] C1 cases (c) and the fail-closed case are green; the changed-scope suite is green through the finish gate (`/skill:test`).

## Assumptions (recorded on the parent)

- A cross-project block can therefore never go stale automatically: when the
  external item lands, the child's owner must refresh the child (status
  `open`, or remove/annotate the `Blocked by` line). This is the fail-closed
  behaviour the parent's AC 3 asks for and is recorded as an assumption.


## Impact

A verification child blocked by a prerequisite declared in another repository's work item is never started until that work really exists, and the report tells the operator exactly which id to check and where.

## Implementation notes (2026-11-09)

- New narrowly scoped parser `_prose_blocker_ids()` reads only an **explicit**
  `Blocked by …` line (bold/labelled and plain forms, case-insensitive); an
  `Unblock condition:` line or a `Related work` list can never be mistaken for
  a blocker. Empty/malformed input returns `[]` — never raises.
- `_prose_blockers()` resolves each declared id through `wl_show` (prefix →
  sibling worklog, no network). Resolved → the item dict, so the existing
  `_is_terminal_child` rule decides stale vs holding. Unresolved → an
  `unresolved` sentinel that **holds** and carries the hint
  "check the owning project's worklog (id prefix …)".
- `phase_parent` merges declared dependency edges with the prose ids into a
  single gating set (`gate_blockers`), used by both the Step 5 classification
  and the Step 6 start decision, so the two can never disagree. The
  classification carries `blocker_details` (id/status/source/resolved/hint) and
  `unresolved_blockers`; the report gains `unresolved_blockers` and names the
  unresolved ids in the "no startable child" message.
- Prose blockers are consulted **only** for a `blocked` child: an open child
  with a stale `Blocked by` line is normal work, not a hold.
- Q3 = A adopted on the parent (producer decision): a resolved cross-project
  blocker that is terminal makes the block stale, so a landed prerequisite
  unblocks the child on the next run. The assumption previously recorded on
  this item ("cross-project blocks can never go stale") is superseded by that
  decision — recorded here rather than left contradictory.
- Tests: C1's case (c) and the fail-closed case are green; new unit tests cover
  the parser (narrow scope, malformed input), resolvable open/terminal prose
  blockers, unresolvable ids with the actionable hint, edge+prose merging, and

# `phase_drive`: propagate `skip-blocked` classification and blocker ids

Parent: **SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2**. Depends on **C2** and **C3**; test-first contract in **C1** (case (d)).

## Goal

As a dispatcher running `implement.py drive <epic>` unattended, I need the
drive report to carry the same blocked-child verdicts as `parent` — with the
blocking ids — so no session is spawned for a `blocked` child and I can see
which id to wait for without re-reading the child's description.

## Context

- `phase_drive()` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, ~line 7934) loops
  over `phase_parent` reports and spawns a fresh Pi session per startable
  child. It already re-propagates `blocked_children` (ids only) on the
  "no startable child" path (~line 8368).
- After C2/C3 a child can be classified `skip-blocked` with `blocking_ids`;
  drive must not spawn a session for it and must surface the ids.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] No session is spawned for a child classified `skip-blocked` by the parent phase; `sessions_spawned` and `children_driven` reflect that (the child is not counted as driven, failed or retried).
- [ ] The drive report carries the blocked verdicts with their blocking ids — `blocked_children` keeps its existing id-list shape **and** the richer per-child entries (child id, status, `blocking_ids`, stale/unvalidated flags) are present, so both existing consumers (`tests/test_implement_drive.py::test_stops_when_no_startable_child`) and new ones work.
- [ ] The "no startable child" message names the blocking ids (not just "blocked or held"), so an unattended dispatcher log is actionable.
- [ ] Existing drive behaviour unchanged: per-child session bound, finish-attempt bound and reset-for-retry recovery, timeout reconciliation (`completed-late`), stranded-child detection, `skipped-held` propagation, recursion guard, and parent-advanced-last.
- [ ] C1 case (d) is green; the changed-scope suite (pytest + node where applicable) is green through the finish gate (`/skill:test`).


## Impact

An unattended `drive` run never spawns a session for a child whose block still holds, and its report names the exact id to wait for instead of just "blocked or held".

## Implementation notes (2026-11-09)

- New `_skip_blocked_details()` turns a `phase_parent` report's
  `children_processed` `skip-blocked` verdicts into drive entries carrying
  `id`, `status`, `action`, `blocking_ids`, `unvalidated` and (when the parent
  reported one) `stale`/`stale_block_ids`; `_describe_skip_blocked()` renders
  the copy-pasteable message clause.
- The "no startable child" path now forwards `children_processed`,
  `blocked_children` (unchanged id-list shape), `blocked_child_details`,
  `stale_blocks`, `unvalidated_blocks` and `unresolved_blockers`, and appends a
  "Blocked children: id (blocked by …)" clause to the message when the parent
  message does not already name every id.
- Defence in depth: if a parent report ever offers a `skip-blocked` child as
  `next_child`, the drive loop refuses to spawn it — no worktree, no lock, no
  session; the verdict is reported and the chain stops with `success: false`.
- No other behaviour changed: per-child session bound, finish-attempt bound and
  reset-for-retry, timeout reconciliation, stranded-child detection,
  `skipped-held` propagation, recursion guard, parent-advanced-last.
- Tests: C1 case (d) is green (marker removed); new tests cover the
  no-spawn guard, the rich no-startable-child report, and stale/unvalidated/
  unresolved forwarding.

## Constraints

- Reporting/loop-control change only — no new spawning policy, no change to
  `parent`'s classification (that is C2/C3) or to single-item `start`/`finish`.
- Do not weaken existing bounds or guards.
- UK English throughout.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive` (~7934, report propagation ~8360-8380), `_reconcile_spawn_failure`, `phase_parent` report fields from C2/C3.
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` — scripted-parent/recording-spawner harness; existing propagation test to extend.

# Regression tests pin the dev-push gate subject

Parent: **SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3** — test-first slice (written before the fix, in the
tracer-bullet `xfail(strict=True)` style already used by
`skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_commit_tree.py`).

## Goal

Pin the invariant *"the dev-push gate's subject is the pushed commit"* with
automated tests, so the code change in the sibling item is verified rather than
asserted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Retry push cwd is the worktree.** A regression test asserts the retry
  push's cwd/root is the worktree: driving `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` in
  a hermetic git sandbox records `git_push_to_dev` called with the **worktree**
  path (not `repo_root`) and with the **rebased** commit, so the hook's
  `--project-root` is the pushed tree.
- **First attempt cwd is the worktree.** A regression test asserts the first
  dev-push attempt also runs from the checkout that has the pushed commit
  checked out, so the main checkout's working tree is never the subject of the
  dev-push gate.
- **HEAD ≠ pushed sha cannot silently gate the wrong tree.** A test asserts the
  mismatch is either corrected or refused: the push is not attempted, and a
  fail-closed error names the commit, branch, worktree and the actual `HEAD`.
- **Gate evidence is surfaced on success.** A test asserts `git_push_to_dev()`
  logs the hook/push `stderr` on success (INFO/DEBUG) and that the logged
  evidence carries the gate's resolved tree — root path, `HEAD` sha, pushed sha
  and executed-vs-cached — so "the gate ran and hit a cache for commit X" is
  distinguishable from "the gate never ran". No wall-clock timing proxies: the
  classification is driven by cache entries set up in the fixture.
- **Hermetic.** Tests use `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` plus stubbed `wl`/store
  boundaries; they invoke no test command themselves and run no wall-clock
  sleeps.
- Tests carry a documented pre-fix baseline and fail before the fix, pass after
  it (markers removed in the fixing change set).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` — extend: retry push
  cwd/subject assertions (fixture already builds a hermetic sandbox + rebase).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_from_worktree.py` — new: first
  attempt cwd, subject guard, evidence logging/classification.
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — factories only (no behaviour change).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Extend the existing recovery-test harness to record `git_push_to_dev` call
   args and the push cwd's `HEAD`.
2. New module: capture `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` and `phase_finish`
   Step-6 push args; assert cwd == worktree and pushed sha == worktree `HEAD`.
3. Assert the fail-closed message fields and the evidence record's fields via
   `caplog` (root, head, pushed, classification).
4. Mark the new expectations `xfail(strict=True)` until the sibling fix lands.

## Definition of Done

- The change-set gate (test skill) is green with the markers in place, and the
  new tests demonstrably fail when the pre-fix behaviour is restored.

## Dependencies / Deliverables

- No prerequisites. Blocks the implementation item (test-first ordering).
- Deliverable: failing-then-passing regression tests, no production code change.

# Push to dev from the worktree that holds the commit

Parent: **SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3** — the core fix (blocks nothing else, unblocks
the evidence and docs slices).

## Goal

`implement.py finish` must run its dev push from the checkout that has the
pushed commit checked out — the worktree — on the **first attempt and the
non-fast-forward retry**, so `.githooks/pre-push` resolves its
`--project-root` to the pushed tree. Fail closed when that tree cannot be
materialised.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Push cwd is the pushed tree.** `implement.py finish` runs its dev push from
  the checkout that has the pushed commit checked out (the worktree) — for the
  first attempt *and* the non-fast-forward retry — so the main checkout's
  working tree is never the subject of the dev-push gate.
- **Retry path re-establishes the subject.** After the recovery rebase rewrites
  the commit, the retry push has the rebased commit checked out (pushed sha ==
  push cwd `HEAD`), so the hook's `--project-root` is the pushed tree.
- **Fails closed with an actionable message.** A pre-push subject guard refuses
  the push when the push cwd does not hold the pushed commit (worktree gone,
  `HEAD` ≠ pushed sha, dirty state that cannot be rebased): finish raises an
  error naming the **commit, branch, worktree and the actual `HEAD`**, and
  never silently pushes from a checkout holding a different commit.
- **Recovery behaviour preserved.** Push timeout → process-group kill +
  recoverable-state comment; non-fast-forward → fetch + rebase + retry;
  worktree retained until the push succeeds. `_restore_local_dev_after_failed_push`
  and `_sync_parent_branch` still operate on the main checkout.
- **Step 5 stays hygiene only.** The local-dev fast-forward remains a main
  checkout hygiene step (never the gate subject); `repo_root` stays the subject
  of the main-checkout guard and of `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev`.
- **Cache compatibility preserved.** Full-suite evidence stays path-independent
  (`HEAD` sha + dirty-content hash + suite command): pushing from the worktree
  reuses/creates the same audit-acceptable `scope: full` entries, and
  `mirror_suite_cache` still mirrors the worktree cache into the main checkout.
- **Docs/comments in scope.** Code comments and docstrings that assert the old
  behaviour (the Step-5/Step-6 comments claiming the hook measures the main
  checkout, `git_push_to_dev`'s "cwd: worktree root" docstring) are corrected
  in this change set.
- **No weakening.** `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` and friends remain explicit escape
  hatches; the default path never fails open.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — phase_finish Step 6 push call site
  (currently `git_push_to_dev(repo_root, branch, commit_hash)`),
  `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` retry push, new subject guard +
  `PushSubjectMismatchError`, Step-5/Step-6 comments.
- `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py`,
  `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_from_worktree.py` (markers
  removed here).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add `_assert_push_subject(push_cwd, commit_hash, branch, worktree_path)`:
   push cwd exists, is a git worktree, and `git -C push_cwd rev-parse HEAD`
   equals `commit_hash` — else raise `PushSubjectMismatchError` naming commit,
   branch, worktree and actual `HEAD`.
2. Step 6: guard, then `git_push_to_dev(worktree_path, branch, commit_hash)`.
   Keep the Step-5 fast-forward and the pre-push main-checkout guard on
   `repo_root`.
3. `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()`: after `git rebase origin/dev`, recompute
   `new_commit` **from the worktree**, guard, then retry
   `git_push_to_dev(worktree_path, branch, new_commit)`; keep the existing
   recoverable-state comments on failure.
4. Leave the ancestry assertion (Step 6a) reading `origin/dev` — it verifies
   what landed, not which cwd pushed.
5. Remove the `xfail(strict=True)` markers from the regression tests.

## Definition of Done

- Change-set tests green (retry cwd == worktree, first attempt cwd == worktree,
  guard refuses a mismatch), and a real `implement.py finish` dev push runs the
  full-suite gate with the worktree as `--project-root`.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (enforced at the
  dev-push gate on the pushed commit).

## Dependencies / Deliverables

- Prerequisite: the regression-test item (test-first ordering).
- Deliverable: `implement.py` push-from-worktree behaviour + guard + corrected
  comments.

# Surface dev-push gate evidence on success

Parent: **SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3** — observability slice; makes the gate auditable
and makes the 2026-10-28 68-second anomaly diagnosable.

## Goal

For every `implement.py finish`, make *"the gate ran and hit a cache for commit
X"* distinguishable from *"the gate never ran"* — without weakening the gate and
without executing tests from the pusher.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Gate evidence is surfaced.** Hook/push `stderr` is logged by
  `git_push_to_dev()` on success too (at least INFO/DEBUG) — today it is
  captured with `subprocess.PIPE` and logged only on failure.
- **Resolved tree visible in that output.** The logged evidence carries the
  gate's resolved tree: root path (the push cwd), the `HEAD` sha at that root,
  the pushed sha, and executed-vs-cached for the full-suite entry — so "the gate
  ran and hit a cache for commit X" is distinguishable from "the gate never
  ran".
- **Executed-vs-cached is derived from the test cache, not wall-clock.** Using
  the read-only `skill/test_cache.py` API for the pushed git state: no valid
  entry before the push + a valid entry after ⇒ `executed`; a valid entry
  already present before the push ⇒ `cached`; still no entry after a successful
  push ⇒ `no-evidence` (warned, and never silently reported as green).
- **Read-only, never weakening.** The evidence path executes no test command
  itself, does not alter the cache, keeps `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` and friends as
  explicit escape hatches, and never turns a gate-accepted push into a failure.
- **Machine-readable.** The classification is added to
  `report["steps"]["push"]` so `implement.py finish --json` exposes it.
- **Tests, no timing proxies.** A test covers the three classifications
  (`executed` / `cached` / `no-evidence`) by staging cache entries in the
  fixture and asserting the logged line via `caplog` — no wall-clock assertions.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_push_to_dev()` (stderr
  logging), phase_finish Step 6 reporting (`report["steps"]["push"]`).
- `skill/test_cache.py` — `compute_git_state()`, `query_cached()` (read-only
  calls only; no changes expected).
- `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py` and/or
  `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_from_worktree.py` — classification
  tests.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Capture `stderr` on success and `LOG.info` it (keep `LOG.error` on failure).
2. Before the push: compute the pushed git state's full-suite cache entry (if
   any) via `query_cached()`; after a successful push: re-query.
3. Emit one structured evidence line — e.g.
   `dev-push gate evidence: root=<cwd> head=<sha> pushed=<sha> full-suite=<executed|cached|no-evidence>`
   — and store the same dict under `report["steps"]["push"]["gate_evidence"]`.
4. Warn (not fail) on `no-evidence`, naming the commit, so a gate that did not
   run is visible without blocking recovery.

## Definition of Done

- Change-set tests green for all three classifications; a real finish over a
  cold cache logs `full-suite=executed`, over a warm cache `full-suite=cached`.

## Dependencies / Deliverables

- Prerequisite: the push-from-worktree item (the evidence must describe the
  pushed tree, which is the worktree).
- Deliverable: success-path hook logging + structured gate evidence in logs and
  `--json` output.

# Live-repo guard: exclude `refs/heads/worklog/data` from mutation surface

## Problem statement

The live-repo mutation guard in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` reports a false-positive suite failure when a concurrent session moves the Worklog data branch `refs/heads/worklog/data` during a test run. Full-suite evidence comes out red for a green tree, blocking the dev-push and release gates.

## Users

- Automated agent sessions running full test suites on a shared multi-agent host.
- The dev-push pre-commit hook, which runs the full suite before pushing to `dev`.

## Problem

`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` maintains three concurrency-exclusion mechanisms:

| Mechanism | Constant | Excludes |
|---|---|---|
| Prefix match | `WORKLOG_REF_PREFIX = "refs/worklog/"` | `refs/worklog/*` |
| Exact match | `CONCURRENCY_EXCLUDED_REF_EXACT = "refs/heads/dev"` | `refs/heads/dev` |
| Namespace | `CONCURRENCY_EXCLUDED_REF_NAMESPACES` | `refs/remotes/origin/*` |

The ref `refs/heads/worklog/data` matches **none** of these:
- It starts with `refs/heads/` not `refs/worklog/`.
- It is not `refs/heads/dev`.
- It is not in `refs/remotes/origin/`.

Every `wl` write (and every `wl sync`) updates this ref, so any concurrent agent session or the pre-push hook's own sync can move it mid-run.

## Suggested change

Add `refs/heads/worklog/` (prefix) or `refs/heads/worklog/data` (exact) to the concurrency exclusion set in `git_sandbox.py`, ideally as a prefix `refs/heads/worklog/` to cover future worklog branches.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A run in which only `refs/heads/worklog/data` moves reports green (excluded as concurrent infrastructure churn, surfaced as an informational note).
2. A run in which an ordinary source branch ref moves is still failed as a mutation.
3. `refs/worklog/*` behaviour is unchanged; no path/branch name-pattern heuristics introduced.
4. Regression tests cover both directions (excluded vs. still-monitored).

## Constraints

- Must use prefix or exact-match ref patterns — no `wl-*` name heuristics (per ownership-work AC4).
- Must not alter existing exclusion behaviour for `refs/worklog/*`, `refs/heads/dev`, or `refs/remotes/origin/*`.
- Exclusion must be reported as an informational note (not silently suppressed).

## Existing state

`git_sandbox.py` lines 110–145 define the three exclusion constants and the `_is_concurrency_excluded_ref()` function. The exclusion logic is used by both `diff_snapshots` and `fingerprint`.

Note on the note channel: ref exclusions are currently filtered out silently — only working-tree churn excluded by provenance attribution produces a note (`excluded_churn_notes()` / `EXCLUDED_CHURN_NOTE_PREFIX`, consumed by `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` and `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`). Satisfying AC1 therefore also needs the excluded-ref churn surfaced through that same note renderer, matching the existing attribution pattern.

## Desired change

1. Add `refs/heads/worklog/` to `CONCURRENCY_EXCLUDED_REF_NAMESPACES` (or add a new constant and extend `_is_concurrency_excluded_ref`). Keep `refs/worklog/*`, `refs/heads/dev` and `refs/remotes/origin/*` behaviour untouched.
2. Surface excluded-ref churn as an informational note via the existing `excluded_churn_notes()` / `EXCLUDED_CHURN_NOTE_PREFIX` channel (generalising it to report excluded ref movements, or adding a sibling renderer that the guard's note list consumes), so the exclusion is never silent (AC1, Constraints).
3. Regression tests (written first, red → green) in `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py` (or the concurrency test file) asserting:
   - Only `refs/heads/worklog/data` moves → green run (`changed is False`) plus an informational note naming the excluded ref.
   - An ordinary source branch ref moves → still-failed run (`changed is True`).
   - `refs/worklog/*` exclusion still behaves as today (no regression in the existing prefix tests).
4. Verification: changed-scope gate via `/skill:test` (agent test runs route through the test skill, never ad-hoc pytest).

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — add exclusion namespace; extend the note renderer for excluded refs
- `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py` — regression tests (both directions + note assertion)
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` — consumes `excluded_churn_notes()`; confirm excluded-ref notes reach the run report
- Possibly `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py` — ensure audit integration is covered

## Related work

- **SA-0MV8311B3005DNG8** — Live-repo test guard false-positives on concurrent agent dev fast-forward and worktree churn
- **SA-0MV87GC8O006RHS8** — Implement ownership-based exclusion in git_sandbox (completed; added `refs/heads/dev` and `refs/remotes/origin/` exclusions)
- **SA-0MV5MYBKJ0033P8U** — Ownership work (source of the ref-based exclusion pattern and AC4 prohibition on name-pattern heuristics)
- **SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG** — Working-tree churn attribution + `excluded_churn_notes()` note channel reused here
- **SA-0MUILGH5E007X627** — Live-repo guard false-positives inside an agent worktree (concurrent worktree ref churn)
- **SA-0MUII5QDI005U2AH** — Related but distinct: shared `refs/stash` churn (separate scope, not covered here)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk:** Adding a broader `refs/heads/worklog/` prefix might mask legitimate fixture mutations if a future fixture uses a `worklog/`-prefixed branch. **Mitigation:** The prefix matches the existing pattern of `refs/remotes/origin/` (a namespace, not a name heuristic); the ref is created only by `wl` infrastructure.
- **Assumption:** `refs/heads/worklog/data` is the sole `refs/heads/worklog/*` branch in active use.
- **Scope-creep:** This fix does not address other potential infrastructure ref movements (e.g. `refs/heads/wl-*` if such a pattern were ever introduced, or `refs/stash` per SA-0MUII5QDI005U2AH). Those can be tracked as separate items.

# Refactor skill: never inject marker blocks above a shebang or encoding line

**Headline:** After the shebang fix (SA-0MVPUVM8F006270F) the refactor skill
still prepends its marker block above a PEP 263 encoding line and above a
Python module docstring, so annotated files implicitly change the file
encoding cookie position that the interpreter reads and trample the module
docstring convention. It also rewrites files without preserving line endings.
The remaining fix: compute an insertion offset from the file head (shebang,
then coding line, then optional module docstring) and splice the marker
block *below* all of them, writing with `newline=""`.

## Problem statement

`skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` places the REFACTOR marker block at the
top of the file and only steps past a leading shebang. Two Python-specific
file-head constructs are still displaced:

1. A **PEP 263 encoding declaration** (`# -*- coding: ... -*-`, or
   `# coding: ...`). PEP 263 requires the cookie on line 1, or line 2 when
   line 1 is a shebang. Prepending the marker pushes the cookie to line 3+,
   so Python no longer honours it — an encoding regression on files the skill
   touched. This gap was explicitly deferred by SA-0MVPUVM8F006270F (its
   "Open Questions" section records the cookie, out of scope there).
2. A **module docstring**. Prepending the marker above a leading module
   docstring splits the docstring from the module head; it also breaks the
   convention that the docstring is the first statement, and produces a
   noisier diff. AC1 therefore places the marker after the docstring too.

A third defect: the file is written with `open(..., "w")` and default line
handling, which can normalise line endings (CRLF → LF) — AC3 requires writing
with `newline=""` so line endings and trailing-newline state are preserved.

Leaving these unhandled means the skill keeps creating preventable lint
findings and file mutations on annotated scripts.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running `/skill:refactor` or the implement
  pipeline's refactor step — they inherit preventable file-head mutations and
  encoding-changes on files the skill touched.
- **Producers triaging the refactor backlog** — self-inflicted findings
  consume triage and implementation capacity.
- **Developers** — annotated scripts must keep a valid encoding declaration
  (when present) and a clean module head.

User stories:

- As an agent running the refactor step, I want the marker block inserted
  *after* any shebang, encoding line, and module docstring, so annotated
  Python files keep their interpreter directive on line 1, their encoding
  cookie where the interpreter reads it, and their docstring as the first
  statement.
- As a maintainer, I want files the skill annotates to remain byte-stable
  apart from the marker (no line-ending normalisation), so diffs are minimal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `inject_refactor_comment()` inserts its block *after* any shebang
      (`#!…`) and any PEP 263 coding line, and after a Python module docstring
      when the file opens with one; on files with none of these the block
      still goes to the top as today.
- [ ] Markdown/HTML block-style markers (`<!-- … -->`) keep their current
      placement behaviour, except that a leading shebang or coding line in a
      non-Markdown file is never displaced.
- [ ] Line endings and trailing newline state are preserved (write with
      `newline=""`), so the fix does not normalise CRLF files.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` cover: a file
      starting with a shebang, a file with shebang + coding line, a file with
      shebang + docstring, a plain Python file with no shebang, and a Markdown
      file — each asserting shebang stays on line 1.
- [ ] A regression test asserts that running the repository's lint gate over a
      file annotated by the skill reports no `EXE005`/`EXE001`-style executable
      findings.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` (the "REFACTOR Comments"
      section), and any relevant docs entries.

## Impact

Agents and producers no longer see self-inflicted encoding/executable-bit
findings or docstring trampling on files the refactor skill annotates; every
annotated script keeps its shebang, encoding declaration, and module docstring
exactly where the interpreter and tools expect them.

## Constraints

- Do **not** change marker syntax, the duplicate-suppression match on smell
  type, or `get_comment_style()` file-type mapping — placement only.
- Removal of stale markers on work-item close is **out of scope**; that is
  `SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9`.
- Keep the change confined to `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` and its
  tests (plus the SKILL.md/docs wording noted in the last AC).

## Existing state

Since SA-0MVPUVM8F006270F, `inject_refactor_comment()` steps past a leading
shebang via `_split_leading_shebang()` and splices the block immediately
below it (dropping the block's own leading newline). The remaining gaps:

```python
# skill/refactor/comment_injection.py
    shebang, body = _split_leading_shebang(original_content)
    if shebang:
        new_content = shebang + comment_block.lstrip("
") + body
    else:
        new_content = comment_block + original_content   # still displaces
                                                         # coding line / docstring

    with open(file_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:    # no newline=""
        f.write(new_content)
```

- A file opening with `# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-` (no shebang) gets the marker
  above the cookie — the cookie then sits at line 2+, which PEP 263 only
  allows when line 1 is a shebang.
- A file opening with a module docstring gets the marker above it.
- The write path does not preserve line endings (no `newline=""`).
- Field evidence: on 2026-10-30 the implement pipeline's refactor step
  annotated `src/rss_server.py` in the ContentCreator project, pushing
  `#!/usr/bin/env python3` from line 1 to line 13 and producing
  `EXE005 Shebang should be at the beginning of the file`. The finding was
  filed as `OSL-0MVVE7V84007DQD0`, implemented as removing the skill's own
  marker, and pinned with `tests/test_rss_script_entrypoint.py`.

## Desired change

`inject_refactor_comment()` computes an insertion offset from the file head
(shebang, then coding line, then optional module docstring) and splices the
block there, leaving the file head byte-identical otherwise. Extend the
shebang-only helper into a general file-head skipper:

- Step past a leading `#!` line (existing behaviour, preserved).
- Step past a PEP 263 encoding declaration on line 1 (no shebang) or line 2
  (after a shebang) — Python-only concern; the marker belongs below the
  cookie, wherever it sits.
- Step past a leading Python module docstring (a triple-quoted string that
  opens the file body and terminates before the first statement). Heuristic:
  match only a leading `"""…"""`/`'''…'''` that closes before any statement;
  fall back to top-of-file placement when parsing is ambiguous
  (see Risks).
- Write the result with `newline=""` so CRLF and trailing-newline state are
  preserved.

Note for the implementer: with docstring placement the marker moves below
the docstring, so the current `TestShebangPreservation` case that asserts
marker-before-docstring (`content.index("REFACTOR") <
content.index('"""Docstring."""')`) must be updated to assert
marker-after-docstring per AC1. `has_existing_comment()` scans the whole
file, so markers below the docstring are still detected (idempotence
holds).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` — generalise the file-head skip
  (shebang → coding line → docstring); write with `newline=""`
- `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` — placement tests for the
  shebang / coding-line / docstring / Markdown cases; update the affected
  shebang+docstring assertion
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — state the placement rule in the "REFACTOR
  Comments" section
- `docs/refactor.md` — add the placement rule to the comment-injection
  documentation (if a suitable section exists)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** a marker placed after the module docstring is still found by
  `has_existing_comment()`, which scans the whole file rather than the head.
- **Risk (low):** docstring detection is heuristic; an over-eager match could
  move the marker into the middle of code. Mitigation: match only a leading
  triple-quoted string that terminates before the first statement, and fall
  back to top-of-file placement when parsing is ambiguous.
- **Risk (low):** mis-detecting a leading `"…"`/`'…'` string literal as a
  docstring would displace the marker. Constrain detection to triple-quoted
  strings and, where practical, to files whose extension maps to the `.py`
  style.
- **Scope-creep risk:** a general "annotation lifecycle" refactor (placement,
  removal, sweep) is tempting. Record such work against
  `SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9`/`SA-0MVZA21600087VRD` instead of widening this item.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVPUVM8F006270F` (completed) — fixed shebang displacement only; its
  deferred PEP 263 cookie question is this item's core scope. Partial overlap
  (shebang placement already shipped) — this item addresses the gaps.
- `SA-0MVGKMNEQ009RZKD` (open) — refactor-skill file-size detection; adjacent
  refactor-skill concern, distinct from comment placement (mutually linked).
- `SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9` — remove stale `REFACTOR-` markers when their work
  item closes (marker lifecycle; complements, does not overlap).
- `SA-0MVZA21600087VRD` — reap `REFACTOR-` marker blocks when the recorded
  smell is fixed (marker lifecycle; complements, does not overlap).
- `SA-0MWFW1ZDT006VYM4` (blocked) — implement: unified parser and
  `remove_refactor_marker()` (marker lifecycle; complements, does not overlap).
- `SA-0MWFW1YQ8007E2CZ` (open) — test: REFACTOR marker removal API (marker
  lifecycle; complements, does not overlap).
- `OSL-0MVVE7V84007DQD0` — the ContentCreator item that this defect created
  (fixed by deleting the marker and pinning the entrypoint contract).
- `OSL-0MVVF1OAO007HIXW` — the ContentCreator sweep of stale markers left in
  tests and scripts.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions were required: the work item description and the
  completed predecessor (SA-0MVPUVM8F006270F, whose scope notes explicitly
  deferred the encoding-cookie question) fully specify the gap, and the
  related-work search found no duplicate or overlapping open item. Recorded
  here for auditability.
  - Research: inspected `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` (shebang
    handled; coding line, docstring, and `newline=""` unhandled),
    `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` (shebang tests present;
    one assertion contradicts the new docstring AC and must be updated),
    `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` "REFACTOR Comments" section (placement rule
    absent), and ran `wl search` duplicate checks (no full duplicate; partial

# Port the post-checkout / post-merge / post-rewrite hooks to the repo-root v2 wrappers

**Headline:** The three committed Worklog hooks are `worklog:post-pull-hook:v1`
wrappers that `exec` an absolute per-machine path,
`$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`. When that path is absent (any
machine where `scripts/install_pi.sh` has not run), every checkout, merge and
`git worktree add` fails with `exec: … not found` (exit 127) and the post-pull
`wl sync` never runs — which broke `wl sync` in this repository on 2026-10-30
until `scripts/install_pi.sh` was re-run.

## Problem statement

`SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP` closed the "nothing creates the central script" half of
the problem by installing it from `install_pi.sh`. The remaining half is the
hard-coded absolute path itself: the hooks only work on a machine where the
installer ran, and a relocation or a fresh host silently disables the Worklog
sync. `ContentCreator` already migrated its hooks to `worklog:post-pull-hook:v2`
wrappers that resolve the delegate from the repository root
(`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`) and fail open; this repository still ships the
v1 form.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** — `implement.py start/finish` and `wl sync` abort
  with exit 127 whenever git creates a worktree or checks out a branch on a
  machine without the central hook.
- **Developers on a fresh clone or a renamed checkout** — merges error on a
  hook they did not write and cannot see.
- **Producers** — Worklog data silently stops syncing when the hook errors.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.githooks/post-checkout`, `.githooks/post-merge` and
      `.githooks/post-rewrite` carry the `worklog:post-pull-hook:v2` marker,
      resolve `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`,
      `cd` there, and `exec` it.
- [ ] All three wrappers are fail-open: no resolvable repository root, a missing
      delegate, or a missing `wl`/`worklog` exits 0 so a merge or checkout never
      fails because of the hook.
- [ ] `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` still short-circuits the sync (delegate
      behaviour unchanged).
- [ ] Tests prove the hooks work with `$HOME` unset or pointing at a sandbox and
      without any `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, from the
      repository root and from a subdirectory, for all three wrappers.
- [ ] A test scans `.githooks/` and fails if any file regains a hard-coded
      absolute checkout path (the `ContentCreator` equivalent lives in
      `tests/test_worklog_hooks.py`).
- [ ] `scripts/install_pi.sh` no longer warns that the wrappers do not delegate
      to the central path, and either stops installing the central script or
      documents it as legacy.
- [ ] `docs/dev/` hook documentation describes the v2 wrappers and the fail-open
      contract.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md` and the `docs/dev/` hook pages.

## Constraints

- Keep `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` as the single implementation of the
  post-pull sync; the wrappers stay thin.
- Do not change the pre-push hook or its gates.
- Removal of the central-script install from `install_pi.sh` is optional; if it
  stays, it must not be required for the hooks to work.

## Existing state

```
$ cat .githooks/post-checkout
#!/bin/sh
# worklog:post-pull-hook:v1
# Wrapper that delegates to central Worklog post-pull script (committed hooks).
exec "/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull" "$@"
```

Observed failure (2026-10-30, `wl sync` in this repository):

```
✗ Sync failed: Command failed with exit code 127: git worktree add --detach '…/.worklog/tmp-worktree-yZC0Kd/wt' 'refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data'
Preparing worktree (detached HEAD a07575c13)
/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.githooks/post-checkout: 4: exec: /home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull: not found
```

Running `scripts/install_pi.sh` created
`$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` and the sync then succeeded — a
workaround, not a fix.

## Desired change

Replace the three v1 wrappers with the v2 wrapper (see
`ContentCreator/.githooks/post-merge` for the canonical text), extend
`tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` (or a new hook test module) with the
`$HOME`-independent cases, and update `scripts/install_pi.sh` and the docs to
match.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.githooks/post-checkout` — v2 wrapper
- `.githooks/post-merge` — v2 wrapper
- `.githooks/post-rewrite` — v2 wrapper
- `tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` — hook behaviour without the central
  script; hard-coded-path scan
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — stop requiring the central script; drop the
  delegation warning
- `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` — v2 wrapper contract (the post-pull hook page;
  there is no `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md`)

## Plan: changelog

- `2026-11-14` (plan skill, SA-0MVVFAM0P002PZYI): pre-check returned
  `skip` (effort Small, risk Low) so no child decomposition was created; the
  item is sized for direct implementation.
- `2026-11-14` (plan skill): corrected the `Key Files` doc reference from
  `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` (does not exist) to `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md`,
  which is the post-pull hook page that already documents the portable
  wrappers and fail-open contract and must be updated to the v2 shape.
- `2026-11-14` (plan skill): noted that `SA-0MVK1Q30O0067NXX` already made the
  committed wrappers portable (repo → local → `$HOME` resolution with the
  `v1` marker); the remaining work is the v2 repo-root-only shape (per
  `ContentCreator/.githooks/post-merge`), so the "existing state" described
  above is historical context, not the current checkout.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` works when executed from the
  repository root; that is how `post-merge` already invokes it.
- **Risk (low):** a `post-checkout` run inside `.worklog/tmp-worktree-*` (the
  Worklog data branch) would sync from that temporary checkout. Mitigation: the
  delegate is already fail-open and warns on failure; verify it does not
  recurse when the temporary worktree has no `.worklog`.
- **Scope-creep risk:** consolidating the hooks with the ContentCreator copy
  into one shared installer is tempting. Record that separately; this item only
  ports the v2 wrapper shape.

## Related work

- `SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP` — installs the central post-pull script (the other half
  of the same failure mode).
- `SA-0MVK1Q30O0067NXX` — fail-open portability warning added to
  `install_pi.sh`.
- `OSL-0MVVE7V84007DQD0` (ContentCreator) — the item whose `wl sync` surfaced
  this failure.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP** – Chore: install central wl post-pull hook (~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull) missing (completed)
- **SA-0MVK1Q30O0067NXX** – Commit hooks exec a missing absolute path (/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull) → git worktree add and wl sync fail (completed)
- **SA-0MVK2PK7F002LET6** – SorraAgents committed git hooks exec a missing central script (~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: abort, absent, absolute, acceptance, add (+205 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: abort, absent, absolute, acceptance, add (+203 more)
