# Add near-duplicate test detection to find redundant test coverage

## Goal

As a maintainer of a large test suite, I want the test-value tooling to report
near-duplicate test blocks and files, so additive accumulation can be measured
and redundant coverage pruned with evidence instead of suspicion.

## Problem statement

The test-churn analysis measured large net test growth (+137,022 lines, +384
files on the reference project) against a **low** rewrite ratio (14.0%
modified-only), so the suite grows by *additive accumulation*, not churn. The
only existing redundancy check — `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`'s
"duplicate coverage" veto — matches test *names* containing `again|also covers|
duplicate|already covered` inside a single file. It cannot see a copy-pasted
test with renamed identifiers, nor the same behaviour re-tested through a
different import path, so redundancy accumulates with nothing forcing a
re-examination.

## Users

- **Producer / engineering manager** — wants the *size* of the redundancy, not
  just total growth, to decide whether pruning is worth runtime.
- **Implementer of the test-value refactor epic** (`SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO`) —
  needs block-level, line-range evidence for the Classify and Prove steps; the
  epic's AC3 forbids deleting a test on suspicion alone.
- **Agent working a prune pass** — needs a deterministic, read-only command
  whose JSON can be joined with churn and usefulness data.

Example user stories:

- As a producer, I want a ranked list of duplicate test clusters with redundant
  line counts so I can see how much of the growth is redundancy.
- As the refactor implementer, I want each cluster to name the file and line
  range of every member so a prune candidate can be proven, not guessed.
- As an agent, I want `expected-repetition` (parametrised/table-driven cases)
  excluded by the tool so I do not file bogus prune items.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — **Detection is structural, not textual.** Near-duplicate test blocks are detected within and across files using normalised representation: Python test blocks via `ast` (docstrings stripped, identifiers replaced by positional placeholders, literals canonicalised to type placeholders so a renamed copy still matches), JavaScript/TypeScript/other test files via comment-stripped token normalisation with brace-matched block boundaries. Raw text equality is never the similarity measure.
- [ ] AC2 — **Clusters are reported with location and score.** Each cluster lists every member's file path, start–end line range, block size (lines and tokens), member-to-member and cluster similarity score, and a redundancy measure (member lines minus the largest member's lines) used to order the report. Both `test_duplicates.json` (versioned schema: thresholds, method, limitations, clusters) and `test_duplicate_report.md` (human, same content, ordered by redundancy) are written to `--output-dir`.
- [ ] AC3 — **Conservatism and legitimate repetition.** Parametrised/table-driven repetition is classified `expected-repetition`, not redundancy: `pytest.mark.parametrize`, `unittest.subTest`, `test.each`/`it.each`, and blocks whose sweep is a data loop over case literals are detected and excluded. Similarity bands are explicit (`duplicate` ≥ threshold, default 0.85; `near-duplicate` between the lower band, default 0.65, and the threshold), every cluster carries a `report-only` verdict, and the tool never edits, deletes or renames anything.
- [ ] AC4 — **Performance is bounded and documented.** Defaults skip trivial blocks (`--min-lines`, default 10) and bound the candidate set; comparison uses an inverted shingle index plus optional MinHash banding rather than all-pairs O(n²). Scope options `--changed-only <base-ref>` (git diff), `--max-files N`, `--min-lines N`, `--threshold` and `--min-shared-tokens` are documented with the complexity they imply, and a measured runtime figure for a ~500-test-file suite is recorded in the docs and in the report preamble.
- [ ] AC5 — **Behaviour is pinned by tests.** Unit tests cover: normalisation invariance (a copy with renamed identifiers still scores ≥ threshold), distinct behaviour staying below the band, `expected-repetition` exclusion for parametrised and table-driven cases, threshold boundary behaviour, cluster ordering and redundant-line arithmetic, JSON and Markdown schema/content, an empty or single-block suite, a non-Python file set, and one end-to-end run over a fixture suite. Every test asserts one documented behaviour and no test re-implements the similarity algorithm under test.
- [ ] AC6 — **Documentation is updated.** `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` gains a "Near-duplicate detection" section wired into the existing pruning workflow (step 2 "inspect candidates" gains the command as the evidence source for the duplicate-coverage bullet); `docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md` records the method, thresholds, complexity/runtime bound, worked example and limitations; the `README.md` skill line mentions it; and the docs state that this analyser supersedes `evaluate_usefulness.py`'s name-marker heuristic for near-duplicates. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] AC7 — **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

A maintainer can see — ranked by redundant line count — exactly which test
blocks duplicate each other and prune them on recorded evidence, instead of
inferring redundancy from a raw growth number.

## Constraints

- **Read-only.** No automatic deletion, editing or renaming of test files; no
  writes outside `--output-dir`.
- **Conservative thresholds.** A false "duplicate" verdict is worse than a
  miss: uncertainty reports, never removes.
- **No hardcoded project paths.** Test/source classification and language
  handling follow the configurable, language-neutral approach already used by
  `ChurnConfig`; extend it rather than forking it.
- **Python standard library only.** The repository has zero third-party
  dependencies (`package.json` `dependencies: {}`, no `requirements.txt`); no
  tree-sitter/esprima/acorn dependency may be added.
- **No network, no per-block subprocess.** The analyser must not shell out to
  `node`, `pytest` or a language server; all parsing is in-process.
- **Deterministic output.** Same tree and flags ⇒ byte-identical JSON, so
  results are comparable over time (the churn analyser's existing property).

## Existing state

- `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py` (1,586 lines) — history-based
  churn: `ChurnConfig`, `is_test_file`, `classify_area`, `build_report`,
  `write_outputs`, CLI (`--project-root --branch --since --max-commits
  --output-dir --config --format --stdout --quiet`). It measures *how test code
  changes over time*; it contains no similarity analysis and never reads test
  bodies.
- `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py` (279 lines) — per-file verdicts.
  `_detect_duplicate` is a name-marker regex plus "imports production code";
  `VERDICT_REPORT` is always used for duplicate-only findings.
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` — anti-pattern 4 "duplicates of
  existing core coverage" (same behaviour via a different import path) is prose
  with no automated check; the churn skill's pruning workflow names it but
  offers only a manual grep.
- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::jaccard_similarity` — word-token Jaccard over
  *text* strings; precedent for the metric, unusable for code ASTs (no
  normalisation, no block boundaries).
- `skill/test-churn/tests/` — `conftest.py` loads the analyser by path
  (`test_churn_analysis_under_test`) so it is not collected as a test module;
  `.pi/test-config.json` has no `test-churn` group, so these tests currently run
  only under `full`.

## Desired change

A new read-only analyser `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_duplicate_detection.py`
with a CLI shaped like its churn sibling:

1. **Collect** test files using the existing classification (`is_test_file` +
   `ChurnConfig`), honouring `--changed-only <base-ref>` / `--max-files`.
2. **Extract blocks** with file + line range: Python via `ast` (top-level
   functions/classes/methods plus `with`-wrapped test bodies), JS/TS and other
   languages via comment-stripped tokenisation with brace/paren matching. Blocks
   smaller than `--min-lines` are skipped.
3. **Normalise** (docstrings and comments dropped, identifiers mapped to
   positional placeholders per scope, literals canonicalised by type, whitespace
   collapsed) so renamed copies remain identical while different behaviour does
   not.
4. **Fingerprint and compare**: token k-gram shingles (k default 5) → Jaccard
   similarity; candidates from an inverted shingle index (optionally MinHash
   banding) instead of all pairs; file-level rollup reports the strongest block
   pair per file pair.
5. **Classify** each pair as `duplicate`, `near-duplicate` or
   `expected-repetition` (parametrisation/data-loop detection), then cluster
   transitively and order clusters by redundant lines.
6. **Write** `test_duplicate_report.md` + `test_duplicates.json` with method,
   thresholds, limitations and measured runtime in the preamble; print a
   one-line summary to stderr.

The script is wired into the churn skill's pruning workflow and reference docs;
`evaluate_usefulness.py` keeps its heuristic unchanged (it answers a different,
per-file question) but its duplicate-coverage reason cross-references the new
tool.

## Key Files

- `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_duplicate_detection.py` — **new** analyser: block extraction, normalisation, shingling/Jaccard, clustering, JSON + Markdown writers, CLI.
- `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py` — reuse `ChurnConfig`/`is_test_file`/`classify_area`; factor any shared helpers rather than duplicating them (no behaviour change to existing metrics).
- `skill/test-churn/tests/test_test_duplicate_detection.py` — **new** unit + end-to-end suite for the analyser.
- `skill/test-churn/tests/conftest.py` — add a path-loaded fixture for the new module (same pattern as `churn`).
- `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` — new "Near-duplicate detection" section; pruning-workflow step 2 gains the command.
- `docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md` — method, thresholds, complexity/runtime bound, worked example, limitations.
- `README.md` — extend the test-churn bullet to name near-duplicate detection.
- `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py` — docstring/reason cross-reference to the new tool (no behaviour change).
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` — anti-pattern 4 gains the automated-evidence pointer.
- `.pi/test-config.json` — optional: add a `test-churn` group (`skill/test-churn/**`) so changed-scope runs execute these tests instead of falling through to `full`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **False-positive duplicates** (shared boilerplate, fixture setup, mechanical
  parameter sweeps) are the dominant risk and the reason for report-only
  verdicts: mitigation is the `expected-repetition` classifier, a conservative
  default threshold of 0.85 with a separate `near-duplicate` band, `--min-lines`
  skipping trivial blocks, and a documented limitations section.
- **Parser fragility outside Python** — brace matching on JS/TS is approximate;
  mitigation is conservative fallback (a block that cannot be delimited is
  reported as "unparsed" in the JSON summary rather than silently compared as a
  whole file), plus a non-Python fixture in the tests.
- **Performance on large suites** — shingle construction is linear in tokens,
  but candidate pairing can still blow up; mitigation is the inverted index,
  `--max-files`/`--changed-only` scope options and a measured runtime figure
  recorded in the docs.
- **Scope creep** — "also fix the duplicated tests" is explicitly out of scope:
  remediation belongs to the epic's prune/rework children. Any duplication the
  tool finds in this repository is reported as evidence in a comment or a
  follow-on item, not fixed here.
- **Assumption A1** — the detector belongs beside the churn analyser in
  `skill/test-churn/` rather than inside `evaluate_usefulness.py`, because it is
  suite-wide measurement, not a per-file verdict, and the churn skill is where
  the pruning workflow lives.
- **Assumption A2** — no new third-party parser dependency (stdlib only), so
  JS/TS detection is token-based rather than AST-based; Python gets exact AST
  normalisation.
- **Assumption A3** — the item stays `discovered-from:SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O`
  rather than being re-parented under `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO`; the epic's
  Classify/Prove children consume its output, and re-parenting a
  `plan_complete` epic would change that epic's scope.
- **Assumption A4** — a `test-churn` test group does not exist in
  `.pi/test-config.json` today; adding one is a small, separable improvement
  that keeps these tests out of the `full`-only path (optional within this
  item).

## Related work

As a producer, I want per-test runtime and flake history so I can express test value as fault detection per second of suite runtime and bound the cost of periodic mutation campaigns.

## Problem statement

Test value is currently measured without its cost. The test runner reports suite-level timing, but there is no per-test timing or flake history, so a valuable-but-slow test and a worthless-but-slow test are indistinguishable, and mutation-campaign runtime cannot be allocated sensibly. The test-value epic (`SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO`, AC7) also needs before/after runtime evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The test runner records per-test duration and a bounded flake history across runs.
- [ ] Emits a machine-readable report consumable by the test-value aggregator (churn/mutation/runtime join).
- [ ] Overhead is bounded and documented; normal runs stay within the existing runtime budget.
- [ ] Flake detection is deterministic for repeated failures and does not hide genuine failures.
- [ ] Integrated into the existing `skill/test` runner rather than a new measurement skill.
- [ ] Covered by tests; all related documentation updated; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Must not change the pass/fail semantics of the test runner.
- History storage is bounded (retention policy documented).
- Follows the test-execution policy: agents still invoke tests only via the test skill; infrastructure gates are out of scope.

# Intake Brief: Repeat producer actions in red on the final report conclusion

## Problem statement

The canonical end-of-session report (`skill/report`) lists blocking producer
actions in `## Producer Actions`, but the `## Conclusion` — the last thing the
operator reads — does not repeat them. When a session ends with something the
producer must do (answer a question, make a decision, grant an approval), the
operator can miss it in the body of a long report. Repeating any genuine
producer action in the Conclusion in red makes the blocking call-to-action
impossible to overlook.

## Users

- **Producer/operator** reading end-of-session reports in the pi TUI: wants the
  blocking action to stand out at the end of the report, not be buried mid-page.
- **Agent (intake/plan/implement/audit/…) authoring the report**: keeps passing
  blocking actions via `--producer-actions`; the renderer handles the red
  repetition deterministically (no per-skill change).

Example user stories:

- "As a producer, when a skill session needs a decision from me, I want that
  decision repeated in red in the conclusion so I cannot miss it."
- "As a producer, when nothing is required of me, I do not want a red warning in
  the conclusion."
- "As an agent, I want the renderer to do this automatically so every skill
  behaves the same way."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the normalised producer actions are a genuine, non-`None needed`
   action, `render_report()` appends the action text **verbatim** to the
   `## Conclusion` section, wrapped in ANSI SGR red (`\x1b[31m…\x1b[0m`) with a
   `⚠️ Producer action required:` lead-in. Verified by unit test asserting the
   escape sequences and the exact action text inside `## Conclusion`.
2. When no producer actions are supplied, or the supplied text is routine
   workflow progression that normalises to `None needed`, the Conclusion
   contains no ANSI escape sequences and no repeated action text. Verified by
   unit tests (absent actions; `Proceed to /skill:plan`; `Review the brief, then
   run /skill:plan`).
3. Colour can be disabled with a new `--no-colour` CLI flag **or** the standard
   `NO_COLOR` environment variable (non-empty). In that mode the Conclusion
   still repeats the action in plain text with the `⚠️` marker and contains no
   ANSI escape sequences. Verified by unit tests for both opt-outs.
4. Multi-line / multi-action producer text is repeated verbatim (line breaks
   preserved) and the rest of the report is unchanged: section order,
   `## Producer Actions` → `## Notes` → `## Conclusion`, the existing
   completed/incomplete conclusion sentences, and the `</end_session>`
   terminator. Verified by regression tests.
5. `skill/report/SKILL.md` documents the conditional red repetition in the
   canonical template, the layout rules, and the colour opt-out
   (`--no-colour` / `NO_COLOR`) alongside the existing icon opt-out. Verified
   by document review.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Implement in the shared renderer only (`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`)
  plus a small shared colour helper — do not fork report logic into the ~17
  calling skills.
- Repeat **after** routine-next-step normalisation (SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW): a
  routine next step must never produce red text.
- Do not use TTY detection to decide colour: the CLI's stdout is captured/piped
  by agents before being pasted into the final response, so TTY detection would
  disable the feature exactly where it is needed. Opt-out must be explicit
  (`--no-colour` / `NO_COLOR`).
- Colour is decorative: the `⚠️` marker and the plain action text must carry the
  meaning when colour is unavailable, so the report stays readable in
  non-ANSI consumers (GitHub, plain-text logs).
- No new runtime dependency; pure-Python, offline-testable.
- Do not change `## Producer Actions` semantics, the pane-status derivation, or
  the existing conclusion wording.

## Existing state

- `render_report()` renders `## Producer Actions` from the normalised
  `producer_actions` string (`None needed` when absent), then `## Notes`, then
  `## Conclusion`.
- The Conclusion currently emits one of two fixed sentences based on AC
  verdicts (`_derive_session_status`): completed → "This completes … Ready for
  `<next_action>`."; incomplete → "… is incomplete. Requires attention
  (`<next_action>`)." Nothing else is appended.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` already provides `icons_enabled(no_icons, env)`
  honouring `--no-icons` / `WL_NO_ICONS=1` — the convention to mirror for
  colour, but colour must be a separate switch (`WL_NO_ICONS` must not disable
  colour).
- No ANSI/colour handling exists anywhere in the report renderer today (the
  only ANSI in the repo is in `tests/integration/test-worktree-workflow.sh`).

## Desired change

- Add `colour_enabled(no_colour=False, env=None)` (and `RED`/`RESET` constants)
  to `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`: enabled by default; disabled by
  `--no-colour` or a non-empty `NO_COLOR`.
- In `render_report()`, after the existing conclusion sentence(s), when the
  normalised producer actions are not `None needed`, append a blank line and a
  red line: `⚠️ Producer action required: <verbatim action text>`. Apply
  `RED … RESET` only when colour is enabled.
- Thread an optional `no_colour: bool = False` parameter through
  `render_report()`, `render_report_from_workitem()`, `render_from_wl()` and the
  CLI, adding the `--no-colour` flag.
- Update `skill/report/SKILL.md` (template, layout rules, example, colour
  opt-out) and the `README.md` report-helper bullet to mention the red
  repetition.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — conditional red repetition in the
  Conclusion; `no_colour` plumbing and `--no-colour` flag.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` — `colour_enabled()` helper + `RED`/`RESET`
  constants mirroring `icons_enabled()`.
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` — new tests: red repetition,
  no-repetition for absent/routine actions, `--no-colour`/`NO_COLOR` fallback,
  multi-line preservation, structure regression.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_herdr_pane.py` — `colour_enabled()` unit tests.
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` — template/layout/example + colour opt-out docs.
- `README.md` — report-helper bullet: note the red repetition of blocking
  producer actions in the Conclusion.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW** — "Don't include producer actions that are next steps"
  (completed): established normalisation to `None needed`; the red repetition
  must run after it.
- **SA-0MULPQ3BK001A1M5** — "Misleading completion message on LLM summaries"
  (completed): made the Conclusion reflect session status; this item extends the
  same section.
- **SA-0MTFLQEQQ0083EW1** — "Update pane title with status emoticon on skill
  completion" (completed): established the ✅/⚠️/🚫 status colour semantics this
  feature reuses for a red call-to-action.
- **SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S** — "Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting
  via helper report skill" (completed): origin of the canonical report contract.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "red font" means ANSI SGR red in terminal output.** The report
  is rendered to stdout and pasted into the pi TUI; ANSI is the only mechanism
  that reliably colours that path. If the producer expects Markdown/HTML
  colouring, the brief should be revised before implementation (documented in
  the Appendix).
- **Assumption — red repeats blocking actions only.** Because routine workflow
  progression is normalised to `None needed` first, it can never trigger red;
  this avoids the false "producer is blocking" signal fixed by
  SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW.
- **Assumption — no TTY detection.** Explicit opt-out only, because agent-captured
  stdout is not a TTY.
- **Risk — ANSI leakage into non-terminal consumers** (GitHub, PRs, plain logs).
  Mitigation: `--no-colour`/`NO_COLOR`, plus the `⚠️` marker and plain text so the
  meaning survives even if escapes are stripped or shown literally.
- **Risk — colour-blindness / theme contrast.** Mitigation: the `⚠️` marker and
  the words "Producer action required" carry the signal; colour is decorative.
- **Risk — multi-line producer text.** Mitigation: wrap the whole block once and
  test line-break preservation rather than prefixing each line.
- **Scope creep.** Adjacent ideas (colouring the `## Producer Actions` section,
  colourising AC verdicts, HTML-export colour) are out of scope — record as
  separate work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What does 'red font' mean for a Markdown report rendered by the LLM/TUI —
  ANSI escape codes, HTML `<span style=\"color:red\">`, or plain emphasis?"
  — **Answer (repo research + design analysis):** ANSI SGR red. The report is
  printed to stdout and pasted into the terminal-rendered TUI; raw ANSI passes
  through and colours the terminal, whereas inline HTML styles are not honoured
  by the Markdown→terminal path and GitHub strips `style` attributes. Recorded
  as an assumption; the producer can request an HTML/bold variant at review.
  No interactive round was required for the rest of the brief.
- Q: "Should routine next-step actions (e.g. 'Proceed to /skill:plan') also be
  repeated in red?" — **Answer (SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW contract):** No. Routine
  workflow progression is normalised to `None needed` and must never be shown as
  a blocking red action; only genuine, current-stage actions are repeated.
- Q: "Should colour be auto-detected (TTY) or explicitly opt-out?" — **Answer
  (design analysis):** Explicit opt-out only. Agent-captured stdout is not a
  TTY, so TTY detection would silently disable the feature on the exact path
  that needs it. `--no-colour` and `NO_COLOR` are the opt-outs.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVQ1QM9L0083KAW** – Producer Actions contract: docs and skill templates (completed)
- **SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW** – Don't include producer actions that are next steps (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: action, actions, conclusion, final, llm, producer, red, repeat, them, there
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — matched: action, actions, final, llm, output, producer, red, repeat, them, there
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: action, actions, final, llm, output, producer, red, repeat, them, there

# Driven child sessions do not hold the per-child lock, so the herdr hydrator demotes them mid-implementation

discovered-from:SA-0MVTE927L0017ND5

## Problem statement

A driven child session is pane-less by construction, so the herdr hydrator's
"busy = pane OR live claim holder" rule is the *only* thing keeping its
`in-progress` claim alive — but the per-child `flock` is acquired and released
inside the short-lived `implement.py start` subprocess, so no live `flock`
exists while the driven session actually works. The hydrator therefore sees a
pane-less item with a dead claim holder and demotes it to `open` mid-session,
which both makes the worklog lie and re-opens the item for a second, duplicate
dispatch onto the same worktree.

## Users

- **Producer / operator watching the herdr UI.** Story: *As a producer, I want
  a driven child that is genuinely being implemented to stay `in-progress` in
  the worklog and the herdr UI, so I can trust the board and do not have to
  re-dispatch or rescue an item the hydrator demoted under a working agent.*
- **Driven child session (the implementing agent).** Story: *As a driven child
  session, I want to hold my own per-child lock for my whole lifetime, so the
  hydrator never demotes me mid-work and no second session is handed my
  worktree.*
- **Drive orchestrator (`implement.py drive`).** Story: *As the drive
  orchestrator, I want to own the child's lock for the duration of the spawned
  session and pass the ownership token to that session, so the documented
  "one child = one holder" contract is true for driven (pane-less) children
  too.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- 1. **Lock is held for the session's whole lifetime.** While a driven child
  session is alive — from the driver's spawn until the session exits —
  `<worklog>/locks/child-<id>.lock` is held by a live kernel `flock` and the
  lock file's recorded `pid` names a live process. The herdr hydrator's
  existing live-claim-holder rule (`WL-0MVWDB3IG004NRIU`, already implemented
  in ContextHub) therefore sees the item as busy and never demotes it to
  `open`.
- 2. **The spawned session receives the ownership token and re-enters.** The
  driven session receives `IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_TOKEN` matching the lock
  file's token, and its own `implement.py start` / `finish` re-enter the lock
  as a token-based re-entrant no-op instead of being refused as
  `skipped-held`. Ownership stays token-based — never inferred from pid
  equality.
- 3. **Release is bounded to the session.** The lock is released when the
  spawned session exits — on success, non-zero exit and timeout — so no stale
  `flock` survives the session, and the next `parent` / `start` acquires the
  lock cleanly (or reclaims a genuinely dead holder with the existing
  warning + report fields).
- 4. **A different live owner is still refused.** If the lock is already held
  by a *different* live owner when the driver tries to hold it for the
  session, the driver reports `skipped-held` (with `held_by`, `held_children`)
  and spawns no session — the existing duplicate-dispatch protection is not
  weakened.
- 5. **Regression test with a fake spawner.** A test drives `phase_drive`
  with an injectable fake spawner and asserts, from inside the spawner, that
  the lock is held (kernel `flock` live, recorded `pid` live, token present
  in the child environment) for the session's lifetime and released once the
  spawner returns; the existing per-child-lock suites
  (`test_phase_start_child_lock.py`, `test_drive_child_lock.py`,
  `test_drive_child_session.py`) stay green.
- 6. **Documentation updated.** `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and
  `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` describe the driven-session
  lock-holder behaviour accurately (who holds the lock, for how long, how the
  token reaches the session, and the failure/timeout release paths).
- 7. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes (enforced by the
  dev-push gate).

## Impact

A driven child that is actively being implemented now stays `in-progress` in
the worklog and the herdr UI instead of being silently demoted to `open` four
minutes into its session, so producers can trust the board and no second agent
is dispatched onto the same worktree.

## Constraints

- **Ownership must stay token-based.** `_probe_child_lock` and
  `WorkItemLock` already treat a matching `IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_TOKEN` as a
  re-entrant no-op; the fix must not add a pid-equality ownership heuristic.
- **The recorded `pid` must name a live process.** The hydrator trusts the
  recorded pid only when it is alive and not a reused pid; a lock file whose
  pid is the dead `start` subprocess is exactly the observed bug.
- **The lock must live in `<worklog>/locks/`**, never inside the worktree
  (the worktree can be removed mid-flight).
- **No change to the hydrator.** The ContextHub side is already fixed
  (`WL-0MVWDB3IG004NRIU` / `WL-0MVWDAZL10025P8J`); this item is the producer
  side of that contract.
- **Existing lock semantics preserved:** fail-closed on ambiguous state,
  stale-dead-pid reclamation with a warning, `skipped-held` classification,
  the `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE` recursion guard, and the worktree placement
  guard.
- **Out of scope:** changing the hydrator, changing `--assignee` scheduling
  semantics, or adding a heartbeat/TTL protocol.

## Existing state

- `phase_start` acquires the per-child lock (`_new_child_lock` →
  `WorkItemLock.acquire()`), holds it for the start critical section, and
  releases it in a `finally` (`implement.py:9983`, `implement.py:10062`).
- `phase_drive` runs `parent` (which runs `start` as a subprocess), then
  spawns a fresh Pi session for `next_child` via `_default_session_spawner`
  or `_pane_session_spawner` (`implement.py:15421`, spawn at
  `implement.py:16188`).
- `_child_session_env` propagates `IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_TOKEN` **only when the
  current process already holds a lock or inherits the env token**
  (`implement.py:13081`, `_child_lock_token` at `implement.py:1298`). The
  driver holds no lock while it waits for the session, so the spawned session
  gets no token.
- Measured during the incident: `.worklog/locks/child-<id>.lock` recorded a
  dead pid (the exited `start` subprocess) and `fuser` showed no holders,
  while the driven session was alive and had already written its red test.
- The documented contract already claims the token is exported "to the driven
  child session" and the lock is "held for the holder's lifetime"
  (`skill/implement/SKILL.md:1078-1102`,
  `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md:2290-2306`); the drive path does not
  meet it.

## Desired change

Make the driven session's per-child lock live for the session's whole
lifetime. **Recommended approach (A):** the long-lived driver (`phase_drive`)
acquires the child's `WorkItemLock` immediately before spawning the session,
keeps it held while the spawner waits for the session, and releases it in a
`finally` after the session exits; it propagates the lock's token to the
spawned session (and to the `parent`/`start`/`finish` subprocesses it invokes)
so they re-enter rather than block. The lock file's recorded pid is then the
live driver pid.

Alternative considered **(B):** have the driven session itself hold the
`flock` for its lifetime. Rejected as the default because the session's
`start`/`finish` are short-lived subprocesses and the Pi agent process does
not hold file descriptors for a lock; option B would need a dedicated
long-lived lock-holder process in the session (more moving parts than
option A). The item's stated direction permits either, and the chosen
approach must still satisfy all ACs above.

Either way: the lock-file `pid` must name a live process, and
`_probe_child_lock` must stay token-based.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive` (acquire/hold/release
  the child lock around the spawn), `_child_session_env` (propagate the held
  lock's token explicitly), `_child_lock_token` / `_new_child_lock` (token
  plumbing), possibly a small helper to hold the lock across the spawn.
- `skill/shared/work_item_lock.py` — only if a re-entrancy or explicit-token
  seam is needed; the primitive itself should stay unchanged.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_child_lock.py` — extend the
  drive-side lock coverage; keep existing re-entrancy tests green.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py` — fake-spawner test for
  the session-lifetime hold (AC5).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_lock.py` — ensure the real
  subprocess two-holder race still passes.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` —
  document the driven-session lock holder.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVTE927L0017ND5` — *implement.py finish deletes a plain leaf session's
  cwd…* (the `discovered-from` parent of this item).
- `SA-0MVOABYW00004978` — *Prevent duplicate drive child sessions (exclusive
  per-child lock)* (introduced the lock).
- `SA-0MVQ5AXLF002PAQ3` — *Implement: acquire lock in phase_start +
  skipped-held* (wired the lock into `phase_start`).
- `SA-0MVQ7VMRL00498YB` — the per-child lock reference section
  (`docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`).
- ContextHub `WL-0MVW9UQQ6004KSXY` — *hydrator demotes in-progress claims of
  pane-less driven sessions* (parent bug); children `WL-0MVWDAZL10025P8J`
  (claim-holder probe), `WL-0MVWDB3IG004NRIU` (busy = pane OR live claim
  holder), `WL-0MVWDB7F2003SORI` (release clears the scheduling hold) — all
  done; they assume the producer-side lock is actually held.
- `SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9` — the "actively worked ⇒ in_progress" invariant.
- `SA-0MVL7YG2S009L6PU` — *wl sync: file-lock age-expiry steals a live
  holder's lock* (a different lock — the ContextHub `wl sync` file lock — but
  the same "a live holder must never be treated as dead" principle).

## Risks

- **Driver death while the session lives (option A).** If the driver is killed
  while a spawned session is still working, the kernel releases the driver's
  `flock` and the hydrator may demote the item even though the session is
  alive. Mitigation: the driver is normally the long-lived process that waits
  for the session; document the residual window. Option B (session-held lock)
  would close it but needs a dedicated lock-holder process.
- **Stale token reuse across children.** A driver that holds child A's token
  and then acquires child B's lock must generate a fresh token for B, not
  inherit A's, or `_probe_child_lock` could misclassify B as self-owned.
  Mitigation: acquire each child's lock with a fresh token and clear/replace
  the env token between iterations.
- **Double-acquire ordering.** `phase_drive` runs `parent` (which runs
  `start`, acquiring and releasing the lock) before spawning the session; the
  driver's own acquire must not collide with a still-held `start` lock.
  Mitigation: acquire only after `parent` returns `next_child` and the
  worktree exists; treat a failed acquire as `skipped-held`.
- **Scope creep.** Adjacent improvements (closing the `start`→driver acquire
  race, hydrator changes, heartbeat) are recorded as separate work items, not
  folded into this fix.

## Assumptions

- **A1:** The recommended fix is option A (the driver holds the lock for the
  spawned session's lifetime and propagates the token). This is a design
  choice; the item permits either option, and the implementer may switch to
  option B if planning finds a concrete blocker, provided all ACs still hold.
- **A2:** The hydrator side is already fixed in ContextHub, so no ContextHub
  change is needed in this item; the AC1 hydrator outcome is a consequence of
  the producer-side lock being held and is covered by ContextHub's existing
  tests.
- **A3:** The driver releases the lock after the spawner returns, before the
  next `parent` iteration, so `parent`/`start`/`finish` acquire a free lock
  (or re-enter by token if invoked while the driver holds it).
- **A4:** The small race between `parent`'s `start` releasing the lock and the
  driver acquiring it for the session is accepted (the worktree already
  exists, so a slipped-in second driver resumes rather than duplicates it);
  closing it entirely is out of scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required. The seed context (observed incident,
root cause with evidence, impact, desired fix direction and proposed ACs) was
sufficient to draft this brief; the only design ambiguity — driver-held versus
session-held lock — is recorded as Assumption A1 with a recommendation, not a
blocking question.

# ship: CHANGELOG release section is discarded by the dev→main merge conflict resolution

**Origin:** observed in the `1916: The Rising` v0.1.23 release (RISE-0MVXXKJGK004WO6L). The Discord release notification went out with no release focus and no changelog body, and `main`'s `CHANGELOG.md` had no `## v0.1.23` section.

## Root cause

In `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` the CHANGELOG is generated **before** `origin/dev` is merged:

1. `generate-changelog.js "$NEW_VERSION"` writes `## v0.1.23 (…)` (with the `> **Release focus:** …` marker) and commits it on the release branch, which is based on `main`.
2. `git merge --no-ff origin/dev` then conflicts on `CHANGELOG.md`, because `dev` carries its own `## Unreleased` block.
3. The auto-resolution runs `git checkout --theirs CHANGELOG.md` — taking dev's whole file and **discarding the generated release section**.
4. The merged tree is tagged, so the released tree carries no `## v<version>` section.

The comment above the resolution (lines 217-219) even claims "generate-changelog.js rewrites it for the new version **afterwards**", contradicting the actual order.

Downstream effects:
- `discord-notify.js` `extractChangelogSection()` returns `null` and `extractReleaseFocus()` finds no marker, so the embed loses both the focus and the release notes (silently — only a focus warning is logged).
- Release notes are absent from `main`/`dev` for that version (recoverable only from the discarded commit).

## Proposed fix

1. Preserve the generated section across the merge: when `CHANGELOG.md` conflicts, take dev's version and then **re-insert** the generated `## v<version>` section (a small, tested helper), instead of discarding it.
2. Assert after the merge that a generated section is still present; abort the release (before tagging) if it was lost. A *failed generation* keeps today's non-fatal behaviour (warn and continue) — this only guards the regression where a successfully generated section is dropped.
3. `discord-notify.js`: log an explicit warning naming the version when no `## v<version>` section is found (still non-blocking).
4. Document the guarantee in `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`.

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/changelog-merge.js` (new helper)
- `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js`
- `skill/ship/tests/test_changelog_merge.mjs` (new)
- `skill/ship/tests/test_discord_notify.mjs`
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`

## Acceptance criteria

1. With dev's `CHANGELOG.md` modified (an `## Unreleased` block present), the merge-resolution path yields a file that contains the generated `## v<version>` section with its `> **Release focus:**` marker **and** keeps dev's content — asserted by a node test over the new merge helper using a dev-style file.
2. When a section was generated but is missing after the merge, the release script aborts before tagging with an actionable message (non-zero exit) — asserted by a test of the resolution helper's "section lost" outcome plus the script-level guard.
3. A failed generation keeps the non-fatal contract: the release continues with an explicit warning, and the guard does not fire for a section that was never generated — asserted by a test.
4. `discord-notify.js` emits an explicit warning naming the version when the `## v<version>` section is absent, and still sends the notification (non-blocking) — unit test with an injected fetch.
5. The Discord embed still carries both the release focus and the changelog body when a generated section is present — unit test on the composition path.
6. `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` documents the ordering/preservation guarantee and the abort-on-loss behaviour.

## Impact

Every release now keeps its generated `## v<version>` changelog section — including the release focus marker — through the dev→main merge, so released trees and Discord notifications always carry the release notes instead of shipping with no `## v<version>` heading, no focus and no changelog body; a release also aborts before tagging rather than silently shipping without its release notes.

## Problem statement

Tests exercising `implement.py`'s main-checkout lock-wait path inherit the ambient
`IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` / `IMPLEMENT_START_LOCK_TIMEOUT` environment variables
and hang for hours instead of refusing immediately (the default `0` = fail-fast).

### Reproduction (verified 2026-11-08 on `dev`)

```
IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT=25 python3 -m pytest \
  skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py::test_finish_refuses_when_lock_held_by_other_finish
# 1 passed in 25.18s   ← the whole ambient timeout is slept, then it refuses
```

The same test normally completes in ~0.05 s. With
`IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT=10800` (the value an agent exports to wait out a
concurrent `finish`) the single test blocks for three hours.

### Mechanism

`test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py::test_finish_refuses_when_lock_held_by_other_finish`
takes the real main-checkout `flock` itself, then calls `phase_finish`, which calls
`_finish_lock_timeout()` → `_resolve_lock_timeout(ENV_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT, 0.0)` →
`os.environ.get(...)`. `RepoLock.acquire` then honours that ambient value and retries
in `time.sleep(RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS)` steps until the deadline — but the lock it is
waiting for is held by the test's own fd, released only in the test's `finally` block.
The test therefore cannot succeed early: it burns the inherited timeout in full.

## Users

- **Agent sessions** running `implement.py finish` that export a high lock timeout to
  wait for a real concurrent finish. A child test suite then hangs for hours on a
  lock-refusal test, masking the real result.
- **CI jobs** and any automated runner that sets these env vars for real `finish` calls.

## Audit findings (2026-11-08)

Completed as part of planning so implementation does not repeat it:

- `skill/implement/tests/` contains **no** test that names either lock-timeout
  variable, so no test sets one deliberately as a test input (confirms the
  "Assumption" below).
- Only two lock-wait timeouts are read from the environment by `implement.py`:
  `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (`_finish_lock_timeout()`) and
  `IMPLEMENT_START_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (`_start_lock_timeout()`), both through
  `_resolve_lock_timeout()`. These are the complete neutralisation set.
- `test_phase_start_child_lock.py` and `test_drive_child_lock.py` exercise child
  locks (`IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_DIR`, already isolated by
  `isolated_implement_child_lock_store`) and patch `_sync_parent_branch`; they do
  not contend the main-checkout lock, so they do not sleep on the ambient value.
- `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_CHILD_TIMEOUT` is a per-child *session* timeout, not a lock wait,
  and no test reads it — out of scope.
- `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` is the test-slot pool bound owned by
  `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, not `implement.py`; the implement tests stub
  `run_gate_suite`, so it is unreachable from `skill/implement/tests/` and out of
  scope given the "changes stay within `skill/implement/tests/`" constraint.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `pytest skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py` passes in under 5 seconds with `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT=10800` and `IMPLEMENT_START_LOCK_TIMEOUT=600` exported.
- An autouse fixture in `skill/implement/tests/conftest.py` neutralises `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` and `IMPLEMENT_START_LOCK_TIMEOUT` for every test in the package, mirroring the existing `_no_ambient_git_index_file` fixture pattern; a test asserts the fixture's effect (both variables absent, or `"0"`, while it is active).
- The regression test `test_finish_refuses_when_lock_held_by_other_finish` completes without sleeping — asserted via elapsed time < 5 seconds (or equivalent clock-patch assertion) with the ambient variables exported.
- The audit above is reflected in the change: no other test in `skill/implement/tests/` reaches `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` / `IMPLEMENT_START_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, and this is stated in a code comment so it need not be re-derived.
- `pytest skill/implement/tests/` passes, and the full project test suite passes with the changes.

## Impact

Agents and CI jobs that export lock-wait timeouts for their own `finish` calls no
longer poison test suites with multi-hour hangs on lock-refusal tests.

## Constraints

- The fix must be additive — no behavioural change to production code.
- Follow the existing `conftest.py` autouse-fixture pattern for environment
  neutralisation.
- Changes stay within `skill/implement/tests/`.

## Existing state

- `_resolve_lock_timeout()` (line ~2908 of `implement.py`) reads from `os.environ` with
  no neutralisation.
- `conftest.py` already neutralises `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and `IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_DIR` via
  autouse fixtures.
- `test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py` calls `phase_finish` which calls
  `_finish_lock_timeout()` — inheriting the ambient value.
- `_sync_parent_branch_locked()` calls `_start_lock_timeout()` → the same inheritance.

## Desired change

Add an autouse fixture (or extend the existing environment-neutralising group) in
`skill/implement/tests/conftest.py` that `monkeypatch.delenv()`s
`IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` and `IMPLEMENT_START_LOCK_TIMEOUT` for every test,
documented with the mechanism above so the reason survives. Add the elapsed-time
assertion to the refusal regression test.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/tests/conftest.py` — add neutralising fixture
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — source of `_finish_lock_timeout()` / `_start_lock_timeout()` / `_resolve_lock_timeout()`
- `skill/shared/repo_lock.py` — `RepoLock.acquire` retry loop that sleeps out the inherited timeout
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py` — affected test
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_lock.py` — audited: child lock only, unaffected
- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_child_lock.py` — audited: child lock only, unaffected

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption**: no test intentionally sets these timeout variables as test inputs.
  The variables represent caller policy, never test inputs, so neutralisation is safe.
  (Where a test *does* need a specific value, it sets it explicitly within the test
  body, after the fixture has run.) Verified by the audit above.
- **Scope-creep risk**: `test_drive_child_lock.py` and other integration tests that
  spawn subprocesses inherit the fixture's env-hermeticity. If a subprocess *must*
  read the ambient timeout, the test should re-export it explicitly after the fixture
  runs. The audit found no such case.
- **Existing pattern**: the `_no_ambient_git_index_file` autouse fixture already
  neutralises an ambient var via `monkeypatch.delenv`. The new fixture follows the
  same pattern.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVY0G5EH000LIMB` — this item
- `SA-0MUV2UBMT008OE2E` — Test infra concurrency issue (related category)
- `SA-0MPGTWHQF005HO05` — Process cleanup (related infrastructure)

## Goal

`_git_commit_evidence` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` resolves a
stranded child's pushed-commit evidence with
`git log <ref> --grep <child_id> -n 1`. `--grep` matches the **whole commit
message including the body**, so a commit that merely *mentions* a work-item id
counts as that item's work.

Observed 2026-11-01 during the epic drive for SA-0MVX1M6HH004YPX2: driven child
SA-0MVX359B7008R9F3 timed out after 3600 s with its own commit (`9119e4117`)
still unpushed in its worktree, and `drive` reported it as *stranded* with
evidence `0fb0e4305` — the **sibling** child's (SA-0MVX31GLC002IPR8) commit,
whose body names SA-0MVX359B7008R9F3 as the future home of the detection
module. The verdict told the operator to `--finalise-stranded` a child whose
work had never been pushed.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Commit evidence matches only commits whose **subject** references the
   work-item id, never a body-only mention.
2. A regression test pins the false-positive: a commit whose body mentions
   another item's id is not evidence for that item.
3. A driven child whose commit is still only in its own worktree is reported
   as non-terminal-with-work, not as stranded on the parent branch.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_git_commit_evidence`
- `skill/implement/tests/` — regression test

# audit skill: AC extraction rejects qualified `Acceptance Criteria` headings

**Symptom (observed auditing RISE-0MVXXKJGK004WO6L, 2026-11-01):** `audit_runner.py issue` returned `Ready to close: No` with `No acceptance criteria defined.` and **0 model calls**, then demoted the item to `open`/`plan_complete` — even though the item's description carries three numbered acceptance criteria under the heading `## Acceptance criteria for this project`.

## Root cause

`_extract_acs()` in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` matches the AC heading with an anchored regex:

```
^(?:Acceptance|Success)\s+Criteria:?\s*(?:\([^)]*\))?\s*$
```

The match is applied to the line **after** `_normalize_heading_line()` strips markdown heading markers — but a trailing qualifier such as `for this project` is not allowed (only an optional colon or parenthetical is), so the heading never matches and the function returns the `["No acceptance criteria defined."]` sentinel. The pipeline then treats that sentinel as the AC body (a `warning` verdict), skips Phase 2, and produces a `No` verdict which demotes the item.

## Consequences

- A valid, auditable item audits as if it has no ACs: Phase 1 and Phase 2 screening are skipped (0 pi calls), and the item is demoted to `open`/`plan_complete` on the normal `No` path.
- The failure is silent to the model — no prompt ever sees the AC list, so no evidence names the extraction failure.

## Reproduction

`audit_runner.py issue` against an item whose description AC-section heading carries a trailing qualifier, e.g. `## Acceptance criteria for this project` (RISE-0MVXXKJGK004WO6L exhibited this; its three criteria were manually verified satisfied, and the heading had to be normalised to `## Acceptance Criteria` before the audit would screen them).

## Suggested fix

Relax the heading pattern to accept trailing free text while keeping canonical headings byte-compatible: e.g. match `Acceptance Criteria` / `Success Criteria` optionally followed by `:`, a parenthetical, a trailing qualifier (`for …`), or end-of-line. Add regression tests covering heading variants: canonical, lowercase `c`, colon, parenthetical, and a trailing-qualifier heading.

### Reuse note (plan review)

The shared extractor `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria` already matches AC headings on a **prefix** basis (`^#+\s+Acceptance\s+Criteria`, case-insensitive), so it already accepts a trailing qualifier. Do not build a second, divergent matcher: keep the relaxed audit pattern semantically aligned with that prefix match so the audit pipeline and the plan/tree-coverage pipeline agree on what is an AC section.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `_extract_acs()` (or the heading matcher it uses) recognises AC headings with a trailing qualifier (e.g. `## Acceptance criteria for this project`), extracting the numbered/bulleted items below them.
2. Canonical headings (`## Acceptance Criteria`, `## Acceptance criteria`, `## Success Criteria`, optional colon/parenthetical) behave unchanged — no regression.
3. A unit test covers the exact qualifier variant from the RISE-0MVXXKJGK004WO6L reproduction.

## Impact

Items whose AC heading carries a short qualifier now get genuinely screened by the audit instead of silently auditing as having no acceptance criteria and being demoted back to planning.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (`_extract_acs`, `_normalize_heading_line`)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` (`TestExtractAcs` — regression tests required by AC 3)
- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` (`extract_acceptance_criteria` — reference semantics to align with, see Reuse note)

# Reduce implement skill cold-start context (regressed ~5× since F5 trim)

## Problem statement

The implement skill starts with a very large context. Measured across real
sessions, a **cold** `/skill:implement` turn is ~24–25k tokens at the 50th
percentile — dominated (~78%) by the skill's own `SKILL.md` body, which is
inlined verbatim into the user message on every invocation. This sits right at
the edge of local acceptance: the near-miss population clusters just above the
38,000 cold threshold (38,298–38,752), and resumed/hydrated sessions blow past
it entirely (216k–452k). Every additional byte of `SKILL.md` inflates *every*
implement turn, not just edge cases.

## Root cause (measured)

1. **`skill/implement/SKILL.md` re-bloated ~5× since the F5 trim.**
   - F5 (SA-0MSLK7SAE0032V9K, 2026-08-10) trimmed it to **15,447 B** with a
     stated budget of ≤15,453 B.
   - It is now **76,286 B / 75,774 chars (≈19k tokens)** — **4.9× over the F5
     budget**.
   - Growth was gradual: each of the ~67 subsequent commits appended new
     feature-card prose back into the brief instead of the reference doc
     (largest single-commit deltas: +6.6k B SA-0MVPZGAU5001FDO3, +4.1k B
     80dbf5a23 stash-hygiene, +3.1k B 19db86445 gate-failure docs, +3.0k B
     a624d18ed outbound-edge gate, +2.1k B each drive and per-child lock).
2. **The largest inline blocks are deep reference material, not operational
   steps.** The `## Steps` section alone is 45.5k chars (~11.4k tok):
   - `6.1 Parent recursion` — **19,068 chars (~4.8k tok)** — drive/parent
     orchestration, per-child locks, failure-recovery tiers, guard tables
   - `9. Commit, Push and mark in_review` — **11,079 chars (~2.8k tok)** —
     push timeout, terminal-status read-back, gate-failure reason tables
   - `### When finish refuses` — **7,202 chars (~1.8k tok)**
   - Background Job Etiquette — 3,927 chars; StatusLifecycle Integration —
     2,785 chars; gate-failure `reason`/facts — 3,142 chars
3. **The deep detail already lives in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`
   (82,844 B) but the SKILL.md body duplicates it inline** instead of linking
   to it. The F5 "operational brief + deep docs" pattern was abandoned.
4. **No regression gate exists on SKILL.md *body* size.** The context-budget
   gate (`measure_context.py`, `.githooks/pre-push`, tests
   `test_context_budget_gate.py`) only measures AGENTS.md files and the
   skills-section *description prose* (`skills_prose` = frontmatter
   `description:`), **not** the `SKILL.md` bodies loaded on invocation. The F5
   budget was a one-shot trim with no ongoing enforcement, so the file could
   silently regrow.
5. **Secondary: the system prompt contributes ~5.3k tokens** (measured 21,080
   chars in a real session) — dominated by `project_context` (AGENTS_GLOBAL.md
   ~3.2k tok + project AGENTS.md). Projects with very large AGENTS.md (e.g.
   AI_Hell system sections = 45,416 chars ≈ 11.3k tok) push near-miss sessions
   over the threshold without any skill change.
6. **The 216k–452k sessions are a separate failure mode** — resumed/hydrated
   sessions where the implement turn arrived after a huge *accumulated*
   context (the tables mark them as such). Not caused by SKILL.md alone, but a
   small SKILL.md body reduces the burn rate toward that failure.

## Users

- **Operator / producer** — runs `/skill:implement` on work items; the local
  proxy must accept the turn's context. A 25k baseline with near-miss at 38k
  is too close to the edge and growing (sessions already exceed 200–450k).
- **Agents** — every implement turn pays the fixed ~19k-token cost of the
  SKILL.md body before doing any work; a smaller brief loads faster and leaves
  more headroom for the work itself.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skill/implement/SKILL.md` is reduced to **≤ 20,000 B** (measurable with
   `wc -c`), a ≥74% cut from the current 76,286 B, restoring the F5
   "operational brief" size class (F5 budget was ≤15,453 B).
2. Every removed/abridged section is preserved — verbatim or summarised with a
   link + SA reference — in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (or an
   appendix there), so no behavioural content is lost (F5 AC2 pattern).
3. The brief still documents every command/flag an operator needs to run the
   workflow end-to-end (worktree creation, `implement.py start/finish/parent/
   drive`, `wl` status transitions, StatusLifecycle, push-to-dev); workflow
   semantics are unchanged.
4. A **regression gate on SKILL.md body size** is added so the file cannot
   silently regrow: extend `measure_context.py` (or the context-budget gate /
   a dedicated test) with a `skill_implement_md` byte threshold committed in
   `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json`, enforced by the pre-push hook
   and a test — mirroring how AGENTS.md sizes are already gated.
5. Tests asserting SKILL.md content are updated and passing:
   `tests/test_implement_skill_session_per_child_doc.py`,
   `tests/test_implement_dirty_tree_guidance.py`,
   `tests/test_implement_parent_recursion.py`,
   `tests/test_implement_tdd.py`, `skill/implement/tests/` etc. — content that
   moved to the reference doc must be asserted against the reference doc
   (F5 AC4 pattern: "SKILL.md-content tests updated to check the reference
   docs").
6. **Measured context reduction:** rerunning the composition measurement shows
   a cold implement turn at ≤ ~6.5k tokens from the skill body (down from
   ~19k), documented as a before/after in `docs/dev/context-budget.md` or the
   implement reference doc.
7. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The `## Steps` operational sequence (1–9) and its gating semantics must
  survive; only deep reference prose (rationale, tables, guard matrices,
  failure-mode taxonomies, SA-tagged feature cards) moves to the reference
  doc.
- Do **not** relax safety content (dirty-tree gate, worktree isolation,
  abort/reset, terminal-status guarantees) — preserve it verbatim or with a
  direct link.
- The implement skill's `tests/` must stay green; doc-content tests that pin
  moved prose must be repointed to the reference doc, not deleted.
- Keep the hidden-skill invocation map and extension conventions intact
  (`extension.json`, `SKILL_PREFIX/POSTFIX.md`).
- No change to `implement.py` runtime behaviour — this is a documentation/
  context-surface change only (SKILL.md + gate + reference docs + tests).

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — 76,286 B / 75,774 chars / ~19k tokens, inlined
  on every implement invocation.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — 82,844 B, already holds deep
  reference material (drive recovery, per-child lock, worktree removal,
  finish guards, push timeout, terminal read-back).
- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` + `context-budget.thresholds.json` — startup
  static-context gate; measures AGENTS files + description prose, **not**
  SKILL.md bodies.
- `skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py` — the canonical measurer;
  needs a SKILL.md-body component for AC4.
- Session evidence: cold implement turns at P50 ≈ 24.2k tokens (skill body
  75,774 chars/4 ≈ 18.9k + system ≈ 5.3k); near-miss 38,298–38,752; giant
  sessions 216k–452k (resumed/hydrated — separate failure mode noted in ACs/
  risks).

## Desired change

- Shrink `skill/implement/SKILL.md` back to an operational brief ≤20 KB by
  relocating the seven largest deep blocks (6.1 Parent recursion, Step 9
  push/commit detail, `When finish refuses`, gate-failure reason tables,
  Background Job Etiquette, StatusLifecycle Integration, worktree
  creation detail) to `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`, leaving a
  link + one-paragraph summary each.
- Add a byte-size regression gate so this can never silently regrow again.
- Document the before/after context composition.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — the file to shrink (76,286 B → ≤20,000 B).
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — destination for relocated deep
  prose (already 82,844 B, has the matching sections).
- `skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py` — add a `skill_implement_md`
  (or per-skill body) measurement component for the regression gate (AC4).
- `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` — commit the new byte threshold.
- `.githooks/pre-push` — enforce the new threshold (AC4).
- `tests/test_context_budget_gate.py`,
  `tests/test_pre_push_context_budget_gate.py` — extend for the body-size
  gate.
- Content-pinning tests — `tests/test_implement_skill_session_per_child_doc.py`,
  `tests/test_implement_dirty_tree_guidance.py`,
  `tests/test_implement_parent_recursion.py`, `tests/test_implement_tdd.py`,
  `tests/test_skill_path_conventions.py`, `skill/implement/tests/`.
- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` — document the before/after cold-turn
  composition (AC6).

## Related work

- **SA-0MSLK7SAE0032V9K** — F5: "Trim six largest SKILL.md files by ≥30%"
  (completed). Established the ≤15,453 B implement budget this item restores;
  its AC2/AC4 patterns are the template for this work.
- **SA-0MSL1Z1J50038RBF** — audit SKILL.md restructure to operational brief +
  deep docs (completed) — the pattern for "brief + reference-doc" splitting.
- **SA-0MSJI53RX006E2PS** — epic: "Reduce initial LLM context from skills and
  skill-related startup files" (completed). Its F1 tooling (measure_context.py)
  and F6 regression gate are the machinery reused here.
- **SA-0MSISKM8F004NW1U** — "Reduce audit skill initial session context size
  (duplicate AGENTS.md + skills section)" (completed) — same class of problem
  for audit.
- **AGENTS_GLOBAL.md / AGENTS.md context budget** — startup surface (~5.3k tok
  system prompt) is the secondary contributor; projects with very large
  AGENTS.md (AI_Hell ≈ 24 KB) amplify near-miss sessions. Out of scope for this
  item but noted as a constraint/risk.
- **SA-0MTT7EUH30054I41** — compaction config for the Local Proxy fallback
  path (client-side compaction disabled) — relevant to the giant 200k–452k
  hydrated-session failure mode, tracked separately, not fixed here.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** the same bloat affects other skills (audit 64.1 KB, ship
  33.8 KB, plan 27.2 KB, intake 21.5 KB, test 20.4 KB). This item is scoped to
  implement only; sibling trims should be separate work items. Risk: an
  operator may expect all skills trimmed at once — the ACs pin implement only.
- **Regression gate ≠ guarantee:** a body-size gate prevents silent regrowth
  but every *intentional* addition must flow through the gate (regenerate
  thresholds with justification, as AGENTS.md bumps do). Decide one
  threshold: F5-budget (15,453 B) vs "brief" allowance (20 KB) — AC1 proposes
  20 KB with F5 as reference. (Choose 20,000 B — see AC1; can be lowered after
  acceptance to the exact F5 figure if the brief compresses further.)
- **Resumed/hydrated giants (216k–452k):** not fully fixable by SKILL.md size
  alone — accumulated context across a long session is the driver. ACs
  intentionally exclude this; a smaller body reduces burn rate toward it but a
  separate work item may be needed for session-hydration limits.
- **Content-pinning tests:** some tests assert exact prose in SKILL.md; the
  almost-verbatim overlap check found ~0% shared lines with the reference doc,
  so moved prose will need deliberate re-pinning in tests — budget for it.
- **Assumption:** a ~19k-token body is the primary lever (78% of a 24.2k cold
  turn; 4.9× over the F5 budget) — verified by direct measurement of the file
  and real session logs on this machine.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which metric defines the problem — P50 cold-start tokens, the 38k
  near-miss threshold, or the 200k–452k hydrated sessions?" — Answer
  (operator, seed context): "At P50 we are around 25k which is right on the
  edge of what can be accepted locally. We need to get this down." The 5
  largest sessions are explicitly "resumed/hydrated — the implement turn
  arrived after a huge accumulated context"; the 38k cluster is the
  near-miss population. Source: intake seed + session tables (2026-11-01).
  Research: verified cold-turn composition = SKILL.md body (~19k tok) +
  system sections (~5.3k tok) ≈ 24.2k, matching P50 ≈ 25k. The giant-session
  mode is a separate failure tracked in Risks.
- Q: "Is a regression gate (AC4) in scope, or just the trim?" — Answer
  (intake inference from F5/F6 precedent + 'get this down'): a gate is
  required — without it the F5 trim (which had a budget that was never
  enforced) simply repeats. Marked AC4; if the operator wants the trim only,
  AC4 can be dropped without weakening ACs 1–3/5–7. OPEN QUESTION: confirm
  the 20,000 B allowance vs the exact F5 15,453 B figure.

## Impact

Agents and operators now start every `/skill:implement` turn with roughly a fifth of the skill's former context weight (≈20 KB instead of ≈100 KB), so implement runs load faster, leave far more headroom for the actual work, and stop pushing near the local model's acceptance edge.

# Clearer audit results

## Problem statement

The audit skill's end-of-session report Conclusion section buries the readiness
verdict ("Ready for ship") at the end of a long sentence, making it easy for
operators to miss when scanning reports. The verdict needs to be visually
prominent so operators can instantly see whether the item is ready to ship or
not.

## Users

- **Operators** reviewing audit results need to see at a glance whether the
  audited item is ready to ship.
- **Producers** scanning a grid of panes need the verdict to be immediately
  visible in the Conclusion section.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the session status is `completed`, the Conclusion section's first line
   is `✅ Ready to ship` (green) on its own line, followed by the completion
   sentence: `This completes the {skill_name} process for {id} ({title}).`
2. When the session status is **not** `completed`, the Conclusion section's
   first line is `🚫 Not ready to ship` (red) on its own line, followed by the
   incomplete-session sentence.
3. The green and red colouring is applied via ANSI escape sequences so that
   terminals supporting colour display the text in the correct colour, while
   plain-text terminals degrade gracefully (no garbled output).
4. All existing end-of-session reports across all skills (audit, intake, plan,
   implement, ship, …) use the new Conclusion format.
5. All existing tests for `render_report.py` pass; new tests cover the
   green/red colour formatting in both completed and incomplete states.

## Impact

Operators can now see at a glance whether an audited item is ready to ship by
looking at the colour and position of the verdict in the audit's Conclusion
section.

## Constraints

- The report renderer must work in plain-text (non-ANSI) terminals — colour
  is best-effort.
- The change must be backward-compatible with existing report consumers that
  parse the Conclusion section.
- The `next_action` parameter should no longer be appended at the end of the
  completion sentence (it is replaced by the standalone "Ready to ship" /
  "Not ready to ship" line).

## Existing state

The `render_report()` function in
`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` builds the Conclusion section as:

```
## Conclusion

This completes the {skill_name} process for {id} ({title}). Ready for {next_action}.
```

For incomplete sessions:

```
## Conclusion

{skill_name} session for {id} ({title}) is incomplete. Requires attention ({next_action}).
```

## Key Files

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — Modify the `render_report()`
  function's Conclusion section to move the readiness verdict to the top,
  in green or red.
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` — Update existing tests and add
  new tests for the colour-coded Conclusion format.

## Related work

- SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S — Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting via
  helper report skill (the skill that introduced the report template).
- SA-0MQ01FDQ5003H09A – Implementation: update AMPA audit handlers to use wl audit-set (completed)
- SA-0MRCQ5K50007G3BB – Add ready-to-close audit gate to ship skill release process (completed)
- SA-0MQ01F8OJ007HEEP – Test: AMPA audit handler writes to audit_results via wl audit-set (completed)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: What format should the "not ready" message use? — Answer: "Not ready to ship" with red colour, mirroring the "Ready to ship" green format. Source: work item description ("or its negative counterpart").
- Q: Should the `next_action` parameter still appear in the Conclusion? — Answer: No — it is replaced by the standalone verdict line. Source: work item description says to "move" the readiness line to appear first.
