## Goal

Fix D1: make the item-level freshness gate pending-screens aware so a stored parent report whose header says `Child screens pending` is never treated as a fresh final verdict. With a pending-screens signal present, `audit_runner.py issue <id>` must fall through to the pipeline (where the checkpoint resume can collect the child verdicts) instead of printing `Skipping: audit still fresh` and exiting 0.

Parent item: SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S (defect D1, root-cause analysis in that item's description).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: With a stored parent audit that is fresh by content fingerprint **and** a `<id>.pending-screens.json` listing ≥ 1 child, `audit_runner.py issue <id>` does not print `Skipping: audit still fresh` and proceeds to the pipeline (parent AC1). `_check_audit_freshness()` itself is unchanged — the decision to honour its result lives in `_phase_gate`.
- AC2: With no signal (missing, empty or corrupt), the freshness short-circuit is byte-identical to today: `Skipping: audit still fresh — Ready to close: <verdict>` (+ `audited <ts>` when known), the stored report printed, exit 0, no model call.
- AC3: The signal path resolves through the same directory resolution as `_open_checkpoint_store` — explicit `--checkpoint-dir` / `AUDIT_CHECKPOINT_DIR` wins, otherwise `resolve_checkpoint_dir(owning_root, None)` — and a `--no-checkpoint` run reads no signal (behaviour unchanged).
- AC4: `--force` semantics are unchanged: force still bypasses the freshness gate entirely and clears the checkpoint.
- AC5: The `--do-not-persist` freshness-refresh path cannot re-publish "fresh" for a run with outstanding screens: a guard (or a test proving unreachability) shows the dry-run `auditedAt` refresh cannot fire while `pending_child_screens` is non-empty — the child-audit execution gate keeps the verdict at `No`, and the refresh only applies to a passing verdict.
- AC6: The skip is observable: when the short-circuit is suppressed because of the signal, a one-line stderr diagnostic names the outstanding child count/ids and the reason.

## Minimal implementation

- Thread the explicit checkpoint directory onto `_AuditContext` (new field set in `cmd_issue` before `_phase_gate`, or resolved inside `_phase_gate`) so the gate can call `_read_pending_screens_signal(issue_id, owning_root, explicit_dir)` — `ctx.checkpoint_dir` is currently only populated later by `_open_checkpoint_store`.
- In `_phase_gate`'s `if not force:` freshness block, read the signal once; take the `return 0` short-circuit only when it is empty, else print the diagnostic and fall through.
- Add an explicit guard/assertion for AC5 at the dry-run refresh site (no new persistence semantics).
- Do not touch `_check_audit_freshness`, the report assembly, the verdict vocabulary, or `--force`.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_phase_gate` freshness block (~:10965-10990), `cmd_issue` checkpoint-store open (~:14829), `_read_pending_screens_signal` (~:6516), `resolve_checkpoint_dir` import (~:117), dry-run freshness refresh (~:14529)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` — AC1/AC2/AC3 tests; remove the D1 `xfail(strict=True)` marker added by the reproduction child
- `skill/audit/scripts/checkpoint_store.py` — read-only (`resolve_checkpoint_dir`, `PENDING_SCREENS_SIGNAL_SUFFIX` lives in `audit_runner.py`)

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the reproduction slice (RED D1 test must exist first).
- Sibling slice (D2 checkpoint resume) depends on this one, because the resume pipeline is unreachable until the gate stops short-circuiting.

## Deliverables

- D1 fix + green AC1-AC6 tests.
- Changelog entry in the parent item's plan block.

## Goal

Fix D2: a `phase1_children` checkpoint whose restored `child_results` still carry `MAIN_SLOT_PENDING_EVIDENCE` must not be treated as a completed phase. Re-resolve those children through the existing child-verdict reuse path so their freshly persisted audits are collected (zero pi calls), the pending list empties, and `_write_pending_screens_signal([])` removes `<id>.pending-screens.json`.

Parent item: SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S (defect D2, root-cause analysis in that item's description).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: With a `phase1_children`-completed checkpoint whose restored `child_results` carry `MAIN_SLOT_PENDING_EVIDENCE` and fresh stored child audits, the phase is not treated as complete for those children: the existing child-verdict reuse path runs (`_get_child_audit_verdict` → `_child_acs_from_own_audit`), setting `reused_from` plus `child_audit_ready`/`child_audit_not_ready` and real `ac_results`, with zero child pi calls.
- AC2: After the pending child screens have been serviced (fresh child audits persisted with v2 fingerprints) and the parent re-run on the same HEAD, the resulting report contains **no** `Child screens pending:` gate, `pending_child_screens` is empty in the JSON payload, and `<id>.pending-screens.json` is removed from the checkpoint directory. No child-screening pi call is made for a child with a fresh stored audit (parent AC2).
- AC3: A child whose screens were serviced but whose stored audit verdict is `Ready to close: No` is reported as assessed / `child_audit_not_ready` (not `not_assessed`), and still blocks the parent's readiness (parent AC3).
- AC4: A child with no stored audit, or with a stale stored audit (changed title/description or `--force`), still appears as pending — the fast path never fabricates a serviced state (parent AC4).
- AC5: No weakening: the child-audit execution gate (`Ready to close: Yes` impossible while screens are pending), the unserviced-in-main-slot classification (`unserviced_in_main_slot` / `not_assessed`), the no-side-effect restore rule and `--force` semantics (force still bypasses child reuse) are unchanged; budget-exceeded children still re-audit on resume; `--no-child-in-main-slot` (separate-process) behaviour is untouched.
- AC6: The refreshed `child_results` are written back into the checkpoint before Phase 2, so a subsequent resume sees resolved children rather than replaying the placeholders again.

## Minimal implementation

- In `_run_phase_children`, after restoring `child_results` from `checkpoint.accumulated_state()`, compute the pending set via `_pending_main_slot_child_ids`; when non-empty, factor the existing child-verdict reuse pre-pass loop body into a helper and run it for exactly those children (restoring the same `reused_from`/`child_audit_ready`/`child_audit_not_ready`/`ac_results` shape), instead of skipping the whole orchestration block.
- Keep the `phase2_checkpointed` early-return, except when pending markers remain.
- Persist the resolved `child_results` back through `checkpoint.mark_completed(PHASE_CHILDREN, ...)`/the accumulated-state writer so the replay cannot recur.
- Leave `_write_pending_screens_signal` call sites unchanged — the signal clears itself once the pending list is empty.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_run_phase_children`/`_phase_children` checkpoint restore (~:12744-12815 and the `if not phase1_checkpointed:` orchestration block ~:12812-12910), child-verdict reuse (~:12863-12895), `_pending_main_slot_child_ids` (~:6323), `_write_pending_screens_signal` (~:6347), `_read_pending_screens_signal` (~:6516), `_get_child_audit_verdict` (~:7765), `_child_acs_from_own_audit` (~:7951), `_reaudit_budget_exceeded_children`
- `skill/audit/scripts/checkpoint_store.py` — `PHASE_CHILDREN`, `accumulated_state()`, `mark_completed()`, `budget_exceeded_children()`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_child_in_main_slot.py` — AC1/AC2 tests; remove the D2 `xfail(strict=True)` marker added by the reproduction child
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_child_reason_diagnostics.py` — AC3 classification test
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_checkpoint.py` — resume fixtures (read-only)

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the D1 slice (the resume pipeline is unreachable while the freshness gate short-circuits) and by the reproduction slice.

## Deliverables

- D2 fix + green AC1-AC6 tests.
- A comment on the parent recording that the production symptom (permanent `Child screens pending` gate on LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0) is now recoverable.

## Goal

Prove the two fixes compose end to end and make the documented contract truthful. This slice adds the composed `cmd_issue`-level verification (fresh parent audit + pending-screens signal → pipeline → checkpoint-resume collection → cleared signal) and reconciles the audit documentation with the fixed behaviour, covering both the same-session service case and the later-session service case.

Parent item: SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S (AC2, AC5, AC6).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: An end-to-end test through `cmd_issue` proves the full cycle composes on the same HEAD: a fresh parent audit by content fingerprint plus a `<id>.pending-screens.json` naming ≥ 1 child → the run does not short-circuit → the `phase1_children` checkpoint resume collects the serviced child audits → the report contains no `Child screens pending:` gate, the JSON payload's `pending_child_screens` is empty, `<id>.pending-screens.json` is removed, and zero child-screening pi calls are made.
- AC2: The end-to-end coverage distinguishes the two documented cases: (a) the invoking session services the screens in the same session as the first run, and (b) a later session services them and re-runs the parent. Both reach the collected/ready state without a full re-audit.
- AC3 (parent AC6): `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (and the audit reference doc if present) documents the now-working resume cycle — including the case where the invoking session services the screens in the *same* session as the first run, and the case where a later session services them — so the "perform the screen, persist the child audit, re-run the parent" instruction is truthful.
- AC4: `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` records the two mechanism changes: the signal-aware freshness gate (a report with outstanding pending child screens is never a fresh final verdict) and the checkpoint-resume re-resolution of pending children (freshness gate section + child-audit execution contract section).

# Goal

One-off operational sweep of the stale `<id>.pending-screens.json` signals left behind by the broken in-main-slot resume cycle fixed in SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S, so the affected items stop being constrained by a gate that can no longer clear.

Discovered-from: SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S (audit comment 2026-10-29, "Adjacent scope note 2"). Blocked-by SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S — now **completed** (`stage: done`, shipped in v0.1.26), so the sweep is actionable.

## Current state (verified at intake, 2026-11-16)

The backlog recorded on 2026-10-29 no longer exists in the `llm` project:

- The `llm` project is `/home/rgardler/projects/llm-manager` (worklog prefix `LP`); all seven backlogged IDs resolve there.
- **0 `LP-*.pending-screens.json` files remain.** `ls /home/rgardler/projects/llm-manager/.worklog/audit-checkpoints/*.pending-screens.json` → no such file; the `audit-checkpoints/` directory itself is absent.
- **All seven backlogged items are terminal:** each is `status: completed`, `stage: done` — LP-0MU3VDB9U008H8CI, LP-0MVB8F5ZU0079DE9, LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4, LP-0MVGT0E6W000Q8CY, LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0, LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X, LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG.
- **One closure cleared a signal without servicing it.** LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0 is closed (`completed`/`done`) but its stored report still reads `Ready to close: No` with `Child screens pending: 1` naming LP-0MVVETUDF004FWEB; that child is independently `open` (a `test-failure` item). The parent was closed by producer decision rather than by collecting the screen; the outstanding child is tracked on its own item.

Net: for this item's **stated `llm` scope** the sweep is already satisfied — no item is constrained by a stale signal, and all seven backlogged parents are terminal.

## Cross-project inventory (new finding)

The same class of signal still exists in other project worklogs — 43 files across 7 projects (machine scan, 2026-11-16):

| Project | Signals |
|---|---|
| SorraAgents | 13 |
| AI_Hell | 9 |
| tce-the-rising | 5 |
| Tableau-Card-Engine | 5 |
| ContextHub | 5 |
| tce-main-street | 4 |
| ToneForge | 2 |

Some are genuinely pending; others are likely stale leftovers of the runner bug SA-0MW9B11HE003AZZU ("audit runner leaves stale pending-screens.json when no child screens remain", open/low), which reports a resume that empties `pending_child_screens` in its payload while leaving the file on disk.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Enumerate every `<id>.pending-screens.json` under each project's `.worklog/audit-checkpoints/` (llm + the 7 projects with signals) and reconcile against the 2026-10-29 table, recording additions/removals in a comment. Intake result: **0 under llm-manager**, 43 across SorraAgents (13), AI_Hell (9), tce-the-rising (5), Tableau-Card-Engine (5), ContextHub (5), tce-main-street (4), ToneForge (2) — recorded as comment evidence.
- AC2: For each remaining signal, run the parent audit once with the D1/D2 fix in place; where the child audits are already serviced the signal clears automatically, otherwise run a forced `--no-child-in-main-slot` audit so child screens execute in the runner instead of being emitted for an absent interactive session.
- AC3: Each affected item's audit state is recorded (report verdict + whether the signal is gone); no signal remains for an item whose children are all audited.
- AC4: The sweep does not change verdicts by hand — `wl audit-set` is never used directly; only real runner audits persist reports.
- AC5: Producer scope decision **Q1 = (b) — widened**. The sweep covers every project worklog enumerated at intake (llm-manager 0, plus 43 signals across 7 other projects); each signal is classified genuine-pending vs stale before any forced re-audit (a forced run re-bills full audit cost).
- AC6 (validation): Validation is evidence-based — signal presence/absence confirmed by filesystem enumeration and `wl audit-show <id> --json`; no verdict is fabricated.
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- AC8: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Operators across all projects stop seeing backlogged items clamped by a `Child screens pending` gate that can no longer clear, and the reconciliation makes explicit that the original seven-item `llm` backlog is already gone while the 43-signal backlog in the other seven projects gets classified and cleared.

## Minimal implementation

- **llm scope (already done at intake):** the reconciliation record — enumerate the (now empty) checkpoint directory, map the seven IDs to their terminal states — is posted as a comment on this item.
- **Widened scope (producer Q1 = (b), 2026-11-16):**
  1. Enumerate every `<project>/.worklog/audit-checkpoints/*.pending-screens.json` across the 7 projects with signals (SorraAgents 13, AI_Hell 9, tce-the-rising 5, Tableau-Card-Engine 5, ContextHub 5, tce-main-street 4, ToneForge 2).
  2. Per signal, classify genuine-pending vs stale from the parent/child audit state via `wl audit-show <id> --json` and the signal's `pending_child_screens` (stale = the pending set is provably empty, or the parent/children are terminal — SA-0MW9B11HE003AZZU leftovers; genuine = a parent still has unserviced, non-terminal children).
  3. Per genuinely pending parent, run `python3 skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py issue <id> --no-child-in-main-slot --force` (or the default mode where a fresh serviced child audit exists) and record log paths + `wl audit-show <id> --json` as evidence.
  4. Record per-item evidence (verdict + signal gone) and the stale/gone classification on this item; never use `wl audit-set`.

## Constraints

- **No fabricated verdicts:** `wl audit-set` is never called directly; only a real runner audit persists a report (AC4).
- **Cost-aware:** a forced `--no-child-in-main-slot` audit re-bills a full audit per item, so classify genuine-pending vs stale before forcing.
- **No manual file surgery beyond a genuine stale cleanup:** deleting a signal is only valid where the pending set is provably empty; otherwise clear it by servicing the children.
- **Operational, not a fix:** this item is a one-off sweep; the root-cause guard against stale leftovers is SA-0MW9B11HE003AZZU and stays out of scope here.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope (resolved):** producer chose Q1 = (b) — the cross-project backlog is in scope for this item; no follow-up item needed for the inventory.
- **Cost blow-out if forced blindly:** mitigate by classifying stale vs genuine first (Q1 recommendation).
- **Assumption:** `llm` = `/home/rgardler/projects/llm-manager` (worklog prefix `LP`) — verified by resolving all seven IDs there.
- **Assumption:** a parent closed while its stored report still shows a pending child (LP-0MVLNBCTN0084MT0) is a producer closure, not evidence that the screen was serviced; the outstanding child is tracked on LP-0MVVETUDF004FWEB.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (read-only — `--force`, `--no-child-in-main-slot`, `_read_pending_screens_signal`/`_write_pending_screens_signal`)
- `<project>/.worklog/audit-checkpoints/*.pending-screens.json` (the sweep target; `llm-manager` currently has none)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` / `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (the documented resume/clear contract)

## Related work

- SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S — parent fix (D1 freshness gate + D2 checkpoint resume); **completed**.
- SA-0MW2J7NGP006CIEG, SA-0MW2J7O3D0044SFM, SA-0MW2J7OPP007MAPV — the four landed fix slices; **completed**.
- SA-0MW9B11HE003AZZU — "audit runner leaves stale pending-screens.json when no child screens remain"; open/low. Root-cause bug for stale leftovers; a sweep is only a workaround.
- SA-0MW2J8G260045D17 — "Dispatched audits should not emit unservicable screens" (adjacent scope note 1); open.
- SA-0MVAWFUU0004VW45, SA-0MVZ3SMK6007431I, SA-0MUH6H87Z001HYJ7 — completed child-screen classification / resume behaviour.

## Producer scope decision (Q1 — answered 2026-11-16)

**Q1 — Scope.** The `llm` backlog this item was written against is now empty (no signals, all seven items terminal), while 43 signals remain across seven other projects. Should this item:

- (a) be **closed as already-satisfied** for its stated `llm` scope, with the cross-project inventory recorded on a new follow-up item; or
- (b) be **widened** to sweep all project worklogs — classify each signal genuine-pending vs stale, and run a forced `--no-child-in-main-slot` audit only where a parent still has genuinely unserviced children?

**Producer answer: (b) — widen.** The sweep covers all project worklogs; classify stale vs genuine first, then force `--no-child-in-main-slot` only for genuinely unserviced parents. Source: interactive reply 2026-11-16 (comment on this item).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Note:** the item was seeded with a complete goal, a known-backlog table, four testable ACs, a minimal implementation sketch and Key Files, so no requirement discovery was needed via interview. The single decision below is a genuine scope choice routed to the producer.

- **Q1 — Scope (see decision above).** **Answer (producer): (b)** — widen the sweep to all project worklogs, classifying each signal genuine-pending vs stale and forcing `--no-child-in-main-slot` only where a parent still has genuinely unserviced children. Source: interactive reply 2026-11-16 (recorded in the question comment on this item). Final: (b). ## Goal

Decide and implement how non-interactive (herdr-downtime-dispatched) audits avoid the in-main-slot pending-screens trap: a dispatched audit has no interactive invoking session to perform the emitted `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` screens, so by construction every dispatched parent audit lands in the unserviced state.

Discovered-from: SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S (audit comment 2026-10-29, "Adjacent scope note 1"). Distinct from the D1/D2 resume defects: even with a working resume cycle, nobody services a dispatched audit's screens.

## Proposal (needs producer decision — not yet approved)

Have the dispatcher pass `--no-child-in-main-slot` for downtime-dispatched audits, or have `cmd_issue` detect a dispatched/non-interactive context and resolve `child_in_main_slot=False`, so child screens run in isolated `pi` subprocesses with the runner's own parsing/retry instead of being emitted for a session that will never run them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The chosen mechanism is recorded on this item with the rationale (dispatcher-side flag vs. runner-side context detection) and the trade-off accepted (separate-process child audits cost one `pi` subprocess per child but need no interactive session).
- AC2: Dispatched audits no longer emit `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` screens that nobody services: a dispatched run either completes its child screens itself or reports a documented, actionable state.
- AC3: An interactive audit launched from an agent session keeps in-main-slot mode by default — no behaviour change for the interactive path.
- AC4: Regression coverage proves the resolution precedence for the new mechanism (explicit flag > env `AUDIT_CHILD_IN_MAIN_SLOT` > dispatch detection > default `true`), with `wl`/`pi` mocked (no real subprocess).

## Minimal implementation

- Preferred (dispatcher-side, smallest blast radius): pass `--no-child-in-main-slot` from the downtime dispatch command; add a test on the dispatch command construction.
- Alternative (runner-side): resolve the mode from a dispatch marker/env in `_resolve_child_in_main_slot` and log the resolution source.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_resolve_child_in_main_slot`, `cmd_issue` child-mode resolution
- dispatcher/downtime-worker command construction (herdr package) — locate before editing
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_child_in_main_slot.py` — `TestChildInMainSlotGateResolution`

## Dependencies

- Related to SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S (its resume fixes are a prerequisite for any in-main-slot dispatch to be recoverable, but this item is not blocked by it).

## Deliverables

- Producer decision recorded + implementation + regression test.

# `scripts/install_pi.sh` wires git hooks but never refreshes the globally resolved `wl`, so a stale `dist` can silently revert the canonical hook template

discovered-from:CG-0MW1ZBKP0006U1YU (Tableau-Card-Engine — "Restore pre-push test-cache mirroring in the canonical wl hook template", AC2 tail clause: recorded as a follow-up, not fixed there)

## Problem statement

`scripts/install_pi.sh` installs and *wires* the project's git hooks
(`.githooks/*` copies + `core.hooksPath`), but it never refreshes the `wl` binary
those hooks depend on. On this framework, `wl` is not installed from a registry
— it is **npm-linked to the `ContextHub` checkout**, and `ContextHub/dist` is
gitignored. So the template that `wl init` / `wl doctor upgrade` emits is
whatever was last built into a *local, uncommitted* `dist`, which can predate (or
diverging from) the committed hook. The next `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` then
silently rewrites a consuming repository's `.githooks/pre-push` from that stale
template and deletes capabilities the repo legitimately carries.

The concrete incident class: `mirror_suite_cache` (the dev-push gate's
test-cache mirroring, `CG-0MW1ZBKP0006U1YU` / ContextHub `WL-0MW20XXWE00466FP`)
existed only in a stale `ContextHub/dist` build for a while. A rebuild of the
linked `wl` from a `dev` that lacked the template change, followed by
`wl doctor upgrade --confirm`, removes the capability from every consuming
repo, with exit 0 and no warning — the invariant "a worktree-originated `dev`
push leaves a green cached full-suite entry the main checkout can read" then
breaks silently.

## Verified facts (checked 2026-11-04 on this host)

1. **`wl` is npm-linked, not registry-installed.**
   - `npm ls -g --depth=0` → `worklog@1.0.27 -> ./../../../home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`
   - `/usr/local/bin/wl` → `../lib/node_modules/worklog/dist/cli.js`, which
     `readlink -f` resolves to `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/dist/cli.js`.
   - The package version stays `1.0.27` across template changes, so the version
     number alone cannot tell you whether the *template* is current.
2. **The template lives only in the built `dist`.** `ContextHub/.gitignore`
   line 86 ignores `dist`; `PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT` is compiled from
   `ContextHub/src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts` into
   `ContextHub/dist/doctor/hook-upgrade.js`, so the `wl` a machine runs is
   whatever branch/dirty state was last built there.
3. **The installer wires hooks but never touches `wl`.** The hook block is
   `scripts/install_pi.sh:317-412` (comment header at :317): step 1 copies
   `$SRC_DIR/.githooks/pre-push` (v3) or `pre-push.v2` into the project's
   `.githooks/` only when absent (:347-361), step 2 sets
   `core.hooksPath = .githooks` (:363-370), then it verifies the global
   context-audit skill (:373-380), per-project thresholds (:383-388) and the git
   identity (:390-408). There is **no** `npm run build`, `npm link`, `npm i -g`
   or version check anywhere in the installer.
4. **The destructive step is `wl doctor upgrade`, not the installer.**
   `ContextHub/src/commands/doctor/upgrade.ts:98` emits the upgrade set and
   `upgradeHooks()` (`ContextHub/src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts:603-643`) writes
   every `outdated` hook with `fs.writeFileSync(hookPath,
   h.committedContent, { mode: 0o755 })` — a **whole-file overwrite** of the
   repo's committed hook with the template baked into the running `wl`, i.e. the
   stale `dist`. The result is reported as success ("Upgraded from
   .githooks/").
5. **Why it matters (consuming repos).** Every repository in the framework uses
   `core.hooksPath = .githooks`, so the hook file *is* the gate. After a stale
   rebuild + upgrade, `.githooks/pre-push` no longer mirrors the gate run's
   cache entries into the main checkout's `.worklog/cache`, and
   `run_tests.py --summary --suite all --json` reports `missing` at the just-
   pushed commit (and audit F3 loses its cached green evidence).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Fail loudly on template skew.** The installer (and/or the hook-wiring
  step it owns) fails loudly — non-zero exit or an explicit, actionable
  `WARNING` naming both sides — when the template baked into the resolved `wl`
  predates/differs from the hook the repository commits, instead of leaving the
  operator with a `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` that deletes the divergence.
  *Verification:* a new test case drives the installer with a sandboxed `HOME`
  and a stub `wl` whose template lacks a marker present in the repo's committed
  hook, and asserts the refusal/warning text; the up-to-date case stays silent.
- **AC2 — Regression test in the existing installer suite.**
  `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` gains the skew cases next to the
  existing hook-wiring cases, with a sandboxed `HOME` (no live `~/.pi`, no live
  npm global root) so the test is hermetic and CI-safe.
  *Verification:* the new cases fail against today's installer and pass after
  the change.
- **AC3 — Documented.** The installer's own documentation and the hook-wiring
  docs state the dependency on the resolved `wl` and how to refresh it
  (`docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` global-install section,
  `docs/dev/context-budget.md` hook-wiring section, `README.md` install entry
  as needed).
  *Verification:* each touched page names the `wl`-refresh step (or the new
  guard) and the failure it prevents.

## Candidate remedies (pros / cons)

**(a) Detect a `ContextHub` checkout and rebuild (or reinstall) the global `wl`
during install.** Resolve the global `worklog` link target; if it is inside a
git checkout, run `npm run build` there (or `npm link`/`npm i -g` when the link
is absent).
- *Pros:* removes the root cause on developer machines; one command still sets
  everything up; no new convention for consuming repos.
- *Cons:* gives a global installer a cross-repo build responsibility (slow,
  needs the link target's dependencies and a working toolchain); it builds
  whatever branch/dirty state that checkout happens to be on, so it can install
  the *wrong* template just as silently; surprising side effect for anyone who
  did not expect the installer to mutate `../ContextHub`.

**(b) Pin an explicit `worklog` version and refuse to run against an unexpected
one.** Commit the expected version (e.g. in the project's installer config or
`package.json`) and have the installer compare it with `wl --version`.
- *Pros:* deterministic and fail-loud; makes the dependency visible in every
  repo; cheap to implement; no cross-repo mutation.
- *Cons:* version numbers do not prove template equality — two builds of
  `1.0.27` can carry different templates, which is exactly the observed hazard;
  a mismatch blocks the operator until they rebuild by hand; needs a per-repo
  convention to keep the pin current.

**(c) Fail loudly when the installed template predates the committed hook.**
Compare the template the resolved `wl` would emit
(`wl init`-equivalent content, e.g. `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json`
hook content, or a `wl hooks print`-style helper) against the repo's committed
`.githooks/pre-push`; refuse (or warn with the exact remedy) when the committed
hook carries capability the template lacks.
- *Pros:* cheap and directly targeted at the silent-deletion mechanism; needs no
  version convention; naturally testable in the existing installer test with a
  stub `wl`; fail-loud, and can be made fail-soft-visible (`WARNING`) where a
  hard failure would be hostile.
- *Cons:* if implemented only in the installer it is an *install-time* guard —
  a later manual `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` bypasses it, so the durable
  "never downgrade a hook" guard belongs upstream in
  `ContextHub/src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts` (with its own test) and this item
  should file that as a linked upstream item rather than assume it here.

### Recommendation

Implement **(c)** in the installer (fail-loud skew check, hermetic test,
documentation), because it is the smallest change that removes the silent
deletion path and it is testable in the existing installer suite. Follow it with
**(b)** as a cheap visibility convention (expected `worklog` version recorded
where the installer can read it), noting explicitly in the docs that the version
is a hint, not proof. Treat **(a)** as an **opt-in** flag
(`--refresh-wl`/`PI_REFRESH_WL=1`) rather than default behaviour, and file the
durable upstream guard (refuse a template "downgrade" inside `upgradeHooks`)
against `ContextHub` where the destructive write actually lives.

## Tests & documentation (explicitly in scope)

- This is a **shared framework script**, so the change cannot ship without
  tests: extend `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` (existing, ~15 KB) with
  sandboxed-`HOME` cases — stale template + divergent committed hook
  (refusal/warning), up-to-date template (silent OK), `wl` absent (`wl`-not-found
  path must remain non-fatal, as the installer is fail-open elsewhere), and the
  opt-in refresh flag if (a) is taken.
- Documentation is part of the deliverable, not a follow-up: the installer's
  install notes, `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` (global install),
  `docs/dev/context-budget.md` (hook wiring) and the `README.md` install entry
  must describe the `wl` dependency and the remedy.
- Any "never downgrade" guard added in `ContextHub` needs its own test there
  (`../ContextHub/tests/`), as a separate `WL-` item.

## Key Files

- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — hook-wiring block (:317-412); the place a skew check
  / opt-in refresh belongs.
- `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` — the installer hook-wiring suite the
  new cases extend (sandboxed `HOME`).
- `../ContextHub/src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts` — `PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT` and
  `upgradeHooks()` (:603-643, whole-file overwrite at :622) — the durable
  "never downgrade" guard target (separate `WL-` item).
- `../ContextHub/src/commands/doctor/upgrade.ts` — the `--dry-run` / `--confirm`
  CLI contract a dry-run-based skew check would consume.
- `../ContextHub/.gitignore` — line 86 (`dist`), the reason the template is not
  version-controlled.
- `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md`, `docs/dev/context-budget.md`, `README.md` —
  documentation surface.

## Constraints

- The installer is shared across every framework project and must stay
  **fail-open** for non-hook concerns (it already warns rather than dies on a
  missing context-audit skill, missing thresholds, or a failed identity guard);
  only the hook-template skew guard may be fail-loud, and its exit behaviour
  needs an explicit decision (blocking vs `WARNING`) recorded in the item.
- No live-`HOME` mutations in tests: sandbox `HOME` (as the existing suite does).
- Do not rebuild a `ContextHub` checkout the operator did not ask to rebuild
  (option (a) must be opt-in), and never mutate another repository from a
  default install.
- Push to `dev` only, never `main`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the resolved `wl` on a framework host is the npm-linked
  `ContextHub` build (verified above); a registry install would make (a)
  meaningless but (c)/(b) still useful.
- **Risk:** a `wl` that cannot print its template (e.g. an older `wl` without a
  print path) forces the check to parse `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json` or
  to fall back to a version comparison — the fallback must be documented and
  must not turn into a hard failure on an old `wl`.
- **Risk:** failing the whole install on skew could block a machine whose only
  problem is a stale `dist`; prefer an actionable `WARNING` plus a clear remedy
  unless the producer prefers a hard failure.
- **Risk:** duplicate coverage with `CG-0MW1ZBKP0006U1YU`'s AC2 tail clause —
  that item explicitly records the gap and does **not** fix it, so this item is
  the fix, not a duplicate.

## Related work

- `CG-0MW1ZBKP0006U1YU` (Tableau-Card-Engine) — discovered-from; the
  template-ownership item whose AC2 tail clause records this gap.
- `WL-0MW20XXWE00466FP` (ContextHub) — the upstream template change
  (`mirror_suite_cache`), the capability whose silent removal motivated this.
- `SA-0MV8M4OVX000QHSM` (completed) — an earlier `install_pi.sh` hook-scope
  defect (v3 gate propagated to non-SorraAgents projects); same block, same
  fail-open principle.
- `SA-0MR3P8N3V001Q3RG` (completed) — "Add rebuild step to implement SKILL.md
  after git pull": the same stale-`dist` failure mode documented for agents,
  fixed by documentation rather than by an installer guard.
- `SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX` (completed) — the installer's git-identity guard, the
  precedent for "surface the problem at install time, fail-open".

## Deliverables

- `scripts/install_pi.sh` skew check (or opt-in refresh flag, per the recorded
  decision) with fail-loud/`WARNING` output naming both hook versions.
- New cases in `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` (sandboxed `HOME`).
- Documentation updates in the installer's install notes,
  `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md`, `docs/dev/context-budget.md`, `README.md`.
- A linked `WL-` item for the durable upstream "never downgrade" guard in
  `upgradeHooks()` (filed, not implemented here).

# Test runs exhaust /tmp inodes under multi-agent load — disk-backed TMPDIR + stale pytest-root prune

## Goal (user story)

As an agent or operator running the test suite / dev-push gate, I want test and
build subprocesses to use disk-backed temporary storage and stale test temp
roots to be pruned automatically, so a host with many concurrent agents cannot
exhaust `/tmp` inodes and turn a green change into a blocked push.

## Problem statement

During **MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV** (tce-main-street) the dev-push gate failed its
full-suite run with an `ENOSPC` raised inside
`PlaywrightBrowserProvider.createContext`, reported by the gate as an
`unparsed`/infrastructure failure. Diagnosis:

- `/tmp` is **tmpfs with 1,048,576 inodes**; it was **100 % used** (`df -i /tmp`
  → `IUse% 100`, `IFree 0`) while the byte budget was only ~24 % used.
- The inode pressure came from many small files: stale
  `/tmp/pytest-of-rgardler/pytest-*` roots (~5–20k files each; 42 stale roots
  ≈ 312k files), Playwright/Chromium profiles, and `tsx`/node compile caches.
- `systemd-tmpfiles` only carries `q /tmp 1777 root root 10d` — age-based, so
  rapid multi-agent churn exhausts inodes long before the 10-day sweep.
- Nothing overrides `TMPDIR`, so every suite/build subprocess defaults to the
  small tmpfs. Manually deleting stale pytest roots (`mtime > 20 min`) freed
  ~679k inodes and the push then passed — confirming the cause.

The gate correctly refused to push, but the failure is host-infrastructure, not
a code failure, and it blocks otherwise-green work. This is a framework/test-
tooling defect, not a tce-main-street defect.

## Desired change (option 1 + option 2)

1. **Disk-backed TMPDIR (option 1).** When the test runner spawns suite
   commands, give them a `TMPDIR` on a disk-backed filesystem (plenty of
   inodes) instead of the ambient small tmpfs. Resolve a candidate in a
   documented precedence order (explicit env override → a configured
   disk-backed dir such as `/var/tmp/pi-test-<uid>` → `tempfile.gettempdir()`),
   create it if needed, and fall back safely when no candidate is usable
   (macOS/Windows/CI).
2. **Stale test-root prune (option 2).** Before running (at least the full
   suite), prune stale `pytest-of-<user>/pytest-*` roots older than a
   configurable threshold (default ~60 min), keeping the `pytest-current`
   symlink target and the N most recent roots, never touching another user's
   directories, and best-effort skipping roots that an active `pytest` process
   may hold.

Both must be **fail-open**: a prune or TMPDIR error is logged and the test run
proceeds unchanged.

## Existing state (verified in the current tree)

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — every suite command is spawned by
  `_run_cmd()` with `env=_suite_command_env()`; `_suite_command_env()` layers
  `test_runner.subprocess_env_with_scrubbed_overrides()` (repository-override
  scrub + `~/.local/bin` PATH injection) and `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS`. That helper
  is the **single insertion point** for a disk-backed `TMPDIR` — the scrub
  touches only repository overrides, so `TMPDIR` passes through untouched
  today and is simply never set.
- `grep -rn "TMPDIR" skill/ .githooks/ scripts/` → **no assignment anywhere**;
  the only hits are test fixtures that set it themselves
  (`skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_abort.py`,
  `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_launch_context.py`) and design notes in
  `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` already imports the test-skill
  helpers (in-process `run_tests`), so build/test subprocesses inherit any
  runner-side change. The **push** path is different: the finish gate spawns
  `git push` with `env={**os.environ}` and the pre-push hook then runs
  `run_tests.py` as a child — so AC4 requires implement.py to export the
  resolved disk-backed `TMPDIR` into its own process environment (or the push
  child env), not merely to call the runner helper.
- `.githooks/pre-push` / `.githooks/pre-push.v2` invoke
  `python3 "$repo_root/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py" --scope full
  --strict-git-env` and appear to create no temp directories of their own —
  inheritance from the parent environment is sufficient there.
- **Documentation target correction:** `docs/dev/testing.md` does **not**
  exist. The documentation lands in `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` (test
  runner behaviour) with a cross-reference from `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`
  (which already discusses `TMPDIR`/`--basetemp` resolution).
- No duplicate work found: `wl search` for the temp/inode/pytest keywords
  returns only this item plus its already-filed host-hardening sibling
  **SA-0MW2QEZBG009I3AI**.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Disk-backed TMPDIR for suite subprocesses.** `run_tests.py` passes a
   disk-backed `TMPDIR` to every suite command it spawns, using the documented
   precedence order and creating the directory when absent. A unit test asserts
   the env handed to the spawned command (and the fallback path when no
   disk-backed candidate exists).
2. **Stale-root prune is correct and safe.** The prune removes
   `pytest-of-<user>/pytest-*` roots older than the threshold, keeps the
   `pytest-current` target and the newest roots, is scoped to the current user,
   and is a no-op when the base directory is absent. A unit test exercises it
   against a temporary fixture directory (stale root removed, current/newest
   root kept).
3. **Fail-open.** A TMPDIR- or prune-related error never changes a run's exit
   status, cache entry, or scope resolution; it is logged only. Covered by a
   test that forces the failure path.
4. **`implement.py` parity.** The `finish` build/test/push subprocesses (and
   therefore the pre-push full-suite gate) inherit the same disk-backed
   `TMPDIR`, so the observed failure mode is closed end-to-end.
5. **Documentation.** `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` (with a cross-reference
   from `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`) documents the TMPDIR precedence, the prune
   behaviour, and the failure signature: `ENOSPC` inside Playwright
   `createContext`, `df -i /tmp` at 100 %, gate `reason:
   unparsed`/`infrastructure` — with the operator remedy.
6. **Regression pin.** A test pins the inode-exhaustion signature so the gate
   classifies it as infrastructure (never a code `test_failure`) and pins the
   TMPDIR/prune helpers.
7. **No behaviour change to test selection or caching.** Changed/full scope
   resolution, cache keys and the audit-accepted full-suite cache entry are
   unchanged (the TMPDIR/prune work must be env-only and must not alter any
   suite command string).
8. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments/docstrings, `README`, and any relevant docs-site entries.
9. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes (via the test
   skill / dev-push gate, per the test execution policy).

## Constraints

- Framework scope only (SorraAgents); no changes in tce-main-street.
- Env-only change: suite command strings and cache keys must stay
  byte-identical so the audit-accepted full-suite cache entry stays valid.
- Must work on Linux, macOS and CI (no hard dependency on `/var/tmp`).
- Never delete another user's temp roots; never delete the `pytest-current`
  target or an active run's root.
- Fail-open on every prune/TMPDIR error path (log, continue).
- No new mandatory dependency; Python standard library only (`pathlib`,
  `shutil`, `tempfile`, `os`).
- **Worktree requirement:** implementation happens in the worktree created by
  `implement.py start <WIP-id>` — all `wl` mutations from the worktree must use
  `wl --worklog-dir <main-checkout>/.worklog`.

## Desired change — implementation notes

- Introduce one small shared helper (e.g. `skill/shared/test_tmpdir.py`) that
  (a) resolves the disk-backed temp dir in the documented precedence order,
  creating it as needed, and (b) prunes stale `pytest-of-<user>/pytest-*`
  roots; both fail-open and return a reason string for logging.
- Call it from `_suite_command_env()` (TMPDIR) and from the full-scope path in
  `run_tests.py` (prune), then export the resolved TMPDIR from `implement.py`
  before build/test and before the finish gate's `git push` spawn.
- Log at INFO when a disk-backed TMPDIR is chosen and when roots are pruned
  (count + freed path), at DEBUG/WARNING when a candidate is unusable.

## Key files (predicted)

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — TMPDIR resolution + prune hook + logging
  (`_suite_command_env`, full-scope entry path).
- `skill/shared/test_tmpdir.py` *(new)* — TMPDIR resolution + stale-root prune
  helpers (single source of truth, importable by both skills).
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — export TMPDIR to build/test
  subprocesses and the finish-gate `git push` child env.
- `.githooks/pre-push`, `.githooks/pre-push.v2` — verify inheritance only (no
  expected change).
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — hook install path (verify no change needed).
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — precedence, prune, failure signature,
  remedy; cross-reference from `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`.
- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_tmpdir.py` *(new)*,
  `skill/test/tests/test_prune_stale_test_roots.py` *(new)* — run_tests tests
  live under `skill/test/tests/`, not a top-level `tests/`.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_test_tmpdir.py` *(new, if the helper lands in
  `skill/shared/`)* — helper unit tests.

## Related work

- Observed during **MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV** (tce-main-street) dev-push gate.
- **SA-0MW2QEZBG009I3AI** (high, open) — host-hardening follow-up (option 3):
  age-based `systemd-tmpfiles` cleanup for the churn directories. Independent
  of this item; neither blocks the other (this item is the framework fix, that
  one the host belt-and-braces).
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — existing analysis of `TMPDIR`/`--basetemp`
  misresolution (a different, contributing hazard: stale roots under a live
  checkout).
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — finish-gate temp-index / isolated
  `TMPDIR` behaviour that AC4 must stay compatible with.

## Risks & assumptions

- Disk-backed temp is slower than tmpfs; acceptable for test churn (correctness
  over microbenchmark). Default only when the ambient tmpfs is small.
- `/var/tmp` may not exist (macOS/Windows) → safe fallback required.
- The prune must never delete an active run's root: keep the current target and
  newest roots, use a generous age threshold, and treat errors as fail-open.
- Prune-by-`mtime` can still race a long-running suite whose root is outside
  the keep window; mitigated by the generous default threshold, the
  newest-N keep set and the `pytest-current` target protection.
- Exporting `TMPDIR` from `implement.py` must not leak into the parent shell of
  an interactive session — scope it to the spawned child environments.
- Scope-creep risk: host-level `systemd-tmpfiles` rules and Playwright/`tsx`
  cache cleanup belong to **SA-0MW2QEZBG009I3AI**, not here; record any new
  opportunity as a linked work item rather than widening this one.
- Assumption: the gate's infrastructure classification path
  (`GATE_FAILURE_UNPARSED` in `implement.py`) stays as-is; this item only pins
  the `ENOSPC`-in-Playwright signature against it.

## Evidence

- `df -i /tmp` → `1048576 1048576 0 100%`; `/` (disk) → ~30M free inodes.
- 42 stale `pytest-of-rgardler/pytest-*` roots ≈ 312k files; pruning roots
  older than 20 min freed ~679k inodes.
- Gate failure text: `ENOSPC` in `@vitest/browser` `PlaywrightBrowserProvider.createContext`;
  `notice_codes: ["unparsed_failure"]`.

data.description:
# Harden /tmp inode headroom — age-based cleanup for test churn directories (host runbook)

## Goal (user story)

As the host owner of a multi-agent workstation, I want age-based cleanup of the
directories that test and build runs churn in `/tmp`, so inode headroom is
reclaimed automatically and a future runner that skips the framework prune
still cannot exhaust `/tmp` inodes.

## Context

Follow-up to the critical framework item (disk-backed `TMPDIR` + stale
pytest-root prune in `run_tests.py`/`implement.py`). That fix prevents new
inode pressure from the test runner; this item is the **host-level belt-and-
braces**: `systemd-tmpfiles` currently only carries `q /tmp 1777 root root 10d`,
so rapid multi-agent churn (stale `pytest-of-*` roots, Playwright/Chromium
profiles, `tsx`/node compile caches) can still fill the tmpfs inode table long
before the 10-day sweep. Observed in practice: `/tmp` at 100 % inodes
(1,048,576 total) while byte usage was ~24 %.

## Desired change (option 3)

Add age-based cleanup rules (systemd-tmpfiles preferred; cron acceptable where
tmpfiles is unavailable) for the high-churn temp directories, with an age
threshold longer than the longest test run, and document a runbook so the
remediation is repeatable.

Candidate patterns (refine during implementation):

- `/tmp/pytest-of-%u/pytest-*`
- `/tmp/playwright*`, `/tmp/.org.chromium.Chromium.*`, `/tmp/.com.google.Chrome.*`
- `/tmp/tsx-*`, `/tmp/node-compile-cache*`

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Rules installed and version-controlled/documented.** Age-based cleanup
   rules exist for the churn patterns above (e.g. `/etc/tmpfiles.d/pi-test-tmp.conf`
   with `e`/`q` lines, age ≥ 1 day), with the exact content recorded in the
   repo (runbook or a committed template under `docs/dev/` or `scripts/`).
2. **Verified.** `systemd-tmpfiles --clean --dry-run` (or the cron equivalent)
   lists the intended removals, and a before/after `df -i /tmp` demonstrates
   reclaimed inodes. Evidence captured in a work-item comment.
3. **Safety.** The age threshold is strictly greater than the longest full-suite
   run (currently ~48 min measured worst case), rules are user-scoped where
   possible, and the active `pytest-current` target / newest root is never
   removed.
4. **Runbook.** `docs/dev/testing.md` (or a new `docs/dev/host-hygiene.md`)
   documents install, verify, rollback, and the inode-exhaustion failure
   signature (`ENOSPC` in Playwright `createContext`, `df -i /tmp` at 100 %,
   gate `reason: unparsed`/`infrastructure`).
5. **No repo code change required for the cleanup itself** beyond the committed
   rule template/runbook; if a scripted installer is added, it is idempotent
   and requires explicit root/host opt-in.

## Key files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/testing.md` or `docs/dev/host-hygiene.md` — runbook + rule template.
- Optional: a committed `scripts/` template for `/etc/tmpfiles.d/` (documented,
  not auto-installed without opt-in).

## Constraints

- **Requires host/root access** (`/etc/tmpfiles.d/`, `systemd-tmpfiles`). The
  repository change is documentation/template only; the host change is applied
  by the operator and evidenced in a work-item comment.
- Do **not** add rules that delete recent or active test roots.
- Complements, and does not replace, the framework TMPDIR + prune item.

## Related work

- Critical framework fix (option 1 + 2): disk-backed `TMPDIR` + stale
  pytest-root prune in `run_tests.py`/`implement.py`.
- Observed during **MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV** (tce-main-street) dev-push gate.

## Risks

- Over-aggressive age thresholds can delete a long-running test's temp files —
  mitigate with a threshold well above the measured worst case and user scoping.
- Host config drift between machines — the committed rule template keeps it
  reproducible.

## Impact

The host reclaims /tmp inode headroom automatically — age-based cleanup of stale pytest roots and browser/build caches runs daily without operator intervention, so a test runner that skips the framework prune can no longer silently fill the tmpfs inode table (ENOSPC in Playwright, `df -i /tmp` at 100 %).

# Shared disk-backed temp-dir resolver + stale pytest-root prune helper

Parent: SA-0MW2QED9M005FWOK (disk-backed TMPDIR + stale pytest-root prune)

## Goal

Provide one small, standard-library-only shared helper that both the test
runner (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`) and `implement.py` can import, so
there is a single source of truth for (a) resolving a disk-backed temporary
directory and (b) pruning stale `pytest-of-<user>/pytest-*` roots. This is the
foundation feature: it lands the helper and its unit tests before any wiring.

## Background

`/tmp` is tmpfs with 1,048,576 inodes. Under multi-agent load, stale
`/tmp/pytest-of-<user>/pytest-*` roots (~5-20k files each) exhausted it
(`df -i /tmp` at 100 %) while the byte budget was only ~24 % used. Nothing in
the framework sets `TMPDIR`, so every suite subprocess defaults to the small
tmpfs. See the parent item for the full evidence and the two-option desired
change.

## Targeted outcome

A new module `skill/shared/test_tmpdir.py` exposes:

- `resolve_test_tmpdir()` → `(path, reason)` resolving a candidate in the
  documented precedence order:
  1. explicit environment override (documented constant, e.g.
     `PI_TEST_TMPDIR`);
  2. a configured disk-backed dir such as `/var/tmp/pi-test-<uid>` (created
     when absent);
  3. `tempfile.gettempdir()` as the final safe fallback (macOS/Windows/CI).
- `prune_stale_test_roots()` → `(removed_count, reason)` removing
  `pytest-of-<user>/pytest-*` roots older than a configurable threshold
  (default ~60 min), never touching another user's roots, keeping the
  `pytest-current` symlink target and the N most recent roots, and
  best-effort skipping roots an active pytest process may hold. No-op when
  the base directory is absent.
- Both helpers are **fail-open**: any error is caught, logged/returned as a
  reason string, and never raised. No new dependency — `pathlib`, `shutil`,
  `tempfile`, `os` only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `skill/shared/test_tmpdir.py` exists with `resolve_test_tmpdir()` and
      `prune_stale_test_roots()`, each returning a resolved value plus a
      reason string, using only the Python standard library.
- [ ] TMPDIR resolution follows the documented precedence order and creates a
      missing disk-backed directory; when no disk-backed candidate is usable
      it falls back to `tempfile.gettempdir()`.
- [ ] Prune removes `pytest-of-<user>/pytest-*` roots older than the
      threshold, keeps the `pytest-current` target and the newest N roots, is
      scoped to the current user, and is a no-op when the base directory is
      absent.
- [ ] Both helpers are fail-open: a forced error returns a reason string and
      never raises.
- [ ] `skill/shared/tests/test_test_tmpdir.py` covers precedence, the
      no-disk-backed fallback (mocked `tempfile.gettempdir()`), the prune
      safety rules against a temporary fixture directory (stale removed,
      current/newest kept), the base-absent no-op, foreign-user safety, and
      both forced-failure paths.
- [ ] Module docstrings document the precedence order, prune rules, and
      fail-open contract.

## Minimal implementation

- Add `skill/shared/test_tmpdir.py` with the two helpers, a configurable env
  override constant, a configurable age threshold and keep-N constants.
- Implement prune with `Path.iterdir()` + `stat().st_mtime`, resolving the
  `pytest-current` symlink target first and keeping the newest-N roots.
- Keep the user scope to `getpass.getuser()` / `os.getuid()`-equivalent.
- Add the unit tests under `skill/shared/tests/`.
- Do NOT wire into run_tests.py or implement.py here — that is the next
  feature's scope.

## Key files

- `skill/shared/test_tmpdir.py` (new)
- `skill/shared/tests/test_test_tmpdir.py` (new)

## Dependencies

- None (foundation feature).

## Risky assumptions

- `/var/tmp` exists and is disk-backed on the affected Linux host; macOS/CI
  fall back to `tempfile.gettempdir()`.
- The `pytest-current` symlink is created by pytest's `--basetemp`/tmpdir
  machinery; resolve it defensively when absent.
data.title: Shared disk-backed temp-dir resolver + stale pytest-root prune helper

# Wire disk-backed TMPDIR + stale-root prune into the test runner

Parent: SA-0MW2QED9M005FWOK (disk-backed TMPDIR + stale pytest-root prune)
Depends on: F1 (shared `skill/shared/test_tmpdir.py` helper)

## Goal

Make the test runner (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`) pass a disk-backed
`TMPDIR` to every suite command it spawns and prune stale pytest roots before
a full-suite run, without changing any suite command string, cache key or
scope resolution.

## Existing state (verified)

- Every suite command is spawned by `_run_cmd()` with
  `env=_suite_command_env()`; `_suite_command_env()` layers
  `test_runner.subprocess_env_with_scrubbed_overrides()` and
  `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS`. That helper is the single insertion point for
  `TMPDIR` — the scrub touches only repository overrides, so `TMPDIR` passes
  through untouched today and is simply never set.
- The full-scope path resolves commands inside `run_all(...)` (the
  `if commands is None` branch, `resolvable_scope = "full"`); the prune hook
  belongs there (or in `guarded_run_all` before `run_all`), so it runs at
  least for full scope.

## Targeted outcome

- `_suite_command_env()` sets `TMPDIR` from
  `shared.test_tmpdir.resolve_test_tmpdir()` (the helper from F1), logging at
  INFO when a disk-backed dir is chosen and at DEBUG/WARNING when a candidate
  is unusable.
- The full-scope entry path calls
  `shared.test_tmpdir.prune_stale_test_roots()` before executing, logging the
  removed count + freed paths at INFO.
- Both calls are fail-open: any helper error is logged and the run proceeds
  unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `_suite_command_env()` sets a disk-backed `TMPDIR` on the child env for
      every suite command; a unit test asserts the env handed to the spawned
      command carries the resolved TMPDIR, and covers the fallback path when
      no disk-backed candidate exists.
- [ ] The full-scope path invokes the stale-root prune before execution; a
      unit test asserts the prune is invoked for full scope (and that a
      changed-scope run does not regress command selection).
- [ ] Fail-open is proven by a test that forces the TMPDIR resolver and the
      prune helper to raise and asserts the run's exit status, cache entry and
      scope resolution are unchanged (log only).
- [ ] Suite command strings, cache keys and changed/full scope resolution are
      byte-identical (env-only change); a regression test pins the command
      string / cache key.
- [ ] Logging uses INFO for a chosen disk-backed TMPDIR and for pruned roots,
      DEBUG/WARNING for an unusable candidate.

- [ ] No behaviour change to test selection or caching: changed/full scope
      resolution, cache keys and the audit-accepted full-suite cache entry
      are unchanged (the TMPDIR/prune work is env-only and does not alter
      any suite command string).

## Minimal implementation

- Import the F1 helpers in `run_tests.py`.
- In `_suite_command_env()`: resolve TMPDIR once (module-level cache is
  acceptable) and set `env["TMPDIR"]`.
- In `guarded_run_all()` (before `run_all`) or the full-scope branch of
  `run_all`: call the prune when the resolved scope is full.
- Add `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_tmpdir.py` and
  `skill/test/tests/test_prune_stale_test_roots.py`.
- Never rewrite a command string; never alter cache key derivation.

## Key files

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `_suite_command_env` + full-scope prune hook + logging
- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_tmpdir.py` (new)
- `skill/test/tests/test_prune_stale_test_roots.py` (new)

## Dependencies

- F1 (helper module + unit tests).

## Risky assumptions

- `_suite_command_env()` is the only child-env construction path for suite
  commands (verified: `_run_cmd()` is the single spawn point).
- Pruning before a changed-scope run is unnecessary; full scope is the
  churn-heavy path the bug reported.
data.title: Wire disk-backed TMPDIR + stale-root prune into the test runner

# implement.py parity — export disk-backed TMPDIR to build/test/push children

Parent: SA-0MW2QED9M005FWOK (disk-backed TMPDIR + stale pytest-root prune)
Depends on: F1 (shared `skill/shared/test_tmpdir.py` helper)

## Goal

Close the observed failure end-to-end: the finish gate's `git push` child and
the build/test subprocesses must inherit the same disk-backed `TMPDIR` that
the test runner uses, so the pre-push full-suite hook never runs on the
inode-starved tmpfs.

## Existing state (verified)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` imports the test-skill helpers and
  runs the suite in-process via `run_tests.guarded_run_all`, so runner-side
  env changes are inherited there.
- The push path is different: `git_push_to_dev()` spawns
  `["git", "push", ...]` with `env={**os.environ}`. The pre-push hook then
  runs `run_tests.py` as a child of `git push`, so it only sees a `TMPDIR`
  that `implement.py` has exported into its own environment (or the push
  child env).

## Targeted outcome

- `implement.py` resolves the disk-backed TMPDIR via the F1 helper and
  exports it into the environment of:
  1. the build subprocess,
  2. the in-process/full-suite test step (child subprocesses it spawns), and
  3. the finish-gate `git push` child (`env={**os.environ}` augmented with the
     resolved `TMPDIR`).
- The export is scoped to spawned child environments: it must not leak into
  the parent interactive shell after the run.
- Fail-open: a resolution error is logged and the push/build proceeds with the
  ambient environment.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `git_push_to_dev()` adds the resolved disk-backed `TMPDIR` to the
      `git push` child environment, so the pre-push hook's `run_tests.py`
      inherits it.
- [ ] The build subprocess and the test-suite step inherit the same resolved
      `TMPDIR`.
- [ ] The export is scoped to child environments and does not mutate the
      operator's parent shell environment.
- [ ] Fail-open: a helper error is logged and the push/build proceeds
      unchanged (exit status unchanged).
- [ ] A test asserts the push child env carries the resolved `TMPDIR` and that
      the build/test env carries it; a forced-failure test proves fail-open.

- [ ] implement.py parity: the finish build/test/push subprocesses (and
      therefore the pre-push full-suite gate) inherit the same disk-backed
      `TMPDIR`, so the observed failure mode is closed end-to-end.

## Minimal implementation

- Import `resolve_test_tmpdir` from the F1 helper (with the same
  import-fallback pattern already used for the test-skill helpers).
- Resolve once per `finish` invocation; inject `TMPDIR` into the child envs
  (build Popen, push Popen). Prefer passing it explicitly to the subprocess
  call rather than leaking into `os.environ`; if a global export is needed for
  the in-process `guarded_run_all`, save/restore around the call.
- Add `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_tmpdir.py`.

## Key files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — build/test/push child env
- `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_tmpdir.py` (new)

## Dependencies

- F1 (helper module).

## Risky assumptions

- The pre-push hook creates no temp dirs of its own and relies on inheritance
  (verified: `.githooks/pre-push` / `pre-push.v2` only invoke
  `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env`).
- The finish gate's temporary-index / isolated-`TMPDIR` behaviour
  (`docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`) stays compatible: the disk-backed
  TMPDIR replaces only the ambient default, not any explicit gate override.

# Full-suite runs can be corrupted mid-run by a concurrent `finish` fast-forward — detect, report and quarantine (`state_changed_during_run`)

> **Tracking:** AI_Hell `AH-0MW0PIE3A005N704` (discovered-from), closed against this item.
> **Supersedes the unimplemented part of** `SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2` (completed `done`, but `grep -rn state_changed_during_run skill/` returns nothing — the contract was never built) and of `AH-0MVSRO0MM004T450` (closed 2026-10-30 as "covered").
> **Producer decisions already taken** (AI_Hell `AH-0MW0PIE3A005N704`, 2026-11-05): Q1 = implement here; Q2 = **HEAD + tracked-tree content of the guarded root, with the existing concurrent-churn attribution**; Q3 = **verification only** — no suite↔finish lock, no forced pinned-worktree execution.

## Problem

A full-suite run started in a checkout can be corrupted **mid-run** when another session's `implement.py finish` fast-forwards that checkout's local `dev` (commit → ff → push). Vitest transforms/imports test files lazily over the whole run, so files rewritten by the incoming commit are picked up part-way through: the run then executes the **new** test files against the **old** sources and reports failures that exist in neither tree.

Three verified defects make this worse than a misreported red:

1. **The live-repo guard cannot see it.** `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` excludes `refs/heads/dev` from the mutation surface **and keeps it silent** (`CONCURRENCY_EXCLUDED_REF_EXACT`; absent from `NOTED_CONCURRENCY_EXCLUDED_REF_NAMESPACES`). The main checkout is normally *on* `dev`, so a fast-forward moves HEAD and rewrites tracked files while `git status --porcelain=v1 -uall` is clean **before and after** (git updates index and worktree together). `_detect_live_repo_mutation()` therefore returns `{"mutation": None}` and `guarded_run_all()` leaves `success` exactly as the mixed suite reported it. The in-code claim at `CONCURRENCY_EXCLUDED_REF_EXACT` that "the incident class stays detectable through the config / working-tree / non-excluded-ref surfaces" is **false** for the own-checkout fast-forward case.
2. **The mixed verdict is cached as evidence for the wrong tree.** `skill/test_cache.py:run_cached()` recomputes `compute_git_state()` after the runner returns and `store()`s the entry under the **post-run** state (deliberate — WL-0MVPO9P610055UQ3 — so a finished run stays queryable), keeping the pre-run value only as `git_state_at_start` metadata. Nothing compares the two, so a mixed red verdict becomes the cached verdict for the **new** commit, and `lookup()`/`query_cached()`/`run_tests.py --summary`/audit F3 all read that key.
3. **One consumer path has no snapshot at all.** `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:_run_suite_and_triage()` calls `test_cache.run_cached(..., force=True)` directly — no `guarded_run_all`, so no snapshot anywhere — and then feeds **every** parsed failure to `triage.scripts.check_or_create.check_or_create()`. An audit F3 auto-run in the shared checkout during a concurrent finish can mint critical `test-failure` items unguarded.

Why it matters: gate evidence and post-push verification are audit inputs. A mixed-tree result can create spurious critical `test-failure` items and can make a *green* tree look red — or a *red* tree look green.

## Evidence (AI_Hell, 2026-11-03 — artefacts still on disk)

- `.worklog/cache/8293e13df8005acbb052446a38652826/metadata.json`: `command=npm --silent test`, `scope=full`, `exit_code=1`, `completed_at=2026-11-03T13:02:07Z`, `git_state_at_start=fd2628298f93…`, `git_state=2c9fc30ca6b6…`, **no** `notice`/`live_repo_mutation` field.
- Its `stdout.txt`: `Test Files 2 failed | 419 passed (421)` / `Tests 13 failed | 9565 passed (9578)`; failing files `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts` (8 tests, 1 failed) and `src/core/featureFlags.test.ts` (24 tests, 12 failed).
- Main-checkout reflog: `86f39d30 dev@{2026-11-03 12:54:44}` → `06ecf940 dev@{2026-11-03 12:58:23}: merge refs/remotes/origin/dev: Fast-forward`. Re-running the suite in a stable worktree at `86f39d30` was green (421 files / 9578 tests); both files pass in isolation at `06ecf940`.
- Scale in that one checkout: **14 of 372** cached entries have `git_state_at_start != git_state`; **8 of the 14 are red**; 10 of the 14 are full-suite runs.
- Earlier recurrences of the same mechanism: `AH-0MVVE2QFP002HSUD` (2026-10-30, `bulletVisuals.test.ts`, 4 failures), the `CombatEffectVisuals` case recorded on `AH-0MVSRO0MM004T450` (2026-10-30, 6 failures, and a spurious critical triage item).

## Users

- **Primary:** AI agents and the automated triage bot consuming test results — they must never see a failure record for a state that existed at no single commit.
- **Secondary:** the audit's F3 auto-verification and the `implement.py` finish gate — they must classify a moved-checkout outcome as infrastructure and must not consume its cache entry as evidence.
- **Tertiary:** operators of a shared checkout that routinely has a suite running while another session's finish fast-forwards it.

## Desired change

1. **Verify, then trust.** Compare the checkout state **before** and **after** execution: the guarded root's own `HEAD` commit **plus** the tracked-tree content it resolves to (Q2 = b). Reuse the existing foreign-churn attribution (`excluded_churn_notes()` / `diff_guarded_roots()`, SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG, AH-0MUIIJ3820034WAZ) so concurrent churn attributable to another session never flags a run.
2. **Report it, never as a test failure.** On mismatch emit a stable machine-readable notice (`state_changed_during_run`) naming the before/after commit and the checkout, set the run non-green with a distinct non-zero exit status, and drop the parsed failure records for that command.
3. **Quarantine the evidence.** Store **no** cache entry under the pre-run *or* post-run state.
4. **Classify uniformly.** `implement.py`'s finish gate reports the flagged outcome as infrastructure (never `test_failure`) with a message naming the checkout movement and the required re-run; `audit_runner.py` skips `check_or_create()` for a flagged command and still refuses a green verdict.
5. **No change on the stable path.** Identical cache key, TTL, failure parsing and triage behaviour when the state does not move (pinned by a control test).
6. **Verification only (Q3 = a).** No suite↔finish lock, no forced pinned-worktree execution in this item. If prevention is wanted later, raise separate items.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Moved-checkout runs are reported, not failed.** A run whose guarded checkout moves between start and end (HEAD and/or the tracked tree it resolves to) emits `state_changed_during_run` in machine-readable output (flag + stable `notice_code` + before/after commit + checkout path), a distinct non-zero exit status, and **no** structured failure records — regardless of whether its output contains parseable test failures.
- [ ] **AC2 — Moved-checkout evidence is quarantined.** Such a run writes **no** cache entry under the pre-run *or* post-run state, so `lookup()`, `query_cached()`, `run_tests.py --summary` and the audit cannot consume it as gate evidence for any tree. Directly targets the 2026-11-03 entry, whose `git_state` is the post-run commit.
- [ ] **AC3 — No false positives on legitimate concurrent churn.** A run whose only difference is churn attributable to another session (existing `excluded_churn_notes` / `diff_guarded_roots` attribution; `refs/heads/dev`, `refs/remotes/origin/*` and `refs/heads/worklog/*` movement elsewhere in the checkout) is **not** flagged: it stores, serves and triages exactly as today. Pinned by an attributed-churn control test.
- [ ] **AC4 — Consumers classify it as infrastructure.** The `implement.py` finish gate classifies a flagged run as infrastructure (never `test_failure`) and its operator-visible message names the checkout movement and the required re-run; `audit_runner.py`'s F3 auto-run makes no `check_or_create()` call for a flagged command, reports the notice, and still fails the verdict rather than reporting green.
- [ ] **AC5 — Regression coverage.** Automated tests simulate a mid-run checkout move by injecting a runner stub into `run_cached(..., runner=…)` that moves `HEAD` during the call, asserting: notice raised with both commits, no cache entry under either state, no failure records, non-green status. Controls: (a) a stable run producing today's store/hit/failure behaviour; (b) an attributed-foreign-churn run that is not flagged (AC3); (c) a tracked-file rewrite with an unchanged `HEAD` (the Q2=b extra dimension).
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` documents the notice code and the gate diagnostics; `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8 corrects the "own-checkout fast-forward stays detectable through the other surfaces" claim and records the new surface. (Informational cross-repo note: AI_Hell's `docs/dev/test-suite-timing.md` currently points at `SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2` as pending — the AH tracking item records that it should be repointed once this ships.)
- [ ] **AC7 — Testing/validation criterion.** The affected suites (test-cache, runner/guard, implement gate, audit) pass, including the new regressions, and the change ships with the tests that would have failed before it.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite.** The full project test suite passes with the new changes, run through the test skill from a stable checkout.

## Constraints

- **Do not make `refs/heads/dev` verdict-bearing.** The exclusion exists because that movement is routine multi-agent churn; detect the **own checkout's tree movement** instead of re-admitting the shared integration branch to the mutation surface.
- **The attribution contract must hold.** Any new "state moved" signal must reuse the existing foreign-churn attribution or it resurrects a closed false-positive class (AH-0MUIIJ3820034WAZ, SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG).
- **The dev-push gate needs no change.** `.githooks/pre-push` passes `--gate-commit <pushed sha>` and the runner resolves a checkout whose `HEAD` is that commit with no dirty paths, so the release gate verdict is already bound to the pushed tree.
- **Cost.** Full suites run 200–400 s under load; Q3 = a deliberately adds no serialisation.
- **CHANGELOG.md** is out of scope (managed by the ship pipeline's release step).
- **No ad-hoc test invocations** — every agent-initiated run goes through the test skill.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test_cache.py` — `run_cached()`: compare start/end checkout state; on mismatch skip `store()` and return `state_changed_during_run` with both commits.
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — own-checkout HEAD/tree fingerprint helper (or a scoped wrapper over `compute_git_state`); keep `refs/heads/dev` silent for the verdict and reuse `excluded_churn_notes` attribution.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — surface the flag in the aggregate (`notice_codes`), drop failure records for that command, exit non-green.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_gate_failure_kind()` / `_gate_failure_detail()`: classify the flag as infrastructure **before** any failure-based classification.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_run_suite_and_triage()`: skip `check_or_create()` for a flagged command.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`, `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8 — notice code and the corrected guard-surface claim.
- Tests: `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py`, `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py`, `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py`, plus the test-cache suite.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — detection granularity.** A whole-checkout `compute_git_state()` comparison would flag any concurrent working-tree churn; scoping the comparison to the guarded root's own HEAD/tree while reusing attribution is the mitigation, pinned by AC3/AC5(b).
- **Risk — half a fix.** Adding only the notice without quarantining the cache entry leaves the damaging half in place (AC2).
- **Risk — silent green.** An implementation that reports the flag but still lets `success=True` through would let a red tree pass (AC1/AC4).
- **Assumption.** `git_state_at_start` is already recorded on every worktree-fingerprint cache entry, so the comparison needs no cache-schema change.
- **Assumption.** No consumer relies on a cached entry for a moved-checkout run (by definition none should).
- **Scope-creep risk.** Suite↔finish locking, always-run-in-a-pinned-worktree, or making the `dev`-ref exclusion verdict-bearing are separate items; raise them separately if wanted.

## Related work

- `AH-0MW0PIE3A005N704` — the AI_Hell tracking item (full intake brief, AC1–AC8, producer Q1/Q2/Q3 answers). Closed against this item.
- `AH-0MVSRO0MM004T450` — same design, closed 2026-10-30 as "covered" by `SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2`; the contract was never implemented.
- `AH-0MVVE2QFP002HSUD` — the 2026-10-30 recurrence (and the AI_Hell operational doc `docs/dev/test-suite-timing.md`).
- `AH-0MUIIJ3820034WAZ` — cross-repo precedent; the concurrent-churn false-positive class this change must not regress.
- `SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2` (+ children `SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB`, `SA-0MVQHVBCC0083VK5`) — the finish-gate/cache-provenance family: completed, but the start≠end drift dimension was never built.
- `SA-0MVEJIRZ60017H4V` — open: unify the test-cache namespace across worktrees and the main checkout (relevant only if a pinned-worktree approach is ever chosen).
- `WL-0MVPO9P610055UQ3` — why the cache entry is keyed on the post-run state (the constraint this change must respect).
- `WL-0MV5MYBKJ0033P8U`, `SA-0MV8311B3005DNG8`, `SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG`, `SA-0MVV2W9610002CLW` — the guard's exclusion/attribution decisions this change must not undo.
