# Regression harness: inject a mid-run checkout move

TDD-first child of `SA-0MW3FF18I003KGZE` (AC5). Writes the failing tests that pin the whole
`state_changed_during_run` contract **before** any implementation child lands, so the rest of the
decomposition is test-driven.

The tests inject a runner stub into `run_cached(..., runner=…)` that mutates the checkout **while
the call is in flight**, which is the only way to reproduce the 2026-11-03 mixed-tree run
deterministically (no reliance on a real concurrent `finish`).

## Contract under test (agreed in the parent plan)

- `run_cached()` returns `state_changed_during_run=None` normally; on movement it returns a dict
  `{"notice_code": "state_changed_during_run", "checkout": <abs path>, "before_commit": <sha>,
  "after_commit": <sha>, "message": <human text>}`.
- A flagged run's `exit_code` is the distinct, exported `STATE_CHANGED_EXIT_CODE` (75, `EX_TEMPFAIL`)
  rather than the stub's own exit code, and `cached` is `False`.
- No cache entry is written under the pre-run **or** post-run fingerprint.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A new `TestStateChangedDuringRun` class in `tests/test_test_cache.py` builds a real checkout under `tmp_path` (via `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` helpers) and drives `run_cached()` with a runner stub that commits during the call.
- [ ] Moved-checkout case asserts `result["state_changed_during_run"]` names the notice code, the resolved checkout path, the pre-run commit and the post-run commit.
- [ ] Moved-checkout case asserts `result["exit_code"] == test_cache.STATE_CHANGED_EXIT_CODE` and `result["cached"] is False`.
- [ ] Moved-checkout case asserts `lookup()` misses under **both** the pre-run and the post-run fingerprint, and that no cache entry directory exists for either key.
- [ ] Control (a) — stable run: a run that does not move still stores, a second identical call is served from cache (`cached is True`), and the stub's own exit code and output are preserved unchanged.
- [ ] Control (b) — attributed foreign churn: a checkout that starts with a dirty tracked path which the stub resolves (another session committing work it had itself dirtied) is **not** flagged and does store its entry.
- [ ] Control (c) — tracked-file rewrite with an unchanged `HEAD` is flagged exactly like a commit move (the Q2 = b dimension).
- [ ] The new tests fail against the current tree (no `state_changed_during_run` key, no `STATE_CHANGED_EXIT_CODE`) and are the regression net for the implementation children.
- [ ] AC5 — Regression coverage. Automated tests simulate a mid-run checkout move by injecting a runner stub into run_cached(..., runner=…) that moves HEAD during the call, asserting: notice raised with both commits, no cache entry under either state, no failure records, non-green status. Controls: (a) a stable run producing today's store/hit/failure behaviour; (b) an attributed-foreign-churn run that is not flagged (AC3); (c) a tracked-file rewrite with an unchanged HEAD (the Q2=b extra dimension). (parent traceability: AC5).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add the git fixture helper(s) the tests need (init repo, commit, dirty a tracked path, fast-forward a branch) reusing `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — no new fixture infrastructure.
2. Write the three test groups (move by commit, move by tracked-file rewrite, controls a/b/c) against the contract above.
3. Run the affected scope through the test skill and record the expected red output (the tests must fail for the right reason: missing contract, not a fixture error).

## Deliverables

- New test classes in `tests/test_test_cache.py` only (no production code).
- Recorded red-run evidence in a work-item comment.

**Key Files:**

- `tests/test_test_cache.py`
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`

# Own-checkout state snapshot with foreign-churn attribution

Child of `SA-0MW3FF18I003KGZE` (AC3, Q2 = b). Adds the read-only comparison primitive the detection
path needs: the guarded checkout's own `HEAD` commit **plus** the tracked-tree content it resolves
to — never the ref surface — with the existing concurrent-churn attribution applied so routine
multi-agent churn never flags a run.

This is the piece that closes defect 1 of the parent: `refs/heads/dev` stays concurrency-excluded and
**silent**, so a fast-forward of the main checkout moves `HEAD` and rewrites tracked files while
`git status --porcelain=v1 -uall` is clean before and after. The new surface is the checkout's own
state, not the shared integration branch being verdict-bearing.

## Design constraints

- Reuse `diff_snapshots()`'s existing start-of-run provenance attribution rather than inventing a
  second rule: a path dirty at the start snapshot and clean at the end is concurrent churn. Any new
  "state moved" signal that bypasses the attribution resurrects the closed false-positive class
  (`AH-0MUIIJ3820034WAZ`, `SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG`).
- `refs/heads/dev`, `refs/remotes/origin/*` and `refs/heads/worklog/*` movement must stay invisible
  to this surface (no ref comparison at all is the simplest compliant choice).
- Read-only plumbing only; standby cost must stay comparable to today's `compute_git_state()` call
  (Q3 = verification only — no lock, no serialisation, no pinned-worktree execution).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A stdlib-only helper in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` returns, for one checkout, its current `HEAD` commit and a fingerprint of the tracked-tree content it resolves to.
- [ ] A comparison helper returns `{"moved": bool, "checkout": <path>, "before_commit": <sha>, "after_commit": <sha>, "attributed": [<note>, …]}` — naming the checkout that moved and both commits.
- [ ] A `HEAD`-only move (fast-forward) is reported as moved with distinct before/after commits.
- [ ] A tracked-file rewrite with an unchanged `HEAD` is reported as moved (the Q2 = b dimension).
- [ ] A difference fully explained by start-of-run-dirty → end-clean resolution is attributed (reported in `attributed`, `moved` false) and reuses the existing attribution code path, not a copy of the rule.
- [ ] Movement of `refs/heads/dev`, `refs/remotes/origin/*` or `refs/heads/worklog/*` alone does not report `moved`.
- [ ] Unit tests cover the helper directly in `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py`, including the pre-existing attribution classes and a pinned boundary for the clean→dirty direction.
- [ ] No change to `snapshot_repo_state()`, `diff_snapshots()` or `fingerprint()` behaviour (existing guard tests stay green unmodified).
- [ ] AC3 — No false positives on legitimate concurrent churn. A run whose only difference is churn attributable to another session (existing excluded_churn_notes / diff_guarded_roots attribution; refs/heads/dev, refs/remotes/origin/* and refs/heads/worklog/* movement elsewhere in the checkout) is not flagged: it stores, serves and triages exactly as today. Pinned by an attributed-churn control test. (parent traceability: AC3).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Extend `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` with the per-checkout state snapshot (HEAD via `rev-parse HEAD`, tracked content via the existing status/plumbing helpers) and the comparison helper.
2. Route resolution differences through the existing `diff_snapshots()` attribution (`excluded_working_tree_churn` / `excluded_churn_notes`) so the note vocabulary is shared.
3. Add the unit tests to `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py`.

## Deliverables

- Helper + unit tests, documented in the module docstring (one paragraph stating the new surface and
  why `refs/heads/dev` remains silent).

**Key Files:**

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`
- `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py`
- `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py`

# run_cached: flag, quarantine and non-green exit status

Child of `SA-0MW3FF18I003KGZE` (AC1, AC2, AC3). Wires the detection helper into
`skill/test_cache.py:run_cached()` so a checkout that moves mid-run is **reported** and its evidence
is **quarantined** — the two halves must land together (the parent's "half a fix" risk).

Today `run_cached()` recomputes `compute_git_state()` after the runner returns and `store()`s the
entry under the **post-run** state (`WL-0MVPO9P610055UQ3`), keeping the pre-run value only as
`git_state_at_start` metadata. Nothing compares the two, so a mixed verdict becomes the cached verdict
for the new commit and `lookup()`, `query_cached()`, `run_tests.py --summary` and audit F3 all read it.

## Contract

- On movement: do **not** call `store()` for either fingerprint; return
  `state_changed_during_run = {"notice_code": "state_changed_during_run", "checkout": …, "before_commit": …, "after_commit": …, "message": …}`,
  `exit_code = STATE_CHANGED_EXIT_CODE` (75, exported), `cached = False`, `git_state = ""`.
- No movement: today's behaviour byte for byte — same cache key, TTL, stored metadata, `cached`
  semantics and exit code.
- Indeterminate fingerprints keep the existing fail-closed behaviour (no lookup, no store) and are
  never reported as movement.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `skill/test_cache.py` exports `STATE_CHANGED_EXIT_CODE = 75` and a `state_changed_during_run` result key that is `None` on every non-moved run (including cache hits, `no_cache=True` and indeterminate-state bypasses).
- [ ] A moved run writes no cache entry: no directory or `metadata.json` exists under the pre-run or post-run fingerprint, and `lookup()` misses for both.
- [ ] A moved run returns the flag with the checkout path, before/after commits and a human message naming the movement and the required re-run.
- [ ] A moved run's `exit_code` is `STATE_CHANGED_EXIT_CODE` even when the runner stub exited 0, and `cached` is `False`.
- [ ] The explicit-fingerprint path (`fingerprint=<tree sha>`, the finish gate) also compares the checkout state and quarantines on movement, while still keying non-moved runs on the supplied fingerprint exactly as today.
- [ ] Attributed foreign churn (AC3) does not flag and does store, pinned end-to-end through `run_cached()`.
- [ ] The regression tests from the harness child pass; the existing test-cache suite passes unmodified except where the new behaviour is asserted.
- [ ] AC1 — Moved-checkout runs are reported, not failed. A run whose guarded checkout moves between start and end (HEAD and/or the tracked tree it resolves to) emits state_changed_during_run in machine-readable output (flag + stable notice_code + before/after commit + checkout path), a distinct non-zero exit status, and no structured failure records — regardless of whether its output contains parseable test failures. (parent traceability: AC1).
- [ ] AC2 — Moved-checkout evidence is quarantined. Such a run writes no cache entry under the pre-run or post-run state, so lookup(), query_cached(), run_tests.py --summary and the audit cannot consume it as gate evidence for any tree. Directly targets the 2026-11-03 entry, whose git_state is the post-run commit. (parent traceability: AC2).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Capture the per-checkout state before the runner executes, alongside the existing fingerprint.
2. After the runner returns, re-capture and compare; on movement skip both `store()` calls, return the flag and the distinct exit code.
3. Document the flag, the exit code and the quarantine rule in the module docstring (entry layout and
   `run_cached()` docs).

## Deliverables

- `skill/test_cache.py` changes + module documentation.

# Test skill: aggregate the notice, drop failures, exit non-green

Child of `SA-0MW3FF18I003KGZE` (AC1, runner surface). `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` must surface
the cache flag as a **stable machine-readable notice** and must never publish the mixed run's parsed
failures or a green verdict.

## Contract

- `run_suite()` on a flagged command: `notice_code = NOTICE_STATE_CHANGED_DURING_RUN`
  (`"state_changed_during_run"`), a human `notice` naming the checkout, both commits and the required
  re-run, `failures = []` for that command, `returncode = exit_code = STATE_CHANGED_EXIT_CODE`,
  `success = False`, and the flag dict carried on the result for consumers that need the detail.
- `run_all()` aggregate: `notice_codes` includes the code, `failures` excludes the flagged command's
  parsed records, `success = False`, and the aggregate carries the flag detail through.
- `guarded_run_all()`: unchanged ownership semantics; a valid (stable) run keeps exactly today's
  result shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `run_suite()` returns `notice_code == "state_changed_during_run"`, `success is False` and `returncode == 75` when `run_cached` reports movement, and carries the checkout/before/after detail.
- [ ] A flagged command contributes **no** structured failure records to `run_suite()["failures"]` or `run_all()["failures"]`, even when its stdout contains the failure text the parser would otherwise match.
- [ ] `run_all()` puts the code in `notice_codes` and fails the aggregate (`success is False`) — never a green verdict.
- [ ] The CLI/json output exposes the code and detail (a `--json` report contains `state_changed_during_run` for the suite and/or the aggregate).
- [ ] The human-readable output prints one `notice: [state_changed_during_run] …` line naming the checkout movement and telling the operator to re-run.
- [ ] A stable run's suite/aggregate result is unchanged (control test: same keys, same success, same failures, same `cached`).
- [ ] Docs-consistency tests that pin the notice-code table (see AC6 child) are updated in this child's scope only if they break.
- [ ] AC1 — Moved-checkout runs are reported, not failed. A run whose guarded checkout moves between start and end (HEAD and/or the tracked tree it resolves to) emits state_changed_during_run in machine-readable output (flag + stable notice_code + before/after commit + checkout path), a distinct non-zero exit status, and no structured failure records — regardless of whether its output contains parseable test failures. (parent traceability: AC1).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add `NOTICE_STATE_CHANGED_DURING_RUN` next to the existing notice codes and import the cache exit
   code, so the runner and the cache cannot drift.
2. In `run_suite()`'s per-command loop, short-circuit on the flag: skip failure parsing for that
   command, record the notice and the flag, and force non-zero.
3. Thread the flag through `run_all()`'s aggregate (notice codes, failures, detail).

## Deliverables

- `run_tests.py` changes + tests in `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py` (parse/notice
  behaviour) and the aggregate shape assertions.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`
- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py`
- `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py`

# Finish gate: classify a moved checkout as infrastructure

Child of `SA-0MW3FF18I003KGZE` (AC4, first half). `implement.py`'s finish gate and the shared
`gate_reason.py` classifier must report a flagged run as **infrastructure**, never `test_failure`,
with an operator message that names the checkout movement and the required re-run.

Classification order matters: the flag must be checked **before** any failure-based classification so
a run that still carries (stale or upstream-produced) failure records cannot be reclassified as a code
failure. Likewise no operator should be told to fix tests that were never run against one tree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `skill/test/scripts/gate_reason.py` gains a state-changed reason path: a result carrying the flag classifies as `infrastructure`, and the check runs before the structured-failure test.
- [ ] `skill/test/scripts/gate_reason.py` exposes an operator-facing message for the moved case that names the checkout, the before/after commits and the required re-run.
- [ ] `implement.py`'s `_gate_failure_kind()` returns `GATE_FAILURE_INFRASTRUCTURE` for a flagged result before any `failures`-based branch, and `_gate_failure_detail()` includes the movement detail (checkout + both commits) rather than an empty `Failures:` block.
- [ ] `_gate_failure_message()` produces a headline stating the checkout moved during the run (infrastructure, not a code failure) and the exact re-run command (`python3 scripts/implement.py finish <id>`).
- [ ] The gate's `pre-push` shared classifier path (`gate_reason=<code>`) reports `gate_reason=infrastructure` for a flagged result, pinned by a test in `tests/test_pre_push_gate_reason.py`.
- [ ] A stable red run still classifies as `test_failure` (control: the new branch cannot swallow genuine failures).
- [ ] No change to the dev-push gate's `--gate-commit` subject binding (pinned by the existing gate-subject tests).
- [ ] AC4 — Consumers classify it as infrastructure. The implement.py finish gate classifies a flagged run as infrastructure (never test_failure) and its operator-visible message names the checkout movement and the required re-run; audit_runner.py's F3 auto-run makes no check_or_create() call for a flagged command, reports the notice, and still fails the verdict rather than reporting green. (parent traceability: AC4).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add the notice-code constant and the reason/message branch to `gate_reason.py` (single shared
   vocabulary, so `implement.py` cannot fork it).
2. Reorder `implement.py:_gate_failure_kind()` to consult the flag first, and extend
   `_gate_failure_detail()`/`_gate_failure_message()` with the movement detail.
3. Carry the flag detail through `_adapt_guarded_result()`'s additive-only result contract.

- `gate_reason.py` + `implement.py` changes with gate-classification tests in
  `skill/implement/tests/` and `tests/test_pre_push_gate_reason.py`.

# Audit F3: skip triage for a flagged command

Child of `SA-0MW3FF18I003KGZE` (AC4, second half). `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`'s suite path
calls `test_cache.run_cached(..., force=True)` directly — no `guarded_run_all`, so no outer snapshot —
and then feeds **every** parsed failure to `triage.scripts.check_or_create.check_or_create()`. A
moved-checkout run there can mint spurious critical `test-failure` items.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The audit's suite path (`_run_tests_via_test_skill`) makes **no** `check_or_create()` call for any command whose result carries `state_changed_during_run`.
- [ ] A flagged command contributes no parsed failure records to the audit's failure list; instead the notice is reported (stderr line and the returned `notice`/report field) naming the checkout movement.
- [ ] A flagged command still makes the run non-green: the returned `success` is `False` and the failing verdict is reported rather than green.
- [ ] The returned dict exposes the flagged commands (e.g. a `state_changed_during_run` list) so the audit report can name them.
- [ ] A stable run keeps today's behaviour exactly: failures parsed, triaged, capped and deduplicated as now (control test).
- [ ] Audit tests pin the no-triage behaviour with a patched `run_cached` returning a flagged result and a spy on `check_or_create`.
- [ ] AC4 — Consumers classify it as infrastructure. The implement.py finish gate classifies a flagged run as infrastructure (never test_failure) and its operator-visible message names the checkout movement and the required re-run; audit_runner.py's F3 auto-run makes no check_or_create() call for a flagged command, reports the notice, and still fails the verdict rather than reporting green. (parent traceability: AC4).

## Minimal Implementation

1. In the per-command loop, treat a flagged result like an entry-level failure: record the notice,
   append nothing to `failures`, mark the run unsuccessful, and skip parsing/triage for that command.
2. Include the flagged commands in the returned dict and in the stderr summary line.
3. Add the tests next to the existing audit suite-execution tests.

# finish: retry the local-dev fast-forward after the recovery rebase, and report a pushed-commit-guard refusal distinctly

## Goal (user story)

As an agent whose `dev` push follows a concurrent `dev` advance, when `implement.py finish`
cannot fast-forward the main checkout before the push, I want finish to still leave the main
checkout's `dev` at the pushed commit after the recovery rebase, and to report a
pushed-commit-guard refusal distinguishably (pushed sha, gate HEAD, gate tree) naming the
worktree push as recovery — instead of a generic push failure.

## Background

Cross-reference: **LP-0MVWB6AOH001MAB0** (llm worklog) — "finish pushes from the main checkout
after a refused local-dev fast-forward, so the pre-push pushed-commit guard refuses". The
producer decided (2026-11-05) that the residual scope lands here (SorraAgents) and the llm item
is kept as a cross-reference that owns no code.

The core symptom (push from the main checkout) was already fixed by **SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3**:
`phase_finish` Step 6 and `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` now push from the worktree that holds
the commit. The residual gaps are:

- **AC1 (fast-forward retry).** `_fast_forward_local_dev_for_push` is called only once, in Step 5,
  *before* the push. When it is refused with `local_dev_diverged` / `commit_not_based_on_remote_tip`
  because a sibling moved `dev`, the recovery rebase produces a commit that *is* based on
  `origin/dev`, but the fast-forward is never retried, so the main checkout's local `dev` stays
  behind the pushed commit.
- **AC4 (distinguishable guard refusal).** When `.githooks/pre-push` §3a refuses a push because
  the gate tree is not the pushed commit (or is dirty at it), `git_push_to_dev` finds no
  `gate_reason=` line and reports a generic push failure. Finish cannot tell the operator that
  the guard refused, nor surface the pushed sha / gate HEAD / gate tree the guard printed.

## Scope

In scope: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (the fast-forward retry inside the non-fast-forward
recovery, and a distinct pushed-commit-guard-refusal classification) and its regression tests.

Out of scope: changing `.githooks/pre-push` in consuming projects. The guard's existing stable
diagnostic text is the contract this item detects against; a hook-side `gate_reason=` emission is
a separate follow-up owned by the llm item.

## Acceptance criteria

1. After a **refused** local-dev fast-forward (`local_dev_diverged` / `commit_not_based_on_remote_tip`),
   when `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` rebases the feature branch onto `origin/dev`, `finish`
   **retries** the fast-forward for the rebased commit and records the retry in
   `report["steps"]["local_dev_fast_forward"]`. When the retry succeeds, the main checkout's
   checked-out `dev` HEAD equals the pushed commit before the retry push.
2. The retried fast-forward never fails the finish: a second refusal is recorded (with its
   reason) and the push still proceeds from the worktree — the current recovery behaviour is
   preserved.
3. `finish` detects the pre-push pushed-commit guard's refusal from its stable diagnostic text and
   reports it distinguishably as `report["steps"]["push"]["reason"] == "refused_by_pushed_commit_guard"`
   carrying the **pushed sha**, the **gate HEAD** and the **gate tree** parsed from the guard's
   output, with recovery guidance that names the worktree push. A non-guard push failure keeps its
   existing classification (`test_failure`, `timeout`, `subject_mismatch`, …).
4. Regression tests drive the **concurrent-move shape** (worktree based on `dev~1`, another commit
   landed on `origin/dev`) and assert the guard's preconditions hold at push time: pushed sha ==
   gate-tree HEAD and the gate tree is clean; and assert the main checkout's `dev` is advanced to
   the pushed commit after the recovery rebase. A second test asserts a guard-refusal stderr is
   classified `refused_by_pushed_commit_guard` with the three values, and a generic failure is not.
5. Full project test suite passes.

## Notes

- Guard: `.githooks/pre-push` §3a (LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9); its refusal prints
  `ERROR: pre-push gate refuses this push: the tree it would measure is not the pushed commit.`
  followed by `pushed commit  (refs/heads/dev): <sha>`, `checked-out HEAD: <sha>`,
  `gate tree: <path>` (and a dirty-tree variant).
- `git_push_to_dev` is around line 4815; `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` around line 10021;
  `_fast_forward_local_dev_for_push` around line 6783.
- Related completed: SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3 (push from worktree), SA-0MVSJX5HS002DJHI (gate reason
  vocabulary / transport retry).

## Problem

`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:_resolve_merge_base()` returns the **candidate ref name** (`origin/dev`) rather than the SHA resolved by `git merge-base`, and `compute_changed_files()` then runs `git diff --name-only <ref>` against that name.

When an implement worktree's branch base is *behind* the ref (a stale base — e.g. the branch was forked while local `dev` lagged `origin/dev`), diffing against the ref includes **dev-side** commits that are not part of the change set. `select_group_from_changed_files()` then picks test groups for unrelated work.

Discovered-from: WL-0MW3LTY9A007ZULJ (ContextHub store) — the stale-base session in which this was observed.

## Evidence

- Observed on 2026-11-05 in a ContextHub implement session (WL-0MW3JIYIR002RCP8): a docs + `tests/setup-tests.ts` change set ran `npm test -- packages/herdr/src` because the stale base made the diff include dev-side `packages/herdr` commits.
- Current code (`run_tests.py`, `_resolve_merge_base`, ~line 506): the loop runs `git merge-base <candidate> HEAD`, then `return candidate` (the ref name) — the resolved `proc.stdout.strip()` SHA is discarded.
- `compute_changed_files()` (~line 462) passes the returned value straight into `git diff --name-only <base>`.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running `implement.py finish` / `run_tests.py --scope changed` — depend on correct changed-file selection.
- **Operators / CI** — depend on changed-scope runs exercising the code that actually changed.

### Example user stories

- As an implementation agent, when my worktree forked from a base behind `origin/dev`, I want changed-scope selection to measure only *my* diff, so the gate runs the right tests.
- As an operator, I want a stale base to degrade into a smaller diff, never into an unrelated named group.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `_resolve_merge_base()` returns the SHA resolved by `git merge-base` (falling back to the next candidate only when `merge-base` yields nothing), never a bare ref name.
- [ ] `compute_changed_files()` diffs against a merge-base SHA, so commits that exist on the ref but not on the branch base are excluded from the change set.
- [ ] Regression test: a fixture repo whose branch base is one commit behind the target ref — the changed-file set must contain only the branch's own files, not the ref-side files.

data.description:
## Headline

Make the audit skill immune to a dirty/stale main checkout by running its
execution-dependent work (full-suite green-run gate, and ideally the whole
Phase 1/2 pipeline) inside a **fresh detached worktree checked out at the
latest `origin/dev`** (or the item's merged tip), so an un-pushed in-flight
commit sitting on the main `dev` branch can never contaminate an audit.

## Problem statement

`audit_runner.py` resolves ALL git-derived audit content (HEAD sha,
file-scope manifest, changed files, repo index, working-tree hash, green-run
attestation, and the F3 full-suite execution cwd) against the **local
checkout at the launch cwd** (`TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT`). The merge gate
(`_integrate_into_dev`, SA-0MT456M27001LRTL) and the stale-audit-base guard
(`_audit_base_freshness`, SA-0MT9EK1UU000DT1R) both integrate/verify against
`origin/dev`, but the pipeline still EXECUTES against the launch checkout.

Observed failure (2026-11-06, audit of RISE-0MW19AROF0035FRH in
tce-the-rising): the main checkout's `dev` branch carried a **local-only,
un-pushed, in-flight commit** (`d538e51`, RISE-0MW3GUQKX004W74K) that
modified `risingMatchHarness.ts`/`src/TheRisingAdversary.ts`, and was 6
commits *behind* `origin/dev`. The F3 full-suite gate ran `npm test` in that
contaminated checkout, failed on four integration suites (all import the
changed harness), and produced `Ready to close: No` with AC8 partial on an
item whose own scope was green at its tip. The merge gate passed because the
item's commits ARE ancestors of `origin/dev`; the stale-base guard passed
because they are also ancestors of the local HEAD — neither checks that
local HEAD == `origin/dev` or that there are no extra un-pushed commits.

The stale-audit-base guard only flags "delivered on origin/dev, absent from
local HEAD" (behind). It does not flag **ahead-with-extra-commits** (in-flight
work parked on the main checkout) or **aside** (local HEAD not an ancestor of
origin/dev), and it does not move execution into an isolated worktree.

## Users

- **Audit consumers (producers, implement agents)** — want an audit verdict
  that reflects the state of merged, checked-in dev — never a developer's
  un-pushed local experiments parked on the main checkout.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The audit runner resolves a **fresh, detached worktree at the latest
   `origin/dev`** (fetched before worktree creation) as the execution base
   for the full-suite green-run gate (F3) — the suite runs from that
   worktree, never from the launch checkout — and the worktree is removed
   afterward.
2. The stale-audit-base guard is extended to also abort (with the same loud
   remediation message) when the launch checkout is **ahead of /
   divergent from** `origin/dev` (local HEAD contains commits not in
   `origin/dev`), since an audit must never run against un-pushed in-flight
   work; a launch from a clean worktree of the owning repo stays valid.
3. Where feasible without changing verdict semantics, Phase 1/2 file-scope
   content (manifest, changed-file list, repo index, working-tree hash) also
   resolves against the origin/dev worktree rather than the launch checkout,
   so evidence never reflects a stale/dirty tree.
4. AC1–AC3 are covered by tests using a local bare "remote" with a dirty
   local checkout ahead of origin/dev (an un-pushed commit touching a
   harness file) — asserting the audit refuses/isolates rather than emitting
   misleading `partial`/`No` verdicts.
5. Existing behaviour is unchanged for a clean launch (launch checkout at
   origin/dev, worktree launches, `--do-not-persist`, batch/issue modes,
   `--no-execute`, child in-main-slot screens).
6. Documentation: audit skill reference (`docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`)
   and the audit SKILL.md are updated to state that audits execute inside a
   fresh origin/dev worktree and never against a stale/dirty launch checkout.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — base resolution for F3 suite
  execution, file-scope manifest, and the stale-audit-base guard.
- `skill/audit/scripts/test_cache.py` — cache keys are cwd-scoped; executing
  in a worktree changes the cwd used for cache hits.
- `skill/audit/tests/` — existing runner unit tests (fresh-base + guard
  coverage to extend).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — docs.

## Related work

- `RISE-0MW19AROF0035FRH` (tce-the-rising) — the audit that exposed this
  gap (spurious AC8 partial from a dirty launch checkout).
- `RISE-0MW3GUQKX004W74K` (tce-the-rising) — the work item whose un-pushed
  commit contaminated the main checkout.
- SA-0MT9EK1UU000DT1R — the existing stale-audit-base guard (behind-only).

## Out of scope

- Enforcing "no commits on the main checkout" (that is implement-skill
  hygiene, tracked elsewhere); this item only makes the audit robust to it.
- Changing the merge gate's integration semantics (that is already
  worktree-isolated at origin/dev).
- Verdict semantics, prompts, or the freshness/content-fingerprint gates.

## Implementation constraints (from audit review addenda)

Recorded from the `herdr-audit` review comments on this item
(SA-C0MW50DKU2005VDO1, SA-C0MW50KPXB001WENO), written after the
RISE-0MW12YSRB007979Y and RISE-0MW19AROF0035FRH incidents. These constrain
AC1/AC2/AC4 — they add no new scope.

- **Ordering (AC2 vs F3).** The ahead/divergent check must be evaluated early
  in `_phase_gate`, right after owning-root resolution and *before*
  `_auto_green_run_outcome`, and/or F3 must be fully isolated on the
  origin/dev worktree (recommended: both — isolation first, early abort as
  belt-and-braces). Otherwise the contaminated suite runs and the triage
  helper auto-creates a spurious critical `test-failure` child parented to
  the audited item before any guard fires.
- **Guard scope.** Abort only when the launch checkout *is the owning repo's
  main checkout* and its `dev` is ahead/divergent. A feature-worktree launch
  (`<owning>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-*`) legitimately has a HEAD ahead of
  `origin/dev`; the existing behind-only check suffices there (AC5).
- **Toolchain in the execution worktree.** Reuse the merge-gate integrator's
  `node_modules` symlink convention (SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B) and add submodule
  initialisation — mirror `implement.py::_ensure_submodules`
  (`git submodule update --init --recursive`, SA-0MSN52GGN002B0AZ). In
  tce-the-rising `core/` is a gitlink submodule and an empty one makes every
  suite command fail at startup (`vitest failed to load config`). Init
  submodules *before* symlinking `node_modules`
  (ordering hazard: SA-0MVTOR53E003IIEQ).
- **Cache expectations.** The main checkout's `.worklog/cache` and the
  worktree git-dir `test-cache` are distinct, so an isolated F3 run starts
  with an empty cache and re-executes fresh at the clean base — expected, not
  a regression (see also SA-0MVCTZRZD004CE3L, cache-key identity).
- **Test fixture.** The AC4 bare-remote fixture must include a tracked
  submodule and an absent `node_modules` so the toolchain-initialisation step
  is pinned by a test.

## Impact

Producers and implement agents can now trust an audit verdict: it reflects merged, checked-in dev and never a developer's un-pushed in-flight work on the main checkout.
data.title: Audit skill: always run the suite/pipeline in a fresh worktree at latest origin/dev

data.description:
# implement.py drive: a driven child strays into another work item's worktree when its first finish gate is red

## Problem statement

When a driven child's first `finish` gate is red for a reason the child did not
introduce (a pre-existing environment-only failure), the child is expected to
stop after triage — but nothing currently stops it from going one step further:
creating a work item for the failure and **starting that item's implementation
itself**, inside a sibling worktree. The existing worktree-placement guard only
detects work that landed in the **main checkout**, so a driven child that
`cd`s into a different linked worktree is invisible to the guard, can race the
session that owns that worktree, silently widen the epic's scope, and consume
the host's test slots.

## Users

- **Implement-skill maintainer** — wants the placement guard to cover every
  linked worktree, not just the main checkout, so a driven child that writes
  into a sibling worktree is detected and refused with an actionable message.
- **Producer/operator running `/skill:implement <epic>`** — wants a drive that
  fails closed with both roots named when a child strays, instead of silently
  editing another item's tree or wedging the epic.
- **Driven child agent** — needs explicit guidance that a red first `finish`
  gate caused by a failure it did not introduce ends with triage and report,
  never with starting that failure's own implementation.

Example user stories:

- As an implement-skill maintainer, I want a driven child that edits another
  linked worktree to be detected by `phase_parent`/`phase_drive` and the run
  to fail closed with an actionable message naming both roots, so isolation
  between concurrent worktrees holds.
- As a producer driving an epic, I want a child whose `finish` gate is red
  because of a pre-existing failure to report the triage work item and stop —
  not begin implementing it in a sibling worktree that another session owns.
- As an agent working a driven child, I want a deterministic rule: a red gate
  I did not cause → triage (create work item) → report → stop.

## Acceptance criteria

- A driven child refuses (or is refused) any write whose path resolves into a
  linked worktree other than `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH`, with an actionable
  message naming both roots.
- A child whose `finish` gate is red because of a failure it did not introduce
  reports and stops (triage → work item), instead of starting that work item's
  implementation itself.
- Regression test: a simulated driven child that `cd`s into a sibling worktree
  is detected and the run fails closed (no status mutation of either item).
- The standard finish gate (`_worktree_placement_violation`) and the parent/
  drive placement guard (`_child_main_checkout_violation`) both treat changes
  in a **registered sibling worktree** of the same repository as a placement
  violation when the child's own worktree holds no work (precise-guard rule:
  unrelated dirt never blocks).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, `skill/implement/SKILL.md`, `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` blocker guidance
  (confined to driven sessions), and `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A driven epic run can no longer be silently derailed: a child whose first
`finish` gate is red stops after triage, and a child that edits another item's
worktree is caught and the run fails closed naming both roots.

## Constraints

- **Do not change driven behaviour otherwise.** `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE=1`
  semantics, driver-side worktree removal and the drive sweep stay exactly as
  they are (parent epic SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9, SA-0MVTE8XAJ002IUDR).
- **Precision over false positives.** The guard fires only when the child's own
  worktree holds NO work (no dirty files, no commits ahead of the parent
  branch) while another change surface (main checkout or a sibling worktree)
  holds changes. Pre-existing/unrelated dirt never blocks a legitimate finish
  or a child whose work lives in its own worktree.
- **Sibling worktree = registered linked worktree** of the same repository
  (via `_registered_worktree_paths`), excluding the main checkout and the
  child's own worktree. A foreign repository checkout — even one reachable by
  path — is never treated as the child's write surface (cross-checkout
  attribution, SA-0MVXVBZF2009HRRN).
- **No status mutation on refusal.** A fail-closed placement refusal must not
  mutate either item's status; it reports (comment + structured report fields)
  and stops the chain, mirroring `_fail_placement`.
- **Do not invent a partial-overlap duplicate.** The completed item
  SA-0MUY9PSRS003V5CM ("cwd is not enough") covers main-checkout writes only;
  this item extends the guard to sibling worktrees and adds the red-gate stop
  rule. It is not a duplicate.
- **Built, tested, committed in a worktree** per the mandatory worktree
  requirement; never commit from the main checkout.

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`:
  - `_child_main_checkout_violation(child_id, worktree_path, parent_branch, repo_root)`
    (~line 18527) — post-hoc guard called from `phase_parent`'s two
    change-surface call sites (~14590, ~14650); fails the chain via
    `_fail_placement` (~14398) when a non-terminal child's worktree holds no
    work while the **main checkout** is dirty.
  - `_worktree_placement_violation(worktree_path, cwd, repo_root, parent_branch)`
    (~line 18428) — the `finish`-phase Step 0.5 gate; refuses when cwd is
    outside the worktree and main checkout holds changes while the worktree has
    none.
  - `_registered_worktree_paths(repo_root)` (~line 7188) — enumerates the
    worktrees git registers for a repo (already used to confine removal
    surfaces); this is the natural enumerator for sibling detection.
  - `_child_session_env()` (~14834) — injects `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH` into
    the driven child's environment; `_child_main_checkout_violation` already
    names it as the contract the child must honour.
  - Drive loop `finish`-failure handling (~17620+) — the exact point where a
    red first gate is observed; the child-level instruction is what currently
    lets the child decide to implement the triaged item itself.
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` line 11: "If you discover a blocker, create a new
  work-item, record the blocking relationship, and start working on it." The
  incident child followed this rule verbatim — which is exactly the behaviour
  AC2 must confine (driven sessions: triage and stop, do not start the new
  item).
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` § Step 5 worktree requirement — `cwd` is not
  sufficient; `test "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" = "$IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH"`
  guard snippet already taught.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — the placement-guard contract document;
  must be updated for the sibling-worktree extension.
- Tests: `skill/implement/tests/test_worktree_has_changes.py`
  (`TestPlacementGuardContract`), `test_finish_cross_checkout_attribution.py`,
  `test_drive_child_session.py`.

## Desired change

1. **Extend the placement guard to sibling worktrees.** Teach
   `_child_main_checkout_violation` (and/or a new sibling-aware sibling)
   to enumerate `_registered_worktree_paths(repo_root)`, and — when the
   child's own worktree has no work — report a violation for any *other*
   registered linked worktree that holds changes, with an actionable message
   naming both roots (`IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH` vs the offending sibling).
   Keep the finish-phase `_worktree_placement_violation` precise and
   symmetric where cwd/resolution indicates a sibling write.
2. **Red-gate stop rule for driven children.** Update
   `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`'s blocker guidance (or the driven-session instruction
   surface) so a driven child whose first `finish` gate is red for a failure
   it did not introduce: triages (creates a work item, records the blocking
   relationship) and **stops** — it does not run `implement.py start` for that
   item and does not edit its worktree. The drive loop already bounds retries;
   the behavioural fix is the instruction + the guard in (1) as the backstop.
3. **Regression tests.** Simulate a driven child that `cd`s into a sibling
   worktree (built with `git_sandbox` worktrees) and writes there; assert
   detection, fail-closed chain stop, and that neither item's status mutated.

## Risks & assumptions

- **False positives on legitimate sibling work.** A sibling worktree may hold
  another (non-driven) session's in-progress changes. Mitigation: the guard
  fires only when the child's own worktree has no work AND the sibling holds
  changes — plus the per-child lock probe (`_probe_child_lock`) can
  distinguish a live owner; an actively-held sibling is reported, not blamed.
- **The red-gate stop rule is instruction-level, so a misbehaving agent can
  ignore it.** Mitigation: the extended placement guard in AC1 is the
  mechanical backstop — even if a child tries to implement the triaged item,
  writing into a sibling worktree fails closed.
- **Wordiness of scope** — the drive's finish-retry/reconcile machinery must

# Standup more focused on user experience (re-homed from ContextHub)

> **Provenance:** re-homed from ContextHub epic WL-0MW397N0Z002AYWP per producer
> decision (Option A). The standup skill source of truth lives in this
> (SorraAgents) repository — `skill/standup/` — which `~/.pi/agent/skills`
> symlinks to. The ContextHub copy is closed as moved.


## Problem statement

The daily standup report is currently a dry, flat bullet list of work items
("things done" + technical summaries), which is hard to read aloud and does
not convey what the user gained from the work. The output should be grouped
into meaningful categories, with each completed item described as a
single sentence about its impact on the user experience — without work item
IDs.

## Users

- The operator, who reads/listens to the daily standup (TTS) and wants a
  readable narrative of what changed and why it matters to the user.
- Agent sessions that generate standups and need clear, stable instructions
  for turning the script's structured data into the grouped report.

Example user stories:
- "As the operator, I want the standup grouped by areas such as 'User
  experience when doing Foo' and 'Back end stability under heavy load', so I
  can quickly grasp where progress happened and what each change means for
  users."
- "As the operator, I want each completed item described as one
  user-experience impact sentence without IDs, e.g. 'Improved the speed of
  user interactions with Foo by providing a one-click setup of the deck'."

## Desired change

1. **Categories** are chosen by the LLM (the invoking agent) at report time;
   labels are free-form (e.g. "User experience when doing Foo", "UI layout to
   improve access to key information"). No fixed taxonomy.
2. **Per-item impact sentences** come from a new explicit `## Impact` line in
   the work item description, written by the agent completing the work. Items
   without one (including all existing legacy items, which are **not**
   retrofitted) fall back to the current `Title — user story` phrasing.
3. **Grouped-paragraph format in every section** — "Yesterday I completed work
   on…", "Open critical items", "Additional focus items for today",
   "Regressions" and "Blockers" — each section grouped **independently**
   (categories are chosen per section, not per whole report).
4. The deterministic script (`generate_standup.py`) continues to fetch and
   compute the selection data; it also extracts each item's `## Impact`
   sentence into the structured output. The LLM (agent session) does the
   clustering and paragraph rendering, keeping the script testable and the
   agent output interpretable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `generate_standup.py` extracts the `## Impact` sentence from each item's
   description into a dedicated structured field (e.g. `impact`), available in
   `--json` output; a missing/malformed Impact section yields an empty field
   without error.
2. The rendered report is readable as a narrative: it organises each section's
   items into categories chosen by the LLM at report time, items are grouped
   **independently within each section**, and no work item IDs appear anywhere
   in the rendered report.
3. Within each category, every item is described as a single
   user-experience-focused sentence: the item's `## Impact` sentence when
   present, else the existing `Title — user story` phrasing (fallback).
4. The report remains first-person and TTS-friendly (spoken-form dates, no
   ID brackets/backticks/underscores in spoken lines) and stays within the
   ~2-minute read budget.
5. CLI behaviour is unchanged for consumers (flags, JSON schema superset,
   `--output-path` write path, sync-first, commit/push); existing tests keep
   passing with additions for the new `impact` extraction.
6. Work-item completion guidance (project AGENTS.md / implement skill / intake
   brief template) is updated so newly completed items carry an `## Impact`
   sentence describing the user-experience impact of the change.
7. Testing/validation: unit tests cover Impact extraction (present, absent,
   malformed) and the fallback; a golden-output test renders a sample report
   and asserts grouped sections, no IDs, and Impact-first sentences.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, the standup SKILL.md, and any wiki/docs entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The script stays deterministic (no LLM calls inside `generate_standup.py`) —
  clustering/rendering happens in the invoking agent session per Q4 answer.
- Existing completed items are NOT retrofitted with `## Impact` lines.
- Report must stay first-person, TTS-friendly, under ~2 minutes reading time.
- No work item IDs in the rendered output.
- Surgical scope: the Herdr selection ordering and data sources are untouched.

## Existing state

- `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` (installed to
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/`) renders a flat markdown report from the
  Herdr selection list; per-item text is `Title — user story/problem/summary`
  extracted heuristically from the description.
- Report structure: `## <project> Standup Report (date)` with sections
  "Yesterday I completed work on…", "Open critical items", "Additional focus
  items for today", "Regressions", "Blockers".
- Items already carry `Key Files` and (mostly) `As a …` user stories in their
  descriptions; there is no standard Impact field today.

## Desired change (implementation sketch)

- `generate_standup.py`: add `extract_impact(description)` (parse the
  `## Impact` section) and include `impact` in `normalize_item`/report data;
  keep `format_report` as a stable fallback for `--json` consumers and tests.
- `skill/standup/SKILL.md`: replace the "Report Structure" template with
  agent-rendered instructions: cluster each section's items into free-form
  categories, render one paragraph per category (one impact sentence per
  item), never render IDs, keep the TTS/first-person rules, note the
  `## Impact` / fallback rule.
- Work-item authoring guidance: add `## Impact` (one sentence,
  user-experience impact) to the completion conventions (implement skill
  output / AGENTS.md), so future standups have real impact sentences.

## Key Files

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/SKILL.md` — report template → clustered paragraph
  rendering instructions; source of truth `skill/standup/SKILL.md` in the
  SorraAgents repo.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` — add `## Impact`
  extraction + `impact` structured field; keep JSON/fallback compat.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/tests/test_generate_standup_*.py` — new tests for
  Impact extraction, fallback, no-ID golden output.
- `AGENTS.md` (project + `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` global) / intake brief
  template — completed items gain an `## Impact` sentence.

## Related work

- **Create a podcast for standups (WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8)** — consumes the
  rendered standup report; ensuring the grouped narrative stays parseable/TTS-
  friendly matters for it.
- Completed standup infra (sync-first WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K, maintenance
  routines WL-0MVIDWJ090090J3Q, scheduled prompts WL-0MTMN7W63001FCQR) —
  unchanged; this is an output-format change.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: existing items are not retrofitted with Impact lines (fallback
  covers them). Confirmed by operator (Q5/A).
- Assumption: LLM clustering runs in the invoking agent session, not in the
  script (Q4/A). Risk: agent non-determinism → mitigations: keep deterministic
  data layer, document expected structure, golden output reviewed in tests at
  the data layer, SKILL.md instructions constrain clustering.
- Risk: paragraphs lengthen the report past 2 minutes → mitigation: the agent
  is instructed to keep each category paragraph tight and cap per-item
  sentences at one.
- Risk: Impact lines may be missing or low-quality → fallback + guidance
  update (AC6); scope-creep risk noted: no changes to Herdr selection or
  podcast pipeline (linked as related work, not scope).
- Risk: agents may accidentally include IDs → explicit "no IDs" rule in
  SKILL.md + golden-output test asserting absence (AC2).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "How should categories be determined?" — Answer (operator): "C — LLM-chosen at report time (free-form labels)". Source: interactive reply (round 1, 2026-11-06).
- Q2: "Where does each item's impact sentence come from?" — Answer (operator): "A — explicit `## Impact` line written into work items at completion; the script reads it". Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q3: "Which sections get the new grouped-paragraph format?" — Answer (operator): "C — every section, but group independently within the sections". Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q4: "Where does the LLM clustering run?" — Answer (operator): "A — in the invoking agent session; script emits structured item data; SKILL.md instructs the agent to cluster and render". Source: interactive reply (round 2).
- Q5: "Items without an `## Impact` line?" — Answer (operator): "A — fall back to current Title — user story phrasing". Source: interactive reply (round 2).
- Assumption (confirmed implicitly): existing completed items are not retrofitted with Impact lines.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRMG8P2X004V6YC** – help line for chord commands too verbose (completed)
- **WL-0MQZX8BTN006N4BF** – Automatically recover from appropriate server errors (completed)
- **WL-0MURJ0LFH002O95I** – r-i (Producer Interview) should focus on the created pane (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: access, back, category, click, completed, currently, defined, discovery, dry, end, etc, example, fit, focused, foo, group, heavy, ids, information, key, layout, lets, list, load, one, output, paragraph, providing, readable, see, should, single, stability, standup, top, under, user, using, when, you
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: access, achieve, back, completed, currently, defined, describing, doing, end, etc, example, fit, focused, foo, group, ids, impact, improve, key, layout, list, load, one, output, paragraph, readable, see, setup, should, single, stability, standup, top, under, user, using, when, you
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: back, completed, defined, discovery, dry, easy, end, etc, fit, focused, foo, group, heavy, ids, improve, improved, key, list, load, one, output, readable, see, setup, should, single, speed, stability, standup, top, under, user, using, when, you

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-06: Plan decomposition complete (plan skill). 7 child work items created in test-first dependency order. AC coverage: 100%. Key Files validated.
  - WL-0MW5HUS5E001SG6H — Unit tests for Impact extraction
  - WL-0MW5HVPJP009MVPQ — Impact extraction implementation in generate_standup.py
  - WL-0MW5HVQ7Z006SI6Q — Impact-aware report rendering + TTS fallback

- [ ] Script accepts two positional args: `TRACKED_DIR DEST_DIR` (e.g. `.pi-config/agent` and `~/.pi/agent`).
- [ ] Merges tracked `providers` and `modelOverrides` into the destination while preserving every local-only provider/model/override verbatim.
- [ ] Unions tracked `enabledModels` into the destination, deduplicated.
- [ ] Non-interactive-safe: no prompts, works with `stdin=/dev/null`.
- [ ] Prints a per-provider summary (`Added ...` / `OK: already present ...`).
- [ ] Stdlib-only: no third-party imports.
- [ ] Handles missing destination files gracefully (fresh `$HOME`).

## Key Files

- `scripts/merge_pi_agent_config.py` — new file, stdlib Python

Running `scripts/install_pi.sh` now applies the tracked paid MunitoAI DeepSeek models to installed machines without hand-editing JSON, while preserving any locally defined providers and settings.

## Goal

Write unit tests for `_evaluate_red_suite` — the verdict integration function that combines mode + classification + relatedness.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Strict mode tests
- Any single failure in strict mode → `blocked` with reason "strict mode"
- Unit + integration mix → `blocked`
- All unit, all unrelated → `blocked` (strict mode ignores relatedness)
- Empty failures list → not applicable (caller handles green)

### Permissive mode tests — excusal path
- All failures unit-classified + all unrelated → `excused` with per-failure evidence
- Single unrelated unit failure → `excused`

### Permissive mode tests — fail-closed path
- Permissive fail-closed cases: in permissive mode the audit still fails when (a) any failure is integration/end-to-end classified, (b) any unit failure is affected by the item's changes, or (c) relatedness is inconclusive and no baseline comparison can be performed; unit tests cover each case individually, plus the mixed case (one excusable + one blocking failure ⇒ audit fails).
- Any integration/e2e failure → `blocked` with reason "integration test failure"
- Any unit failure classified as affected → `blocked` with reason "affected by item changes"
- Any unit failure classified as inconclusive (no baseline or baseline inconclusive) → `blocked` with reason "relatedness inconclusive"
- Mixed: one excusable unit + one blocking integration → `blocked` with both reasons recorded
- Mixed: one excusable unit + one affected unit → `blocked` with both reasons recorded

### Verdict structure
- `excused` verdict carries per-failure classification, relatedness, and evidence
- `blocked` verdict carries per-failure reasons
- Both verdicts include mode metadata

## Goal

Implement the failure classification and relatedness helper functions in `audit_runner.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_classify_test_failure_scope(failure)` returns `"unit"` or `"integration"`:
   - Path convention: `tests/integration/**`, `tests/e2e/**`, `tests/manual/**`, `**/*_e2e*`, `**/*integration*` → `integration`
   - Everything else → `unit`
   - Unclassifiable (no path data) → `integration` (fail closed)

2. `_failure_relatedness(failure, touched_files, key_files, project_root)` returns `"affected"`, `"unrelated"`, or `"inconclusive"`:
   - Test file path ∈ changed files → `affected`
   - Module imported by test file ∈ changed files → `affected`
   - Changed file is shared test infrastructure (`conftest.py`, `tests/helpers/**`) → `affected`
   - No match → `inconclusive`

3. `_baseline_unrelated(failures, project_root, baseline_commit)` returns per-failure verdicts:
   - Creates scratch worktree at baseline commit (pre-change commit)
   - Runs only inconclusive failures through `paced_runner()` under `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` stand-down
   - Identical failure → `unrelated`; Pass → `affected`
   - Any baseline failure → `affected` (fail closed)
   - Any baseline error (worktree add, merge-base unresolvable, test absent) → `affected` (fail closed, no crash)
   - Never executes the main checkout; never recurses into nested suite runs

4. Scope classification and relatedness algorithm: failures are classified by path convention (`tests/integration/**`, `tests/e2e/**`, `tests/manual/**`, `**/*_e2e*`, `**/*integration*` ⇒ integration/end-to-end; everything else ⇒ unit; unclassifiable ⇒ integration, fail closed). Relatedness is decided by deterministic mapping first (failing test file ∈ item's changed files; a module the test imports ∈ changed files; a changed shared test-infrastructure file such as `conftest.py`/`tests/helpers/**`), then — only for inconclusive failures — by a baseline re-run of just those failures in a scratch worktree at the item's pre-change commit (fails identically ⇒ unrelated; passes ⇒ affected). Unit tests cover the pattern table, the import-mapping step, and the baseline comparison (both outcomes), with no real suite execution.

5. No real suite execution in unit tests (mock `paced_runner` / subprocess)
6. Unit tests pass (see child test items)

## Deliverables
- `_classify_test_failure_scope()` — path-pattern classifier
- `_failure_relatedness()` — deterministic mapping + import scan
- `_baseline_unrelated()` — scratch worktree baseline re-run
- Error handling: never crashes, always returns `affected` for infrastructure failures

## Key Files
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (new functions)

## Impact

Delivered as part of parent SA-0MW0JJ36Z000AF57 (commit 4bc7a5f7b): the strict/permissive audit test-failure modes are implemented, tested and documented.

## Problem

`implement.py drive --pane-sessions` cannot drive a real (multi-minute) child
session. `_pane_session_spawner` calls
`HerdrSessionClient.prompt_agent(..., timeout_ms=child_timeout * 1000)`, but
the client is constructed with `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 60.0` and `_invoke()` passes
that value as `subprocess.run(timeout=...)`. The herdr CLI's own `--timeout`
argument is therefore irrelevant: the client kills the
`herdr agent prompt --wait` subprocess after 60 seconds and the spawner
reports `Pane agent for <child> did not complete: herdr call timed out`.

Observed during SA-0MVXWMVTH007MNJR: the driven child's pane was closed and its
session killed after ~70 s, with the child still `in-progress` and an empty
worktree, so the drive chain stopped on its first child and had to fall back
to the headless transport.

## Desired change

Scale the client's per-call subprocess timeout to the wait it is performing
(e.g. build the pane spawner's client with `timeout=child_budget + slack`, or
add a per-call timeout override to `_invoke`), so a pane-driven child session
can run for its whole documented budget.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A pane-driven child session whose turn takes longer than 60 s is not
  killed by the client; the recorded failure is the CLI's own `--timeout`
  verdict, never `herdr call timed out`.
- AC2: A unit test drives `_pane_session_spawner` with a slow fake herdr
  runner and asserts the client's subprocess timeout exceeds the requested
  child budget.
- AC3: The headless transport is unchanged.

## Notes

Discovered while implementing SA-0MVXWMVTH007MNJR; that item fell back to the
headless spawner (`--no-pane-sessions`) to avoid the 60 s kill.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVEDIUA80038VAQ** – Audit timeout constants: single source of truth shared across audit/test skills (open)
- **SA-0MVLJWMQ8007EDW0** – Reconcile terminal child after spawn failure (completed)
- **SA-0MVPHZ1CI0045QR0** – Drive pane lifecycle and report parity (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 60s, ac1, ac2, ac3, acceptance (+83 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mvxwmvth007mnjr, ac1, ac2, ac3, acceptance (+82 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: 60s, ac1, ac2, ac3, acceptance (+77 more)

## Impact
Operators can now drive multi-minute child sessions in herdr panes: a child whose turn runs past 60 s is no longer killed by the drive client, so pane-driven epics complete instead of silently falling back to the headless transport.

# Intake Brief — Move the detailed descriptions of the metrics into an appendix (SA-0MW7QD3CJ00208YS)

## Problem statement

The usage report produced by the `proxy-usage-analysis` skill (`report.md`)
interleaves the raw generated data with long descriptive prose explaining each
metric. The report opens with a header bullet block and detailed metric
explanations (availability-state footnote, total-tokens formula, busy-time
methodology, slot-seconds semantics, engine-cross-check caveats, …), so an
operator cannot read the day's numbers "at a glance" and the descriptive text
drowns the data. The detailed metric descriptions should move to an appendix
at the end of the document, the main body should contain only the data
generated (tables plus at most a one-sentence reminder of each metric's
definition), and the appendix should carry an equivalent description for
**all** metrics in the report. This item is merged with
**LP-0MW0FU5Z6006A4P3** ("Performance metrics in usage report"), so it also
delivers that item's first-section scorecard (metrics with baseline, target,
actual, met/unmet) and its per-metric detail content (why important, how
calculated, levers, trade-offs) — which now lives in the appendix.

## Users

- **Proxy operators / the producer** — want an "at a glance" view of how well
  the local LLMs are performing (optimisation of use and amount of content
  processed) without wading through methodology prose.
- **Engineers and agents** — want a detailed breakdown of each top-level
  measure (definition, calculation, levers, trade-offs) to improve the
  numbers.

User stories:

- As an operator, I open the usage report and immediately see the data tables
  and a top-of-report scorecard (metric, baseline, target, actual, met/unmet),
  so I can tell at a glance whether local LLM usage is healthy.
- As an operator, I can find a one-sentence reminder of what each metric means
  next to its table, without the full methodology.
- As an engineer/agent, I can open a metric-glossary appendix at the end of
  the report and read, for every metric in the report, why it matters, how it
  is calculated, and what levers/trade-offs exist to improve it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The generated `report.md` main body contains only data generated
  (tables/graphs and section headers); every detailed metric-description
  passage currently embedded in the body (header block, `## Summary by hour`
  availability footnote, `## Total tokens` prose, `## Local model
  utilization` "Busy = …"/"Method:" paragraphs, `## Prefill vs decode`
  slot-seconds explanation, `## Engine cross-check` caveats, and any similar
  inline prose in other sections) moves to an appendix at the end of the
  document.
- AC2: Each metric in the main body is accompanied by at most a **one-sentence
  reminder** of its definition (e.g. a short gloss next to the table or under
  the section header); a reminder is present for every metrics table whose
  full description moved to the appendix.
- AC3: A metric-glossary appendix (`## Appendix: Metric definitions` or
  equivalent) at the end of `report.md` contains an entry for **every metric
  in the report** (per producer answer Q2=A — full glossary): definition,
  why it matters, how it is calculated, and — for the performance/scorecard
  metrics — levers and trade-offs (LP-0MW0FU5Z6006A4P3 content).
- AC4: A top-of-report scorecard section (metrics, baseline, target, actual,
  met/unmet observation) is added per LP-0MW0FU5Z6006A4P3, built from the
  validation work items' measured figures; every scorecard metric has its
  detail entry in the appendix (not duplicated in the body).
- AC5: While building the appendix, opportunities to improve the report were
  considered — any metric added, removed, or restructured is documented in the
  work-item description or a follow-on item; the report keeps its two intended
  uses (at-a-glance data + detailed breakdown).
- AC6: The `report.md` still renders for every window shape (empty window,
  zero-traffic, no llama-server logs, GPU data absent) without errors, and the
  existing per-section regression tests are updated where section content
  changed (full project test suite passes).
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, SKILL.md, REFERENCE.md and any relevant wiki or docs
  site entries for `proxy-usage-analysis`.

## Constraints

- Implementation lives in the **llm-manager** project
  (`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/`); tracking/worklog is in SorraAgents
  (cross-repo pattern per SA-0MTM3LKP1003S28J — commit on llm-manager `dev`).
- The pipeline stays fully deterministic and rule-based (no LLM in the
  report); changing the report must not change the proxy, the parser, or the
  `--json` summary keys.
- The daily 05:00 cron path (agent-free) must keep working unchanged; the
  report layout change must not break `cron.log` or archival.
- The one-sentence reminder rule: descriptions shorten, never bloat the body;
  the appendix is the single home for detail (producer Q1=C, Q3=A).

## Existing state

- `reporting.py::build_report()` appends ~30 sections, several of which embed
  long descriptive prose (verified: availability footnote + 4 state notes in
  `## Summary by hour`; "Total = prompt (input) + completion (output)…"
  paragraph in `## Total tokens`; "Busy = at least one local slot active…" +
  "Method: streams are paired…" in `## Local model utilization`; "Every figure
  here is slot-seconds…" in `## Prefill vs decode`; engine-vs-proxy caveat
  paragraphs in `## Engine cross-check`; per-section interpretation notes).
- The report has two intended uses (from the item description): (1) at-a-glance
  local-LLM performance view; (2) detailed breakdown enabling improvement.
- LP-0MW0FU5Z6006A4P3 (critical, open, llm worklog) already asks for the
  first-section scorecard + per-metric detail; merged here by producer
  decision (Q1=C). Documented on both items (`Merged-into` / `Merged-with`,
  `Blocks:` / `Blocked-by:`).

## Desired change

- Extract all inline metric-description prose from the report body into a
  single appended glossary; keep one-sentence reminders in the body.
- Add the LP scorecard section at the top of the report.
- Write the glossary so every metric in the report is covered, with the
  "why / how / levers / trade-offs" shape for scorecard metrics.
- Improve/restructure opportunistically (add/remove metrics) with
  documentation; surface any large proposals as linked work items.

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — report generation;
  the inline prose lives here (`build_report` and the `_append_*` helpers); new
  scorecard + appendix sections added here.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` (and
  section-specific test files) — update assertions that pin section prose.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md`, `REFERENCE.md`, `README.md` —
  document the new report structure (body data-only, scorecard, appendix).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` — CLI entry;
  unchanged unless the scorecard needs config (e.g. baseline/target values per
  metric).
- `proxy/config.yaml` (llm project) — source of any configured thresholds used
  by scorecard met/unmet, only if needed.

## Related work

- **LP-0MW0FU5Z6006A4P3** — Performance metrics in usage report (critical,
  open): merged into this item per producer decision; its scorecard + detail
  content is delivered here. Dep edge recorded as comments on both items.
- **SA-0MTM3LKP1003S28J** — Add Total Tokens breakdown to usage report
  (completed): prior cross-repo delivery pattern (SorraAgents worklog,
  llm-manager implementation, commit on dev).
- **LP-0MVT2QHMU0008F2V / LP-0MVN4LCQJ0034S5S / LP-0MVU8O4EL005IYP9 /
  LP-0MVGR2OXT0096OGK / LP-0MVNWULLI006ZYXX** — metric sections whose
  descriptions move to the appendix (measurement breakdown, evictions,
  capacity signals, contention prediction, engine cross-check).
- **find_related scan (SA worklog)** — SA-0MQC4A11A008BSRI (TDD),
  SA-0MSLK78W7009HIXC (skill descriptions), SA-0MW3GCVPX00642FV (finish
  gate) matched on keywords only; no genuine overlap — the real related items
  (LP work, cross-repo skill) are listed above. Full report:
  `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-SA-0MW7QD3CJ00208YS.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope risk**: "all metrics" is a large glossary (~30 sections, dozens of
  metrics); mitigate by generating the appendix from the same data structures
  that feed each section, so entries stay in sync (additive key rule: no
  parser/`--json` key changes).
- **Test breakage**: many tests assert exact section prose; expect broad
  updates in the section tests (covered by AC6).
- **LP merge**: LP-0MW0FU5Z6006A4P3 baseline/target figures come from recent
  completed validation items; if a baseline is not yet measured, the scorecard
  renders the metric with an explicit "no baseline yet" note rather than a
  fabricated number (honest-degradation rule already used by the report).
- Assumption: "one-sentence reminder" may be a short gloss under each affected
  section header or next to its table; exact placement is an implementation
  choice as long as body stays data-focused.
- Assumption: scorecard met/unmet uses configured thresholds or measured
  baselines; default thresholds documented in the report when unset.
- Cross-repo delivery: implementation lands on llm-manager `dev` and is
  tracked under this SA item; the LP item is left open, blocked by this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Placement conflict with LP-0MW0FU5Z6006A4P3 — how do the two
  coordinate?" — Answer (Map, producer): "**C — merge**, with the refinement
  that the main body keeps a **one-sentence reminder** of each metric's
  definition and the appendix carries the full detail." Source: interactive
  reply, 2026-11-16.
- Q2: "Scope of 'all metrics' — full glossary or only currently-described
  top-level measures?" — Answer (Map, producer): "**A — full glossary** —
  every metric in the report gets an appendix entry." Source: interactive
  reply, 2026-11-16.
- Q3: "Which 'first section' carries the description to move?" — Answer (Map,
  producer): "**A —** the whole top-of-report block moves; the body keeps the
  tables **plus a single-sentence reminder** of metric definitions." Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-11-16.

## Summary

Refactor duplicate prevention is a **substring match over other items' titles and descriptions**, keyed on file + line + rule code. It silently fails whenever the line number moves by one, whenever the path prefix differs (worktree vs main checkout), or whenever the title has been truncated — so the same smell is re-filed on every scan.

## Evidence

Function: `_has_existing_worklog_item()` in `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py`. It lists `wl list --tags Refactor --json`, concatenates each item's title and description, and returns a match only when **all three** of `target_file`, `target_code` and `str(target_line)` appear anywhere in that blob.

Open-backlog duplicates measured on 2026-11-08:

| Target | Rule | Open items for the same file+rule |
|---|---|---|
| `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` | `S112` | 22 |
| `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_from_worktree.py` | `SIM117` | 10 |
| `tests/test_assignee_release_all_skills.py` | `ISC004` | 7 |
| `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_temp_index.py` | `SIM117` | 4 |
| `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` | `RUF015` | 4 |

Failure modes that defeat the guard:

1. **Line drift** — inserting one line above a finding changes every subsequent line number, so `str(target_line) in combined` no longer matches.
2. **Path-prefix drift** — the identical file is recorded as `/repo/.worklog/worktrees/<wt>/skill/x.py` from one scan and `/repo/skill/x.py` from another; neither is a substring of the other.
3. **Truncation** — titles are truncated in listing output (e.g. `[MEDIUM] /home/…/test_implement_push_fro`), so the full path is not present to match on.
4. **Cross-family blindness** — the guard only inspects `Refactor`-tagged items, so the audit-side family `ruff <RULE> in <path> — candidate false positive` (73 open items, created by `audit_runner.py`) is invisible to it and mints parallel twins for the same diagnostics.

Note also that a substring match on a *line number* is not an identity: `str(12)` matches `:12`, `:120`, `:312`, and any mention of 12 anywhere in a long description.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Identity for a refactor finding is `(repository-relative path, rule/smell code)` — **not** the line number, and not the absolute path. The content fingerprint required by the re-verification item (`SA-0MW7Z1JCE009G6J3`) is stored alongside it so occurrences can be counted rather than guessed at.
2. Before creating an item the skill queries the existing open items for that exact identity **and** for the audit-created `ruff <RULE> in <path>` family, so the two producers cannot mint twins.
3. A repeat finding on an existing identity does not create a new item: it appends a comment recording the new line numbers/occurrences, or updates the existing item, per a documented rule.
4. Worktree path prefixes are normalised before comparison (shared helper, reused by the critical bug on worktree-path recording).
5. Line-level reporting is preserved: the item lists every affected line, so consolidation loses no diagnostic detail.
6. Regression tests covering: same smell twice in one run; smell re-found after a line shift; same file scanned from two worktrees; two different rules in one file; refactor-created vs audit-created twin suppression.
7. A one-off consolidation of the existing duplicates is possible from the same helper (dry-run first), so the backlog can be collapsed without manual wl calls.

## Related

- Critical bug `SA-0MW7Z11PV003V7O2`: refactor filings record ephemeral implement-worktree paths (the path-drift half of this problem; the shared path-normalisation helper is specified there and reused here).
- High feature `SA-0MW7Z1JCE009G6J3`: linter-derived items are never re-verified — supplies the content fingerprint and the occurrence re-check.
- High feature `SA-0MW7Z1PR20094WIS`: children survive parent deletion — the orphan half of the same backlog-hygiene gap.

## Impact

The same code smell is tracked once instead of up to twenty-two times, so the backlog reflects genuine debt and agents stop re-fixing work that is already queued.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVGKMNEQ009RZKD** – Refactor skill: detect files > 1000 lines, evaluate refactor need, and file work items (open)
- **SA-0MRIIQLQI001RQVB** – Refactor command/doc.md for conciseness (completed)
- **SA-0MRMB6P6M008H4U4** – Fix legacy skill/ path reference in planall SKILL.md (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: absolute, acceptance, affected, agents, alongside (+191 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: absolute, acceptance, affected, agents, alongside (+181 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: absolute, acceptance, affected, agents, alongside (+176 more)


## Plan: changelog (2026-11-12)

Planned by the `plan` skill (session via herdr-downtime dispatch):

- Computed effort/risk estimate (Small/Medium, 74% confidence) via the effort-and-risk skill; stored on the item and recorded as a comment.
- Created 5 children in test-first dependency order (F1 tests → F2 identity marker → F3 cross-family twins → F4 repeat comments → F5 consolidation); dependency edges wired; tree coverage review passed (100% of parent ACs covered, `proceed`).
