## Summary

Nothing ever re-checks a linter-derived work item against the current tree. Once filed, a refactor or audit finding stays open until a human or agent happens to look at it — even when the target file has been deleted or the diagnostic has not fired for weeks.

During the 2026-11-08 backlog review this was measured directly, and every sampled family was stale.

## Evidence

**115 open refactor items whose titled path no longer resolves or whose diagnostic no longer reproduces:**

| Class | Items | Verification |
|---|---|---|
| Target file deleted from the repo (`skill/proxy-usage-analysis/**`, a removed skill) | 37 | path does not exist |
| Target file exists, diagnostic no longer fires | 78 | `ruff check --isolated --select <RULE> <path>` → 0 hits in all 34 (path, rule) groups |

**73 open audit-side items** of the form `ruff <RULE> in <path> — candidate false positive` (`audit_runner.py` `FP_CANDIDATE_ANNOTATION`, created as "producer decision required" chores): **0 of 19 (path, rule) groups still fire** on the current tree.

Concrete examples of no-longer-reproducing findings that remained open:
- `S112` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — 22 items, 0 hits now.
- `SIM117` in `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_from_worktree.py` — 10 items, 0 hits now.
- `ISC004` in `tests/test_assignee_release_all_skills.py` — 7 items, 0 hits now.
- `PYI034`/`PYI036` in `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — 4 items, 0 hits now (these were orphaned children too).

Some of these block audits rather than sitting idle, so stale findings are not merely noise: `SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42` records the audit-side variant where every medium/low candidate-false-positive chore sets `needsProducerReview` and blocks closure.

## Why it matters

Stale items are indistinguishable from live work in every view. `wl next` will dispatch them, an agent will implement, and the audit skill must then decide whether a finding that no longer reproduces has been "fixed". The backlog reads as 444 actionable items when a large share are already resolved.

## Required behaviour (acceptance criteria)

1. Every linter-derived item records, at creation, the **exact verification command** and a **content fingerprint** (file hash + rule set) that produced it.
2. A re-verification sweep re-runs that command and, per item, classifies it as `still-reproduces`, `no-longer-reproduces` or `target-gone`, recording the evidence in a comment.
3. Items classified `target-gone` are closed with a rationale (or flagged for deletion), and items classified `no-longer-reproduces` are closed with the evidence comment — **never silently**.
4. The sweep is **dry-run by default** and only ever touches items it can attribute to a linter family (`Refactor` tag, `[SEVERITY] <path>` titles, `ruff <RULE> in <path>` titles). It must never close a human-authored bug or feature.
5. The sweep is runnable both ad hoc and as a scheduled/gated step (e.g. from the refactor skill or a `wl doctor`-style hook), and is idempotent.
6. Tests: target deleted → `target-gone`; diagnostic fixed → `no-longer-reproduces`; diagnostic still firing → untouched; human-authored item → never touched; dry-run makes no writes.

## Scope note

The sweep itself belongs in this repository (`skill/refactor/`, and the audit side in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`). # Children survive deletion of their parent work item and become unreachable orphans

## Summary

Deleting a parent work item does not dispose of its open children. They survive as **orphans**: their `parentId` points at an id that no longer resolves (or resolves only to a soft-deleted item), so they appear in no rollup, are never closed by the parent's closure path, and are invisible to every parent-level report.

## Evidence (2026-11-08 backlog review)

55 of the 444 open-scope items had an unresolvable parent:

| Lost parent | Resolution | Open children |
|---|---|---|
| `SA-0MSC7QZQL006Q747` | hard-deleted (id not found at all) | 46 |
| `SA-0MLDAXNBQ17OA9PT` "Scheduler Configuration & Scoping" | soft-deleted | 5 |
| `SA-0MLPU8H3B1LWK3B3` "Add closing of work item to cleanup skill" | soft-deleted | 3 |
| `SA-0ML7NOSHP0MJC6HS` "AMPA Daemon: Discord heartbeat & notifier" | soft-deleted | 1 |

The 46 hard-deleted orphans were all refactor findings from 2026-08-02, filed under a scan-batch parent that was removed while its children stayed behind; the oldest were 258 days old. None of them surfaced in any progress view, and none could be closed by the normal "parent closes when all children close" path — the parent was already gone.

Deleting the parent recursively is the documented default (`wl delete` "Recursively deletes child items by default"), but `--no-recursive` exists ("leaving children orphaned") and a hard delete evidently bypassed the children — the exact route that produced the 46-item batch needs confirming as part of the fix.

## Intake re-scope (2026-11-13): most of the guard already exists

Investigation of the current Worklog CLI (`ContextHub` main @ `77264ee6a`) shows the original acceptance criteria are now **substantially shipped**, which narrows the residual work considerably. Verified:

- **Recursive delete ships.** `wl delete` is recursive by default, has an explicit `--no-recursive` opt-out, records `--reason`, and reports the deleted descendants — `src/commands/delete.ts`; precedent item **WL-0MQFZ81MO000QSRL** (completed), follow-up **SA-0MQFXG76T000A3LR** (completed).
- **Doctor already flags orphans.** Root `wl doctor` (`validate`) emits a distinct per-item finding via `validateParentReferences()`: code `parent.missing-endpoint`, type `missing-parent`, carrying the lost parent id in `context.parentId` and a safe `parentId: null` proposed fix — `src/doctor/parent-check.ts`, `src/commands/doctor/validate.ts`.
- **Promotion path exists.** `wl doctor dangling-parents [--apply]` detects dangling parents and detaches them (`parentId -> null`) — `src/commands/doctor/dangling-parents.ts` (**WL-0MUJM2LV1000IHKR**, completed), and `wl update <id> --parent null` now detaches instead of writing `WL-NULL`.

The remaining defects are therefore narrower than the original five ACs:

- **R1 — Hard-delete admin paths can still orphan children silently.** `wl doctor prune` hard-deletes a single id via `store.deleteWorkItem(id)` without touching its descendants (`src/commands/doctor/prune.ts`), so pruning a parent leaves children pointing at a removed id. This is the strongest candidate for the route that produced the 46-item hard-deleted batch.
- **R2 — Promotion/detach loses the history.** Neither `wl doctor --fix`, `wl doctor dangling-parents --apply`, nor `wl update <id> --parent null` records a comment naming the previous parent and the reason for the decision (original AC4).
- **R3 — Orphan reporting is not grouped.** Findings are emitted per child; there is no grouped summary keyed by lost-parent id giving the count and child ids as a distinct finding (original AC2's "count / lost-parent id / child ids").

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every hard-delete admin path that can leave children without a resolvable parent (notably `wl doctor prune`; audit `wl doctor foreign-items --apply` and any other store-level `deleteWorkItem` caller) either cascades to descendants or refuses without an explicit opt-in, so no silent orphaning remains.
2. Any explicit orphaning opt-in (`wl delete --no-recursive`) records a comment on each orphaned child naming the previous parent and the explicit decision.
3. `wl doctor` reports orphans as a distinct finding that includes the lost-parent id and the child id; `wl doctor dangling-parents --dry-run` summarises the grouped count of children per lost-parent id.
4. Promotion (`parentId -> null`, via `wl doctor --fix`, `wl doctor dangling-parents --apply`, or `wl update --parent null`) records a comment naming the previous parent and the rationale (promote-because-live vs retire-because-stale), so the history is not lost.
5. The retention rule — promote when the child's subject is still live; retire when it is superseded, its target is gone, or the abandoned parent's feature was never delivered — is documented alongside the remediation path.
6. Automated tests cover: pruning a parent with children does not orphan them; explicit orphaning records the previous parent; doctor output names the lost parent and the children; promotion clears `parentId`, keeps the children reachable, and records the comment.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (CLI/doctor docs and the remediation/retention guidance).
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Work can no longer disappear from every view because its parent was removed, so nothing sits in the queue invisible and unclosable.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the 46-item hard-deleted batch came from a single-id hard-delete admin path (`wl doctor prune` being the leading candidate); the exact route is to be confirmed during implementation.
- **Risk:** changing prune/foreign-items cascade behaviour could delete more than intended — mitigate with a dry-run-first default and explicit opt-in for destructive cascades.
- **Risk (scope creep):** incidental doctor/delete cleanups discovered during the fix should be filed as separate items, not folded in. Note that the delete-reason defect is already owned by WL-0MW8078CA006Q2P7.
- **Assumption:** the guard belongs in the Worklog CLI, not this data-carrying repository (see Q1).

## Constraints

- **Implementation target is the Worklog CLI (`ContextHub`, `WL-*` prefix), not this repository** — this repository only carries the data. See Open Question Q1 on migrating the item.
- Do **not** re-implement already-shipped behaviour (recursive `wl delete`, the `parent.missing-endpoint` doctor finding, `--parent null` detach); build only the residual gaps R1–R3.
- Preserve the cross-project sync guard (no foreign `WL-` items reintroduced).
- The separate delete-reason-clobbering defect is owned by **WL-0MW8078CA006Q2P7** and is out of scope here.
- CHANGELOG is managed by the ship release pipeline, not this item.

## Existing state

- `wl delete` recursive-by-default with `--no-recursive` and `--reason` (`src/commands/delete.ts`); recursive deletion shipped in WL-0MQFZ81MO000QSRL.
- `wl doctor` root `validate` includes `validateParentReferences()` → `parent.missing-endpoint` / `missing-parent` findings with a safe `parentId: null` fix (`src/doctor/parent-check.ts`, `src/commands/doctor/validate.ts`).
- `wl doctor dangling-parents [--dry-run|--apply]` detaches dangling parents (`src/commands/doctor/dangling-parents.ts`, WL-0MUJM2LV1000IHKR).
- `wl doctor prune` hard-deletes a single id via `store.deleteWorkItem(id)` with no descendant handling (`src/commands/doctor/prune.ts`) — the residual orphaning route.
- `wl doctor foreign-items --apply` hard-deletes with a "full cascade" (`src/commands/doctor/foreign-items.ts`).

## Desired change

Close the residual gaps: make hard-delete admin paths cascade-or-refuse (R1), record the previous parent + decision whenever a child is orphaned or promoted (R2), and report orphans grouped by lost-parent id in `wl doctor` output (R3), with a documented retention/remediation rule and tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/doctor/prune.ts` — cascade to descendants or refuse when pruning a parent that still has children.
- `src/doctor/parent-check.ts` — keep/extend the `parent.missing-endpoint` finding (lost-parent id, child id).
- `src/commands/doctor/validate.ts` — grouped orphan summary and comment-on-detach for `--fix`.
- `src/commands/doctor/dangling-parents.ts` — grouped count per lost parent and comment on detach.
- `src/commands/delete.ts` — comment on each child when `--no-recursive` orphaning is applied.
- `src/commands/update.ts` — comment on `--parent null` detach naming the previous parent.
- `CLI.md`, `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` — retention rule and remediation path.

## Related work

- **SA-0MQFXG76T000A3LR** (completed) — `wl delete` should recursively delete child work items.
- **WL-0MQFZ81MO000QSRL** (completed) — recursive deletion implementation in the Worklog CLI.
- **WL-0MUJM2LV1000IHKR** (completed) — treat `--parent null` as detach instead of a bogus `WL-NULL` parent.
- **WL-0MW8078CA006Q2P7** (open, critical) — delete reasons clobbered; owns the delete-attribution fix (out of scope here).
- **SA-0MW7Z1YE9004P41D** (completed) — 2026-11-08 backlog triage that retired the 55 orphans found in this item's evidence.
- **SA-0MW7Z1AU1006UT9C**, **SA-0MW7Z1JCE009G6J3** — sibling findings from the same 2026-11-08 backlog review.

## Open questions (producer review)

- **Q1 — Migration.** Should this item migrate to the Worklog CLI project (`ContextHub`), where all target files live, or remain in SorraAgents as a cross-project tracking item? **Recommended: migrate to the WL project** — the implementation is entirely in ContextHub; keeping it in SorraAgents forces cross-repo work that worktree isolation forbids.
- **Q2 — Re-scope confirmation.** Confirm the narrowed ACs (residual gaps R1–R3) rather than the original five. **Recommended: accept the re-scope** — AC1/2/3 of the original are substantially shipped (WL-0MQFZ81MO000QSRL, WL-0MUJM2LV1000IHKR), so re-implementing them would duplicate delivered work.
- **Q3 — On migration.** If Q1 approves migration, should this SorraAgents item be closed as "moved" with a link to the new WL item, or kept open as the tracking record until the fix ships? **Recommended: close as moved** and track delivery in the WL item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (migration):** "Should this item migrate to the Worklog CLI project (`ContextHub`), where all target files live, or remain in SorraAgents as a cross-project tracking item?" — **OPEN QUESTION** (awaiting producer). Recommended: migrate to WL. Research: all `Key Files` are under `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/src`; this repo carries data only.
- **Q2 (re-scope):** "Confirm the narrowed ACs (residual gaps R1–R3) rather than the original five?" — **OPEN QUESTION** (awaiting producer). Recommended: accept. Research: recursive delete (WL-0MQFZ81MO000QSRL) and `--parent null` detach (WL-0MUJM2LV1000IHKR) are completed; `parent.missing-endpoint` doctor finding already ships.
- **Q3 (on migration):** "If Q1 approves migration, should this SorraAgents item be closed as 'moved' with a link to the new WL item?" — **OPEN QUESTION** (awaiting producer). Recommended: close as moved.

# Audit integration worktree does not populate git submodules, causing false-negative build verdicts

## Problem statement

The audit's merge-gate integration step (`_integrate_into_dev`) creates a fresh
detached worktree at `origin/dev` with `git worktree add --detach` and runs
`npm run build` inside it. `git worktree add` never populates tracked
submodules, so any repository that vendors a submodule builds against an
**empty** submodule directory. The build fails with a module-resolution error,
execution-dependent ACs (e.g. "Build and full test suite pass") are marked
`partial`, and the item's verdict becomes "Ready to close: No" — a false
negative on a tree that builds green in the real, populated checkout.

## Users

- **Audit consumers (producers, implement agents)** — need an audit verdict
  that reflects the real tree; today a submodule-vendoring repo is
  systematically misjudged.
  - *As a producer, I want the audit's build verdict to reflect the populated
    checkout, so a green item isn't blocked by an environmental build failure.*
  - *As a ship/release operator, I want releases not to stall on a
    false-negative "not ready to close" caused by empty submodules.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- The integration worktree created by `_integrate_into_dev` has its tracked submodules populated **before** the build runs, so a repo with a submodule dependency has a non-empty submodule directory in that worktree.
- A build run in the integration worktree succeeds on a tree that builds green in the main checkout, so execution-dependent ACs are not marked `partial` for the empty-submodule reason.
- A repository without submodules is unaffected (fail-open), and a submodule-init failure logs a warning without aborting the audit.
- A regression test covers the submodule-population step in the integration worktree (uses the existing tracked-submodule fixture; red before the fix, green after).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Audits of build-dependent items on any submodule-vendoring repository reflect
the real tree, and releases stop being blocked by false-negative "not ready to
close" verdicts.

## Constraints

- **Fail-open is mandatory.** A repo without `.gitmodules` and any submodule-init
  failure must never abort or fail the audit — the worktree is then no worse
  than the launch checkout.
- **Do not re-implement the logic.** The audit runner already has
  `_ensure_execution_worktree_submodules` (added for the F3 execution worktree,
  SA-0MW4ZRLSI005PHL6), which mirrors `implement.py::_ensure_submodules`
  (SA-0MSN52GGN002B0AZ). Reuse it (or promote it to a shared helper) rather
  than adding a third copy.
- **Ordering hazard (SA-0MVTOR53E003IIEQ):** submodule init must run *before*
  the `node_modules` symlink step in the worktree.
- Prefer the `git -c protocol.file.allow=always submodule update --init
  --recursive` invocation the existing audit helper uses (git ≥ 2.38 blocks the
  `file` transport by default, which breaks local-path submodules).
- Never `npm install` inside a worktree — the shared `node_modules` symlink
  convention (SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B) stands.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the integration worktree is the only remaining audit worktree
  that runs a build/test against un-populated submodules (the execution
  worktree is already covered). Verified by grep; if a third worktree appears
  later it must apply the same helper.
- **Risk:** submodule init can be slow (large recursive trees) on the merge-gate
  critical path. Mitigation: keep the existing 600 s timeout and fail-open so a
  slow/failed fetch degrades to the old behaviour rather than blocking.
- **Risk:** network-dependent submodules can fail offline. Mitigation:
  fail-open with a warning in the integration evidence — never abort the audit.
- **Scope creep:** a build being green in *this* framework repo does not prove
  the tce-the-rising scenario; the regression test must use a tracked local-path
  submodule fixture, not a network clone. Other submodule-adjacent waxes (e.g.
  derived-file pin restoration) are separate items, already filed.

## Existing state

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_integrate_into_dev` (≈ line 11924)
  creates `audit-merge-<id>` with `git worktree add --detach`, symlinks
  `node_modules`, runs `npm run build`, then the suite, then pushes to `dev`.
  It contains **no** `git submodule update --init` call.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_ensure_execution_worktree_submodules`
  (≈ line 12149) already implements the exact fail-open behaviour for the
  **execution** worktree (`audit-exec-<id>`), including the `file`-protocol
  allowance and git-env scrubbing.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py::_ensure_submodules` (≈ line 7150)
  is the precedent helper for implement worktrees (SA-0MSN52GGN002B0AZ).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_contaminated_launch.py` has a
  tracked-submodule fixture (`build_contaminated_launch_scenario` →
  `skill/audit/tests/fixtures/contaminated_launch.py`) used to prove the
  execution worktree submodule population.

## Desired change

In `_integrate_into_dev`, after the worktree is created and before the build,
populate tracked submodules using the existing audit helper (rename/generalise
`_ensure_execution_worktree_submodules` to a shared `_ensure_worktree_submodules`
if that reads cleaner). Append the outcome to the integration evidence. Cover
the new step with a regression test in the audit test suite.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — call the submodule-population helper from `_integrate_into_dev` before the build step; possibly generalise the existing helper name.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_merge_gate.py` — add the integration-worktree submodule regression test.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_contaminated_launch.py` / `skill/audit/tests/fixtures/contaminated_launch.py` — reusable tracked-submodule fixture (reuse or extend).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — document the integration-worktree
  submodule population alongside the existing execution-worktree note (AC5).
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — precedent `_ensure_submodules` (reference only, not modified).

## Related work

- **SA-0MW4ZRLSI005PHL6** (completed) — audit runs its pipeline in a fresh
  `origin/dev` worktree; added `_ensure_execution_worktree_submodules` for the
  *execution* worktree. This item closes the sibling gap in the *integration*
  worktree.
- **SA-0MWC6JJBR0050PGQ** (completed) — F3 suite executes in the fresh
  `origin/dev` worktree.
- **SA-0MSN52GGN002B0AZ** (completed) — `_ensure_submodules` for implement
  worktrees (the precedent).
- **SA-0MVTOR53E003IIEQ** — submodule-before-node_modules ordering hazard.
- **SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B** — worktree `node_modules` symlink convention.
- **RISE-0MW7YP6SD0091MKJ** (tce-the-rising) — per-project item superseded by
  this generic framework item (to be deleted).
- **SA-0MT456M27001LRTL** — merge gate / `verifyIntegration` origin.

### Related work (automated report)

- **SA-0MW6LOXBO0008706** – Ship release derived-files step must restore a build-rewritten submodule pin alongside the restored gitlink (completed)
- **SA-0MW06FLFR009F0P4** – Finish gate: report a lagging engine pin when the build fails after engine:sync (completed)
- **SA-0MVB71260006J3FY** – Migrate implement.py repo/worktree fixtures to git_sandbox (blocked)

#### Repository file matches

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`

## Evidence (preserved from seed)

- 2026-11-08 `tce-the-rising` audit of `RISE-0MVXSNH71005PONU` AC4: build
  failed (exit 2) on missing vite config modules, not on the item's changes.
  The real populated tree builds green (`npm run build` exits 0) and the
  cached full suite is green.
- `vite.config.ts` imports from `./core/scripts/…`; `core/` is a tracked
  submodule. `git -c submodule.recurse=true worktree add --detach` leaves
  `core/` with 0 entries (git 2.53.0).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required: the seed context (problem statement,
precedent, evidence, and four draft ACs) was complete enough to draft this
brief. Gaps filled by research rather than interview:

- Q: *Which helper should the fix reuse?* — Answer (research): the audit
  runner already has `_ensure_execution_worktree_submodules`
  (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` ≈ line 12149) implementing the exact
  fail-open, `file`-protocol-allowed `git submodule update --init --recursive`
  pattern; reuse/generalise it rather than copying `implement.py::_ensure_submodules`.
  Source: `grep` of `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`.
- Q: *Is there an existing tracked-submodule test fixture?* — Answer
  (research): yes — `skill/audit/tests/fixtures/contaminated_launch.py` builds
  a scenario with a `core/` submodule; the regression test can reuse/extend it.
  Source: `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_contaminated_launch.py`.

# Audit runner leaves items at open/plan_complete after a failing/aborted audit when a concurrent wl sync races its restore (lost update)

## Problem statement

During an audit, `audit_runner.py` transitions the target item out of
`completed`/`in_review` (to `in-progress`/`in_review` or `open`/`plan_complete`)
and is supposed to **restore it to `completed`/`in_review`** on every exit path
(the abort path logs `Aborted audit for <id>: restoring "completed" "in_review"`).

Under concurrency this restore is **lost**: a `wl sync` running in another
session (or the audit runner's own sync) races the restore, and the item is
left stuck at `open`/`plan_complete` (status `open`, stage `plan_complete`,
`auditResult: null`). The item silently drops out of the release candidate set
(`stage: in_review`) and looks like brand-new, un-implemented work — a
**worklog data-integrity regression**, not a cosmetic glitch.

This is the same class as the known concurrent-`wl sync` lost-update race
(WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ); the audit runner's own status restore is not
race-safe against it.

## Users

- **Release operators** running `/skill:ship release` — corrupted items silently
  drop out of the release candidate set, causing releases to omit valid items or
  include items that failed audit.
- **Agents** implementing work — an item left at `open`/`plan_complete` looks
  like un-implemented work and may be picked up for re-implementation.
- **Producer reviewers** — corrupted items appear in the wrong state in the
  worklog dashboard and reports.

## Observed (2026-11-08, tce-the-rising `/skill:ship release`)

A single release attempt corrupted **four** items, each left at
`open`/`plan_complete` although all four were `completed`/`in_review` before:

| Item | Corrupted by | Prior state (from worklog-data history) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RISE-0MVWWBT8Y009FMZ6` | release gate audit remediation (14:00) | `completed`/`in_review` |
| `RISE-0MW3MXVU5009GMLR` | `--refresh-audits` (14:38) | `completed`/`in_review` |
| `RISE-0MVXSNH71005PONU` | `audit_runner.py issue` (14:57) | `completed`/`in_review` |
| `RISE-0MW3GUQKX004W74K` | `audit_runner.py issue` (14:59) | `completed`/`in_review` |

All four were repaired by hand (`wl update <id> --status completed --stage
in_review`) after reconstructing the prior state from the `refs/worklog/...`
delta history. The corruption spans both the failing-verdict path (a
persisted "Ready to close: No" still left the item at `open`/`plan_complete`)
and the aborted path (the "restoring" message logged but the restore did not
persist).

## Root-cause hypotheses to confirm

- The restore is a plain `wl update` with no compare-and-swap / version guard,
  so a concurrent `wl sync` (pull→merge→push) overwrites it (last-writer-wins
  on a stale snapshot).
- A failing/aborted audit may not run the restore at all on some exit paths
  (the observed `open`/`plan_complete` with a persisted failing verdict
  suggests the restore is skipped when the verdict is not "Yes").

## Desired change

Make the audit runner's status restore **race-safe and unconditional**:

- Restore `completed`/`in_review` on **every** exit path — success, failing
  verdict, abort, exception, timeout — via `try/finally`.
- Use the shared `StatusLifecycle` helper (`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`)
  and its claim/assignee handling so the restore participates in the same
  lost-update protection as other lifecycle exits.
- Guard the restore against a concurrent `wl sync` (e.g. re-read after write,
  retry on mismatch — the same verification pattern the ship skill uses for
  close verification, SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5).
- Never leave an item at `open`/`plan_complete` merely because an audit failed
  — a failing verdict is recorded while the item stays `completed`/`in_review`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An explicit `Ready to close: No` verdict demotes the item to `open`/`plan_complete` deliberately and verified (this is the audit-reject contract); an infra-fallback-tainted, aborted, timed-out or crashed audit never demotes.
- [ ] An aborted audit restores the item to `completed`/`in_review`, verified after write and retried once if a concurrent `wl sync` clobbered the restore.
- [ ] The restore runs on every exit path via `try/finally`, including exceptions raised after the `in_progress` claim.
- [ ] A regression test injects a concurrent `wl sync` between the audit status change and its restore and asserts the item ends `completed`/`in_review`.
- [ ] No item is left at `open`/`plan_complete` or `in_progress` as a side effect of any audit path, and an unverified restore is never reported as success.

## Impact

Auditing an `in_review` item can no longer silently revert it to un-implemented
work, so release candidate sets and worklog state stay correct under
concurrent agent sessions.

## Constraints

- The audit runner's core auditing semantics (what gets audited, how verdicts
  are calculated) must not change — only the status-restore path is affected.
- The fix must not introduce additional contention on the worklog database
  that would slow down normal audit throughput.
- The restore must use the same `--worklog-dir` resolution as the rest of the
  audit runner (cwd-independent).

## Existing state

`audit_runner.py` transitions the target item to `open`/`plan_complete` at the
start of an audit and has restore logic on the abort path, but:
- The restore is not wrapped in `try/finally` (missing on some exit paths).
- The restore is a plain `wl update` — no re-read/verify/retry against concurrent
  `wl sync` (the same pattern fixed in SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5).
- The failing-verdict path may skip the restore entirely.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Audit runner core; status transition and restore logic live here.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — Shared lifecycle helper with claim/assignee semantics.
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — Reference for the close-verification retry pattern (SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5).
- `skill/audit/tests/` — Test directory for audit runner tests.
- `skill/shared/worklog_sync.py` — The `wl sync` helper that the race originates from.

## Related work

- **SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5** — Ship release must verify in-scope work items are actually closed before reporting success (lost-update close verification pattern).
- **SA-0MVE34D9B005TUYJ** — wl sync --if-idle reverts actively-worked items to open/intake_complete (lost-update race fix).
- **SA-0MVWFPI31000HP3H** — Only mark as complete when fully complete (adjacent lifecycle-transition safety).
- **SA-0MVI35BIU002MTZQ** — Audit runner: parent-persisted child audits demote in_review children (completed) (adjacent audit-raced-lifecycle-transition precedent).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The restore logic exists on the abort path but is lost to race — not completely absent. Needs code verification.
- **Risk:** Adding a retry loop to the restore could introduce subtle timing issues if the retry window overlaps with other concurrent operations.
- **Risk:** The fix must not change audit timing behaviour — agents must not see longer audit durations.
- **Scope creep:** Fixing the general `wl sync` lost-update race (WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ) is out of scope; this item only fixes the audit runner's restore path.


## Plan (plan skill, 2026-11-13)

Planning decision: **plan required** (effort Small / risk Medium — above the
auto-skip threshold). Approval gate not requested (only *Extra Large* effort
**and** *High/Severe* risk triggers an approval pause).

### Code inspection results (closes the two open questions in this item)

1. **"Has the failing-verdict path been verified to run the restore?"**
   Partly — and the reported symptom is (mostly) a misdiagnosis. A genuine
   explicit `Ready to close: No` verdict **deliberately demotes** to
   `open`/`plan_complete` (the audit-reject workflow: `_apply_terminal_lifecycle`
   'no' branch; documented in `skill/audit/SKILL.md` → Status Lifecycle;
   pinned by `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`
   `test_ready_no_sets_open_plan_complete` and `test_audit_runner_core.py`
   "A 'No' verdict still demotes to open/plan_complete"). An
   **infra-fallback-tainted** `No`, a timeout, a provider error, a parse
   failure or a crash takes the **restore** branch and must never demote.
   The observed `open`/`plan_complete` items all had `auditResult: null`,
   i.e. the run never persisted a verdict — consistent with an aborted run
   whose restore was lost, not with a demoting `No`.
2. **"Does `StatusLifecycle` provide verify-then-retry?"** No. The in-run
   lifecycle verification/retry (3 attempts, linear backoff) lives in
   `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` (WL-0MSVVFBJ2003RRYK), *not* in
   `StatusLifecycle`. Three restore paths are weaker or unverified:
   - `_restore_pre_audit_state_on_failure` — one write, one readback, no retry.
   - `_restore_work_item_status` (SIGTERM/SIGINT handler) — one write, **no
     readback**.
   - `check-audit-gate.js::checkAndRestoreStuckAudit` — the parent-side
     SIGKILL recovery that logs `Aborted audit for <id>: restoring ...`:
     a bare `wl update`, **no readback, no retry**, and the state file is
     deleted even when the restore did not persist (so a lost update is
     unrecoverable). This is the exact log line quoted in the problem
     statement. The same gap applies to every other state-file consumer.
   - `cmd_issue`'s `finally` is entered *after* the `in_progress` claim in
     `_phase_gate`, so an exception between the claim and the `try`
     (`audit_lease_begin`, `_open_checkpoint_store`) leaves the claim behind.
   - `wl audit-set --ready-to-close no` demotes as a *persist-time side
     effect* (worklog `revertToPlanComplete`), before the terminal
     lifecycle corrects it — an unguarded window on restore-bound runs
     (same class as SA-0MVI35BIU002MTZQ, fixed there for children only).

### Plan decision D1 — AC1 wording reconciled (producer confirmation requested)

AC1 as originally written ("a failing verdict leaves the item at
`completed`/`in_review` — never `open`/`plan_complete`") **contradicts the
documented, tested audit-reject contract** described above; implementing it
literally would remove the mechanism that returns rejected work to the
actionable queue, invalidate 8+ existing tests, and change release-gate
semantics. Evidence (source code and tests override the worklog text)
supports narrowing AC1 to: *an explicit `No` demotes deliberately and
verified; nothing else may demote, ever*. This is recorded as producer
question Q3 in the Appendix and the item carries `needsProducerReview`, so
the producer can overrule before the policy child is implemented. If
overruled, only child F4 (policy) and AC1 change — the three mechanical
fixes stand unchanged.

### Features (vertical slices, test-first order)

| # | Child | Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F1 | Race-clobber restore regression tests | task | Deterministic clobber injection (tests first, red before the fix) |
| F2 | Verified-retry in-run lifecycle restore | task | Python runner: settle-verify-retry on every restore path + claim inside the guard |
| F3 | Verified-retry parent-side abort restore | task | `check-audit-gate.js` state-file restore: readback + one retry + retained state file |
| F4 | Verdict-demotion policy documented and pinned | docs | Document reconciled contract; pin explicit-`No` demotion vs never-demote paths |

Each child is a deliverable end-to-end slice (code + tests + docs where
applicable). No horizontal layer phases are needed at this size.

### Requirement to feature mapping

| Requirement (this item) | Covered by |
| --- | --- |
| Desired change 1 - restore on every exit path (`try/finally`, exceptions) | F2 (in-run, claim inside the guard), F3 (parent-side abort) |
| Desired change 2 - use the shared `StatusLifecycle` claim/assignee handling | F2 (key file + assignee-release semantics; reuse the shared claim-release predicate) |
| Desired change 3 - guard the restore against a concurrent `wl sync` (re-read/retry) | F1 (red test), F2, F3 |
| Desired change 4 - never leave an item `open`/`plan_complete` merely because an audit failed (reconciled by D1: only a genuine explicit `No` demotes) | F2, F4 |
| AC1 (reworded by D1) | F2 (non-demoting paths) + F4 (contract pinned; awaits Q3) |
| AC4 (regression test injecting a concurrent `wl sync`) | F1 |
| Constraints - semantics unchanged, no added contention, cwd-independent `--worklog-dir` | F2 (explicit ACs); F3 (state-file dirs unchanged) |

### Traceability

- Duplicate check performed (`wl search` "restore race lifecycle", `wl search`
  "audit restore lost update"): no full duplicate. Precedents:
  SA-0MRNKVPTA005FKBG (restore-pre-audit-state), SA-0MTRH8C5O005URGR (abort
  recovery state file), SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5 (close verification), and the
  partially overlapping open idea SA-0MVIO0WQW006Y1FS (audit slot + verdict
  lifecycle idempotence) — related, not duplicate.
- Children F2/F3 depend on F1 (tests first); F4 depends on F2 and F3 (it
  documents the behaviour those slices land).

## Appendix

- Q: "Has the failing-verdict path been verified to run the restore?" — A: OPEN QUESTION — code inspection needed. The observed `open`/`plan_complete` with a persisted failing verdict suggests it does not.
- Q: "Does StatusLifecycle provide a mechanism for verify-then-retry on status restoration?" — A: To be confirmed — StatusLifecycle has claim/assignee handling; verify-then-retry may need to be added or handled externally (as the ship skill does).
- Q (Q1): "Has the failing-verdict path been verified to run the restore?" -
  **Answer (code inspection, plan 2026-11-13):** a genuine explicit `No`
  demotes **by design** (`_apply_terminal_lifecycle` 'no' branch, documented in
  `skill/audit/SKILL.md` and pinned by `test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`);
  infra-fallback/timeout/abort runs take the restore branch. The corrupted
  items had `auditResult: null`, i.e. no verdict was persisted - an aborted run
  with a lost restore, not a demoting `No`. Evidence:
  `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (`_apply_terminal_lifecycle`,
  `_compute_fallback_tainted`), `skill/audit/SKILL.md` section "Status
  Lifecycle", `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`.
- Q (Q2): "Does `StatusLifecycle` provide verify-then-retry on status
  restoration?" - **Answer (plan 2026-11-13):** No. Verify-then-retry lives in
  `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` (3 attempts, linear backoff, WL-0MSVVFBJ2003RRYK).
  `_restore_pre_audit_state_on_failure` (single write, single readback),
  `_restore_work_item_status` (signal handler: write only) and
  `check-audit-gate.js::checkAndRestoreStuckAudit` (bare `wl update`, no
  readback, state file deleted regardless) are unprotected - the last one emits
  the exact `Aborted audit for <id>: restoring ...` line from the problem
  statement.
- Q (Q3, OPEN QUESTION - producer): "AC1 as written says a failing verdict must
  leave the item at `completed`/`in_review`, but the audit-reject contract
  (documented in `skill/audit/SKILL.md` and covered by existing tests) requires
  a genuine explicit `No` to demote to `open`/`plan_complete`. Which wins?" -
  **Plan recommendation:** keep the documented demotion for a genuine explicit
  `No` (verified), and make every other path non-demoting (plan decision D1,
  AC1 reworded accordingly). Directed to: producer, because overruling would
  change release-gate/reject semantics. Matters because AC1 and child F4
  (policy documentation) depend on it.
data.title: Audit runner leaves items at open/plan_complete after a failing/aborted audit when a concurrent wl sync races its restore (lost update)

data.description:
# Intake Brief: Ship skill triggered audits should not mark for producer review

## Problem statement

When the ship skill's release gates auto-remediate a missing/stale/transient
audit by re-running `audit_runner.py issue <id> --strict`, that run follows the
**independent audit** contract and can write `--needs-producer-review yes`: a
top-level 'Ready to close: Yes' verdict that needs a producer decision, or an
independent top-level 'No' verdict, both arm the producer-review hold. These
are release-automation verification runs, not independent reviews, so the
release silently self-inflicts producer-review holds that block its own gates
(exit 9 producer-review gate, exit 12 final-validation sweep) and flood the
producer queue with items the release itself just touched. The audit behaviour
when run independently must stay exactly as it is today.

## Users

- **Producers running a release** — user story: "When I run `/skill:ship`, the
  release's own audit remediation must not set `needsProducerReview` on the
  items it re-audits — I don't want the release to block itself or queue
  spurious producer approvals I then have to clear."
- **Audit operators** — user story: "I want a ship-triggered re-audit to be
  distinguishable from an independent review: it verifies, it never queues
  producer attention; an independent audit still flags exactly as documented."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Ship-triggered runs leave the flag untouched.** When the ship skill's
   release gates (Step 2 audit readiness gate, Step 6 final-validation sweep)
   or its pre-flight `--refresh-audits` re-audit an item via
   `audit_runner.py issue <id> --strict` with a ship-trigger marker, the runner
   never writes `--needs-producer-review` — a top-level 'Yes' verdict that would
   otherwise require a producer decision leaves `needsProducerReview` untouched,
   and a top-level 'No' verdict also leaves it untouched (neither
   set nor cleared).
2. **Independent audit behaviour is unchanged.** An audit run without the ship
   marker behaves exactly as today: a top-level 'Yes' with a producer decision
   required still writes `--needs-producer-review yes` (subject to the
   preserved/untouched carve-outs of SA-0MVR9B1UH002BUST and
   SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42), and an independent top-level 'No' still flags the item.
3. **Only the flag write is suppressed.** All other lifecycle behaviour of a
   ship-triggered run is unchanged: 'Yes' still advances to
   `completed`/`in_review`; 'No' still demotes to `open`/`plan_complete` (and
   stays subject to cascade-demotion suppression); the persisted report still
   records the verdict and a `Producer review: untouched (…)` metadata line.
4. **Targeted tests.** Tests exercise production code (not re-implementations)
   and lock: ship-triggered 'Yes' (top-level) → no `--needs-producer-review`
   write; ship-triggered 'No' (top-level) → no flag write, demotion still
   applied; marker absence → independent 'Yes'/'No' writes the flag exactly as
   today; the marker cannot leak (a run without it never suppresses).
5. **Documentation updated.** `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (producer-review rules),
   `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (Producer-review flag lifecycle) and
   `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` (audit-gate remediation
   sections) document that ship-triggered audits leave `needsProducerReview`
   untouched, and that surfaced manual remediation commands (operator-invoked)
   remain independent.
6. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Impact

Producers no longer see a release's own audit remediation queue spurious
producer-review holds that block that same release, so `/skill:ship` no longer
self-blocks or forces manual flag clearing after every release.

## Constraints

- **Independent runs untouched:** the marker must only ever be set by
  ship-automated invocations; operator-invoked commands (the surfaced
  `python3 … audit_runner.py issue <id> --strict [--force]` remediation hints
  and the `batch --strict` offline-refresh hint) stay marker-free and keep
  independent flagging behaviour.
- **No new flag-clearing behaviour:** the runner never writes
  `--needs-producer-review no`; ship-triggered suppression means "don't write
  the flag at all", not "clear it afterwards". The ship close step's authorised
  override (`wl update <child> --needs-producer-review false`, SA-0MUJLWPB10038Z8Q)
  is unchanged.
- **No leakage risk from the mechanism:** the chosen trigger marker must not be
  accidentally set in an operator's shell, or every audit on that host would
  silently suppress producer flagging.
- **Verdict semantics unchanged:** suppression is about the producer-review
  flag only; 'Ready to close' conclusions, freshness, and gate blocking are
  untouched.
- **Repository boundary:** this repo (SorraAgents) owns both skills; no herdr/
  ContextHub change is required.

## Existing state

- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — Step 2 audit-gate remediation:
  `runAuditCommand` default runs `python3 "<runnerPath>" issue ${workItemId} --strict`
  (~line 860); surfaced manual hints at ~lines 404/536/656 carry no marker.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` — Step 6 sweep remediation:
  `runAuditCommand` default runs the same `issue <id> --strict` (~line 479).
- `skill/ship/scripts/refresh-audits.js` — pre-flight `--refresh-audits`:
  `runAuditCommand` default runs the same `issue <id> --strict` (~line 132).
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_resolve_producer_review_decision()`
  (~line 2747) returns `required` for (a) a top-level 'Yes' needing a producer
  decision and (b) an independent top-level 'No'; `_apply_terminal_lifecycle()`
  (~lines 17122–17220) writes `--needs-producer-review yes` whenever
  `producer_review["action"] == PRODUCER_REVIEW_REQUIRED`. The only existing
  trigger-context carve-out is the child-audit cascade marker
  (`AUDIT_CASCADE_AUDIT`, ~line 257): children are never flagged, and a
  cascade-demotion-suppressed 'No' leaves the flag untouched. There is no
  ship-trigger context today, so every gate-remediation re-audit is treated as
  independent.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (~lines 35/38) and
  `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (~lines 444–542) document the
  produce-review flag lifecycle; `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`
  documents the audit-gate remediation paths that invoke the runner.

## Desired change

Pass a **ship-trigger marker** on the audit runner invocation from the three
ship remediation call sites, and have the runner consult it in
`_resolve_producer_review_decision()` so a marked run resolves
`PRODUCER_REVIEW_UNTOUCHED` (reason: "ship-triggered audit — flag untouched")
for both 'Yes' and 'No' verdicts, recorded in the persisted report as
`Producer review: untouched (ship-triggered audit — flag untouched)`. No other
lifecycle code path changes: advance/demote/cascade behaviour and the
independent-run flag rules are exactly as today. Document the contract in the
audit and ship skill docs.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_resolve_producer_review_decision()`
  (~line 2747), `_apply_terminal_lifecycle()` (~lines 17122–17220),
  `PRODUCER_REVIEW_UNTOUCHED`, the `issue` arg parser (~lines 18227–18440);
  the ship-trigger marker check and the new flag/arg.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — `runAuditCommand` default (~line 860);
  append the marker to the remediation invocation.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` — `runAuditCommand` default (~line 479).
- `skill/ship/scripts/refresh-audits.js` — `runAuditCommand` default (~line 132).
- `skill/audit/tests/` — producer-review decision tests
  (`test_audit_runner_producer_review.py`), lifecycle/flag tests
  (`test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`), merge-gate flag tests
  (`test_audit_runner_merge_gate.py`); new ship-trigger coverage.
- `skill/ship/tests/` — gate remediation / pre-flight tests asserting the
  marker is present on remediation invocations.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`,
  `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — producer-review lifecycle and
  remediation docs.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVR9B1UH002BUST** — Audit runner: preserve a producer's review across
  passing re-audits; flag failing audits for producer review (completed).
  Defines the `preserved|required|untouched` decision; this item adds the
  ship-trigger context to that decision.
- **SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42** — audit_runner sets needsProducerReview for every
  medium/low 'candidate false positive' chore, blocking releases (completed).
  Extended the `untouched` carve-outs; same spirit as this item's suppression.
- **SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H** — Audit pass should set needsProducerReview only for
  top-level items (completed). Children are never flagged; this item extends
  "not flagged" to ship-triggered runs while keeping child rule intact.
- **SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW** — Set producerReview flag when automated audit marks
  item as ready to close (completed). Foundational flag-on-yes rule; the
  ship-trigger context is the exception this item carves out.
- **SA-0MVX4EHUP0042V9G** — Ship skill invalidates audits (in-progress).
  Adjacent ship/audit interaction concern (freshness signal), distinct ACs;
  no overlap in the flag write.
- **SA-0MUJLWPB10038Z8Q** — Ship skill: release-ready
  parent must override or absorb needsProducerReview on children (completed).
  The ship close-step override is out of scope here and must keep working.
- **SA-0MWIIOMY10054VJI** — Audit report Conclusion can claim 'Ready to ship'
  when the audit failed (in-progress). Distinct (report text), link for
  awareness.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — the gate-remediation `issue <id> --strict` invocations are the
  only ship-triggered audits.** The `batch --strict`, `check-freshness` and the
  surfaced text-only remediation hints are not executed by the release
  automation itself (verified by grepping the three `runAuditCommand` defaults
  and the hint strings).
- **Assumption — the flag is the only suppressed write.** The item wording
  limits scope to `needsProducerReview`; advance/demote/cascade behaviour stays
  (AC3). An alternative ("suppress demotion entirely, like a cascade audit")
  is recorded as an OPEN QUESTION in the Appendix.
- **Risk — marker leakage.** An env-var marker could be set accidentally in an
  operator's shell and silence producer flagging host-wide; a CLI flag cannot
  leak the same way. Recommend CLI flag (see Appendix Q1).
- **Risk — test-isolation regression.** Ship `runAuditCommand` boundaries are
  injectable; new marker assertions must keep tests hermetic (no live `wl`/
  runner calls), per the established convention.
- **Risk — scope creep into the report/metadata contract.** The persisted
  report gains a new `untouched` reason; existing consumers must tolerate it
  (it already tolerates arbitrary `untouched (<reason>)` strings).
- **Scope-creep guard.** Options recorded in the Appendix OPEN QUESTIONS
  (env-var marker, demotion suppression, marking operator-invoked hints) are
  deliberately out of scope here; if the producer wants any of them they are
  separate linked work items, not scope for this one.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **OPEN QUESTION (mechanism, SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ):** How should the audit
  runner know a run is ship-triggered? (a) **New CLI flag
  `--ship-triggered` on `issue`** — visible in logs and surfaced commands, no
  shell-leakage risk, matches the runner's flag-driven CLI (`--strict`,
  `--do-not-persist`, `--audit-children`); (b) an env var such as
  `AUDIT_SHIP_TRIGGERED=1` set in the execSync environment, mirroring the
  existing `AUDIT_CASCADE_AUDIT` pattern; (c) ship clears the flag after each
  remediation run. **Recommended (Map, intake): (a) — explicit and leakage-safe;
  an env var can silently taint every audit on the host if set in a shell
  profile, and option (c) fights the runner's never-clear contract.** Source:
  inspection of `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` arg parser and
  `_resolve_producer_review_decision`, and `skill/ship/scripts/*.js`
  `runAuditCommand` defaults. Not producer-confirmed.
- **OPEN QUESTION ('No' verdict scope):** For a ship-triggered re-audit whose
  verdict is 'Ready to close: No', should the item still be demoted to
  `open`/`plan_complete` (only the flag suppressed), or should the demotion be
  suppressed too (behaving like the cascade-demotion carve-out for already
  `in_review`/`done` items)? **Recommended (Map, intake): keep the demotion,
  suppress only the flag — the item genuinely failed, so it must leave the
  release queue; the release gate already blocks on the failing verdict (exit
  12), and AC3/AC1 wording limits the change to the flag.** Source:
  `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` 'No' branch. Not producer-confirmed.
- **OPEN QUESTION (manual/operator runs):** The release gate output surfaces
  marker-free `python3 … audit_runner.py issue <id> --strict [--force]` and
  `batch --strict` hints for the operator to run manually. Should those
  operator-invoked runs also be treated as ship-triggered? **Recommended (Map,
  intake): no — they are independent audits by definition; only the three
  release-automation invocation sites get the marker (the seed context states
  "audit behaviour when run independently should continue to behave as it does
  now").** Source: check-audit-gate.js hint builders (~lines 404/536/656) and
  audit-remediation.js `OFFLINE_AUDIT_REFRESH_HINT`. Not producer-confirmed.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MRL8W6V7006LH5I** – If a child audit is not ready to close then the parent must also be marked as no ready to close (completed)
- **SA-0MRGVN9XM003LNQ7** – Close work items when shipping (completed)
- **SA-0MSKB6V5Q007YDHE** – Audit: opt-in child audit cascade with run cap (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: audit, audits, behave, behaviour, change, checks, continue, flag, independently, mark, needsproducerreview, now, producer, release, run, runs, ship, should, triggered, when
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: audit, audits, behave, behaviour, change, checks, continue, flag, independently, mark, needsproducerreview, now, producer, release, run, runs, ship, should, triggered, when
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: audit, audits, behave, behaviour, change, checks, continue, flag, independently, mark, needsproducerreview, now, producer, release, run, runs, ship, should, triggered, when


---

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-11-16 (plan skill, Map/dispatcher dispatch)**: Decomposed into 4 children in test-first dependency order:
  1. `SA-0MWJ7ECZV0050OEZ` — Test: audit_runner ship-trigger producer review decision (leaf, no deps)
  2. `SA-0MWJ7K962006646G` — Implement: audit_runner ship-trigger marker (depends on test)
  3. `SA-0MWJ7KPC00073EMP` — Implement: ship skill ship-trigger marker threading (depends on runner implement)
  4. `SA-0MWJ7KZT7009480N` — Implement: documentation updates (depends on both implement items)
  - Chosen mechanism: CLI flag `--ship-triggered` on the `issue` subcommand (recommended in Appendix Q1; leakage-safe vs env var).
  - AC coverage review: 100% covered, `proceed`.

## Plan: Appendix (questions & answers)

- Q1 (mechanism): How should the audit runner know a run is ship-triggered? **Answer (plan, adopting intake recommendation):** a new CLI flag `--ship-triggered` on the `issue` subcommand — visible in logs, no shell-leakage risk, matches the runner's flag-driven CLI. Env-var marker and ship-side clearing rejected (leakage risk / violates never-clear contract). Consistent with the item's "No leakage risk from the mechanism" constraint.

Only the three release-automation invocation sites get the marker.

## Objective

Make `/skill:ship release` judge the importance of the work items in the release and propose the semantically correct semver bump (patch, minor, or major), instead of always bumping patch — with the producer asked in the PI session before any non-patch bump is applied.

## Problem Statement

The ship skill currently always increments the `z` (patch) component of the release version (`merge-dev-to-main.sh` defaults `BUMP="patch"`), even when the release adds new or breaking capability. Releases that add features therefore ship as patch versions (e.g. `v0.1.19` instead of `v0.2.0`), misrepresenting the release's impact and forcing the producer to remember `--bump minor` manually.

## Users

- **Release manager (the PI agent running `/skill:ship release`)** — must judge the release's importance from the items being shipped and propose the right bump without extra flags.
- **Producer** — must see and approve any non-patch bump, in the session, with a full justification naming the items that triggered it.

Example user stories:

- As a release manager, when every item in the release is a fix, chore, or documentation change, I want the release to bump patch automatically so that I don't have to think about semver.
- As a release manager, when the release contains meaningful new capability, I want to propose a minor bump with evidence, rather than silently shipping it as a patch.
- As a producer, I want to be asked, in the session, before a minor or major bump is applied, with a justification naming the items and why they warrant the bump — and I want to be able to decline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The ship skill's release workflow gains a startup **version-bump evaluation** step that runs before any git mutation and gathers every release candidate (`wl list --stage in_review`) with enough context for a judgement: ID, title, type, priority, `## Impact`/user story and a short description excerpt.
- The agent judges the importance of the release from those items and proposes exactly one bump: **patch** when the release only fixes, documents, or maintains; **minor** when it adds meaningful new capability; **major** when it breaks or removes existing capability or otherwise changes behaviour incompatibly (the existing `--bump` override remains available).
- A **patch** proposal proceeds automatically with no producer interaction — the current `--bump patch` behaviour and `merge-dev-to-main.sh` default are unchanged.
- A **minor or major** proposal prints a full justification — each contributing item ID and title, why it warrants the bump, and the proposed `old → new` version — and the agent asks the producer **in the PI session**; no git mutation, tag, PR, or worklog close occurs until the producer approves.
- Producer approval proceeds with the approved `--bump`; a declined non-patch proposal is honoured (the agent does not apply it, and records the decision and the producer's preferred bump in the session and on the release's work item).
- In a non-interactive/headless context where the producer cannot be asked, a minor or major proposal is never auto-approved: the agent records the justification, flags the item for producer review, and stops.
- The judgement is based on the release items' content (Impact/description/capability), not on `issueType` or a label lookup; the justification cites the evidence used.
- Minor bumps reset `z` to `0`, and major bumps reset `y` and `z` to `0`, reusing the existing `release/bump-version.js` semantics rather than duplicating version arithmetic.
- Unit tests cover: candidate gathering (including an empty candidate set), the review packet/justification rendering, patch auto-proceed, and the non-patch approval-pending behaviour (no mutation); no test reads or mutates the live worklog.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including `skill/ship/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`, and code comments.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Releases that add or break capability will carry a version number that reflects it, and producers will be asked in-session to approve that call with evidence instead of policing `--bump` flags by hand.

## Existing State

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` sets `BUMP="patch"` by default and accepts `--bump patch|minor|major` (already validates the value).
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` parses and forwards `--bump` to the merge script; the wrapper has no bump evaluation step and its documented exit codes are `0`–`14`.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js` already implements `patch`/`minor`/`major` arithmetic correctly (including `z = 0` on minor and `y = z = 0` on major) and resolves `package.json` or `pyproject.toml` as the version source.
- Release candidates are items with `stage: in_review` (`check-audit-gate.js::getCandidateItems`), so the candidate set already exists.
- The release wrapper subprocess is non-interactive, but the ship skill itself is a PI skill executed by an agent in a session — the agent, not the shell script, is the component that can ask the producer.

## Desired Change

1. Add a small, unit-testable helper (e.g. `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js`) that gathers release candidates and renders a compact review packet: per item `id`, `title`, `issueType`, `priority`, `## Impact` (or user story) and a truncated description excerpt, plus the current version and the three candidate bump outcomes. It gathers and renders only — no judgement, no mutation.
2. Add a "Version bump evaluation" step at the start of the documented release workflow in `skill/ship/SKILL.md` (before gates and merge): run the preflight, judge the release's importance, and choose patch/minor/major.
3. Patch → run the release normally (patch is the existing default).
4. Minor/major → present the justification to the producer in the session and wait for approval; on approval run `run-release.js --bump <approved>`; on decline, do not apply.
5. Keep the judgement rationale and the producer's decision in the session output and, where the release is tied to a work item, in a comment so the version choice is auditable.
6. Update `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` and the SKILL.md workflow/argument docs to describe the evaluation step and the in-session approval gate.

## Constraints

- **Judgement stays with the agent:** no issue-type or label mapping, and no mechanical classifier is added — the evaluation prompt/rubric is documented, and the agent makes the call from the items' content.
- **Producer gates non-patch bumps:** minor and major bumps must never be applied without an explicit producer approval in the session. Patch bumps stay automatic.
- **Fail-closed in headless runs:** where no producer is available (downtime/automated dispatches), a minor/major proposal must stop with producer review rather than self-approve.
- **Backward compatible:** an explicit `--bump` keeps its current meaning and precedence; invoking `merge-dev-to-main.sh` directly keeps its `patch` default.
- **No duplicated version arithmetic:** reuse `bump-version.js` for the actual bump; the new code only gathers evidence and renders the proposal.
- **Fail-safe:** an unreadable/empty candidate set must default to patch with a warning and must never block a release that would otherwise succeed; a preflight failure must not mutate the repository.
- **No live-worklog test access:** unit tests must inject the candidate-fetch boundary.
- **Auditability:** the proposed and approved bump, the justification, and the producer's decision are recorded (session output plus a work-item comment for item-linked releases).

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — new "Version bump evaluation" workflow step, in-session approval gate, argument/behaviour docs.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` — new candidate-gathering/review-packet helper (and its tests).
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — unchanged `--bump` forwarding, plus any logging of the decided bump; verify no new git side effects.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — receives the decided `--bump`; default unchanged.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js` — reused as-is for arithmetic (verify minor resets patch to `0`, major resets minor and patch).
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — `getCandidateItems` is the release-candidate source.
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — reference for the evaluation step and approval gate.
- `skill/ship/tests/` — new unit tests for the preflight helper and the approval-pending path.

## Related Work

- **SA-0MPYO85WW006CXPL** — Add version numbering to ship skill for releases (introduced the bump step and `v<semver>` tag convention).
- **SA-0MVN2B0DJ00135W0** — ship: bump-version.js must support Python projects (version source resolution).
- **SA-0MRB2FB5X008X4MM** — Fix bump-version.js REPO_ROOT resolution for global skill installs.
- **SA-0MQI6MDUP001S8NL** — bump-version.js isMainModule check fails on symlinked install paths.
- **SA-0MRGVN9XM003LNQ7** — Close work items when shipping (uses the released version in `Shipped in v<version>` markers).
- **SA-0MV0PZYMI004SUFR** — Newly-created-tag gate (precedent for a fail-closed startup gate with a distinct exit code).
- **SA-0MUIVIJFT0009ZNV** — Missing-script fail-fast (precedent for refusing early, before any git/worklog side effects).

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Judgement subjectivity (risk):** "meaningful new capability" is a judgement call, and two agents could judge the same release differently. Mitigation: a documented rubric (new capability → minor, breaking change → major, fixes/docs/maintenance only → patch), the evidence-based justification, and the producer's in-session approval for every non-patch bump.
- **Producer availability (risk):** a headless release cannot ask anyone. Mitigation: a non-patch proposal in a headless run stops with producer review instead of self-approving; patch releases are unaffected.
- **Agent discipline (risk):** the gate lives in the documented workflow, so a release run by bypassing the skill (direct `run-release.js`) is not gated. Mitigation: document the workflow as the canonical path, and keep the version arithmetic and safety gates in the script unchanged.
- **Scope-creep risk:** per-item bump annotations, automatic CHANGELOG grouping, and mechanical classification are separate opportunities and should be filed as follow-up items rather than folded into this change.
- **Empty candidate set:** a release with no `in_review` items (e.g. hotfix) defaults to patch and logs why.
- **`--skip-checks` interaction (assumption):** `--skip-checks` bypasses branch/critical gates only; the bump evaluation still runs, and an explicit `--bump` remains an operator override.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 (basis for minor-worthiness):** How should the release's importance be judged?
  - Options considered: (A) by `issueType`; (B) by `priority`; (C) by an explicit label/tag; (D) the agent's interpretation of the items' importance.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-14):** "It's not about issue type or label. It's about your interpretation of the importance of the items in the release. Make the best call you can. Check with the producer." → **Option D**, with a documented rubric and producer confirmation.
- **Q2 (approval mechanism):** How is the producer asked to approve a proposed minor/major bump?
  - Options considered: (A) fail-closed exit code + producer re-runs with `--bump`; (B) an interactive prompt inside the PI session; (C) automatic bump with a warning.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-14):** "It's a skill in PI, ask in the session." → **Option B**: the agent presents the justification and asks the producer in the session; the subprocess itself stays non-interactive.
- **Q3 (major inference):** Should a `major` (x) bump be inferred?
  - Options considered: (A) no — only minor/patch; (B) infer and suggest major, but never apply without producer approval.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-14):** "You can infer it and suggest it, but never implement without checking with the producer." → **Option B**: major may be proposed and justified, gated by the same in-session producer approval as minor.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MPYO85WW006CXPL** – Add version numbering to ship skill for releases (completed)
- **SA-0MRB2FB5X008X4MM** – Fix bump-version.js REPO_ROOT resolution for global skill installs (completed)
- **SA-0MVN2B0DJ00135W0** – ship: bump-version.js must support Python projects (pyproject.toml version source) (completed)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: able, acceptance, accepts, access, actual (+331 more)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: able, acceptance, accepts, actual, add (+325 more)

# `finish` cannot converge after an interrupted push: a prior-run commit is not attributed

## Problem statement

SA-0MVYYL7X9008MGA1 made `finish` refuse the terminal write when its run creates no commit (AC1). The refusal triggers on `CommitOutcome.committed` being false — i.e. **only commits created by the current run count**.

That misses the documented interruption-recovery contract in `phase_finish`'s own docstring (SA-0MVXUSJJY009HMQ0): "Re-running `finish` then converges to `completed` / `in_review` through the ordinary no-diff/no-op-push path." After an interrupted push the worktree is **clean** and its commit already exists, so a re-run creates no commit and is now refused with `commit.reason = "no_commit_no_signal"` — a message that also states, falsely, that "nothing was committed or pushed".

Observed (2026-11-09): SA-0MW74IKJE008JXDQ's session timed out during the dev push. Commit `049ff2669` existed on the worktree branch and on local `dev` but not on `origin/dev`; `finish` could not be re-run to publish and finalise it. The work had to be pushed and reconciled by hand.

Parent AC2 already scopes attribution correctly — a report "may only name a commit that is attributable to this item (created by this finish run **or a prior run of this item's worktree**)" — so this is the missing half of that requirement, not new scope.

## Users

- Agent sessions running `implement.py finish` that were interrupted during the push phase, which must now be recovered without manual intervention.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — `phase_finish` attributes a commit created by a **prior run of this item's worktree**: when `git_commit` reports no new commit but HEAD carries commits that are ahead of the parent branch (`origin/<parent_branch>`) and whose messages reference the work-item id, finish proceeds with the existing fast-forward/push path, names that commit in the report, the completion comment and the retained-state interruption record (`_set_finish_progress`), and finalises normally.
- AC2 — The refusal still fires for a genuinely work-less worktree: no attributable commit ahead of the parent branch and no verification-only signal → `commit.reason = "no_commit_no_signal"`, no terminal write, no push, no completion comment (the parent epic's AC1).
- AC3 — The no-op refusal message no longer claims "nothing was committed or pushed" when an attributable commit exists but is not being attributed; wording is accurate for both paths.
- AC4 — Automated regression coverage: (i) an interrupted-push re-run (clean tree, attributable commit ahead of `origin/dev`, absent from `origin/dev`) converges to `completed`/`in_review` and publishes the commit; (ii) the existing no-work refusal test still fails loudly; (iii) `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_interruption_recovery.py` exercises the **real** `git_commit` boundary (not a truthy stub) for the converging re-run, so the stub can no longer mask this path.
- AC5 — `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` state that a re-run after an interrupted push finalises by attributing the prior-run commit.

## Impact

A finish interrupted during its push can be re-run to completion instead of being refused as a no-op, so an agent never has to push and reconcile a half-finished item by hand.

## Constraints

- Attribution must be strict: only commits whose messages reference the work-item id and that are attributable to this worktree are considered. Ambient HEAD from another item's commit must never be claimed (parent epic AC2).
- The refusal path must remain intact for genuinely work-less items.
- The fix must not change the behaviour when `git_commit` succeeds (creates a new commit).

## Existing state

`phase_finish` (commit-outcome branch, ~line 11900 of `implement.py`; line numbers as of this plan) checks `commit_outcome.committed`. When `False`, it:
1. Sets `commit_hash = git_get_commit_hash(worktree_path)` (ambient HEAD — discarded from the report)
2. Sets `reason = "no_commit_no_signal"`
3. Refuses the terminal write with a message that says "nothing was committed or pushed"

The code at ~line 11969 sets `_set_finish_progress` with `commit=""` (never attributes the ambient HEAD), confirming the design intent to not misattribute. But it also never looks for an attributable commit from a prior run.

## Desired change

When `commit_created` is False in `phase_finish`:
1. Check whether HEAD of the worktree has commits ahead of the parent branch whose messages reference the work-item id.
2. If an attributable commit is found, use it for the report and push path (proceed as if committed).
3. If not, refuse with an updated message that does not falsely claim "nothing was committed or pushed".

## Plan (plan skill, 2026-11-10)

Effort **Small**, risk **Low** — below the decomposition threshold, so no child
work items: this is one end-to-end slice.

**Implementation order (test-first).**

1. Extend `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_interruption_recovery.py` with the
   interrupted-push re-run case driven through the **real** `git_commit`
   boundary: a temporary repository whose worktree is clean, whose HEAD is one
   commit ahead of `origin/dev` with a message referencing the item id, and
   which is absent from `origin/dev`. It must fail before the fix (AC4 i/iii).
2. Attribute the prior-run commit in `phase_finish` and correct the refusal
   wording (AC1/AC3); the `--verification-only` path stays untouched.
3. Confirm `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` still fails
   loudly on a genuinely work-less worktree (AC2/AC4 ii).
4. Update `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`
   (AC5).

**Reuse.** `_classify_child_worktree` (~line 2097) already carries the exact
attribution shape AC1 needs — `git rev-list --count <base>..HEAD`, then
`git log <base>..HEAD --grep <item-id> -n 1 --format=%H`. Share that as a
helper rather than reimplementing it, with one crucial difference in the base:
AC1 compares against `origin/<parent_branch>`, not local `<parent_branch>` —
after an interrupted push the commit is already on *local* `dev`, so a
local-`dev` base reports "0 ahead" and would re-refuse. Attribution stays
strict: no `--grep` match → no attribution (parent epic AC2).

**Duplicate check.** Searched `no_commit_no_signal`, `prior-run commit` and
`attributable commit`: SA-0MW74IJWI009NRZ1 (completed) scopes only the
refusal, and parent epic SA-0MVYYL7X9008MGA1 explicitly leaves this half out.
No item satisfies these ACs; no duplicate created or closed.

**Vertical slice.** A single slice through code + tests + docs; phasing is
unnecessary here and deliberately not applied.

**Plan: changelog (2026-11-10).** AC1 now names the retained-state
interruption record alongside the report and completion comment (the
`_set_finish_progress` call is the third place the description's "Existing
state" flags as never attributing). Stale line anchors refreshed; Plan block
added with test-first order, the reuse note (including the
`origin/<parent_branch>` base caveat) and the duplicate-check result. No AC
was added, removed or re-scoped; no child items were created.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` commit-outcome branch (~line 11580), `git_get_commit_hash`, the refusal message, `_set_finish_progress`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_interruption_recovery.py` — new test for the interrupted-push re-run convergence
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` — ensure existing no-work refusal test still passes
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — document the re-run attribution behaviour
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — document the re-run attribution behaviour

## Related work

- SA-0MVYYL7X9008MGA1 — Parent epic: "Finish must not mark an item terminal when its worktree produced no commit and its ACs need an operational run"
- SA-0MVXUSJJY009HMQ0 — Interruption recovery: the documented contract this fix enables
- SA-0MW74IJWI009NRZ1 — The refusal slice that introduced the gap (SA-0MVYYL7X9008MGA1 child)
- SA-0MW74IKJE008JXDQ — The observed live incident: timed-out session with unpushed commit

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

None — the work item was already sufficiently defined with clear ACs, key files, and an existing bug report. All acceptance criteria are testable and measurable.

- Q: none directed to the producer — planning auto-skipped the interview
  (effort Small / risk Low) and no question was needed.
  Research note (plan, 2026-11-10): `_classify_child_worktree`
  (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py:2097`) already implements the
  `<base>..HEAD` + `--grep <item-id>` attribution pattern AC1 needs. AC1 must
  use `origin/<parent_branch>` as its base because after an interrupted push
  the commit is already on local `dev`. Source: code inspection of
  `implement.py` and `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_interruption_recovery.py`.
- Review evidence (plan, 2026-11-10): all five predicted key files exist and
  pass `validate_key_files_format()`; the AC section parses to exactly 5 ACs.

## Problem

The audit runner's in-main-slot resume clears its own view of pending child screens but does not delete the on-disk signal file.

Observed on 2026-11-09 auditing `CG-0MW917K7V009LMLE` (Tableau-Card-Engine):

- Run 1 (12:09-12:11) emitted one in-main-slot child screen for `CG-0MW97UZ68001JTGK` and wrote `.worklog/audit-checkpoints/CG-0MW917K7V009LMLE.pending-screens.json`.
- The child was then closed (duplicate, failure fixed upstream).
- Resume run (13:33-13:34) reported `"pending_child_screens": []` in its JSON and a `Ready to close: Yes` verdict, **but the signal file was still present afterwards**, still naming the closed child.

## Impact

`cmd_issue` bypasses the freshness gate while `pending-screens.json` names any child (SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S). A stale file therefore forces every later audit of that item to re-run the whole Phase 1 pipeline (one model call each) even though nothing is pending — a silent, repeatable cost. The document says the signal 'is cleared automatically when no screens remain'; it is not.

## Reproduction

1. Audit an item with one unaudited child in default in-main-slot mode to get the pending signal written.
2. Persist/close the child so no screens remain, then re-run the parent audit.
3. Observe `pending_child_screens: []` in the JSON while `.worklog/audit-checkpoints/<id>.pending-screens.json` still lists the child.

## Expected

The signal file is removed (or rewritten empty and then removed) whenever the collected pending set is empty, on both the fresh-run and resume paths.

## Actual

The file persists with its previous content.

## Workaround applied

Deleted the stale file manually so the next audit can take the freshness fast path.

## Discovered from

CG-0MW917K7V009LMLE (Tableau-Card-Engine docs audit)
