# Intake Brief: Do not require repeated producer reviews during release

## Problem statement

When a release re-audits work items (gate remediation, freshness re-runs), the
items are sometimes re-armed with `needsProducerReview`, so the producer is
asked to re-approve work the release itself has just touched. The desired rule
is simple: **require a producer review only when the audit failed for any
reason, or when code/content changed since the last review** — never because a
passing re-audit of unchanged work ran during a release.

## Users

- **Producer (operator)** — user story: "When I run a release I don't want the
  release's own re-audits to put passing, unchanged items back into my review
  queue; I only want to see genuine failures or actual changes."
- **Release engineer / automated release agent** — user story: "I want the
  producer-review flag to mean exactly 'the producer must look now', so the
  release gate neither blocks on already-reviewed unchanged work nor silently
  lets a failed item drop off the queue."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Producer-review policy is stated and enforced.** `needsProducerReview` is
   set only when (a) the audit failed for any reason (an independent or
   ship-triggered verdict of `Ready to close: No`), or (b) the item's audited
   content/code changed since the last producer review. A passing re-audit of
   unchanged work — including during a release — never sets it.
2. **Failed ship-triggered re-audits still surface to the producer.** A
   ship-gate re-audit (SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ's planned `--ship-triggered` path)
   whose verdict is `Ready to close: No` still sets `needsProducerReview` for
   the item to reach the producer queue; the ship-triggered carve-out
   suppresses only the passing/verification case. Where this diverges from
   SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ AC1 ('No' verdict leaves the flag untouched), the
   producer's stated rule in this item takes precedence and the divergence is
   reconciled (that item's Appendix Q2 explicitly awaited producer
   confirmation, which this item provides).
3. **Code/content-change trigger is not swallowed.** The ship-triggered
   suppression never overrides the content-fingerprint change signal: a
   ship-triggered re-audit of an item whose audited content changed since the
   last review still resolves to `required`, exactly as an independent audit
   would.
4. **Targeted tests.** Tests exercise production code and lock: passing
   unchanged re-audit → no flag write; failed re-audit (independent and
   ship-triggered) → flag write; content change → flag write; marker absence
   → flag behaviour unchanged.
5. **Documentation updated.** `skill/audit/SKILL.md`,
   `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` and
   `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` document the
   only-when-failed-or-changed flag rule and the ship-triggered carve-out
   boundary (passing suppressed, failing/change still flagged).
6. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Impact

Producers stop being asked to re-review work the release simply re-audited,
while genuine audit failures and real changes still land in their queue.

## Constraints

- **Independent audit behaviour unchanged.** Audits run outside release
  automation keep today's flag rules exactly (SA-0MVR9B1UH002BUST,
  SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42, SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H preserve/required/untouched
  semantics); only ship-automated verification runs are touched.
- **No new flag-clearing behaviour.** Suppression means "don't write the
  flag", never `--needs-producer-review no` retro-clearing; the ship close
  step's authorised override (SA-0MUJLWPB10038Z8Q) is unchanged.
- **Reconcile with SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ before/while implementing.** That item
  is already planned (plan_complete); its 'No'-verdict suppression must be
  reconciled with AC2 of this item rather than silently shipping both.
- **Repository boundary.** Changes live in SorraAgents skills (audit, ship)
  and their docs; no herdr/ContextHub change required.

## Existing state

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_resolve_producer_review_decision()`
  (~line 2745) resolves `preserved`/`required`/`untouched`;
  `_passing_audit_producer_decision()` (~line 2674) mirrors the passing
  verdict; `_apply_terminal_lifecycle()` (~line 17122) writes
  `--needs-producer-review yes` when `required`. Existing carve-outs: child
  items never flagged; cascade-demotion-suppressed 'No' untouched;
  tracked/accepted medium/low candidate-false-positive chores untouched.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`, `check-final-validation.js`,
  `refresh-audits.js` — release-gate re-audit call sites that run
  `audit_runner.py issue <id> --strict` (the SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ marker
  threading is planned but not yet implemented).
- Flag-rule precedents: SA-0MVR9B1UH002BUST (preserve review across passing
  re-audits, flag independent failures), SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW (flag when
  automated audit says ready to close), SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H (top-level only).

## Desired change

- Confirm the producer-review flag rule as stated in AC1 and enforce it in the
  audit runner and the release flow: passing re-audits of unchanged items never
  set the flag; failing re-audits and content/code changes always do.
- Reconcile with SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ: its ship-triggered marker suppression
  covers the passing/verification case only; the failing-verdict case keeps
  flagging (or the divergence is explicitly recorded and producer-approved).

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_resolve_producer_review_decision()`
  and `_passing_audit_producer_decision()`: enforce only-when-failed-or-changed;
  ship-triggered marker consultation must not swallow failure/change signals.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`, `check-final-validation.js`,
  `refresh-audits.js` — reconciliation with SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ marker
  threading (failing-verdict boundary).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`,
  `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — document the flag rule and
  the carve-out boundary.
- `skill/audit/tests/` (`test_audit_runner_producer_review.py`,
  `test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`) — AC4 coverage.

## Related work

- **SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ** — Ship skill triggered audits should not mark for
  producer review (open, plan_complete): the planned ship-triggered marker
  mechanism this item's rule constrains; reconciliation required (AC2).
- **SA-0MVR9B1UH002BUST** — Audit runner: preserve a producer's review across
  passing re-audits; flag failing audits (completed): defines the
  preserved/required/untouched decision the release rule extends.
- **SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW** — Set producerReview flag when automated audit marks
  item as ready to close (completed): the foundational flag-on-yes rule.
- **SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H** — Audit pass should set needsProducerReview only for
  top-level items (completed): child carve-out.
- **SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42** — audit_runner sets needsProducerReview for every
  medium/low CFP chore (completed): CFP carve-out (same suppression spirit).
- **SA-0MUJLWPB10038Z8Q** — Ship skill: release-ready parent must override or
  absorb needsProducerReview on children (completed): close-step override kept
  out of scope here.
- **SA-0MVX4EHUP0042V9G** — Ship skill invalidates audits (open): adjacent
  freshness concern, distinct ACs.
- Potentially related docs: `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`
  (Producer-review flag lifecycle ~lines 444–542), `skill/audit/SKILL.md`,
  `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — contradictory ACs between items.** SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ's planned
  AC1 suppresses the flag for ship-triggered 'No' verdicts; AC2 of this item
  requires a failing ship-triggered re-audit to flag. Mitigation: this item
  records Blocked-by (SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ) and the reconciliation is made
  explicit before either is implemented; if the producer prefers the
  SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ behaviour, AC2 is amended via that item's plan, not
  silently.
- **Risk — marker leakage** (from SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ): the ship-triggered
  marker must not be settable in an operator's shell. Mitigation: adopt the
  planned CLI-flag mechanism, never an env var.
- **Assumption — 'code was changed' = content-fingerprint change.** The only
  change signal the runner has today is the title/description content
  fingerprint; a repo/commits-change signal is out of scope (separate work
  item if desired).
- **Scope-creep guard.** Verdict semantics, close-step overrides, and the
  freshness/time-gate concerns of SA-0MVX4EHUP0042V9G are deliberately out of
  scope; they remain linked work items.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **OPEN QUESTION (failing ship-triggered re-audit):** Should a ship-gate
  re-audit whose verdict is `Ready to close: No` still set
  `needsProducerReview`, or is demotion out of the release queue sufficient (as
  SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ's plan assumes)? **Recommended (Map, intake): flag it /
  keep AC2 — this item's seed states the producer's rule that a producer review
  is required whenever the audit failed for any reason, and SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ
  Appendix Q2 explicitly awaited producer confirmation on exactly this point;
  this item is that confirmation.** Source: seed context of SA-0MWJ8WGQD0073MG1
  ("We should only require a producer review if the audit failed for any
  reason, or if code was changed"), SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ Appendix Q2. Not
  independently re-confirmed (operator instructed no repeated producer reviews
  during this intake).
- **Assumption ("code was changed"):** "Code was changed" maps to the audit
  runner's existing content-fingerprint change signal (title/description
  content changed since the last review → fresh audit required), which is the
  only change signal the runner currently has; the item records the policy that
  this signal must keep arming the flag including for ship-triggered runs.
  A broader "repo/commits changed" signal would be a separate work item.
- **Assumption (relationship):** SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ (already planned) is the
  implementation vehicle for the passing-verification suppression; this item
  carries the flag-rule policy and the failing/change boundary; the plan stage
  should reconcile the two (this item records Blocked-by SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ).

## Review log

- Completeness review: brief covers problem, users, ACs, constraints, existing
  state, desired change, key files, related work, appendix — no gaps found.
- Capture fidelity review: seed intent ('only require producer review when the
  audit failed for any reason, or if code was changed') preserved in AC1–AC3;
  SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ 'No'-verdict divergence recorded neutrally.
- Related-work & traceability review: all linked items verified against wl;
  typo SA-0MUJLWPB10038ZQ → SA-0MUJLWPB10038Z8Q corrected.
- Risks & assumptions review: added Risks section (contradictory ACs, marker
  leakage, 'code changed' interpretation, scope-creep guard).
- Polish & handoff review: wording tightened; commands are skill-standard.

## Related work (automated report — find-related)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MPD8NXCS0091ZF4** – Ralph crashes reading persisted audit when workItem.audit is an object (completed)
- **SA-0MPYO85WW006CXPL** – Add version numbering to ship skill for releases (completed)
- **SA-0MQ01FDQ5003H09A** – Implementation: update AMPA audit handlers to use wl audit-set (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: afterwards, audit, auditing, automatically, back (+14 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: afterwards, audit, auditing, automatically, back (+13 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: afterwards, audit, auditing, automatically, back (+13 more)

# Section-test rewrite: body-data-only + appendix coverage (T1)

Test-side slice of SA-0MW7QD3CJ00208YS ("Move the detailed descriptions of the
metrics into an appendix", incl. merged LP-0MW0FU5Z6006A4P3). Rewrites the
per-section regression tests in `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/` that
currently pin the inline metric-description prose so they assert the **new**
report contract instead:

1. The main body of `report.md` contains only **data** (tables, section
   headers, one-sentence metric reminders); every detailed metric-description
   passage moves to an appendix at the end of the document (AC1).
2. Each metrics table in the body carries at most a **one-sentence reminder**
   of its metric's definition (AC2).
3. A metric-glossary appendix (`## Appendix: Metric definitions` or equivalent)
   at the end of `report.md` has an entry for **every** metric in the report
   (AC3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: For every prose passage identified in the parent's Existing state
  (header block; `## Summary by hour` availability footnote + state notes;
  `## Total tokens` formula paragraph; `## Local model utilization`
  `Busy = …` / `Method:` paragraphs; `## Prefill vs decode` slot-seconds
  explanation; `## Engine cross-check` caveats; per-section interpretation
  notes), a test asserts the passage is **not** present verbatim in the body
  section it used to live in.
- AC2: For every metrics table whose full description moved to the appendix, a
  test asserts a **one-sentence reminder** (≤1 sentence gloss) appears in the
  body next to that table or under its section header.
- AC3: A test asserts the metric-glossary appendix
  (`## Appendix: Metric definitions` or equivalent) exists at the end of the
  document (after the last body section and after `## Recommendations` /
  `## Notes and limitations`) and contains a glossary entry for **every
  metric in the report** (full glossary rule, producer Q2=A) with the
  definition, why it matters, how it is calculated, and — for the
  performance/scorecard metrics — levers and trade-offs
  (LP-0MW0FU5Z6006A4P3 content).
- AC4: The tests exercise the report through `build_report()` /
  `analyze_proxy_usage.py` fixtures already present in the test suite; no
  fixture data is reduced relative to today (all existing window shapes still
  covered by T3).
- AC5: The rewritten tests pass with the new report layout and fail (or are
  trivially updated in lock-step) if someone re-inserts a full methodology
  passage into the body — the tests are the regression guard for AC1/AC2/AC3.
- AC6: Test suite stays deterministic and rule-based — no LLM, no network,
  no timing-dependent assertions added.

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` (8.9k

## Goal

Enforce SA-0MWJ8WGQD0073MG1 AC1/AC3 in \`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py\`: \`needsProducerReview\` is set only when (a) the audit failed for any reason (independent or ship-triggered verdict 'Ready to close: No'), or (b) the audited content/code changed since the last producer review. A passing re-audit of unchanged work — including during a release — never sets it. The ship-triggered carving (planned in SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ) must NEVER swallow the failure signal or the content-change signal.

- \`_resolve_producer_review_decision()\` (\`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py\`) resolves \`required\` for a top-level failing verdict (independent and ship-triggered), and for a passing verdict whose content fingerprint changed since the last review — regardless of the ship-triggered marker.

data.comment:
question: intake research shows the item's premise is **partly superseded** by newer work; two design choices need your call before the brief can be finalised.

## Research against current `dev`

- **Post-push verification is now read-only and tree-keyed.** `_resolve_post_push_verification()` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` executes **nothing**: it queries the cache for the pushed commit's tree SHA (`fingerprint_kind="tree"`), first in the pushed worktree, then in the main checkout. `skill/implement/SKILL.md` Step 9 no longer instructs a bare `/skill:test` post-push. So AC1 ("post-push verification executes a fresh run") contradicts the shipped read-only design (SA-0MVXUSED6008J04R), and AC2's "bare `/skill:test`" branch no longer exists in the skill text.
- **The pre-push hook no longer exits 0 for worktrees.** `.githooks/pre-push` runs `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env --gate-commit <sha>`, resolves a **clean checkout of the pushed commit** (the worktree in place — by design, because a fresh checkout has no dependencies; `resolve_gate_subject()`), then `mirror_suite_cache()` copies its entries into `<main>/.worklog/cache`, explicitly on the assumption "an identical key is an identical run".
- **Cache key = command + fingerprint + scope/type namespace.** Worktree fingerprint = HEAD + content of every dirty path; tree fingerprint = the pushed tree SHA. `store()` records only `interpreter` as environment provenance — no checkout path, submodule completeness, or `node_modules` resolution.
- **Residual hazard is real but narrower than described**: a green entry recorded in a worktree whose environment differs (ungated submodule, symlinked `node_modules`, different interpreter) is key-identical to a canonical-checkout run of the same tree, and is deliberately mirrored for the finish/audit consumers. "Identical key = identical run" holds for git content, not for runtime environment.

**Duplicate check performed** — no overlapping item satisfies these ACs. Related: SA-0MWAXC5TD00461FN and SA-0MW7C6BMZ00931JG (tree-keyed gate/key, completed), SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2 (verdict provenance, completed), SA-0MWAXZHOU000UBG1 and SA-0MWB1H4RF006R7SI (audit cache reuse, open — both rely on path-independent reuse), SA-0MVCF5SHU002WNYU (pre-push documentation).

## Q1 — Which half (or both) should close the gap?

- **(a) Evidence policy only** — keep the read-only verification; record environment provenance per entry and treat a provenance mismatch with the canonical checkout as a miss. No key change, no fresh execution inside `finish`.
- **(b) Key integrity only** — fold an environment fingerprint into the cache key so a drifted-worktree entry can never be served to a canonical-checkout consumer; verification stays read-only.
- **(c) Both** — provenance recorded *and* keyed, and the post-push step escalates to a forced targeted run when no canonical-environment entry exists.

**Recommended:** (c) — (b) alone leaves the finish verdict `missing` after an already-landed push with no recovery inside `finish`; (a) alone still lets a plain `/skill:test` in the main checkout be served a drifted-worktree green.

## Q2 — If the key changes, what counts as environment identity?

- **(a) Coarse, path-independent environment fingerprint** — submodule checkout completeness (`git submodule status`), `node_modules` resolution (symlink target / installed lockfile state), interpreter identity, folded into the fingerprint. Same tree + equivalent environment still shares entries across checkouts (finish gate ↔ pre-push ↔ audit), preserving mirroring and AC4.
- **(b) Full checkout identity** — git common dir + absolute worktree path in the key. Strictest isolation, but kills cross-checkout reuse (each `finish` declares a new worktree, so audit/verification would re-execute the full suite) and directly conflicts with SA-0MWAXZHOU000UBG1 / SA-0MWB1H4RF006R7SI.
- **(c) Provenance metadata only, key unchanged** — consumers enforce policy (the key half of Q1(a)). Cheapest, but a plain `/skill:test` in the main checkout can still be served a drifted-worktree green.

**Recommended:** (a) — it makes the documented "identical key = identical run" assumption actually true for runtime environment without the reuse loss of (b).

## Q3 — Post-push behaviour when the only entry is drift-keyed

- **(a) Escalate once, targeted** — run `--scope changed --force` in the canonical checkout and use that as the verdict; escalate to a forced full run for broad/refactor changes or detected divergence (submodule/`node_modules`).
- **(b) Refuse the transition** (`missing`) and let the agent recover manually — honest, but leaves an already-pushed commit with an unfinished `finish`.
- **(c) Accept with a recorded `environment_drift` note** — cheapest, but is exactly the silent cache-serve this item reports.

**Recommended:** (a) — matches AC1/AC4 and keeps fast iteration for narrow changes.

**Assumption recorded:** the RISE evidence in the description (pre-push `exit 0` for worktrees at line ~80) is historical; current hook behaviour supersedes it, so the brief will target today's design. The item is left at `idea`/`open` pending these answers.

data.comment:
Auto-plan completed with review: effort and risk below threshold (Extra Small / Low), so the item stays a single direct-implementation chore with no child decomposition. Review summary:

1. **Requirements & AC alignment review**: Req 4's second clause (worktree-local `.worklog` presence no longer forks the namespace) had no tracing AC — extended AC1 to name the `implement.py start` worktree layout. Every requirement now traces to an AC and no AC is invented.
2. **Completeness review**: Goal/Requirements/ACs present; added a `**Key Files:**` section listing `skill/test_cache.py`, `tests/test_test_cache.py`, `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py`, `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` doc comments and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` cache-compat passages that describe the split namespace and must be updated.
3. **Sequencing & dependencies review**: N/A — no children; direct implementation (build -> test -> commit per the implement skill).
4. **Scope sizing review**: Extra Small effort / Low risk — appropriately sized for direct implementation; all ACs are 2-6 measurable bullets.
5. **Acceptance & testability review**: AC1 (linked-worktree integration, fixture pattern already at tests/test_test_cache.py:270-292 plus `run_tests.py --summary` read-only path), AC2 (byte-identical plain-clone pins at tests/test_test_cache.py:652-673, preserved by the non-linked fallback), AC3 (concurrent writers, requires a unique temp-file name in `_atomic_write` — the current fixed `.tmp` name can tear under two concurrent writers), AC4 (test-skill gate). All pass/fail and testable.
6. **Polish & handoff review**: Description clear and actionable after the two conservative fixes; no open questions.

Design note for implementation: the two options in Requirement 1 are not equivalent. Only Option A (linked worktree resolves to the main checkout's cache: `<main>/.worklog/cache` when main has `.worklog`, else `<git-common-dir>/test-cache`) unifies the two namespaces while keeping repos without worktrees byte-identical (Requirement 3). A universal shared `<git-common-dir>/test-cache` (Option B applied to the main checkout too) would change the plain-clone `.worklog` case and violate Requirement 3. Recommend detecting linked worktrees as `git rev-parse --git-dir` != `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` and resolving via the common dir's parent (the main checkout root). The pre-push hook's `mirror_suite_cache` (shipped by the worklog package, not this repo) becomes redundant for the unified entries but is out of scope to remove.

Appendix (questions & answers):
- Q: Should the namespace be the main checkout's `.worklog/cache` or a shared `<git-common-dir>/test-cache`? Answer (research, eng): Option A (main checkout's resolved cache) is the only self-consistent reading — Requirement 3 (byte-identical non-worktree repos) rules out a universal shared common-dir namespace, and a worktree-only shared common-dir path would still differ from the main checkout's `.worklog/cache`. Final: Option A, with `<git-common-dir>/test-cache` as the fallback when the main checkout lacks `.worklog`. Evidence: work item requirements + skill/test_cache.py:cache_dir().
- Q: Is the existing atomic-write pattern sufficient for AC3 (2 concurrent writers, no torn write)? Answer (research, eng): No — `_atomic_write` uses a fixed `.tmp` name, so two concurrent writers can interleave into the same temp file and one `os.replace` can publish torn content. Final: give each writer a unique temp name (pid/uuid suffix) before `os.replace`, keeping the API unchanged. Evidence: skill/test_cache.py:_atomic_write.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
question: Fix scope for the age-expiry hazard in acquireFileLock() (src/file-lock.ts). The discovery note says 'Treat a same-host live holder as authoritative ... and/or refresh the lock (acquiredAt heartbeat) during long syncs' — the 'and/or' leaves the choice open and it changes the ACs/effort, so the intake needs your pick before finalising.

**A) Minimal (recommended):** same-host live PID is authoritative — never age-expire a lock whose holder PID is alive on this host; keep age-expiry for same-host dead PIDs, foreign-host locks, and unparseable/corrupt locks. Rationale: closes the reported same-host hazard (all wl processes run on this host) with the smallest change and no new runtime machinery.

**B) Minimal + heartbeat:** also refresh the lock's acquiredAt while a long sync runs, so the lock never appears age-expired to any observer (protects foreign-host readers; removes the PID-recycling corner entirely).

**C) Heartbeat only:** keep age-expiry but make the live holder refresh, so a live (refreshing) holder's lock is never old enough to steal.

Full draft brief (without this answer only the decision-gated AC is unfinished) is at .worklog/tmp/intake-draft-file-lock-age-expiry-SA-0MVL7YG2S009L6PU.md — left un-finalised and the item staged 'idea' pending this answer.

Context gathered so far — real observed PSI data (archived session logs):
- CPU `some` avg10 = 88.78 at 16-core load ~44/50/33 (2026-09-27, severely oversubscribed) → current 70/85 classifies **critical**.
- CPU `some` avg10 = 11.58 at load 11.92 (2026-10-21 discovery run, busy multi-agent host) → current 70/85 classifies **low**.
- IO `full` avg10 = 0.00–0.05 (all archived observations; **no genuine I/O-starvation sample exists**).
- `memory_pressure` (also `full` avg10) precedent: warning 5 / critical 20.

Q1. **cpu_pressure target (some avg10)** — observed "busy healthy" ≈ 11.6, "extreme" ≈ 88.8. Current 70/85 keeps both classified sensibly but only alarms near-death.
  - A) Keep 70/85 — validate against real data, document rationale.
  - B) Lower to catch contention earlier (e.g. warn 30 / crit 60) — the skill's value is proactive remediation before the host thrashes.
  - C) Middle ground (e.g. warn 50 / crit 75).
  **Recommended:** B — 70 % `some`-stall means the host is already severely degraded; an amber band from ~30 % lets the skill propose renice/kill remediation while the host is still responsive. (Advisory — your call.)

Q2. **io_pressure target (full avg10)** — observed values ≤ 0.05; 50/80 never fires (the item itself flags this as broken). `memory_pressure` full-line precedent is 5/20.
  - A) Mirror memory_pressure: warn 5 / crit 20 (same full-line semantics).
  - B) Slightly higher (warn 10 / crit 30) — I/O stalls may be noisier than memory stalls.
  - C) Keep 50/80 but document (no functional change).
  **Recommended:** A — identical `full`-line semantics and an established 5/20 precedent; keeps the genuine I/O-starvation signal without false alarms at idle.

Q3. **Validation data sufficiency (AC1: "validated against observed stall percentages on a busy multi-agent host")** — CPU has two real archived samples (11.58, 88.78); IO has only idle samples.
  - A) Validate with archived observations + this host's live `/proc/pressure`; calibrate IO from full-line semantics/memory precedent; cover classification boundaries with tests. (Pragmatic — genuine I/O-starvation samples are rare.)
  - B) Also induce a controlled I/O stall (e.g. a bounded `dd`/write burst) to capture a real IO `full` sample before finalising. (Stronger validation, small added effort + host load.)
  **Recommended:** B — AC1 explicitly demands validation against observed busy-host stall percentages, and IO currently has **zero** busy samples; one bounded induced sample makes the calibration evidence-based rather than assumed. (Advisory — your call.)

Answers will unblock the intake brief (ACs to be updated with calibrated values, key files, effort/risk).

- **Incident mechanism (from worklog evidence):** on SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2 the
  operator confirmation ("Effort M / risk High carried over from the OSL intake",
  2026-10-23 comment) was recorded **in a comment**, and the effort/risk **fields
  were empty** when `plan-if-needed` ran on 2026-10-27 09:38. Proof: the estimator
  ran at all — `is_effort_risk_computed` returns True whenever **both** fields are
  non-empty, so the fields cannot have held High/M. The estimator then wrote
  Extra Small/Low via `orchestrate_estimate.py::_update_work_item`
  (`wl update --effort --risk` — it blindly overwrites), and Map manually
  restored the fields to High/M (restore comment SA-C0MVQKM7XD0089OVQ).
- **Residual gaps in current code** (the zeroed-placeholder root cause is already
  fixed by SA-0MW0LPXXY0002CQ0, and the fetch-failure corruption by
  SA-0MSIUJQAK008AQV8):
  1. *Comment-only confirmation:* fields empty + comment confirms values + the
     item HAS estimable inputs (children with effort labels) → the derived
     estimate is written over the confirmation.
  2. *Partial-set:* only one field deliberately set (e.g. effort=M, risk empty) →
     `is_effort_risk_computed` is False (needs BOTH) → the estimator overwrites
     the deliberately-set field.
  3. *No warning surface:* when the estimator does run, it replaces existing
     field values with no warning/approval.
- **Duplicate check performed:** no full duplicate. Overlapping (related, both
  completed): SA-0MW0LPXXY0002CQ0 (zeroed payload), SA-0MSIUJQAK008AQV8
  (fetch-failure corruption). Origin: SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2.

## Questions

### Q1 — What counts as "an explicitly set/human-confirmed" value (recognition mechanism)?

- (a) **Fields + provenance:** any stored effort/risk value is *deliberate* unless
  it is attributable to a prior estimator run (an `effort_and_risk_skill` comment
  or `autoplan-decision-hash` marker explains it). Empty fields → estimator may
  run. Does NOT protect comment-only confirmations (the exact incident shape).
- (b) **Fields + intake-side recording:** (a) plus a convention that operator
  confirmations (e.g. carry-over values like the incident's) are written into the
  fields at confirmation time, so the existing fields gate protects them. Closes
  the incident end-to-end; touches intake/plan flows as a small convention change.
- (c) **Fields + comment marker:** (a) plus recognising a new explicit marker
  (e.g. `operator-confirmed-effort:M`, `operator-confirmed-risk:High`) in comments.

**Recommended: (b)** — writes confirmations where the gate already looks (the
fields), avoids fragile comment parsing, and fixes the exact incident shape.

### Q2 — Remediation when a genuine recomputation would overwrite a deliberate value (AC1's "or")?

- (a) **Gate:** skip the recomputation entirely and record the rationale
  (dedicated comment/log entry); the deliberate value stays.
- (b) **Surface:** post an explicit warning comment and refuse to overwrite
  without explicit confirmation (e.g. operator-approved `--force` / approval gate).
- (c) **Both:** gate by default; `--force` escape hatch that surfaces the warning
  and requires confirmation before overwriting.

**Recommended: (c)** — gate by default (plan-if-needed runs in automation with no
interactive approval channel), with an explicit, approval-gated opt-out for
genuinely needed recomputations.

### Q3 — Regression-test coverage for AC2 (test must be RED before the fix to be meaningful)?

- (a) **Exact incident shape:** operator confirmation present (per Q1's chosen
  mechanism), no prior estimator comment → value preserved.
- (b) **Partial-set shape:** only one field deliberately set → the set field is
  preserved.
- (c) **Both (a) and (b).**

**Recommended: (c)** — both, matching AC1's "an explicitly set/human-confirmed
effort OR risk" (per-field protection).

## Scope inventory and assumptions

- **In scope:** 431 tracked test files — 375 pytest (`test_*.py`) and 56 node (`*.test.mjs` / `test-*.mjs`). Areas: `tests/` 176, `skill/audit` 64, `skill/implement` 51, `skill/shared` 30, `skill/test` 15, `skill/standup` 12, `skill/machine-hygiene` 7, `skill/intake` 5, others ≤3, `command/` 1.

- **Planning probe (evidence the scope is real, not the committed baseline):** `evaluate_usefulness.py` over the 431 tracked files returned **376 keep / 55 remove**. The dominant class is source-grep. Note the evaluator is *file-scoped*: a file with one offending case is reported `remove`, so a `remove` verdict is never authority to delete a file — hence the separate rework and prune children.
- **Assumption (documented, not blocking):** the 55 flagged files are mostly rework-not-prune; the delete list is expected to be much smaller and is authorised only by the Prove child's evidence.

| 1 | Measure: capture test suite baseline metrics (SA-0MWG509GZ002JIBB) | Measure | — |

Every child now carries a Goal, deliverables, minimal implementation, key files, measurable acceptance criteria, constraints and related work. Two children were added/changed at this planning pass: the new Verify child (SA-0MWIHSSCU002FJRL, previously missing — epic AC6's before/after coverage map had no owner) and four new dependency edges so the guard and the coverage map land on a remediated suite.

## Vertical slice check

Each child cuts through all layers for its phase (analysis/code + tests + committed artefact under `docs/dev/` + review evidence). Between phases: re-read the next child before starting it, and update its description if the previous phase changed the numbers (for example, the final prune list can only be sized after Prove). No horizontal "all docs at the end" phasing except the deliberate Guard-docs child, whose content depends on what the pass learned.

## Automated review stages

Finished Requirements & AC alignment review: all 10 epic acceptance criteria map to at least one child AC (10/10, Jaccard ≥ 0.4 verified with `shared/tree_coverage.compute_coverage`); 41 child ACs, each traced to a scope phase — no invented requirements, no contradictions. The one AC that had no owner (AC6, before/after coverage map) was given the new Verify child, whose first AC restates AC6 verbatim.
Finished Completeness review: all 9 children contain Goal, Deliverables, Minimal Implementation, Key Files, Acceptance Criteria, Constraints and Related work; `validate_key_files_format()` reports no issues on any child; key-file sets include both the inputs each child consumes and the artefacts it must produce.
Finished Sequencing & dependencies review: graph is acyclic and topologically ordered (Measure → Classify → Prove → {prune, rework} → {guard, verify} → {guard-docs, report}). Test/verification items (guard regression test, coverage map) are ordered *after* remediation deliberately: they must observe a cleaned suite, otherwise they would be red from the day they land; this is documented in each item's Context.
Finished Scope sizing review: 9 children, each an end-to-end deliverable. The two remediation children carry an explicit batch rule — split by area into child work items as soon as a list exceeds ~25 files — so no implementation session is unbounded.
Finished Acceptance & testability review: every AC is pass/fail observable (committed artefact, cited run, reconciled total, measured drop). Vague candidates were tightened during drafting (for example "measurable reduction" became "before/after numbers per suite, median of ≥2 runs through the test skill"). The Report child's "limitations stated explicitly" is a reviewable artefact requirement, accepted as testable.
Finished Polish & handoff review: UK English throughout, headings and bullet format consistent, commands copy-pasteable and routed through the test skill (no ad-hoc `pytest`/`node --test` invocations anywhere in the plan).

- **Risk: High** (probability 3.09 × impact 4.12 = 13). Top drivers: the Measure/Classify/Prove evidence chain, from which every irreversible deletion hangs.
- Plan-approval gate: Large effort + High risk is **not** Extra Large + High, so no approval pause was required (`request_approval: false`).

**Question (from the planning pass):** does epic AC4 ("no remaining test file reads a source/markdown file and asserts on its text") intend to eliminate this repository's repository-contract and inventory tests?

**Decision (producer delegated the call; option (c) adopted):** no. Tests that read files are **not one class**, and "reads a markdown file" is not a defect. The pass keeps the contract/hygiene tests but requires them to assert parsed structure, and it explicitly exempts the classes where the `.md` is incidental or is production output.

**Evidence behind it.** Of the 431 in-scope test files, 181 reference a `.md` path and ~127 read one. Sampled inspection gives a closed five-class taxonomy:

| Class | What it is | ≈Files | Treatment |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A — sandbox fixture** | the test writes `README.md`/`notes.md` inside a temp `git_sandbox` repo to exercise production code (e.g. `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_commit_tree.py`, `tests/test_implement_finish_local_dev_verified_sync.py`) | 104 | exempt — `.md` is incidental; swap it for `.txt` and nothing changes |
| **B — production output** | production code writes the markdown and the test asserts the artefact (e.g. `tests/node/test-generate-changelog.mjs` asserting the generated `CHANGELOG.md` structure) | 22 | exempt — behavioural test of an observable artefact |
| **C — link/structure hygiene** | parses markdown to assert links resolve / referenced paths exist / headings present (e.g. `tests/test_skill_link_hygiene.py`, which catches the `../docs/dev/...` dead-link class) | 9 | keep — asserts resolvability, not prose |
| **D — doc-contract** | asserts a document states a rule or invariant (e.g. `tests/test_finish_gate_docs.py` vs `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`) | 22 | **rework** to parsed structure |
| **E — duplicate convention grep** | a narrow per-skill text grep whose convention is already covered generically (e.g. `tests/unit/test-triage-skill.mjs`, superseded by `tests/test_skill_path_conventions.py`) | several | **prune** |

**Class D rule.** Assert parsed structure — headings, frontmatter keys, labelled bullets, table cells, resolved links — or, where the exact wording *is* the contract (a sentence agents are told to quote), cite in a comment the work item that mandates that wording. No raw prose substring assertions.

**Why not option (b) (absolute).** Reading AC4 absolutely would churn ~135 files (classes A–C) for zero behavioural gain and real regression risk — precisely the "growth without value" pattern this epic exists to remove. Option (a) (leave contract tests untouched) was rejected because prose substrings are what actually rot: they fail on rewording and never on a regression, so class D gets converted rather than preserved as-is.

**Changes applied to the plan (epic AC coverage re-verified at 10/10, 46 child ACs):**
- `SA-0MWG50OB2003ON99` (Classify) — tags every `.md`-touching file with its class; A/B/C cannot be rework/prune on the strength of reading markdown.
- `SA-0MWG51S1D0084L0H` (Rework) — closed taxonomy in context; AC4 scoped to classes D/E; A/B/C explicitly exempt; class D parsed-structure/citation rule.
- `SA-0MWG5284K004J1YN` (Guard) — class-aware exemption entries (`{path, class, work-item-id}`), with fixtures proving A/B/C are not flagged and D/E never exemptable.
- `SA-0MWG52KSC008DFKC` (Guard docs) — the taxonomy and class D rule are published in `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` with one real example per class.

Effort/risk unchanged (Large / High — score 13). The decision narrows the remediation surface (no work in classes A–C), which is why no re-estimate is needed.

data.comment:
# Plan: test-value aggregator — decomposition

**Decision model, in one paragraph (for review).** Each test file receives a
verdict from four signals: **anti-pattern** (`evaluate_usefulness.py`,
static), **churn** (`test_churn_data.json` → `file_stability.top_files`,
evolution), **mutation** (planned `mutation_report.json` +
`suite_source_map.json`, behavioural) and optional **runtime/flake**. Rule
order is conservative and deterministic: (1) a healthy mutation score blocks
`prune` outright — behavioural evidence outranks a static veto; (2) `prune`
requires **two independent** prune-leaning signals; (3) contradictory
signals resolve to `rework` with the conflict recorded; (4) cost/stability-only
signals give `rework`; (5) a file with no signals at all gets a conservative
default flagged `insufficient`. Thresholds are documented, configurable
defaults (mutation healthy ≥ 0.60 / weak ≤ 0.20; churn rewrite ratio high
≥ 40 %; ≥ 4 feature commits), and `prune` is advisory — nothing is deleted.

## Features (test-first order)

| # | ID | Title | Type | Depends on |
|---|----|-------|------|-----------|
| 1 | SA-0MWISIOLU007TOIW | Signal fixtures and loader contract tests | task | — |
| 2 | SA-0MWISIPG3001SHGA | Verdict decision-model tests | task | — |
| 3 | SA-0MWISIQ7Z002RMGZ | Signal loaders for upstream analyser outputs | feature | 1 |
| 4 | SA-0MWISIR1T008FJTM | Documented keep/rework/prune decision model | feature | 2 |
| 5 | SA-0MWISIRVN008H7DU | Aggregator entry point and dual artefacts | feature | 3, 4 |
| 6 | SA-0MWISISOD005DOU4 | Aggregator end-to-end tests | task | 5 |
| 7 | SA-0MWISITH3003EFBF | SKILL.md contract for test-value | docs | 5 |
| 8 | SA-0MWISIU9R008ZSAO | Reference docs and README registration | docs | 7 |
| 9 | SA-0MWISIV36008FFE0 | Real-signal validation run on this repository | task | 6, 8 |

## Vertical-slice phasing

Each phase cuts through code + tests + docs end to end; review the next
phase's items and update their descriptions before starting it.

1. **Evidence ingestion** (1 → 3): fixture + loader contract test, then the
   loaders that satisfy it. Deliverable: every signal is readable, and its
   absence is a first-class, reported state.
2. **Verdict reconciliation** (2 → 4): case-table tests, then the documented
   model. Deliverable: one conservative, deterministic verdict per file with
   cited evidence.
3. **Report delivery** (5 → 6): entry point + dual artefacts, then
   CLI-level end-to-end tests including the
   orchestrates-not-reimplements assertions. Deliverable: the two artefacts.
4. **Contract & reference docs** (7 → 8): SKILL.md, then the developer
   reference + README registration.
5. **Real-signal validation** (9): run against this repository and record the
   register, proving honest degradation with mutation absent.

## Reuse identified (no reimplementation)

- `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py` — churn artefacts **and**
  its `is_test_file` classifier is imported for scope resolution rather than
  duplicated.
- `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py` — per-file anti-pattern verdicts
  (`keep` / `remove` / `report-to-user`), consumed or invoked, never
  reimplemented.
- `skill/mutation-test/` — planned by `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O`; consumed as an
  honestly-absent signal until it lands.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` symlinks the whole `skill/` tree, so a new skill
  needs no per-skill install wiring.

## Six automated review stages

Finished Requirements & AC alignment review: mapped all nine parent ACs to
owning children; found four weak mappings (ingestion, one-verdict-per-file,
totals reconciliation, orchestration) and three effectively uncovered ACs
(honest degradation, reproducibility, documentation) — fixed by making the
owning child's AC explicit rather than creating near-duplicate children. No
invented requirements; nothing changed in the parent's AC set.

Finished Completeness review: all nine children carry Goal, Target outcome,
Definition of done, Constraints, Risky assumptions, Acceptance Criteria and
Key Files; `validate_key_files_in_description()` reports no issues; every
`feature`/`task`/`docs` child has a parseable `## Acceptance Criteria` section.

Finished Sequencing & dependencies review: both test-first items (1, 2)
precede their implementations (3, 4); the entry point (5) follows the
modules it composes; end-to-end tests (6) follow the entry point; validation
(9) is last. All edges wired with `wl dep add` and acyclic.

Finished Scope sizing review: each child is a deliverable increment; item 5 is
the largest and is deliberately kept whole — it is a single entry point with
one CLI surface, and splitting it would create two half-wired items.

Finished Acceptance & testability review: every AC is pass/fail and testable;
threshold-sensitive behaviour is pinned via exported `DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS` so a
documented retune does not force test rewrites; determinism assertions are
timestamp-normalised.

Finished Polish & handoff review: descriptions are copy-pasteable and in UK
English; one malformed AC block introduced during review was repaired on
SA-0MWISIRVN008H7DU; JSON/YAML-free prose throughout.

**AC coverage review: `proceed` — 100 % of parent ACs covered (0 gaps, 0
conflicts).** Stage advanced to `plan_complete`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (this run, agent):** "Do the nine parent ACs already determine the
  decomposition, or is a producer interview needed?" — **Answer (agent):** they
  determine it. Every AC maps to a concrete artefact (loaders, decision model,
  entry point, two artefacts, tests, docs, validation run); seed reading of
  `skill/test-churn/`, `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py` and the
  planned mutation arm resolved the remaining inputs. Source: repository reads
  listed under **Key Files** in each child.
- **Duplicate check (this run):** searched `wl` for `test value verdict` and
  walked the epic `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO`'s nine children (all downstream
  Remediate/Guard/Report items) and the sibling arms
  `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` (mutation), `SA-0MVXVC9FM003ZJKJ` (runtime/flake),
  `SA-0MVXVC6C4009661D` (near-duplicate), `SA-0MVXVC33N007Q71K`
  (assertion quality). No existing item produces a per-file reconciled
  keep/rework/prune register; no duplicate or overlapping completed item
  found. Source: `wl search`, `wl list --parent SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO --json`.
- **Confirmed input:** churn per-file evidence is **top-20 only**
  (`analyse_per_file_stability(limit=20)`, feature commits only), so "churn
  absent" is the normal case for most test files. Recorded in the loader
  contract (item 1) and the limitations (items 7, 8) rather than being papered
  over with an inferred zero. Source:
  `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py:787-823`.
- **Confirmed input:** `evaluate_usefulness.py` emits
  `{file, verdict ∈ keep|remove|report-to-user, reasons[], summary}` per file
  and is per-file only today (whole-suite classification is blocked item
  `SA-0MWG50OB2003ON99`). The aggregator therefore owns the file iteration.
  Source: `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py:87-99, 253-275`.
- **OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking, producer):** what should a file with **no
  signals at all** report? Option A (recommended): one of the three verdicts —
  `keep` — flagged `insufficient_evidence`, so `keep + rework + prune` still
  sums to files in scope while the report states no evidence exists. Option B:
  a fourth outcome (`unknown`) reported outside the three-value totals.
  **Recommended: A** — it keeps the reconciled-totals AC true and
  "never fabricates a verdict" true, and it is the conservative choice (no
  recommendation without evidence). Why it does not block: both options yield
  the same decomposition — only a constant and one documented rule differ, and
  item 4 owns that rule; if you choose B, only that item's default changes.
  Source: parent ACs "Emits one verdict per file" and "never fabricates a
  verdict".

- 2026-11-16 — Decomposed SA-0MVXVBZT7003VOCO into 9 children (2 test-first,

question: intake is blocked on three producer decisions (also recorded as OPEN QUESTION entries in the description Appendix).

**Q1 — How is an item judged minor-worthy?** Options: (A) by issueType — feature/epic → minor, bug/chore/task/docs/empty → patch; (B) by priority — high/critical → minor; (C) explicit new label/tag on the item. **Recommended: A** — closest existing proxy for new user-facing capability, no new metadata, and overridable with --bump.

**Q2 — How does the producer approve a proposed minor bump in a non-interactive pipeline?** Options: (A) fail-closed: exit with a distinct code plus a copy-pasteable approval command, producer re-runs with --bump minor (or a dedicated --confirm-bump minor); (B) interactive TTY prompt with A as the non-TTY fallback; (C) automatic minor bump with a warning (rejected: seed requires approval). **Recommended: A** — deterministic for agents, no ambiguous prompt, mirrors existing fail-closed gates, keeps the justification in the release log.

**Q3 — Should the inference ever propose a major (x) bump?** Options: (A) no — only minor/patch are inferred; major remains explicit --bump major; (B) yes — infer major from a new breaking-change convention. **Recommended: A** — matches the seed description and avoids inventing a new convention.

# Planning Complete — Ship skill semver management

## Plan summary

Decomposed into **3 test-first vertical slices** (test-first ordered: C1 enables C2 enables C3). Each slice authors its tests first (TDD) and lands code + tests together, because a standalone red-baseline test child cannot pass the changed-scope test gate.

| # | ID | Title | Type | Priority | Depends on |
|---|----|-------|------|----------|------------|
| 1 | SA-0MWFVQWGN006G4KA | Bump preflight helper: gather release candidates + review packet | feature | high | — |
| 2 | SA-0MWFVQX4W0080O86 | Version bump evaluation workflow + in-session approval gate | feature | high | C1 |
| 3 | SA-0MWFVQXSZ000EN5I | Document bump evaluation in ship reference + run-release logging | task | medium | C2 |

### What each slice delivers

1. **Preflight helper** (`skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` + tests): gathers `in_review` candidates via an injectable boundary, renders a review packet (id/title/issueType/priority/Impact-or-user-story/description excerpt, current version, patch/minor/major outcomes computed with `bumpVersion`). Read-only, fail-safe to `patch` on empty/unreadable candidates, no duplicated semver arithmetic.
2. **Workflow + approval gate** (`skill/ship/SKILL.md` + contract tests): the startup "Version bump evaluation" step before any git mutation, the content-based rubric, patch auto-proceed, minor/major justification + **in-session** producer approval, decline handling, headless fail-closed, and auditability.
3. **Reference docs + logging** (`docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`, optional log-only `run-release.js` line): documents the evaluation step/approval gate, adds the helper to the scripts table, keeps `--bump` forwarding unchanged.

Coverage: all 11 parent acceptance criteria map onto C1–C3; AC coverage review returned **proceed** (no auto-created children remain — two generated coverage-gap stubs were redundant and were deleted, with their parent ACs restated verbatim in C1/C2).

## Six automated review stages

- Finished Requirements & AC alignment review: every parent AC traces to a child AC; explicit restatements added for the semver-reset, unit-test-coverage, documentation, and full-suite ACs.
- Finished Completeness review: all three children have Objective, User Story, Acceptance Criteria, Minimal Implementation, Key Files (path format valid), Constraints, Deliverables.
- Finished Sequencing & dependencies review: test-first within each slice; C2 depends on C1, C3 depends on C2; no cycles.
- Finished Scope sizing review: three deliverable increments, one module / one workflow+docs / one reference-doc slice.
- Finished Acceptance & testability review: all ACs are pass/fail and observable; hermetic tests (injected worklog/git boundaries) required throughout.
- Finished Polish & handoff review: descriptions are copy-pasteable and name the exact files and behaviours to change.

## Design decision (documented assumption)

A standalone TDD "red baseline" test child was **not** created: the implement skill's changed-scope test gate refuses a commit whose tests fail, so a pure red-test item cannot be closed independently. Each slice is therefore a vertical, test-first slice (tests authored first inside the slice). This follows the repo's vertical-slice guidance and TDD preference.

## Effort & risk

Deterministic re-estimate: **Small** effort (~7.2 h expected, ~11.2 h recommended), **Medium** risk (9/25), 87% confidence. Note: the auto-generated WBS lists two "Close coverage gap" rows; those are the deleted coverage-gap stubs and are **not** part of the plan — actual decomposition is the 3 children above.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-14: Plan created (plan skill, downtime dispatch). 3 children created, dependencies wired C1→C2→C3, AC coverage review `proceed`, stage advanced to `plan_complete`, effort/risk re-estimated.

data.comment:
Test-first contract defined (no production behaviour changed).

**Files**
- `tests/test_refactor/test_dedupe_identity.py` (new): unit contract for identity build/parse, marker + fingerprint emission, batch identity grouping, repeat formatting, consolidation grouping.
- `tests/test_refactor/test_workitem_creation.py` (extended): end-to-end cross-family twin suppression (AC5).

**Dormant-until-sibling convention.** A test whose production helper has not landed skips with `not yet implemented (<sibling-id>)`. Each guard probes the *specific* helper/constant its sibling introduces, so F2–F5 each turn on only the tests they implement and every sibling's changed-scope gate stays green. This mirrors the repository's existing `pytest.skip("... not yet available")` test-first convention. Result now: 53 passed, 17 skipped (each skip names its owning sibling).

**API surface the tests lock in** (siblings must implement to match):
- Identity: `build_finding_key(smell, repo_root=None) -> "<code>:<repo-relative-path>"`; `parse_finding_key(key) -> (code, path)`; no line number, no absolute/worktree path; reuses `_repo_relative_path`.
- Description markers (near top): `Refactor-Finding-Key: <code>:<path>`, `Refactor-Fingerprint: <64-hex sha256>`, `Refactor-Affected-Lines: <n>, <m>` (deduped, ascending). `compute_content_fingerprint(smell, repo_root=None) -> <64 hex>`, content-sensitive.
- `create_smell_work_items` groups same-identity findings into one item (union affected lines); different rule codes file distinct items.
- Repeat: `build_repeat_comment(smell, repo_root=None) -> "Refactor-Repeat: <code> in <path> — lines <n>, <m>"`; a line-shifted re-find returns the existing item id and appends this comment, never files a new item.
- Cross-family (F3): module constant `AUDIT_FP_TITLE_MARKER = "candidate false positive"`; an open audit chore titled `ruff <RULE> in <path> — candidate false positive` suppresses refactor creation; terminal chores do not; the refactor producer never closes/patch-mutates the audit chore.
- Consolidation (F5): `refactor.scripts.consolidate_duplicates.group_by_identity(items) -> [{"key", "canonical", "duplicates"}]`; canonical = oldest open (earliest `createdAt`); terminal items excluded; dry-run performs no subprocess/worklog mutation.

**Assumption:** the `Refactor-Finding-Key: <code>:<path>` format follows the audit-side `CFP-Chore-Key` precedent (colon-separated, path may contain colons only after the first split).

data.comment:
## Design decision: resolve the tree-keyed verdict before the lock

Approach: reuse the existing tree-keyed verdict cache (no new indexing).

1. `phase_finish` Step 3b (new, before Step 3c): `resolve_prelock_full_suite_verdict(worktree_path, gate_tree, parent_branch)` runs `run_tests(worktree, scope="full", fingerprint=<would-be-commit tree>)`. The would-be-commit tree is the one `stage_tested_tree` (Step 3d) proves the commit produces, so the entry is keyed exactly on the pushed commit's tree.
2. The pre-push hook's `--gate-commit` run derives `commit^{tree}` (identical) and is served the entry (`verdict=cached`) — so the suite does not execute inside `main-checkout.lock`.
3. The lock still covers only: commit → fast-forward → push → ancestry assertion.
4. Red verdict aborts before the lock (nothing committed/pushed; item released to `open`); classified as a `gate` failure (`full_suite_prelock`, wildcard) so drive never retries it as infrastructure.
5. Stand-down paths (no gate weakening): no would-be-commit tree (`not_a_git_worktree`) and the hook's own `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`.
6. `report["steps"]["main_checkout_lock"]["waited_seconds"]` added as the measurable lock-wait metric.

Safety invariants preserved: the hook still binds the verdict to the pushed commit's tree (a different tree = cache miss = the suite really runs), the bounded `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` is untouched, and single-owner mutation of `dev` is untouched.

Tests: `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py` (lock free while the suite runs; tree binding; lock window excludes the suite; red aborts pre-lock; stand-down paths; two concurrent finishes overlap their suites via a barrier), `tests/test_pre_push_gate_reuse.py` (the verdict recorded by the real `implement.run_tests` entry point IS served to the `--gate-commit` gate — proving the cache keys agree), and `tests/test_implement_finish_no_full_gate.py` (sentinel updated: the one full-scope run is tree-bound and pre-lock).

data.author: Map
data.comment:
Covered by the same commit as its Test sibling: cd0676752 (pushed to dev).

## Why one commit, not one per child

The planned ordering was test-first (Fix depends-on Test), but `implement.py finish` refuses to push a red tree: landing the failing regression tests on their own child would have required pushing a red suite to dev. The session therefore implemented the tests **and** the fix in the Test child's worktree — tests written first, fix second — and shipped them together in cd0676752.

## What shipped for this child's ACs

- `record_spawn_failure` / `read_spawn_failure` / `clear_spawn_failure` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (record under `<worktree>/.worklog/spawn-failure.json`, a path every dirty-path helper excludes, so the record is never mistaken for work).
- `phase_drive` records the evidence on its **non-terminal** spawn-failure path, only for a child with no attributable work (`CHILD_CLEAN`/`CHILD_NO_WORK`), and reports `spawn_failure_recorded` per child.
- `phase_start` clears the record when the next session begins.
- `_child_main_checkout_violation` returns no violation for a child carrying matching evidence, so both `phase_parent` call sites (skip-in-progress and implement) treat the child as startable again; `report["spawn_failure"]` names the evidence in the operator message.

## Deviation from the planned approach (important)

The plan said to branch on `worktree_verdict` alone (`CHILD_CLEAN` → still call the guard). That cannot satisfy this child's first AC: `.implement_state.json` is gitignored, so a spawn-failed child is `CHILD_CLEAN` — indistinguishable on disk from a genuine stray child, and the guard would still blame unrelated dirt. The verdicts were therefore left alone and the missing datum was recorded by the driver, which is the only party that knows the session died. Genuine cross-worktree detection is unchanged and pinned by the existing (unmodified) sibling-stray tests plus a new evidence-free regression on the `skip-in-progress` path.

Tests: `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` (`TestSpawnFailureEvidence`, `TestSpawnFailedChildIsStartableAgain`, `TestDriveRecordsSpawnFailureEvidence`).
